entries.title: I don't have time for this
entries.description:
The Base Commander of Area MC5 couldn't really be bothered to talk to you.

He told you to talk to the Civil Administrator in the middle of the room instead, who apparently talks a lot.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Base Commander / Area MC5

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete I never asked for this
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Civil Administrator / Area MC5

REWARDS
• 50 credits
• 50 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: What are you doing up here? Talk to the Security Chief first, and get your clearance. Or I'll have you shot!

NPC: Listen, pal, I've really had it with your yappin'. Shut up, and talk to the Civil Administrator!

Your response: Yes sir, I will talk to the Civil Administrator immediately!

Your response: Maybe later.

NPC: Didn't I make myself clear? Get lost!

NPC: What are you doing up here already?

Your response: Your Security Chief gave me clearance to be up here. And I'm mighty glad to be here, haha! Really looking forward to be a productive citizen of Neocron!

NPC: Ugh. Do you always talk that much?

Your response: What? No! I mean, yes, I- may perhaps have let my enthusiasm get the better of me there, but...

NPC: You really need to shut your trap, civilian. Say, I've had an idea. Why don't you talk to the Civil Administrator over there. He likes to hear himself talk just as much as you do.

Your response: Yes sir, I will talk to the Civil Administrator immediately!

Your response: Maybe later.

NPC: A simple 'yes' would've sufficed. Now get lost.

NPC: I hate civilians...

NPC: I told you to go talk to the Civil Administrator.

entries.title: Insufficient level
entries.description:
The Chief Technician wouldn't have you going after those security bots with you barely conscious. He told you to come back later, and help out someone outside called Lorcan.

Step outside. Lorcan is down the ramp.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Chief Technician / Area MC5

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete A loquacious intermediary
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Lorcan

REWARDS
• 100 credits
• 100 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: What do you want? I'm busy!

NPC: I'm still pretty busy, you know...

Your response: The Civil Administrator mentioned some problem you need help with?

NPC: I told you: I won't have you put yourself in danger while you're still weak! Come back later.

NPC: Yes, you're strong enough to help me with my problem now, if you're still interested.

Your response: I can still use some cash, if that's included in the offer.

Your response: Not right now, sorry.

NPC: I have nothing else for you to do. You should really leave this place by now. The Gene Replicator is outside, in that little building on the hill, to the left of the ramp.

NPC: What do you want? I'm busy!

Your response: The Civil Administrator mentioned some problem you need help with?

Your response: I won't bother you, then.

NPC: He did, did he? Hell yes, I got a problem. That new program for the security bots in the energy cores is a huge mess! Now they've gone completely off the grid and won't even respond to commands!

Your response: So what do you want me to do?

NPC: YOU?! Don't make me laugh. Look at you! You can barely stand up straight. I bet you are even fresh out of the tubes. No way.

Your response: I can deal with a couple bots!

NPC: Listen, I admire your spirit. Which is why I will not give that job to you. You'd only end up dead.

Your response: But I really need some cash! I can work!

Your response: You're probably right.

NPC: Good. Bye.

NPC: You're persistent, I'll give you that. Listen, I mean it when I say, that in your current condition, these things would turn you into a dust pile. Tell you what. Get out there, get your breath back, maybe some better equipment, then you come back and we'll talk about it, okay?

Your response: Okay, fair enough. But how do I get better equipment?

NPC: Out there, in the outdoor area of the base, you will meet all sorts of people. Maybe start with the guy at the bottom of the ramp. Fancies himself a bit of a doctor. Maybe he needs help. Eh, just ask around. You'll manage.

NPC: Talk to that guy at the bottom of the ramp.

NPC: You again? I told you, you're not... whoa. Is that body armor? And you... gosh, you weren't kidding, when you said that you'd come back stronger! Loot at you! Better equipped, too! You look like you could take on anything!

Your response: Thanks for the vote of confidence.

NPC: Hey, I was only looking out for ya, honest! And I'm a man of my word, so that job offer stands, if you're still interested!

Your response: I can still use some cash, if that's included in the offer.

Your response: Not right now, sorry.

NPC: Offer remains open. It's not like I got anyone else to go after the damn things.

NPC: Sure is. Here's the thing: Headquarters developed new processors to control those security bots in the energy cores out there. It was supposed to work like this: There are some control bots equipped with this processor, and they can control the security bots around them. Quite an ingenious piece of engineering. But somebody messed up. The control bots were supposed to make the security system autonomous, but that wasn't supposed to mean, that they break of all contact and shoot at everything that moves. But that's precisely what happened.

Your response: So you want me to put those things on the scrap heap?

NPC: Only so far as that's strictly necessary. The bots aren't worth much, but HQ is gonna have my ass if I have to report to them, that their precious prototype processors ended up in the junk yard. Destroy security bots until this alerts one of the control bots. Once it appears, destroy it and bring me back its 'AMC5 Prototype Processor', so I can read out its flash memory. If I can't even tell HQ what's wrong, they're just gonna pin the blame for the whole fiasco on me.

Your response: One 'AMC5 Prototype Processor', coming right up!

NPC: Great! Hey, thanks for coming back. Appreciate it.

NPC: You got one of those prototype processors! I'm so relieved! Now I can finally start figuring out what's wrong with the damn things. Here, take your reward. You really earned it.

Your response: And here you go, with my compliments.

NPC: You need to destroy security bots until a control bot appears, then destroy that and loot the processor from its remains.

NPC: Have you obtained one of those prototype processors?

NPC: Thanks. Now if I might make a suggestion: You're more than strong enough to leave this place by now. Don't stick around. Staying too long around here ain't good for no one. The Gene Replicator is outside, in that little building on the hill, to the left of the ramp. It's been real. Take care.

entries.title: A loquacious intermediary
entries.description:
The Civil Administrator told you, that the Chief Technician has some trouble with security bots.

Ask the Chief Technician for work. He is up the steps, opposite the Civil Administrator.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Civil Administrator / Area MC5

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete I don't have time for this
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Chief Technician / Area MC5

REWARDS
• 50 credits
• 50 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: I'm not really supposed to talk to people if the Commander over there hasn't ordered it yet!

NPC: The Chief Technician over there could probably still use your help! Or do you still have more questions?

Your response: Okay, I'll bite. What should I know before I head home?

Your response: Right. I'll talk to him, now.

Your response: I may help him later.

NPC: There's nothing else I can do for you, really.

NPC: Ah, did the Base Commander send you over to me? Fresh out of the tubes, huh? Treatment go well? I bet you have lots and lots of questions, hm?

Your response: Is it that obvious? Yeah, I'm good. Just looking around for some stuff to do and some bucks to make before I head home.

NPC: Oh, I think I can help you out in those areas. There is some stuff you should know before you head home. Also, I can tell you where to make money around here before you do.

Your response: Okay, I'll bite. What should I know before I head home?

Your response: I'd really like to make some money around here. Any hints on that?

Your response: Thank you, but I'm pretty beat. I'd like to sleep on my own pillow now.

NPC: Earning money is fairly simple. At first, you should stick around where your faction is located, ask around for stuff to do, or just go to the CityCom terminals for missions. All factions offer various missions through those terminals. Also, you should pay a visit to your faction headquarter. They always have odd jobs that need doing.

Your response: What if they're too difficult?

NPC: At worst, you notice that a mission is above you, so you abort it and come back to it later. Or, you can join up with other runners in a team. That way, you can share any experiences and rewards, and stuff gets a lot easier. There is a 'Team' menu in your R.P.O.S, your Retinal Projected Operating System. Just keep in mind, that when you do kill missions, you need to do at least some of the damage for a kill to count towards your mission goal.

Your response: Okay, but what about around here? Can I earn some money here, before I go home?

NPC: Sure you can! You might want to talk to our Chief Technician over there. I heard him muttering about some bots malfunctioning or whatever. Wouldn't at all be surprised if he would offer someone like you a handsome reward for looking into that.

Your response: That's all? Just a job for the Chief Technician?

NPC: Nah, there's probably more, that's just the thing I could think of off the top of my head. You will probably encounter more people later on. They will have stuff for you to do as well, I am sure of it.

Your response: I'll just head over to the Chief Technician, then!

NPC: You should really make your first experiences and credits around here. But it is your choice, of course. Good luck!

NPC: You do that! Tell him I said hi!

NPC: Did you talk to the Chief Technician, yet?

NPC: Quite a lot, actually. For example, have they explained your Law Enforcer implant to you?

Your response: Yes, they have. I cannot be hurt by other runners while wearing it.

NPC: True, but there's more you should know. Yes, you cannot be hurt by other runners. But the same does not apply to all the mutants, animals and lowlifes out there. They can, and will hurt you. Kill you, even, if you don't fight back. Also, you cannot hurt other runners while wearing the Law Enforcer, but you still need to be careful. The limitation does not apply to yourself. Shoot a rocket into a corner with you standing on it, and Medicare will scrape your bits together with a dustpan, Law Enforcer or not.

Your response: I wasn't planning on being stupid enough to try that out, thank you very much.

NPC: Hey, just sayin'. Some people think they're invincible with their Law Enforcer in. Yeah, they're not.

Your response: Anything else about that blasted implant that I should know?

NPC: Oh yes. If you pull your Law Enforcer out, and you die somewhere in the outskirts, wastelands or dungeons, you're gonna drop one of the most valuable items you have with you.

Your response: Uh, you lost me. If I die, I'm dead, right? Everything is gone...

NPC: No, no no no. We have the Gene Replicator system. A clone of you will just pop out of a Gene Replicator of your choice, one which you have activated before. That clone will even retain your memories. So for all intents and purposes, it is you. You will also still have all your inventory. Minus one item, as I said.

Your response: Of course, the GenReps. How could I have forgotten them. But that item you spoke of, that is gone?

NPC: Not necessarily. You're gonna drop it inside a drop belt, and those need to be hacked. So as long as nobody passes by who knows how to hack, your item is safe inside your belt. And it is not an easy hack. The higher your Soul Light, the more skilled your potential hacker-thief needs to be to hack your belt.

Your response: You lost me again. What is a 'Soul Light'?

NPC: Oh yeah. Soul Light. Basically, you lose Soul Light if you're a murderer and you kill people who have done you no harm. Do good things, such as some missions for your faction, and you gain Soul Light. Also, if your Soul Light is too low, beware of the CopBots.

Your response: CopBots... I think I remember those. They are in Neocron, right?

NPC: Yes, in the urban areas of Neocron, at least. Their functions are pretty simple, they will usually leave you in peace, as long as you don't draw a gun at them. But if your Soul Light is too low, they will attack you on sight. And those things pack a punch so... yeah, don't get on their bad side.

Your response: Okay, got it. So how do I earn money and improve my skills?

Your response: I think I heard enough now, thanks. I really want to get home now.

entries.title: It's just my trashy hobby

Ezra agreed to teach you how to use Recycling to clone.

As payment for his services, he asked you to bring him 2 Entrails, which can be found on most of the critters around here.

Other conditions may also apply.

NPC: Can't you see I have my own problems right now?!

NPC: What're you looking at?

Your response: That glider of yours, to be perfectly honest. How did it end up there?

Your response: Lorcan sent me over. Anything I can help you with?

NPC: Talk to that monk gal now, she looked like she could use some help.

Your response: I'll go talk to her now.

Your response: Actually, I'm busy right now.

NPC: Why are you back here?

NPC: What're you looking at?

Your response: That glider of yours, to be perfectly honest. How did it end up there?

Your response: Lorcan sent me over. Anything I can help you with?

NPC: Well, I'm fresh outta ammo. Luckily, I have learned some recycling. Get me some junk so I can clone me some ammo. If you do, I'll even teach you how to do it.

Your response: Deal! But how do I get junk?

Your response: I can't do that right now.

NPC: Just kill anything that creeps, slithers, buzzes or oozes around here. They will provide you with all the junk you could wish for.

Your response: Uh... could you give me a pointer on how to fight?

Your response: Right. Will any junk do?

NPC: Geez, you must be fresh out of the tubes. You have some kind of weapon, right? Open your inventory (F2), and pull that weapon into the first slot of your quickbelt (on the right side). If it needs ammo, drag and drop some ammo on it, to load it. If you need to cast, don't forget to open your implant window (F3), and pull your gauntlet into the hand slot. Then close your R.P.O.S. (Esc), equip your weapon (1), point and shoot, cast, beat, whatever. It's not exactly rocket science. Unless you've got a rocket launcher. Then it is rocket science.

Your response: Funny. Okay, I guess I'll manage. Will any junk do?

NPC: No. Well, yes, but I want to get proper results. Collect all the junk you can find, but get me two Entrails. Then we'll talk, and I'll explain to you the fine art of Recycling.

NPC: Suit yourself.

NPC: See? Easy as pie. Remember though, that it is especially easy here, under my guidance. You will need to increase your own Recycling skill to the TechLevel of the item you want to clone. Most people who learn Recycling fare rather well with a skill of around 36. Just as an Eff-Why-Aye.

Your response: This is awesome! I'll never run out of ammo, med kits or boosters!

NPC: Thanks! Those Entrails will do nicely.

Your response: You said you'd teach me how to recycle, now...

NPC: I need two Entrails! You don't have them!

NPC: Get me two Entrails. Then we'll talk.

NPC: Remember: Open your processor window, put your recycling tool into the first slot, a 7.62 rifle round into the second, then fill the remaining slots up with as much junk as you have, and press start.

NPC: Remember: Open your processor window, put your recycling tool into the first slot, a flamer gas into the second, then fill the remaining slots up with as much junk as you have, and press start.

NPC: Remember: Open your processor window, put your recycling tool into the first slot, a first aid kit into the second, then fill the remaining slots up with as much junk as you have, and press start.

NPC: Remember: Open your processor window, put your recycling tool into the first slot, a psi booster into the second, then fill the remaining slots up with as much junk as you have, and press start.

NPC: Remember: Open your processor window, put your recycling tool into the first slot, a stamina booster into the second, then fill the remaining slots up with as much junk as you have, and press start.

NPC: Yes. You can actually do quite a lot of different things with Recycling. I'm gonna teach you the simplest one: Cloning. It's a very easy and cheap way to get more ammo, medkits or boosters. You do have a Recycling Tool, don't you?

Your response: Yes, I have it right here.

NPC: Good. What you do is: Open your processor (F7) and put the tool into its first slot. Then place an item you wish to clone into the second slot. Just one. The rest of the slots, you fill up with junk. Then you press Start, and Bob's your uncle. The junk is gone, and where you only had one item, you now have several.

Your response: Sounds simple enough. Will any kind of junk work?

NPC: Yes, but only proper junk, no item parts, implants, mods... ah, you'll find out soon enough which stuff the tool eats, and which it spits back into your inventory. Also, the bigger the better. Not just the TechLevel of the junk, but also its sheer size in your inventory. Why don't you go ahead and try it out? Clone fifteen 7.62 rifle rounds, then talk to me again.

Your response: I'll go talk to her now.

NPC: Go ahead, then. And thanks for your help.

NPC: Talk to that monk gal now, she looked like she could use some help.

NPC: I flew over that hill too fast and got stuck between these trees. Damn thing won't budge.

Your response: Maybe we can get it free together, the both of us?

NPC: Nah. The controls are shot anyway. Just waiting for it to recall.

Your response: What do you mean, 'recall'?

NPC: Yeah, recall. Don't own a ride? Remember this, then. If you lose a vehicle somewhere in the wastelands or it gets stuck, it will eventually recall to the vehicle depot. It can take some time, though.

Your response: So, why are you waiting here by its side, if it would automatically recall anyway?

NPC: There are always jackasses in this world, and they would absolutely love to blow this baby up. They'd find it funny.

Your response: How pathetic is that.

NPC: Yes, well, you don't have to worry about that, if you drive carefully. Don't be me. And always remember to dismiss your vehicle. Even when you're at the depot, and your vehicle is somewhere out there. Believe me, you'd much rather pay the fee to have it towed, than the price of a new one.

Your response: Good advice, thanks. Any way I can help you, to return the favor?

entries.title: It's just my trashy hobby
entries.description:
Ezra agreed to teach you how to use Recycling to clone.

As payment for his services, he asked you to bring him 2 Entrails, which can be found on most of the critters around here.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Ezra Reid

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Top Gun
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 2 × Entrails
• Talk to Ezra Reid
    Note: Now that you have brought Ezra his entrails, he explained to you how Cloning works. He has asked you to clone %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(recycle) %OBJECTIVE_ITEM(recycle).
• Use a tradeskill on 9mm Clip
• Talk to Ezra Reid

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

entries.title: It's just my trashy hobby
entries.description:
Ezra agreed to teach you how to use Recycling to clone.

As payment for his services, he asked you to bring him 2 Entrails, which can be found on most of the critters around here.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Ezra Reid

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Top Gun
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 2 × Entrails
• Talk to Ezra Reid
    Note: Now that you have brought Ezra his entrails, he explained to you how Cloning works. He has asked you to clone %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(recycle) %OBJECTIVE_ITEM(recycle).
• Use a tradeskill on Flamer Gas
• Talk to Ezra Reid

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

NPC: Yeah, recall. Don't own a ride? Remember this, then. If you lose a vehicle somewhere in the wastelands or it gets stuck, it will eventually recall to the vehicle depot. It can take some time, though.

Your response: So, why are you waiting here by its side, if it would automatically recall anyway?

NPC: There are always jackasses in this world, and they would absolutely love to blow this baby up. They'd find it funny.

Your response: How pathetic is that.

NPC: Yes, well, you don't have to worry about that, if you drive carefully. Don't be me. And always remember to dismiss your vehicle. Even when you're at the depot, and your vehicle is somewhere out there. Believe me, you'd much rather pay the fee to have it towed, than the price of a new one.

Your response: Good advice, thanks. Any way I can help you, to return the favor?

entries.title: It's just my trashy hobby
entries.description:
Ezra agreed to teach you how to use Recycling to clone.

As payment for his services, he asked you to bring him 2 Entrails, which can be found on most of the critters around here.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Ezra Reid

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Top Gun
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 2 × Entrails
• Talk to Ezra Reid
    Note: Now that you have brought Ezra his entrails, he explained to you how Cloning works. He has asked you to clone %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(recycle) %OBJECTIVE_ITEM(recycle).
• Use a tradeskill on First Aid
• Talk to Ezra Reid

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

Your response: Lorcan sent me over. Anything I can help you with?

NPC: Well, I'm fresh outta ammo. Luckily, I have learned some recycling. Get me some junk so I can clone me some ammo. If you do, I'll even teach you how to do it.

Your response: Deal! But how do I get junk?

Your response: I can't do that right now.

NPC: Just kill anything that creeps, slithers, buzzes or oozes around here. They will provide you with all the junk you could wish for.

Your response: Uh... could you give me a pointer on how to fight?

Your response: Right. Will any junk do?

NPC: No. Well, yes, but I want to get proper results. Collect all the junk you can find, but get me two Entrails. Then we'll talk, and I'll explain to you the fine art of Recycling.

NPC: Suit yourself.

Your response: This is awesome! I'll never run out of ammo, med kits or boosters!

entries.title: It's just my trashy hobby
entries.description:
Ezra agreed to teach you how to use Recycling to clone.

As payment for his services, he asked you to bring him 2 Entrails, which can be found on most of the critters around here.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Ezra Reid

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Top Gun
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 2 × Entrails
• Talk to Ezra Reid
    Note: Now that you have brought Ezra his entrails, he explained to you how Cloning works. He has asked you to clone %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(recycle) %OBJECTIVE_ITEM(recycle).
• Use a tradeskill on PSI Booster 1
• Talk to Ezra Reid

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

entries.title: It's just my trashy hobby
entries.description:
Ezra agreed to teach you how to use Recycling to clone.

As payment for his services, he asked you to bring him 2 Entrails, which can be found on most of the critters around here.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Ezra Reid

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Top Gun
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES

• Use a tradeskill on Stamina Booster
• Talk to Ezra Reid

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

Your response: Yes, I have it right here.

NPC: Good. What you do is: Open your processor (F7) and put the tool into its first slot. Then place an item you wish to clone into the second slot. Just one. Your response: Sounds simple enough. Will any kind of junk work?

NPC: Go ahead, then. And thanks for your help.

NPC: Talk to that monk gal now, she looked like she could use some help.

NPC: I flew over that hill too fast and got stuck between these trees. Damn thing won't budge.

Your response: Maybe we can get it free together, the both of us?

NPC: Nah. The controls are shot anyway. Just waiting for it to recall.

Your response: What do you mean, 'recall'?

NPC: Yeah, recall. Don't own a ride? Remember this, then. If you lose a vehicle somewhere in the wastelands or it gets stuck, it will eventually recall to the vehicle depot. It can take some time, though.

Your response: So, why are you waiting here by its side, if it would automatically recall anyway?

NPC: There are always jackasses in this world, and they would absolutely love to blow this baby up. They'd find it funny.

Your response: How pathetic is that.

NPC: Yes, well, you don't have to worry about that, if you drive carefully. Don't be me. And always remember to dismiss your vehicle. Even when you're at the depot, and your vehicle is somewhere out there. Believe me, you'd much rather pay the fee to have it towed, than the price of a new one.

Your response: Good advice, thanks. Any way I can help you, to return the favor?

entries.description: Ezra suggested that you go talk to Tasha, a monk lady in the valley behind the Gene Replicator Building.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Ezra Reid

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
Conditions are present in the source; see Original source for details.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Tasha

REWARDS
• 100 credits
• 100 experience

NPC: Well, I'm fresh outta ammo. Luckily, I have learned some recycling. Get me some junk so I can clone me some ammo. If you do, I'll even teach you how to do it.

Your response: Deal! But how do I get junk?

Your response: I can't do that right now.

NPC: Just kill anything that creeps, slithers, buzzes or oozes around here. They will provide you with all the junk you could wish for.

Your response: Uh... could you give me a pointer on how to fight?

Your response: Right. Will any junk do?

NPC: Geez, you must be fresh out of the tubes. You have some kind of weapon, right? Open your inventory (F2), and pull that weapon into the first slot of your quickbelt (on the right side). If it needs ammo, drag and drop some ammo on it, to load it. If you need to cast, don't forget to open your implant window (F3), and pull your gauntlet into the hand slot. Then close your R.P.O.S. (Esc), equip your weapon (1), point and shoot, cast, beat, whatever. It's not exactly rocket science. Unless you've got a rocket launcher. Then it is rocket science.

Your response: Funny. Okay, I guess I'll manage. Will any junk do?

NPC: No. Well, yes, but I want to get proper results. Collect all the junk you can find, but get me two Entrails. Then we'll talk, and I'll explain to you the fine art of Recycling.

NPC: Suit yourself.

entries.title: My new weapon, weapon of choice
entries.description: Geordi is going to help you craft a better weapon for yourself. To do this, he asked you to buy the kind of weapon you want to have from a trader.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Geordi

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete He can actually see just fine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 1 × Mendicant Rifle
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Having bought a template, Geordi has now asked you to research it, by placing first the research tool, then the item into your processor, and press start.
• Use a tradeskill on Mendicant Rifle
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Now that you have created a blueprint, Geordi wants you to build your new weapon by placing first the construction tool, then the blueprint into your processor. Check the blueprint if you don't know which parts you need.
• Use a tradeskill on Mendicant Rifle
• Talk to Geordi

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: We don't know you! Go away!

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: You still want to get better armor, right?

Your response: Right.

Your response: I may do that later.

NPC: You helped Tasha, so we helped you. We're even.

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: Tasha? She's a very good friend. She sent you? Welcome! Any friend of Tasha's is a good friend of ours. Now: What is it you need?

Your response: Well, a better weapon would be good. What I have is rather crummy.

NPC: I see. It is, isn't it? Well, sure thing! I'll show you how to build a nice weapon.

Your response: Hang on, I may be an engineer, but I still don't know how to do that...

Your response: Woah, wait, what? I don't know how to do that!

NPC: Don't you worry. With my equipment, and my guidance, you'll be able to do it easily.

Your response: But why go for the trouble at all? Can't I simply buy a better weapon somewhere?

Your response: I'll get back to you on that.

Your response: Okay then. Let's do this.

NPC: Yes. Sure.

NPC: Yes, let's. Now what kind of weapon do you need?

Your response: I want a rifle, please.

Your response: A pistol would be good.

Your response: I need a cannon.

Your response: Can I get a drone, instead?

Your response: None, but I'd like a psi module.

Your response: Just something so I can melee.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant Rifle. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant SMG. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Street Model Grenade Launcher. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Crahn Energy Ball. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a AMC5 Baseball Bat. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: There you go! You did it!

Your response: This is so cool! Way better than that bought one!

NPC: Buy the construction parts from the nomad traders. The blueprint will tell you which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then, put the tool into the first slot of your processor (F7), the blueprint into the second, and press start.

NPC: There you go. See? Nothing to it, really. Now the next step is to build the actual item.

Your response: What do I need for that?

NPC: Remember: The tool always goes into the first slot. And the weapon goes into the second. Nothing in between them. Then you press start. Once the process completes, you have your blueprint.

NPC: Alright. Now you got your template. As you can see, it is rather shabby.

Your response: You weren't kidding. That is some shoddy workmanship right there.

NPC: Go to that nomad trader camp and buy the weapon.

NPC: Right? Even you as a beginner can do better. Now, here's my research tool and a data cube. Put the research tool in the first slot of your processor (F7), and the weapon into the second. Then start the process, it will automatically pull the data cube in there as well. Talk to me again once you have successfully created the blueprint.

NPC: Use my construction tool. Again, it goes into the first slot of your processor (F7), and the blueprint in the second. But you'll also need construction parts. Inspect the blueprint to find out which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then head over to the nomad traders again to buy those parts. Like the cube, the tool will pull those into the processor if you press start. Or, it will tell you, that parts are missing. Then check your blueprint again.

NPC: (Geordi looks at you expectantly, clearly waiting for you to hand him his tool back)

NPC: It is, isn't it? Remember this for all your future weapon needs. Yes, you can get them in a shop, but you'll be much better off with proper craftsmanship.

Your response: I do not seem to be able to use that weapon, though...

Your response: I love it. Thank you! Can you do something about my armor as well?

Your response: I'll come back once I have tried this bad boy out!

NPC: If you can't use your weapon yet, check its requirements (right click on the weapon, show info). If there are any you do not match yet, check your skill window (F5) to see if you have enough skill points to remedy the problem, then increase your skill in whatever is required with that little plus sign. If not, gain more experience.

Your response: I see. Anyway, can you do something about my armor as well?

NPC: For that, I'm gonna direct you to my good colleague Wesley, over here!

NPC: Talk to Wesley, now!

NPC: Well... yes, you can, but- listen, most traders really have little sense for quality. As long as it shoots bullets, or lightning, or flies through the air or whatever, they're gonna sell it. Even if it couldn't hit the broad side of a barn, not matter how well you aim, and it explodes on third usage.

Your response: Right. That sucks, of course.

NPC: Right. The solution is to get a researcher and an engineer to build you something of a much higher quality. Once you've had one of these babies in your hand, you'll never settle for store bought again.

Your response: So why do I need an engineer and a researcher?

NPC: In a sentence: Engineers need blueprints to construct from, and researchers create blueprints. Strictly speaking, you may not need the researcher if you obtained the blueprint in some other way. Well... strictly strictly speaking, you may not need an engineer either, if you find some Runner who sells you the finished weapon in proper quality. Others might sell readymade blueprints. But let's assume that you have neither.

Your response: That's probably for the best.

NPC: Yup. So you buy the weapon you want at a store. Then you find a researcher, and you pay them to create a blueprint of that weapon for you.

Your response: What if they just take off with my weapon and my money?

NPC: Then you've lost both, I'd say. Just don't take your business to the first drunkard you see. Most trading runners are decent people- at least while they're doing commerce. Someone who screws over their clients will soon have no clients left. Word gets around.

Your response: I see. Okay, so I got my blueprint, one way or another. And then I take it to an engineer?

NPC: Only if you want to make them rather angry. Engineers have little patience for people who come badly prepared. You don't just need the blueprint, you also need the construction parts. Check out your blueprint, to find out which ones you need (right click on blueprint, show info). Most of them, you can get in a store. For others, which you're gonna need for the higher end weapons, you're gonna have to ask around.

Your response: Alright, so I have my blueprint, I buy all the parts, and then I take them to an engineer, and they build me my weapon?

NPC: After you've paid them, of course. But yes. And you'll want to look around for the best engineer you can find. The higher the skill of the engineer, the bigger your chance to get slots.

Your response: You lost me. What are 'slots'?

NPC: Slots are what turns a good weapon into a great one. See, an engineers' skill will only take them so far. For that extra bit of firing speed, accuracy, damage and so on, you'll need mods. And you fit those mods into the slots of your weapon. There's also the modding option of retrofitting your weapon with different kinds of ammo, so you deal different kinds of damage. So the more slots your weapon has, the better it is going to be. The maximum you can have is five slots, but I tell ya: Five slotters are worth their weight in gold. They are extremely rare.

Your response: Can I exchange my mods, too, once they're in?

NPC: Nope. A mod is for life. Well, the life of that weapon. There's no taking it out again. So choose well. Don't put a flashlight in there.

Your response: Tasha told me about rare parts, and the weapons and tools you build from them. Does all of this apply to them, as well?

NPC: Not all of it, no. Rares can be built to a much higher quality than regular weapons, so you can spend your slots on more exciting stuff that just increasing its accuracy or damage. Also, an engineer just needs the parts set for that specific rare. No need for blueprints in this case. That you still need a researcher to identify the parts, Tasha probably already told you.

Your response: She did. Alright, thanks for all that information. Let's build a weapon, now.

entries.title: My new weapon, weapon of choice
entries.description: Geordi is going to help you craft a better weapon for yourself. To do this, he asked you to buy the kind of weapon you want to have from a trader.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Geordi

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete He can actually see just fine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 1 × Mendicant SMG
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Having bought a template, Geordi has now asked you to research it, by placing first the research tool, then the item into your processor, and press start.
• Use a tradeskill on Mendicant SMG
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Now that you have created a blueprint, Geordi wants you to build your new weapon by placing first the construction tool, then the blueprint into your processor. Check the blueprint if you don't know which parts you need.
• Use a tradeskill on Mendicant SMG
• Talk to Geordi

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

NPC: We don't know you! Go away!

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: You still want to get better armor, right?

Your response: Right.

Your response: I may do that later.

NPC: You helped Tasha, so we helped you. We're even.

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: Tasha? She's a very good friend. She sent you? Welcome! Any friend of Tasha's is a good friend of ours. Now: What is it you need?

Your response: Well, a better weapon would be good. What I have is rather crummy.

NPC: I see. It is, isn't it? Well, sure thing! I'll show you how to build a nice weapon.

Your response: Hang on, I may be an engineer, but I still don't know how to do that...

Your response: Woah, wait, what? I don't know how to do that!

NPC: Don't you worry. With my equipment, and my guidance, you'll be able to do it easily.

Your response: But why go for the trouble at all? Can't I simply buy a better weapon somewhere?

Your response: I'll get back to you on that.

Your response: Okay then. Let's do this.

NPC: Yes. Sure.

NPC: Yes, let's. Now what kind of weapon do you need?

Your response: I want a rifle, please.

Your response: A pistol would be good.

Your response: I need a cannon.

Your response: Can I get a drone, instead?

Your response: None, but I'd like a psi module.

Your response: Just something so I can melee.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant Rifle. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant SMG. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Street Model Grenade Launcher. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Crahn Energy Ball. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a AMC5 Baseball Bat. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: There you go! You did it!

Your response: This is so cool! Way better than that bought one!

NPC: Buy the construction parts from the nomad traders. The blueprint will tell you which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then, put the tool into the first slot of your processor (F7), the blueprint into the second, and press start.

NPC: There you go. See? Nothing to it, really. Now the next step is to build the actual item.

Your response: What do I need for that?

NPC: Remember: The tool always goes into the first slot. And the weapon goes into the second. Nothing in between them. Then you press start. Once the process completes, you have your blueprint.

NPC: Alright. Now you got your template. As you can see, it is rather shabby.

Your response: You weren't kidding. That is some shoddy workmanship right there.

NPC: Go to that nomad trader camp and buy the weapon.

NPC: Right? Even you as a beginner can do better. Now, here's my research tool and a data cube. Put the research tool in the first slot of your processor (F7), and the weapon into the second. Then start the process, it will automatically pull the data cube in there as well. Talk to me again once you have successfully created the blueprint.

NPC: Use my construction tool. Again, it goes into the first slot of your processor (F7), and the blueprint in the second. But you'll also need construction parts. Inspect the blueprint to find out which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then head over to the nomad traders again to buy those parts. Like the cube, the tool will pull those into the processor if you press start. Or, it will tell you, that parts are missing. Then check your blueprint again.

NPC: (Geordi looks at you expectantly, clearly waiting for you to hand him his tool back)

NPC: It is, isn't it? Remember this for all your future weapon needs. Yes, you can get them in a shop, but you'll be much better off with proper craftsmanship.

Your response: I do not seem to be able to use that weapon, though...

Your response: I love it. Thank you! Can you do something about my armor as well?

Your response: I'll come back once I have tried this bad boy out!

NPC: If you can't use your weapon yet, check its requirements (right click on the weapon, show info). If there are any you do not match yet, check your skill window (F5) to see if you have enough skill points to remedy the problem, then increase your skill in whatever is required with that little plus sign. If not, gain more experience.

NPC: For that, I'm gonna direct you to my good colleague Wesley, over here!

NPC: Talk to Wesley, now!

NPC: Well... yes, you can, but- listen, most traders really have little sense for quality. As long as it shoots bullets, or lightning, or flies through the air or whatever, they're gonna sell it. NPC: Right. The solution is to get a researcher and an engineer to build you something of a much higher quality. Once you've had one of these babies in your hand, you'll never settle for store bought again.

Your response: So why do I need an engineer and a researcher?

NPC: In a sentence: Engineers need blueprints to construct from, and researchers create blueprints. Strictly speaking, you may not need the researcher if you obtained the blueprint in some other way. Well... strictly strictly speaking, you may not need an engineer either, if you find some Runner who sells you the finished weapon in proper quality. Others might sell readymade blueprints. But let's assume that you have neither.

NPC: Yup. So you buy the weapon you want at a store. Then you find a researcher, and you pay them to create a blueprint of that weapon for you.

NPC: Then you've lost both, I'd say. Just don't take your business to the first drunkard you see. Most trading runners are decent people- at least while they're doing commerce. Someone who screws over their clients will soon have no clients left. Word gets around.

For others, which you're gonna need for the higher end weapons, you're gonna have to ask around.

entries.title: My new weapon, weapon of choice
entries.description: Geordi is going to help you craft a better weapon for yourself. To do this, he asked you to buy the kind of weapon you want to have from a trader.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Geordi

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete He can actually see just fine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 1 × Street Model Grenade Launcher
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Having bought a template, Geordi has now asked you to research it, by placing first the research tool, then the item into your processor, and press start.
• Use a tradeskill on Street Model Grenade Launcher
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Now that you have created a blueprint, Geordi wants you to build your new weapon by placing first the construction tool, then the blueprint into your processor. Check the blueprint if you don't know which parts you need.
• Use a tradeskill on Street Model Grenade Launcher
• Talk to Geordi

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

entries.title: My new weapon, weapon of choice
entries.description: Geordi is going to help you craft a better weapon for yourself. To do this, he asked you to buy the kind of weapon you want to have from a trader.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Geordi

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete He can actually see just fine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 1 × A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Having bought a template, Geordi has now asked you to research it, by placing first the research tool, then the item into your processor, and press start.
• Use a tradeskill on A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Now that you have created a blueprint, Geordi wants you to build your new weapon by placing first the construction tool, then the blueprint into your processor. Check the blueprint if you don't know which parts you need.
• Use a tradeskill on A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2
• Talk to Geordi

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

NPC: We don't know you! Go away!

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: You still want to get better armor, right?

Your response: Right.

Your response: I may do that later.

NPC: You helped Tasha, so we helped you. We're even.

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: Tasha? She's a very good friend. She sent you? Welcome! Any friend of Tasha's is a good friend of ours. Now: What is it you need?

Your response: Well, a better weapon would be good. What I have is rather crummy.

NPC: I see. It is, isn't it? Well, sure thing! I'll show you how to build a nice weapon.

Your response: Hang on, I may be an engineer, but I still don't know how to do that...

Your response: Woah, wait, what? I don't know how to do that!

NPC: Don't you worry. With my equipment, and my guidance, you'll be able to do it easily.

Your response: But why go for the trouble at all? Can't I simply buy a better weapon somewhere?

Your response: I'll get back to you on that.

Your response: Okay then. Let's do this.

NPC: Yes. Sure.

NPC: Yes, let's. Now what kind of weapon do you need?

Your response: I want a rifle, please.

Your response: A pistol would be good.

Your response: I need a cannon.

Your response: Can I get a drone, instead?

Your response: None, but I'd like a psi module.

Your response: Just something so I can melee.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant Rifle. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant SMG. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Street Model Grenade Launcher. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Crahn Energy Ball. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a AMC5 Baseball Bat. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: There you go! You did it!

Your response: This is so cool! Way better than that bought one!

NPC: Buy the construction parts from the nomad traders. The blueprint will tell you which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then, put the tool into the first slot of your processor (F7), the blueprint into the second, and press start.

NPC: There you go. See? Nothing to it, really. Now the next step is to build the actual item.

Your response: What do I need for that?

NPC: Remember: The tool always goes into the first slot. And the weapon goes into the second. Nothing in between them. Then you press start. Once the process completes, you have your blueprint.

NPC: Alright. Now you got your template. As you can see, it is rather shabby.

Your response: You weren't kidding. That is some shoddy workmanship right there.

NPC: Go to that nomad trader camp and buy the weapon.

NPC: Right? Even you as a beginner can do better. Now, here's my research tool and a data cube. Put the research tool in the first slot of your processor (F7), and the weapon into the second. Then start the process, it will automatically pull the data cube in there as well. Talk to me again once you have successfully created the blueprint.

NPC: Use my construction tool. Again, it goes into the first slot of your processor (F7), and the blueprint in the second. But you'll also need construction parts. Inspect the blueprint to find out which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then head over to the nomad traders again to buy those parts. Like the cube, the tool will pull those into the processor if you press start. Or, it will tell you, that parts are missing. Then check your blueprint again.

NPC: (Geordi looks at you expectantly, clearly waiting for you to hand him his tool back)

NPC: It is, isn't it? Remember this for all your future weapon needs. Yes, you can get them in a shop, but you'll be much better off with proper craftsmanship.

Your response: I do not seem to be able to use that weapon, though...

Your response: I love it. Thank you! Can you do something about my armor as well?

Your response: I'll come back once I have tried this bad boy out!

NPC: If you can't use your weapon yet, check its requirements (right click on the weapon, show info). If there are any you do not match yet, check your skill window (F5) to see if you have enough skill points to remedy the problem, then increase your skill in whatever is required with that little plus sign. If not, gain more experience.

Your response: I see. Anyway, can you do something about my armor as well?

NPC: For that, I'm gonna direct you to my good colleague Wesley, over here!

NPC: Talk to Wesley, now!

NPC: Well... yes, you can, but- listen, most traders really have little sense for quality. As long as it shoots bullets, or lightning, or flies through the air or whatever, they're gonna sell it. Your response: Right. That sucks, of course.

NPC: Right. The solution is to get a researcher and an engineer to build you something of a much higher quality. Once you've had one of these babies in your hand, you'll never settle for store bought again.

Your response: So why do I need an engineer and a researcher?

NPC: In a sentence: Engineers need blueprints to construct from, and researchers create blueprints. Strictly speaking, you may not need the researcher if you obtained the blueprint in some other way. Well... strictly strictly speaking, you may not need an engineer either, if you find some Runner who sells you the finished weapon in proper quality. Others might sell readymade blueprints. But let's assume that you have neither.

Your response: That's probably for the best.

NPC: Yup. So you buy the weapon you want at a store. Then you find a researcher, and you pay them to create a blueprint of that weapon for you.

Your response: What if they just take off with my weapon and my money?

NPC: Then you've lost both, I'd say. Just don't take your business to the first drunkard you see. Most trading runners are decent people- at least while they're doing commerce. Someone who screws over their clients will soon have no clients left. Word gets around.

Your response: I see. Okay, so I got my blueprint, one way or another. And then I take it to an engineer?

NPC: Only if you want to make them rather angry. Engineers have little patience for people who come badly prepared. You don't just need the blueprint, you also need the construction parts. Check out your blueprint, to find out which ones you need (right click on blueprint, show info). Most of them, you can get in a store. For others, which you're gonna need for the higher end weapons, you're gonna have to ask around.

Your response: Alright, so I have my blueprint, I buy all the parts, and then I take them to an engineer, and they build me my weapon?

Also, an engineer just needs the parts set for that specific rare. No need for blueprints in this case. That you still need a researcher to identify the parts, Tasha probably already told you.

entries.title: My new weapon, weapon of choice
entries.description: Geordi is going to help you craft a better weapon for yourself. To do this, he asked you to buy the kind of weapon you want to have from a trader.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Geordi

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete He can actually see just fine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 1 × Crahn Energy Ball
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Having bought a template, Geordi has now asked you to research it, by placing first the research tool, then the item into your processor, and press start.
• Use a tradeskill on Crahn Energy Ball
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Now that you have created a blueprint, Geordi wants you to build your new weapon by placing first the construction tool, then the blueprint into your processor. Check the blueprint if you don't know which parts you need.
• Use a tradeskill on Crahn Energy Ball
• Talk to Geordi

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

entries.title: My new weapon, weapon of choice
entries.description: Geordi is going to help you craft a better weapon for yourself. To do this, he asked you to buy the kind of weapon you want to have from a trader.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Geordi

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete He can actually see just fine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 1 × AMC5 Baseball Bat
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Having bought a template, Geordi has now asked you to research it, by placing first the research tool, then the item into your processor, and press start.
• Use a tradeskill on AMC5 Baseball Bat
• Talk to Geordi
    Note: Now that you have created a blueprint, Geordi wants you to build your new weapon by placing first the construction tool, then the blueprint into your processor. Check the blueprint if you don't know which parts you need.
• Use a tradeskill on AMC5 Baseball Bat
• Talk to Geordi

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 800 experience

NPC: We don't know you! Go away!

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: You still want to get better armor, right?

Your response: Right.

Your response: I may do that later.

NPC: You helped Tasha, so we helped you. We're even.

NPC: We don't know you!

Your response: Tasha sent me over to you. Said something about you helping me to get better equipment?

NPC: Tasha? She's a very good friend. She sent you? Welcome! Any friend of Tasha's is a good friend of ours. Now: What is it you need?

Your response: Well, a better weapon would be good. What I have is rather crummy.

NPC: I see. It is, isn't it? Well, sure thing! I'll show you how to build a nice weapon.

Your response: Hang on, I may be an engineer, but I still don't know how to do that...

Your response: Woah, wait, what? I don't know how to do that!

NPC: Don't you worry. With my equipment, and my guidance, you'll be able to do it easily.

Your response: But why go for the trouble at all? Can't I simply buy a better weapon somewhere?

Your response: I'll get back to you on that.

Your response: Okay then. Let's do this.

NPC: Yes. Sure.

NPC: Yes, let's. Now what kind of weapon do you need?

Your response: I want a rifle, please.

Your response: A pistol would be good.

Your response: I need a cannon.

Your response: Can I get a drone, instead?

Your response: None, but I'd like a psi module.

Your response: Just something so I can melee.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant Rifle. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Mendicant SMG. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Street Model Grenade Launcher. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a A&W Marksman Assault Drone RF-2. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a Crahn Energy Ball. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: Alright. Then head over to the nomad trader camp to your left. They should stock a AMC5 Baseball Bat. Buy one of those, and bring it here.

NPC: There you go! You did it!

Your response: This is so cool! Way better than that bought one!

NPC: Buy the construction parts from the nomad traders. The blueprint will tell you which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then, put the tool into the first slot of your processor (F7), the blueprint into the second, and press start.

NPC: There you go. See? Nothing to it, really. Now the next step is to build the actual item.

Your response: What do I need for that?

NPC: Remember: The tool always goes into the first slot. And the weapon goes into the second. Nothing in between them. Then you press start. Once the process completes, you have your blueprint.

NPC: Alright. Now you got your template. As you can see, it is rather shabby.

Your response: You weren't kidding. That is some shoddy workmanship right there.

NPC: Go to that nomad trader camp and buy the weapon.

NPC: Right? Even you as a beginner can do better. Now, here's my research tool and a data cube. Put the research tool in the first slot of your processor (F7), and the weapon into the second. Then start the process, it will automatically pull the data cube in there as well. Talk to me again once you have successfully created the blueprint.

NPC: Use my construction tool. Again, it goes into the first slot of your processor (F7), and the blueprint in the second. But you'll also need construction parts. Inspect the blueprint to find out which ones (right click on the blueprint, show info). Then head over to the nomad traders again to buy those parts. Like the cube, the tool will pull those into the processor if you press start. Or, it will tell you, that parts are missing. Then check your blueprint again.

NPC: (Geordi looks at you expectantly, clearly waiting for you to hand him his tool back)

NPC: It is, isn't it? Remember this for all your future weapon needs. Yes, you can get them in a shop, but you'll be much better off with proper craftsmanship.

Your response: I do not seem to be able to use that weapon, though...

Your response: I love it. Thank you! Can you do something about my armor as well?

Your response: I'll come back once I have tried this bad boy out!

NPC: If you can't use your weapon yet, check its requirements (right click on the weapon, show info). If there are any you do not match yet, check your skill window (F5) to see if you have enough skill points to remedy the problem, then increase your skill in whatever is required with that little plus sign. If not, gain more experience.

Your response: I see. Anyway, can you do something about my armor as well?

NPC: For that, I'm gonna direct you to my good colleague Wesley, over here!

NPC: Talk to Wesley, now!

NPC: Well... yes, you can, but- listen, most traders really have little sense for quality. As long as it shoots bullets, or lightning, or flies through the air or whatever, they're gonna sell it. Even if it couldn't hit the broad side of a barn, not matter how well you aim, and it explodes on third usage.

Your response: Right. That sucks, of course.

NPC: Right. The solution is to get a researcher and an engineer to build you something of a much higher quality. Once you've had one of these babies in your hand, you'll never settle for store bought again.

Your response: So why do I need an engineer and a researcher?

NPC: In a sentence: Engineers need blueprints to construct from, and researchers create blueprints. Strictly speaking, you may not need the researcher if you obtained the blueprint in some other way. Well... strictly strictly speaking, you may not need an engineer either, if you find some Runner who sells you the finished weapon in proper quality. Others might sell readymade blueprints. But let's assume that you have neither.

Your response: That's probably for the best.

NPC: Yup. So you buy the weapon you want at a store. Then you find a researcher, and you pay them to create a blueprint of that weapon for you.

Your response: What if they just take off with my weapon and my money?

NPC: Then you've lost both, I'd say. Just don't take your business to the first drunkard you see. Most trading runners are decent people- at least while they're doing commerce. Someone who screws over their clients will soon have no clients left. Word gets around.

Your response: I see. Okay, so I got my blueprint, one way or another. And then I take it to an engineer?

NPC: Only if you want to make them rather angry. Engineers have little patience for people who come badly prepared. You don't just need the blueprint, you also need the construction parts. Check out your blueprint, to find out which ones you need (right click on blueprint, show info). Most of them, you can get in a store. For others, which you're gonna need for the higher end weapons, you're gonna have to ask around.

Your response: Alright, so I have my blueprint, I buy all the parts, and then I take them to an engineer, and they build me my weapon?

NPC: After you've paid them, of course. But yes. And you'll want to look around for the best engineer you can find. The higher the skill of the engineer, the bigger your chance to get slots.

Your response: You lost me. What are 'slots'?

NPC: Slots are what turns a good weapon into a great one. See, an engineers' skill will only take them so far. For that extra bit of firing speed, accuracy, damage and so on, you'll need mods. And you fit those mods into the slots of your weapon. There's also the modding option of retrofitting your weapon with different kinds of ammo, so you deal different kinds of damage. NPC: Nope. A mod is for life. Well, the life of that weapon. There's no taking it out again. So choose well. Don't put a flashlight in there.

NPC: Not all of it, no. Rares can be built to a much higher quality than regular weapons, so you can spend your slots on more exciting stuff that just increasing its accuracy or damage. Also, an engineer just needs the parts set for that specific rare. No need for blueprints in this case. That you still need a researcher to identify the parts, Tasha probably already told you.

Your response: She did. Alright, thanks for all that information. Let's build a weapon, now.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Lorcan

REPEAT
One time

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Insufficient level
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 5 × Solantium
• Talk to Lorcan

REWARDS
• 900 credits
• 700 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Uh, no offense, but I don't think you should already be out here...

NPC: Fresh out of the tubes? Any lingering problems?

Your response: Just a headache from that damn Law Enforcer. Who are you?

Your response: Don't mind me, I'm fine. Do you offer any jobs?

NPC: Maybe you should talk to that chap with his glider now.

Your response: Yes, sure, I'll talk to him.

Your response: Actually, I'm busy right now.

NPC: I have nothing else for you.

NPC: Haven't seen you around here before. Fresh out of the tubes? Any lingering problems?

Your response: Just a headache from that damn Law Enforcer. Who are you?

Your response: Don't mind me, I'm fine. Do you offer any jobs?

NPC: Well, when I treat those poor bastards in need of help around here, I often finish the implant jobs they couldn't be bothered to do properly up there. To do that, I need Solantium, and I barely have any left in my box. Luckily, they have plenty of Solantium around here.

Your response: I'll get you some Solantium, then.

Your response: I would, but I'm already carrying quite a lot of stuff around.

Your response: I can't help you right now.

NPC: That's no problem. A GoGuardian is right behind you, to the left of the ramp.

Your response: A 'GoGuardian'? What's that?

NPC: Anything you put into any GoGu, you can access from any GoGu. Put stuff in while you're here, then later, when you're at home, take it out again.

Your response: Right. GoGuardian. GoGu. Got it. I'll get you some Solantium, then.

NPC: That's brilliant. Get me five Solantium, and this week's victims will all get proper treatment. You can find Solantium tubules in those chemical boxes all around here. They look just like the box I am standing on.

NPC: Maybe later?

NPC: You got the Solantium! Awesome, thank you very much! Now I can treat my next patients without any shortages.

Your response: Do you have any other jobs that need doing?

NPC: You don't have five Solantium with you...

NPC: I really need those five Solantium, please.

NPC: I don't, really. But why don't you pay a visit to that funny fella behind me, who seems to have parked his glider into a tree? He sure looks like he could use some help.

Your response: Yes, sure, I'll talk to him.

Your response: Actually, I'm busy right now.

NPC: Thanks again for your help!

NPC: Talk to that bloke behind me.

NPC: Are you sure you don't want to take a seat and let me take a look at that implant job they did on you? No? Oh well. My name's Lorcan. I do my best to take care of those coming down that ramp behind you that couldn't stomach the treatment in there as well as you apparently could.

Your response: So you're a doctor?

NPC: Who knows what I was, before I ended up here? I don't. But I seem to have retained some knowledge in that area, plus a really intense helper syndrome. Which is why I decided to stay, set up shop here.

Your response: That's... noble of you.

NPC: Oh, stuff it. The way I see it, this place is relatively safe. Which is more that can be said about the world out there, apparently.

Your response: What do you mean? Because people end up here?

NPC: No, no no. I've heard... let's call them rumors. Well, memories, actually. Some people remember a little more, when they stagger or even crawl down that ramp. Out there, describing it as a dog eat dog world doesn't even begin to do it justice.

Your response: Tell me!

NPC: Well, essentially, it's one big fight for resources. The corporations of Neocron with their little schemes and plots against each other, the criminal organisations, Crahn Sect nutjobs, Twilight Guardian rebels without a clue, Fallen Angel technocrats, CityMerc mercenaries... In the end, they all pit their runners against each other in the fight for outposts in the wastelands.

Your response: What kind of outposts are those?

NPC: There's all kinds of outposts. Factories, Laboratories, Uplinks... Most of them give your clan a hefty bonus on your trade. If you craft weapons, for example- Well, they are gonna be of a much higher quality if you build them in a factory.

Your response: My clan? What's a clan?

NPC: Department, Chapter, Team, Cell, call it whatever you like. It's a part of the faction you belong to. You can join one, or even found one yourself.

Your response: Ah, I see. What about those other outpost types?

NPC: Laboratories make research much easier. If you find some artifact in the wastelands, and want to research what it is, you don't want to risk accidentally breaking it. Uplinks control certain HackNet hubs. And there's other types, but listen, you don't need to understand it all right away. What's important is that in the end, no matter if they're corporate, criminals, idealists or just power hungry nut jobs, they all compete for those outposts.

Your response: And that didn't appeal to you?

NPC: With my talents, all I would contribute is stitching back together the victims of those fights. Only for them to jump up and immediately rejoin the fray. No, thank you. I'm gonna stay here. Help those in need of help. And keep the world out there from being my problem.

Your response: Anything I could do to help you?

entries.title: I never asked for this
entries.description:
You awoke in a high security facility with no idea how you got there and very few memories.

The shifty Security Chief wants you to talk to the Base Commander upstairs, on the right side behind the doors.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Security Chief / Area MC5

REPEAT
One time

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Base Commander / Area MC5

REWARDS
• 50 credits
• 50 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You're awake. Good. I know you must have a million questions right now, but time is short. Tell me: Do you remember anything?

Your response: What is going on? Where am I? Who are you? Owwww, my head...

Your response: No. I don't want to talk to you, at all. I just want to get home. How do I do that?

NPC: What are you doing back here?! Get out!

NPC: You're disoriented. That's to be expected. They did a real number on you. But you need to tell me, right now: What do you remember?

Your response: I don't- I don't remember anything! What is this place? What have you done to me?!

NPC: Damn. I'm sorry to hear that. I wish I could've saved more of you. Guess I was too late. I hate it when this happens.

Your response: Saved more? What are you talking about?

NPC: Listen, I can't explain it all right now, we have to keep it short, or it's both our asses. General Failure up there is already getting suspicious as it is. The gist of it is: This is a brainwashing facility, and I secretly interrupted your process.

Your response: Brainwashing? But if you interrupted the process, then why can't I remember anything?

NPC: You can't remember anything precisely because I intervened. If I hadn't, you would sing the Neocron anthem and happily volunteer for a suicide mission right now. I just wish I could've stopped it sooner. At least some of your memories would have survived, then.

Your response: Then I suppose I should thank you. But why would they do this? Who are they, anyway?

NPC: They are employees of Neocrons City Administration, in this facility called Area MC5. Those convicts who aren't put to death by CityAdmin end up here.

Your response: Convicts? This is punishment? What'd I do?

NPC: Who knows? I don't. Neither do they, probably. Maybe you were an employee of a corporation, and you spilled the CEO's coffee. Maybe you were a drifter, and you spoiled the balcony view of some rich brat. Doesn't really matter. If it were something really bad, you'd be dead. You're not, so there you have it.

Your response: Ugh, I feel really sick. And my head, it hurts so bad...

NPC: Uh, yeah. About that. Part of the process is putting a brain implant into you. And they aren't exactly being delicate when they do this. Hence, the headache. The sickness is a side effect of all the medication they pumped into you.

Your response: A brain implant? What kind of brain implant?

NPC: It's called a 'Law Enforcer'. Like I said, I can't explain it all, we have to make sure not to get caught. Basically, while you have that thing inside you, you can neither attack other runners, nor get attacked by them. It's how they try to enforce their little utopia.

Your response: But I don't like not being able to defend myself. How do I get rid of it?

NPC: Well, they weren't gentle when putting it in, so it will come out easily enough. You probably won't even need a doc for that, just pull it out. However, I would advise against it, at least right now. In your weakened state, you would be easy prey to all kinds of scum. Get home first, regroup, talk to whoever it is you're working for. Gather your strength.

Your response: Home! How do I get home? Am I a prisoner here?

NPC: Well... no, not really. This facility isn't properly equipped to house prisoners. It is quite well equipped to kill them, though. And that is what they do, if they have the slightest inkling that the process might have failed on you. So you need to be really careful, and act as though the brainwashing worked as they would expect.

Your response: But didn't you say, that someone up there is already suspicious?

NPC: Oh yes. Major Malfunction up there knows that someone is sabotaging his facility and interrupts some of his brainwashing processes, and he is absolutely livid about it. That's why he tasked his Security Chief with finding out who it is. But so far, I haven't. Heh heh.

Your response: So how do I get past him? I really need to get home.

NPC: The best way out is to avert suspicion by facing them head on. Go upstairs and talk directly to the Base Commander. Tell him how happy you are and how much you are looking forward to live and die for the city of Neocron, no matter if that's where you live or not. After that, one thing is bound to lead to another. And with the gene replicator outside, you can go home.

Your response: Okay then, I will talk to that Base Commander.

NPC: Tell him, that you got clearance from me. Be careful. And don't come back down here. You would only raise suspicion.

NPC: Stop dawdling. Get up there!

However, I would advise against it, at least right now. In your weakened state, you would be easy prey to all kinds of scum. Get home first, regroup, talk to whoever it is you're working for. Gather your strength.

Your response: Home! How do I get home? Am I a prisoner here?

NPC: Well... no, not really. This facility isn't properly equipped to house prisoners. It is quite well equipped to kill them, though. And that is what they do, if they have the slightest inkling that the process might have failed on you. So you need to be really careful, and act as though the brainwashing worked as they would expect.

Your response: But didn't you say, that someone up there is already suspicious?

NPC: Oh yes. Major Malfunction up there knows that someone is sabotaging his facility and interrupts some of his brainwashing processes, and he is absolutely livid about it. That's why he tasked his Security Chief with finding out who it is. But so far, I haven't. Heh heh.

Your response: So how do I get past him? I really need to get home.

NPC: The best way out is to avert suspicion by facing them head on. Go upstairs and talk directly to the Base Commander. Tell him how happy you are and how much you are looking forward to live and die for the city of Neocron, no matter if that's where you live or not. After that, one thing is bound to lead to another. And with the gene replicator outside, you can go home.

Your response: Okay then, I will talk to that Base Commander.

NPC: Tell him, that you got clearance from me. Be careful. And don't come back down here. You would only raise suspicion.

NPC: Stop dawdling. Get up there!
