entries.title: Mission 1: Nothing In The Caches
entries.description: The aid post is empty and Mrs. Jones has casualties. Go to the CITYMERCS HQ medbay - the room with the Medicare recreation units and the Paramedic - and find Doc Ferreira there. Twelve emergency caches are scattered through the medbay and the corridors around it, and they look like ordinary boxes. Open them and bring Mrs. Jones %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(collect_dressings) Sealed Field Dressings, because not all of them still have one.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 6 × Sealed Field Dressing
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have a problem and no time to be gentle about it. Three of my people came up out of the storage sublevel this morning bleeding, and the aid post could not treat them, because the aid post has nothing in it. Your file says you can patch a runner up. Right now I need somebody who can find me something to patch them with.

Your response: Tell me where to look.

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: The emergency caches. They are scattered all around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and the corridors around it - the room with the Medicare recreation units and the Paramedic in it. By regulation every one of those caches holds sealed dressings against exactly this. Nobody has opened one in a year.

Your response: How many do you need?

NPC: Six would let the aid post work today. Yeah. Bring me six sealed dressings out of those caches and do not be gentle with the lids. And find the old medic who works out of that medbay while you are there - his name is Ferreira and you will need him tomorrow. CityMercs HQ. Go.

NPC: You are the one Jones sent for dressings. Good luck to you.

Your response: She said there were caches around here.

NPC: There are. Take a look around, you'll spot them easy enough. Nobody has opened one since before I got here.

Your response: So they're all full?

NPC: I didn't say that. I said that nobody has opened them since before I got here. Just walk the whole quarter and open every medical box you find. And do not be disappointed: about half of them have nothing in them at all, and that is a conversation you and I are going to have later.

NPC: The caches are in and around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, and I need the contents of six of them. Go.

NPC: Very good. The aid post is working and all three of my people are still breathing. Now tell me the part you are chewing on, because you came in here with a face.

Your response: I opened all twelve caches to get six. Half of them were empty, and every one of the empty ones had a restock seal on it dated last month.

NPC: Mmh. Sealed last month and empty this month. Somebody signed for stock that never went in, and my people bled on a corridor floor this morning to prove it. That is a thread I'm gonna pull on. But not with you, not yet: you are a medic who has never been taught the one thing that actually keeps casualties alive, and I am not sending you out until you have been. Come back when you are rested. I am sending you to the man who taught me.

NPC: Ready to be taught something by somebody with far more right to teach it than me?

Your response: Ready. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. He is not going anywhere and neither is the lesson.

NPC: Doc Ferreira. You may have already met him. He runs the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, the one you emptied the caches out of this morning. He was a field medic for eighteen years before his knees retired him and he has forgotten more about triage than this Base collectively knows. He will not be kind about it. He has earned that.

Your response: I'll go and get told.

NPC: Yeah. Good. Listen to all of it, even when he repeats himself. Especially then. Same medbay as before. Go.

NPC: You are the one who emptied every cache in my medbay. Get comfortable. No, I'm not treating you, I'm talking at you, which will be a lot more painful for you. What I'm teaching you is not a technique. Two men down in front of you. One is screaming and one is not saying anything at all. Which one do you go to?

Your response: The one screaming. He is clearly in agony.

Your response: The quiet one.

NPC: You do, don't you? Your feet will take you to the noise. Everybody's do. But he is screaming because he has air in his lungs and blood in his brain to be frightened with: that is a man with time.

Your response: And the quiet one doesn't.

NPC: Exactly. The quiet one has nothing, especially not time, and quiet is not patience, it is a countdown. The whole job is learning to walk past the screaming.

Your response: How do you learn that?

NPC: Badly, and only once. Some day you will walk past somebody begging you for help and go to the man who cannot ask, and you will be right, and it will feel exactly like being a monster. Do it anyway. Now, while you are there: you emptied twelve caches this morning to find six dressings. Do me a favor and look at this.

Your response: What am I looking at?

NPC: My stock book. Eleven months of deliveries I signed for and never saw. Every line closed out as expended before it reached me. I have raised it four times and been thanked four times. If your Mrs. Jones has any teeth left, tell her about it, because I have run out.

Your response: I'll tell her tonight.

NPC: Good. Now get out of my medbay and go and be monstrous at somebody screaming.

NPC: Go on. The quiet one. Every time.

NPC: Ferreira is in the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and he is expecting you. Go.

NPC: Well? What did the old man leave you with?

Your response: The order, and the rest of my answer. Those caches are his to stock. He has been signing for medical stock he never receives - eleven months of it, written off as expended.

NPC: Expended. That word does a great deal of quiet work around here. Six dressings out of twelve caches, and the reason is sitting in a requisition ledger with somebody's initials on it. Get some rest. Then we are going to go and get to the bottom of this.

NPC: There you are. Ready to go and be very polite to somebody who is about to have a really bad afternoon?

Your response: I'm ready. Who signs the ledger?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. Ledgers get tidied.

NPC: Corporal Vane, Supply Depot, Sector 1. Every one of those write-offs went through his desk. I will say this before you go and I will not say it again afterwards: Vane is not a thief. He is a man who does what the paper in front of him says, and somebody has figured that out about him.

Your response: So I am not there to accuse him.

NPC: You are there to make him look at what he has been signing. That is worse than an accusation and considerably more useful. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go.

NPC: What is it? If it is not on a requisition I cannot help you, and if it is on a requisition it is probably nine weeks out.

Your response: It is about medical stock. Eleven months of it, closed out as expended before it ever reached the medics.

NPC: That is- those are all properly signed. I do them myself. Expended is what you write when a consignment is used before it is booked in, it is standard, it happens every-

Your response: Eleven months, Corporal. Every consignment. Read your own ledger back to yourself.

NPC: ...That is not possible. That would be every single one. I would have- I have been signing what came down on the sheet. The sheet comes from the quartermaster's office, it arrives already filled in, I check the totals against the manifest and the totals always match-

Your response: Because whoever fills in the sheet also writes the manifest.

NPC: Yes. Yes, they do. Oh, that is- I have been the signature on this. Not the hand. The signature. Somebody has figured out that I check totals and never check the paper the totals came on, and they have been using me as the honest part of it ever since.

Your response: Then be the honest part properly. Give it to Jones, all eleven months.

NPC: All of it. Every sheet, every manifest, and the names on the covering slips. Tell her I want to be in the room when it is read. I would like to be useful for once. Apparently, I haven't been.

NPC: It is all in her hands now. Go on, I have a lot of reading to do.

NPC: Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1 and that ledger is not going to read itself. Go.

NPC: Vane sent me eleven months of paper himself and asked to be in the room when it is read. I have never seen him volunteer for anything. What did you do to him?

Your response: Made him read his own ledger out loud. He was not stealing anything. He was being used because he checks totals and never checks the paper they came on.

NPC: Yeah. Used. That word does some heavy lifting around here. But anyway, the provosts have the covering slips and the names on them, and the medics get their stock back this week, which is the only part that saves anybody.

Your response: Ferreira raised this four times.

NPC: Four times, and was thanked four times, and nothing moved until somebody who had just carried a bunch of gauze up the stairs said it in front of me. That is not a compliment to you, recruit. It is a fairly ugly thing to know about how this place works, and you should always keep that in mind.

Your response: So what do I take away from all this?

NPC: Two things, and they are the same thing. Go to the quiet one, and read the paper the totals came on. A sealed cache nobody opens is the quiet casualty of a supply chain, and it stayed quiet for a year because everybody trusted a sheet that arrived already filled in. There is a healing module coming your way for the work, so keep training that PSI Use and stay the person who walks past the screaming. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

entries.title: Mission 2: Triage
entries.description: Mrs. Jones wants you taught the order casualties are actually treated in. Find Doc Ferreira in the CITYMERCS HQ medbay and sit through it.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Nothing In The Caches
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Doc Ferreira
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have a problem and no time to be gentle about it. Three of my people came up out of the storage sublevel this morning bleeding, and the aid post could not treat them, because the aid post has nothing in it. Your file says you can patch a runner up. Right now I need somebody who can find me something to patch them with.

Your response: Tell me where to look.

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: The emergency caches. They are scattered all around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and the corridors around it - the room with the Medicare recreation units and the Paramedic in it. By regulation every one of those caches holds sealed dressings against exactly this. Nobody has opened one in a year.

Your response: How many do you need?

NPC: Six would let the aid post work today. Yeah. Bring me six sealed dressings out of those caches and do not be gentle with the lids. And find the old medic who works out of that medbay while you are there - his name is Ferreira and you will need him tomorrow. CityMercs HQ. Go.

NPC: You are the one Jones sent for dressings. Good luck to you.

Your response: She said there were caches around here.

NPC: There are. Take a look around, you'll spot them easy enough. Nobody has opened one since before I got here.

Your response: So they're all full?

NPC: I didn't say that. I said that nobody has opened them since before I got here. Just walk the whole quarter and open every medical box you find. And do not be disappointed: about half of them have nothing in them at all, and that is a conversation you and I are going to have later.

NPC: The caches are in and around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, and I need the contents of six of them. Go.

NPC: Very good. The aid post is working and all three of my people are still breathing. Now tell me the part you are chewing on, because you came in here with a face.

Your response: I opened all twelve caches to get six. Half of them were empty, and every one of the empty ones had a restock seal on it dated last month.

NPC: Mmh. Sealed last month and empty this month. Somebody signed for stock that never went in, and my people bled on a corridor floor this morning to prove it. That is a thread I'm gonna pull on. But not with you, not yet: you are a medic who has never been taught the one thing that actually keeps casualties alive, and I am not sending you out until you have been. Come back when you are rested. I am sending you to the man who taught me.

NPC: Ready to be taught something by somebody with far more right to teach it than me?

Your response: Ready. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. He is not going anywhere and neither is the lesson.

NPC: Doc Ferreira. You may have already met him. He runs the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, the one you emptied the caches out of this morning. He was a field medic for eighteen years before his knees retired him and he has forgotten more about triage than this Base collectively knows. He will not be kind about it. He has earned that.

Your response: I'll go and get told.

NPC: Yeah. Good. Listen to all of it, even when he repeats himself. Especially then. Same medbay as before. Go.

NPC: You are the one who emptied every cache in my medbay. Get comfortable. No, I'm not treating you, I'm talking at you, which will be a lot more painful for you. What I'm teaching you is not a technique. Two men down in front of you. One is screaming and one is not saying anything at all. Which one do you go to?

Your response: The one screaming. He is clearly in agony.

Your response: The quiet one.

NPC: You do, don't you? Your feet will take you to the noise. Everybody's do. But he is screaming because he has air in his lungs and blood in his brain to be frightened with: that is a man with time.

Your response: And the quiet one doesn't.

NPC: Exactly. The quiet one has nothing, especially not time, and quiet is not patience, it is a countdown. The whole job is learning to walk past the screaming.

Your response: How do you learn that?

NPC: Badly, and only once. Some day you will walk past somebody begging you for help and go to the man who cannot ask, and you will be right, and it will feel exactly like being a monster. Do it anyway. Now, while you are there: you emptied twelve caches this morning to find six dressings. Do me a favor and look at this.

Your response: What am I looking at?

NPC: My stock book. Eleven months of deliveries I signed for and never saw. Every line closed out as expended before it reached me. I have raised it four times and been thanked four times. If your Mrs. Jones has any teeth left, tell her about it, because I have run out.

Your response: I'll tell her tonight.

NPC: Good. Now get out of my medbay and go and be monstrous at somebody screaming.

NPC: Go on. The quiet one. Every time.

NPC: Ferreira is in the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and he is expecting you. Go.

NPC: Well? What did the old man leave you with?

Your response: The order, and the rest of my answer. Those caches are his to stock. He has been signing for medical stock he never receives - eleven months of it, written off as expended.

NPC: Expended. That word does a great deal of quiet work around here. Six dressings out of twelve caches, and the reason is sitting in a requisition ledger with somebody's initials on it. Get some rest. Then we are going to go and get to the bottom of this.

NPC: What is it? If it is not on a requisition I cannot help you, and if it is on a requisition it is probably nine weeks out.

NPC: That is- those are all properly signed. I do them myself. Expended is what you write when a consignment is used before it is booked in, it is standard, it happens every-

Your response: Eleven months, Corporal. Every consignment. Read your own ledger back to yourself.

NPC: ...That is not possible. That would be every single one. I would have- I have been signing what came down on the sheet. The sheet comes from the quartermaster's office, it arrives already filled in, I check the totals against the manifest and the totals always match-

entries.title: Mission 3: Written Off As Expended
entries.description: Medical requisitions are being closed out as expended and never reaching anybody. Question Corporal Vane at the Supply Depot in MILITARY BASE SEC-1, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: Triage
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Corporal Vane
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: The emergency caches. They are scattered all around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and the corridors around it - the room with the Medicare recreation units and the Paramedic in it.  184          - "Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there."
 185  
 186      jones_m1_briefing:
 187        say:
 188          - "The emergency caches. They are scattered all around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and the corridors around it - the room with the Medicare recreation units and the Paramedic in it. By regulation every one of those caches holds sealed dressings against exactly this. Nobody has opened one in a year."
 189        answer:
 190          jones_m1_go:
 191            - "How many do you need?"
 192  
 193      jones_m1_go:
 194        do:
 195          - offer_mission: mb_fieldmedic.mission1
 196        say:
 197          - "Six would let the aid post work today. Yeah. Bring me six sealed dressings out of those caches and do not be gentle with the lids. And find the old medic who works out of that medbay while you are there - his name is Ferreira and you will need him tomorrow. CityMercs HQ. Go."
 198        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 199  
 200      ferreira_caches:
 201        say:
 202          - "You are the one Jones sent for dressings. Good luck to you."
 203        answer:
 204          ferreira_caches_spot:
 205            - "She said there were caches around here."
 206  
 207      ferreira_caches_spot:
 208        say:
 209          - "There are. Take a look around, you'll spot them easy enough. Nobody has opened one since before I got here."
 210        answer:
 211          ferreira_caches_half_empty:
 212            - "So they're all full?"
 213  
 214      ferreira_caches_half_empty:
 215        say:
 216          - "I didn't say that. I said that nobody has opened them since before I got here. Just walk the whole quarter and open every medical box you find. And do not be disappointed: about half of them have nothing in them at all, and that is a conversation you and I are going to have later."
 217        resume_at: ferreira_caches
 218  
 219      jones_m1_return:
 220        do:
 221          - goto: jones_m1_report
 222            when:
 223              objective_done:
 224                objective: collect_dressings
 225          - goto: jones_m1_not_done
 226  
 227      jones_m1_not_done:
 228        say:
 229          - "The caches are in and around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, and I need the contents of six of them. Go."
 230        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 231  
 232      jones_m1_report:
 233        say:
 234          - "Very good. The aid post is working and all three of my people are still breathing. Now tell me the part you are chewing on, because you came in here with a face."
 235        answer:
 236          jones_m1_done:
 237            - "I opened all twelve caches to get six. Half of them were empty, and every one of the empty ones had a restock seal on it dated last month."
 238        resume_at: jones_m1_done
 239  
 240      jones_m1_done:
 241        do:
 242          - set_flag:
 243              flag: mb_fieldmedic
 244              value: 1
 245          - take_item:
 246              item: 8630
 247              count: 6
 248          - complete_objective: report
 249        say:
 250          - "Mmh. Sealed last month and empty this month. Somebody signed for stock that never went in, and my people bled on a corridor floor this morning to prove it. That is a thread I'm gonna pull on. But not with you, not yet: you are a medic who has never been taught the one thing that actually keeps casualties alive, and I am not sending you out until you have been. Come back when you are rested. I am sending you to the man who taught me."
 251  
 252      jones_m2_offer:
 253        say:
 254          - "Ready to be taught something by somebody with far more right to teach it than me?"
 255        answer:
 256          jones_m2_briefing:
 257            - "Ready. Who is he?"
 258          jones_m2_later:
 259            - "Give me a minute."
 260  
 261      jones_m2_later:
 262        say:
 263          - "Take it. He is not going anywhere and neither is the lesson."
 264  
 265      jones_m2_briefing:
 266        say:
 267          - "Doc Ferreira. You may have already met him. He runs the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, the one you emptied the caches out of this morning. He was a field medic for eighteen years before his knees retired him and he has forgotten more about triage than this Base collectively knows. He will not be kind about it. He has earned that."
 268        answer:
 269          jones_m2_go:
 270            - "I'll go and get told."
 271  
 272      jones_m2_go:
 273        do:
 274          - offer_mission: mb_fieldmedic.mission2
 275        say:
 276          - "Yeah. Good. Listen to all of it, even when he repeats himself. Especially then. Same medbay as before. Go."
 277        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 278  
 279      ferreira_triage:
 280        say:
 281          - "You are the one who emptied every cache in my medbay. Get comfortable. No, I'm not treating you, I'm talking at you, which will be a lot more painful for you. What I'm teaching you is not a technique. Two men down in front of you. One is screaming and one is not saying anything at all. Which one do you go to?"
 282        answer:
 283          ferreira_triage_screaming:
 284            - "The one screaming. He is clearly in agony."
 285          ferreira_triage_quiet:
 286            - "The quiet one."
 287  
 288      ferreira_triage_screaming:
 289        say:
 290          - "You do, don't you? Your feet will take you to the noise. Everybody's do. But he is screaming because he has air in his lungs and blood in his brain to be frightened with: that is a man with time."
 291        answer:
 292          ferreira_triage_quiet:
 293            - "And the quiet one doesn't."
 294  
 295      ferreira_triage_quiet:
 296        say:
 297          - "Exactly. The quiet one has nothing, especially not time, and quiet is not patience, it is a countdown. The whole job is learning to walk past the screaming."
 298        answer:
 299          ferreira_triage_learning:
 300            - "How do you learn that?"
 301  
 302      ferreira_triage_learning:
 303        say:
 304          - "Badly, and only once. Some day you will walk past somebody begging you for help and go to the man who cannot ask, and you will be right, and it will feel exactly like being a monster. Do it anyway. Now, while you are there: you emptied twelve caches this morning to find six dressings. Do me a favor and look at this."
 305        answer:
 306          ferreira_stock_book:
 307            - "What am I looking at?"
 308  
 309      ferreira_stock_book:
 310        say:
 311          - "My stock book. Eleven months of deliveries I signed for and never saw. Every line closed out as expended before it reached me. I have raised it four times and been thanked four times. If your Mrs. Jones has any teeth left, tell her about it, because I have run out."
 312        answer:
 313          ferreira_dismissal:
 314            - "I'll tell her tonight."
 315  
 316      ferreira_dismissal:
 317        do:
 318          - complete_objective: learn_triage
 319        say:
 320          - "Good. Now get out of my medbay and go and be monstrous at somebody screaming."
 321        resume_at: ferreira_triage_done
 322  
 323      ferreira_triage_done:
 324        say:
 325          - "Go on. The quiet one. Every time."
 326  
 327      jones_m2_return:
 328        do:
 329          - goto: jones_m2_report
 330            when:
 331              objective_done:
 332                objective: learn_triage
 333          - goto: jones_m2_not_done
 334  
 335      jones_m2_not_done:
 336        say:
 337          - "Ferreira is in the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and he is expecting you. Go."
 338        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 339  
 340      jones_m2_report:
 341        say:
 342          - "Well? What did the old man leave you with?"
 343        answer:
 344          jones_m2_done:
 345            - "The order, and the rest of my answer. Those caches are his to stock. He has been signing for medical stock he never receives - eleven months of it, written off as expended."
 346        resume_at: jones_m2_done
 347  
 348      jones_m2_done:
 349        do:
 350          - set_flag:
 351              flag: mb_fieldmedic
 352              value: 2
 353          - complete_objective: report
 354        say:
 355          - "Expended. That word does a great deal of quiet work around here. Six dressings out of twelve caches, and the reason is sitting in a requisition ledger with somebody's initials on it. Get some rest. Then we are going to go and get to the bottom of this."
 356  
 357      jones_m3_offer:
 358        say:
 359          - "There you are. Ready to go and be very polite to somebody who is about to have a really bad afternoon?"
 360        answer:
 361          jones_m3_briefing:
 362            - "I'm ready. Who signs the ledger?"
 363          jones_m3_later:
 364            - "Give me a moment."
 365  
 366      jones_m3_later:
 367        say:
 368          - "Do not be long. Ledgers get tidied."
 369  
 370      jones_m3_briefing:
 371        say:
 372          - "Corporal Vane, Supply Depot, Sector 1. Every one of those write-offs went through his desk. I will say this before you go and I will not say it again afterwards: Vane is not a thief. He is a man who does what the paper in front of him says, and somebody has figured that out about him."
 373        answer:
 374          jones_m3_go:
 375            - "So I am not there to accuse him."
 376  
 377      jones_m3_go:
 378        do:
 379          - offer_mission: mb_fieldmedic.mission3
 380        say:
 381          - "You are there to make him look at what he has been signing. That is worse than an accusation and considerably more useful. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go."
 382        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 383  
 384      vane_greeting:
 385        say:
 386          - "What is it? If it is not on a requisition I cannot help you, and if it is on a requisition it is probably nine weeks out."
 387        answer:
 388          vane_properly_signed:
 389            - "It is about medical stock. Eleven months of it, closed out as expended before it ever reached the medics."
 390  
 391      vane_properly_signed:
 392        say:
 393          - "That is- those are all properly signed. I do them myself. Expended is what you write when a consignment is used before it is booked in, it is standard, it happens every-"
 394        answer:
 395          vane_not_possible:
 396            - "Eleven months, Corporal. Every consignment. Read your own ledger back to yourself."
 397  
 398      vane_not_possible:
 399        say:
 400          - "...That is not possible. That would be every single one. I would have- I have been signing what came down on the sheet. The sheet comes from the quartermaster's office, it arrives already filled in, I check the totals against the manifest and the totals always match-"
 401        answer:
 402          vane_the_signature:
 403            - "Because whoever fills in the sheet also writes the manifest."
 404  
 405      vane_the_signature:
 406        say:
 407          - "Yes. Yes, they do. Oh, that is- I have been the signature on this. Not the hand. The signature. Somebody has figured out that I check totals and never check the paper the totals came on, and they have been using me as the honest part of it ever since."
 408        answer:
 409          vane_all_of_it:
 410            - "Then be the honest part properly. Give it to Jones, all eleven months."
 411  
 412      vane_all_of_it:
 413        do:
 414          - complete_objective: question_vane
 415        say:
 416          - "All of it. Every sheet, every manifest, and the names on the covering slips. Tell her I want to be in the room when it is read. I would like to be useful for once. Apparently, I haven't been."
 417        resume_at: vane_reading
 418  
 419      vane_reading:
 420        say:
 421          - "It is all in her hands now. Go on, I have a lot of reading to do."
 422  
 423      jones_m3_return:
 424        do:
 425          - goto: jones_m3_report
 426            when:
 427              objective_done:
 428                objective: question_vane
 429          - goto: jones_m3_not_done
 430  
 431      jones_m3_not_done:
 432        say:
 433          - "Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1 and that ledger is not going to read itself. Go."
 434        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 435  
 436      jones_m3_report:
 437        say:
 438          - "Vane sent me eleven months of paper himself and asked to be in the room when it is read. I have never seen him volunteer for anything. What did you do to him?"
 439        answer:
 440          jones_m3_debrief:
 441            - "Made him read his own ledger out loud. He was not stealing anything. He was being used because he checks totals and never checks the paper they came on."
 442        resume_at: jones_m3_debrief
 443  
 444      jones_m3_debrief:
 445        say:
 446          - "Yeah. Used. That word does some heavy lifting around here. But anyway, the provosts have the covering slips and the names on them, and the medics get their stock back this week, which is the only part that saves anybody."
 447        answer:
 448          jones_m3_four_times:
 449            - "Ferreira raised this four times."
 450  
 451      jones_m3_four_times:
 452        say:
 453          - "Four times, and was thanked four times, and nothing moved until somebody who had just carried a bunch of gauze up the stairs said it in front of me. That is not a compliment to you, recruit. It is a fairly ugly thing to know about how this place works, and you should always keep that in mind."
 454        answer:
 455          jones_m3_done:
 456            - "So what do I take away from all this?"
 457  
 458      jones_m3_done:
 459        do:
 460          - set_flag:
 461              flag: mb_fieldmedic
 462              value: 3
 463          - give_item:
 464              item: 8556
 465              quality: 150
 466              slots: 3
 467          - complete_objective: report
 468          - remove
 469        say:
 470          - "Two things, and they are the same thing. Go to the quiet one, and read the paper the totals came on. A sealed cache nobody opens is the quiet casualty of a supply chain, and it stayed quiet for a year because everybody trusted a sheet that arrived already filled in. There is a healing module coming your way for the work, so keep training that PSI Use and stay the person who walks past the screaming. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs."

entries.title: Mission 1: Clean Logs
entries.description: Mrs. Jones has an access log with nothing wrong in it, which is what worries her. Find Sable at the Supply Depot in MILITARY BASE SEC-1 and have her read it.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Sable
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have a month of door logs for the armory level and there is nothing wrong with them. No failed entries. No mistyped codes. Not one drunk corporal leaning on a panel at four in the morning. A month of perfect human beings. Does that sound like this Base to you?

Your response: It sounds like somebody tidied up.

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: That was quick. Good. I cannot take this to anybody upstairs on a feeling, so I want it read properly by somebody who does this for a living. Sector 1, the Supply Depot. Ask for Sable. She used to do rather more interesting work than selling software and she still knows what a scrubbed log looks like from across the room.

Your response: And if she says I'm imagining it?

NPC: Then I am wrong and we both get an early night. That would be a nice change. Sector 1, the Supply Depot. Take the log to her and listen to the whole answer, not just the part you already agree with. Go.

NPC: What do you want? Software is on the rack, licenses are on the board, and no, I do not do custom work any more.

Your response: Mrs. Jones sent me. She wants you to read a door log.

NPC: Of course she did. Give it here. A month of the armory level, and- huh. Well, that is clean.

Your response: Too clean. Somebody scrubbed it.

NPC: No. That is what you are supposed to think, and it is what I thought for a few seconds. A scrub leaves a shape: gaps, reindexed sequence numbers, timestamps that step wrong. This has none of that. The sequence is perfect. These failures were not deleted, they were never generated.

Your response: Then the panel never rejected anybody all month.

NPC: The panel was never asked. Somebody is authorizing upstream of it. Ancient trick, and it needs real access to set up: you bypass the control system altogether and just tell the door to open. So the panel has nothing to fail and nothing to log. To the system, nobody was ever there.

Your response: So how do you catch somebody the system cannot see?

NPC: You stop asking the system. Everything digital in this Base can be told what to remember. Go and find someone who remembers with their brain and writes with a pen. Tell Jones that, and tell her I said she still owes me for the last time she was right.

NPC: Go on. Someone with a pen.

NPC: Sable is somewhere around the Supply Depot in Sector 1 and that log is not getting any younger. Go.

NPC: Well? Am I paranoid or am I right?

Your response: You are right, but not the way you thought. Nothing was deleted. The failures were never written. Somebody is telling the door to open directly instead of authorizing at the panel, so the panel has nothing to fail.

NPC: Never written. That is worse, and it is also a lot harder to do. You do not fake a clean month, recruit, you build a way of walking through a door that no system ever has to think about. Somebody in this Base has forsaken keys altogether. Get some sleep. Tomorrow we go and find the one log they could not reach.

NPC: Ready to go and read something extremely boring very carefully?

Your response: Which log could they not reach?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. Boring things keep.

NPC: The gate. Every door in this Base is a system, and systems can be taught to look the other way. The gate is a man with a clipboard called Pell, and clipboards are stupid in a way that is very hard to corrupt. If somebody is walking through doors unseen by the system, they are still walking past Pell to do it.

Your response: So I put the two lists side by side.

NPC: You do, and you do it with him, because he has been at that gate for years and years, and he remembers faces the way you remember syntax. Military Entrance. Find me the name that is in one list and not the other.

NPC: Whatever it is, it will be in the book. Everything is in the book. That's the only reason anybody talks to me.

Your response: That is exactly why I am here. I need your crossings against a month of armory door entries.

NPC: Now that is a proper question. Get comfortable, this may take a while and I am not letting you touch the book. Read me your names, I will tell you who came through my gate.

Your response: Start with the ones that repeat. Karn. Nineteen entries at the armory doors this month.

NPC: Karn. Karn... no. Not once. Not one crossing in the book all month, and I would remember, because I know her face. Comes in most mornings. Contractor, ducting work, signs the day sheet, very polite. Never once in my crossings book because contractors sign the sheet, not the book.

Your response: Whose chip does she sign with?

NPC: Let's find out - here. Hollis. That is Hollis's number. Hollis has been dead since spring, went out on a wastes patrol and did not come back. Nobody deactivates a dead soldier's chip. It's on a form, and the form is on a desk, and the desk is weeks behind, like everything else in this Base.

Your response: Then Karn has been walking around with the ID of a dead Merc all that time.

NPC: And my book says she was never here at all. Take that to Jones and tell her the book is still right. It is the only thing around here that is.

NPC: Nineteen times. And not one crossing. Go on, tell her.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance with eleven years of clipboards. Go and read them with him.

NPC: Give me the name.

Your response: Karn. Nineteen entries at the armory doors this month and not one crossing at the gate. Pell knows the face. She signs in every morning as a contractor with somebody else's chip - a Merc who died in the wastes in spring and was never taken off active.

NPC: A dead man's credentials. We bury people out here, and their chips keep walking around, because deactivation is somebody's third priority on a bad week. She is not breaking our security, recruit. She is using it exactly as designed. That is the part that should keep you awake. Come back when you are ready to finish up.

NPC: Karn signed in this morning and has not signed out. In?

Your response: I'm in. Where is she?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not take long. She does not stay in one place for a whole afternoon.

NPC: Sitting out the afternoon in the Black Ribbon Bar at the CityMercs HQ, because she does not move until the evening shift change and the man on the evening gate does not look up. She is carrying whatever she took off the armory level this month, and that chip. I want both back. Preferably intact.

Your response: And if she will not hand it over?

NPC: Then drop her where she stands, and let the guys from reclamation do their jobs. She is not a soldier, she is a woman who has spent a lot of time being invisible, and invisible people fight badly when somebody finally looks straight at them. CityMercs HQ, the Black Ribbon Bar. Go.

NPC: Afternoon. Waiting on the shift change like everybody else. You want the bar, it is behind me.

Your response: Hollis died in spring, Karn. You have been walking around the place on his chip, teaching the security systems to look the other way.

NPC: ...Ah. You are the reason the panel logs got pulled. I did wonder who they would send and I will be honest, I expected somebody with more rank and less curiosity.

Your response: Nineteen entries this month. What have you been taking out?

NPC: Nothing they were using. Not defending myself, it's just true. This Base writes off more hardware in a month than most clans own, including mine. None of it is missed, because nobody counts what is already dead on paper. I didn't break anything to do this. I read your paperwork properly, which is more than anyone here has managed in years.

Your response: You're done. Hand over whatever you took this time, and the chip.

NPC: No, I do not think I will. Do you know what happens to a woman who gets caught being invisible? She stops being anything at all.

NPC: ...

NPC: Karn is in the Black Ribbon Bar at the CityMercs HQ until the shift change, and after that she is gone. Go.

NPC: The Black Ribbon is asking why there is a body in their bar and no name in the book to go with it. What about the chip?

Your response: Intact, I checked. She did not think much of our security. She was mostly complimenting our paperwork.

NPC: She was right to. Hollis's chip should have been dead the week Hollis was. Instead it has been walking through our armory for months because deactivation is a low priority for people already overworked. That is what makes me tired.

Your response: So the system was never actually broken.

NPC: Not broken, bypassed in some places, outwitted in others. And that is the whole lesson, so take it properly: a system does not have to be broken to be wrong. It only has to be obeyed by somebody who understood it better than the people who built it. You will spend your career being that person. Try to spend it on our side of the door.

Your response: What happens to the dead chips?

NPC: They get deactivated this week, all of them, because I am about to make that somebody's first priority instead of their third. There is a hacktool coming your way and a piece of software Sable insisted on throwing in, so keep training that Hacking and remember what you learned at a gate with a paper book on it: when everything digital agrees, go and find the thing that writes with a pen. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Karn. Karn... no. Not once. Not one crossing in the book all month, and I would remember, because I know her face. Comes in most mornings. Contractor, ducting work, signs the day sheet, very polite. Never once in my crossings book because contractors sign the sheet, not the book.

Your response: Whose chip does she sign with?

NPC: Let's find out - here. Hollis. That is Hollis's number. Hollis has been dead since spring, went out on a wastes patrol and did not come back. Nobody deactivates a dead soldier's chip. It's on a form, and the form is on a desk, and the desk is weeks behind, like everything else in this Base.

Your response: Then Karn has been walking around with the ID of a dead Merc all that time.

NPC: And my book says she was never here at all. Take that to Jones and tell her the book is still right. It is the only thing around here that is.

NPC: Nineteen times. And not one crossing. Go on, tell her.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance with eleven years of clipboards. Go and read them with him.

NPC: Give me the name.

Your response: Karn. Nineteen entries at the armory doors this month and not one crossing at the gate. Pell knows the face. She signs in every morning as a contractor with somebody else's chip - a Merc who died in the wastes in spring and was never taken off active.

NPC: A dead man's credentials. We bury people out here, and their chips keep walking around, because deactivation is somebody's third priority on a bad week. She is not breaking our security, recruit. She is using it exactly as designed. That is the part that should keep you awake. Come back when you are ready to finish up.

NPC: Karn signed in this morning and has not signed out. In?

Your response: I'm in. Where is she?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not take long. She does not stay in one place for a whole afternoon.

NPC: Sitting out the afternoon in the Black Ribbon Bar at the CityMercs HQ, because she does not move until the evening shift change and the man on the evening gate does not look up. She is carrying whatever she took off the armory level this month, and that chip. I want both back. Preferably intact.

Your response: And if she will not hand it over?

NPC: Then drop her where she stands, and let the guys from reclamation do their jobs. She is not a soldier, she is a woman who has spent a lot of time being invisible, and invisible people fight badly when somebody finally looks straight at them. CityMercs HQ, the Black Ribbon Bar. Go.

NPC: Afternoon. Waiting on the shift change like everybody else. You want the bar, it is behind me.

Your response: Hollis died in spring, Karn. You have been walking around the place on his chip, teaching the security systems to look the other way.

NPC: ...Ah. You are the reason the panel logs got pulled. I did wonder who they would send and I will be honest, I expected somebody with more rank and less curiosity.

Your response: Nineteen entries this month. What have you been taking out?

NPC: Nothing they were using. Not defending myself, it's just true. This Base writes off more hardware in a month than most clans own, including mine. None of it is missed, because nobody counts what is already dead on paper. I didn't break anything to do this. I read your paperwork properly, which is more than anyone here has managed in years.

Your response: You're done. Hand over whatever you took this time, and the chip.

NPC: No, I do not think I will. Do you know what happens to a woman who gets caught being invisible? She stops being anything at all.

NPC: ...

NPC: Karn is in the Black Ribbon Bar at the CityMercs HQ until the shift change, and after that she is gone. Go.

NPC: The Black Ribbon is asking why there is a body in their bar and no name in the book to go with it. What about the chip?

Your response: Intact, I checked. She did not think much of our security. She was mostly complimenting our paperwork.

NPC: She was right to. Hollis's chip should have been dead the week Hollis was. Instead it has been walking through our armory for months because deactivation is a low priority for people already overworked. That is what makes me tired.

Your response: So the system was never actually broken.

NPC: Not broken, bypassed in some places, outwitted in others. And that is the whole lesson, so take it properly: a system does not have to be broken to be wrong. It only has to be obeyed by somebody who understood it better than the people who built it. You will spend your career being that person. Try to spend it on our side of the door.

Your response: What happens to the dead chips?

NPC: They get deactivated this week, all of them, because I am about to make that somebody's first priority instead of their third. There is a hacktool coming your way and a piece of software Sable insisted on throwing in, so keep training that Hacking and remember what you learned at a gate with a paper book on it: when everything digital agrees, go and find the thing that writes with a pen. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

entries.title: Mission 1: Ways In
entries.description: Before you learn to go where you are not wanted, learn who watches what. Talk to Corporal Vane at the Supply Depot in MILITARY BASE SEC-1, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Corporal Vane
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Everybody in your line of work who comes to me asks the same question first, which is how to not be seen. But that's the wrong question and it would get you killed soon. Would you like to know the right one?

Your response: Go on. What is the right question?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Who is looking, and at what. Nobody watches everything, recruit. People watch the thing they are responsible for and they are magnificently blind to everything else, and if you know which is which, you can walk through the middle of a room with nobody noticing you. Your response: A supply clerk? Really?

NPC: A supply clerk who can tell you the weight of a crate by the sound it makes on the ramp and could not tell you the color of the door it came through. That is the most useful conversation you will have for some time. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go and listen.

NPC: Depot's closed for intake until further notice. If it's not a requisition, it can wait.

Your response: It's not a requisition. What do you actually watch, Corporal?

NPC: What do I w- the stock. I watch the stock. Weight, count, seal numbers. I can tell you what is in a crate from the noise it makes coming down the ramp and I can tell you if a pallet is two units light from across the bay.

Your response: And the people carrying it?

NPC: What about them? They are hands. I do not- all right, I can see where this is going, and Jones has made this point at me before. No, I could not pick out even one man who has carried a crate through that door this year. Yes, I have been robbed twice, and both times I stood there and watched it happen and gave the provosts nothing worth writing down.

Your response: Because you were looking at the crate.

NPC: Because I was counting the crate. That's my job. Nobody has ever once asked me to look at a face, and if I started, I would miss a short pallet in no time, and somebody in the wastes would run out of ammunition because of it. So no, I do not watch people. I watch numbers, and I'm very good at it.

Your response: That is exactly what she wanted me to hear.

NPC: Then tell her she has made her point and she can stop sending people to make it. Go on, intake is in ten minutes.

NPC: Numbers. Every time. Now let me count.

NPC: Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Go and ask him what he actually looks at.

NPC: What does Corporal Vane watch?

Your response: Numbers. He knows every crate in his depot by weight and count, but he couldn't describe one person who carried one in. He has been robbed twice this year by people he looked directly at.

NPC: Twice that he knows of. It's actually been five times, and he still could not pick any of them out of a line. You will just be standing in the part of the room nobody is responsible for.

NPC: Theory is over. Time for practice. Ready for the part where it is dark and something is already in there?

Your response: Ready. Where am I going?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. The dark is patient. That is rather the point of it.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3, where the recovery sled drops what it drags in. No clean lines, no lit corridors, nothing that behaves like a room. I want you in and out of there. There are things living in there and they do not care how quiet you are, which is exactly the lesson.

Your response: So this is not a stealth exercise.

NPC: It is the other half of one. Sooner or later something sees you, and everything you know about not being seen becomes worthless in the same second. Put down eight of them and come back out. I want to know what you are like after it goes wrong.

NPC: You're still here. The wreck yard in Storage 3. Go.

NPC: So you're back, and in one piece I might add. How far did you get before something noticed you?

Your response: About a third. After that it was just work. I stopped trying to be quiet and started trying to be finished.

NPC: Good. That is how you do it. Most recruits try to do it another way, where they get all the way through untouched. NPC: There is a man in this Base selling the result of what I have been trying to teach you. In?

Your response: I'm in. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not be long. He is careful, and careful men get restless.

NPC: Ivo Mattis, CityMercs HQ. He has spent quite some time mapping what every post in this Base fails to look at, and for the last few weeks he has been selling that information to whoever is buying. Not our layout, or our codes, but our blind spots. Somebody walked into the armory level last week on the strength of it.

Your response: Sounds like he is very good at the job you are teaching me.

NPC: He is the best I ever taught. Yes, it was me who taught him. And yes, I am aware of what that makes today. He will know you are there before you are close, so do not waste your afternoon trying to be invisible at a man who knows every trick in the book. Walk up to him. CityMercs HQ. Finish it.

NPC: You have been in the doorway for about five seconds. Come in properly, she taught you better than that. How do I know that? She taught me as well, and now she has taught you, and here we are.

Your response: You have been selling the Base's blind spots.

NPC: I have been selling a lot of work that nobody here would pay me for. I brought her the first survey right at the beginning. Do you know what it got me? Filed. Filed, and a note about my initiative. Every post in this Base is blind in an almost ridiculous way. I can draw that on a page. In fact, I did. But nobody upstairs wanted that page.

Your response: So you sold it to people who came in through the armory last week.

NPC: What I sold is basically a map. What anybody does with it is not my department. And before you say the word: I did not tell them about Hollis, or the sublevel, or any of the other holes this place opens on its own every other week. I only ever wrote down what was already true.

Your response: Two Mercs died on the armory level standing in a spot you drew a circle around.

NPC: Yes. They did. I know both names. I have known them every day since. They hound me every night. And do you know what I do? I keep selling.

NPC: ...

NPC: Mattis is at the CityMercs HQ and he does not sit still forever. Go.

NPC: It is done, then. Did he talk?

Your response: He said he brought you the first survey right at the beginning and it got filed. He knew the names of the two who died in that robbery, and he kept selling anyway.

NPC: He did bring me that survey. I read it, I agreed with every line, and I passed it up. It came back stamped and went in a drawer. And I let it stay in the drawer because I had eleven other things to do. So he is not lying and I do not get to pretend that he is.

Your response: That is not the same as what he did with it.

NPC: No, it's not, and I do not need comforting, thank you very much. He made the choice. I made the filing. Both of those are real, only one of them is a crime, and I have to live in a Base where the second one happens every week.

Your response: So what am I supposed to do differently?

NPC: Know who is looking and at what: that is the craft, and it is yours now. But when you bring somebody the page and they file it, do not go quiet and do not go and sell it. Come back and put it on the desk again, and keep doing that until somebody finally pays attention or throws you out. There is a stealth tool coming your way, so keep training that Pistol Combat and stay somewhere you can stand being invisible. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

CONTACT

1

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Everybody in your line of work who comes to me asks the same question first, which is how to not be seen. But that's the wrong question and it would get you killed soon. Would you like to know the right one?

Your response: Go on. What is the right question?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Who is looking, and at what. Nobody watches everything, recruit. People watch the thing they are responsible for and they are magnificently blind to everything else, and if you know which is which, you can walk through the middle of a room with nobody noticing you. Go to Corporal Vane at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Find out what it is that he watches.

Your response: A supply clerk? Really?

NPC: A supply clerk who can tell you the weight of a crate by the sound it makes on the ramp and could not tell you the color of the door it came through. That is the most useful conversation you will have for some time. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go and listen.

NPC: Depot's closed for intake until further notice. If it's not a requisition, it can wait.

Your response: It's not a requisition. What do you actually watch, Corporal?

NPC: What do I w- the stock. I watch the stock. Weight, count, seal numbers. I can tell you what is in a crate from the noise it makes coming down the ramp and I can tell you if a pallet is two units light from across the bay.

Your response: And the people carrying it?

NPC: What about them? They are hands. I do not- all right, I can see where this is going, and Jones has made this point at me before. No, I could not pick out even one man who has carried a crate through that door this year. Yes, I have been robbed twice, and both times I stood there and watched it happen and gave the provosts nothing worth writing down.

Your response: Because you were looking at the crate.

NPC: Because I was counting the crate. That's my job. Nobody has ever once asked me to look at a face, and if I started, I would miss a short pallet in no time, and somebody in the wastes would run out of ammunition because of it. So no, I do not watch people. I watch numbers, and I'm very good at it.

Your response: That is exactly what she wanted me to hear.

NPC: Then tell her she has made her point and she can stop sending people to make it. Go on, intake is in ten minutes.

NPC: Numbers. Every time. Now let me count.

NPC: Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Go and ask him what he actually looks at.

NPC: What does Corporal Vane watch?

Your response: Numbers. He knows every crate in his depot by weight and count, but he couldn't describe one person who carried one in. He has been robbed twice this year by people he looked directly at.

NPC: Twice that he knows of. It's actually been five times, and he still could not pick any of them out of a line. Now do that for every post in this Base: the gate watches faces, the armory watches badges, the medics watch bodies. Learn the shape of what each of them is not looking at, do your best to become that shape, and people will simply look past you. You will just be standing in the part of the room nobody is responsible for.

NPC: Theory is over. Time for practice. Ready for the part where it is dark and something is already in there?

Your response: Ready. Where am I going?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. The dark is patient. That is rather the point of it.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3, where the recovery sled drops what it drags in. No clean lines, no lit corridors, nothing that behaves like a room. I want you in and out of there. There are things living in there and they do not care how quiet you are, which is exactly the lesson.

Your response: So this is not a stealth exercise.

NPC: It is the other half of one. Sooner or later something sees you, and everything you know about not being seen becomes worthless in the same second. Put down eight of them and come back out. I want to know what you are like after it goes wrong.

NPC: You're still here. The wreck yard in Storage 3. Go.

NPC: So you're back, and in one piece I might add. How far did you get before something noticed you?

Your response: About a third. After that it was just work. I stopped trying to be quiet and started trying to be finished.

NPC: Good. That is how you do it. Most recruits try to do it another way, where they get all the way through untouched. Those recruits are either lying or extremely lucky, and both of those would eventually run out. Next thing to do will be both halves, all in one afternoon. Come back when you have your wind.

NPC: There is a man in this Base selling the result of what I have been trying to teach you. In?

Your response: I'm in. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not be long. He is careful, and careful men get restless.

NPC: Ivo Mattis, CityMercs HQ. He has spent quite some time mapping what every post in this Base fails to look at, and for the last few weeks he has been selling that information to whoever is buying. Not our layout, or our codes, but our blind spots. Somebody walked into the armory level last week on the strength of it.

Your response: Sounds like he is very good at the job you are teaching me.

NPC: He is the best I ever taught. Yes, it was me who taught him. And yes, I am aware of what that makes today. He will know you are there before you are close, so do not waste your afternoon trying to be invisible at a man who knows every trick in the book. Walk up to him. CityMercs HQ. Finish it.

NPC: You have been in the doorway for about five seconds. Come in properly, she taught you better than that. How do I know that? She taught me as well, and now she has taught you, and here we are.

Your response: You have been selling the Base's blind spots.

NPC: I have been selling a lot of work that nobody here would pay me for. I brought her the first survey right at the beginning. Do you know what it got me? Filed. Filed, and a note about my initiative. Every post in this Base is blind in an almost ridiculous way. I can draw that on a page. In fact, I did. But nobody upstairs wanted that page.

Your response: So you sold it to people who came in through the armory last week.

NPC: What I sold is basically a map. What anybody does with it is not my department. And before you say the word: I did not tell them about Hollis, or the sublevel, or any of the other holes this place opens on its own every other week. I only ever wrote down what was already true.

Your response: Two Mercs died on the armory level standing in a spot you drew a circle around.

NPC: Yes. They did. I know both names. I have known them every day since. They hound me every night. And do you know what I do? I keep selling.

NPC: ...

NPC: Mattis is at the CityMercs HQ and he does not sit still forever. Go.

NPC: It is done, then. Did he talk?

Your response: He said he brought you the first survey right at the beginning and it got filed. He knew the names of the two who died in that robbery, and he kept selling anyway.

NPC: He did bring me that survey. I read it, I agreed with every line, and I passed it up. It came back stamped and went in a drawer. And I let it stay in the drawer because I had eleven other things to do. So he is not lying and I do not get to pretend that he is.

Your response: That is not the same as what he did with it.

NPC: No, it's not, and I do not need comforting, thank you very much. He made the choice. I made the filing. Both of those are real, only one of them is a crime, and I have to live in a Base where the second one happens every week.

Your response: So what am I supposed to do differently?

NPC: Know who is looking and at what: that is the craft, and it is yours now. But when you bring somebody the page and they file it, do not go quiet and do not go and sell it. Come back and put it on the desk again, and keep doing that until somebody finally pays attention or throws you out. There is a stealth tool coming your way, so keep training that Pistol Combat and stay somewhere you can stand being invisible. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

entries.title: Mission 3: The Quiet Door
entries.description: Ivo Mattis has been selling the Base's blind spots. End it at the CITYMERCS HQ, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: The Long Way Through
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat Ivo Mattis
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Everybody in your line of work who comes to me asks the same question first, which is how to not be seen. But that's the wrong question and it would get you killed soon. Would you like to know the right one?

Your response: Go on. What is the right question?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Who is looking, and at what. Nobody watches everything, recruit. People watch the thing they are responsible for and they are magnificently blind to everything else, and if you know which is which, you can walk through the middle of a room with nobody noticing you. Go to Corporal Vane at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Find out what it is that he watches.

Your response: A supply clerk? Really?

NPC: A supply clerk who can tell you the weight of a crate by the sound it makes on the ramp and could not tell you the color of the door it came through. That is the most useful conversation you will have for some time. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go and listen.

NPC: Depot's closed for intake until further notice. If it's not a requisition, it can wait.

Your response: It's not a requisition. What do you actually watch, Corporal?

NPC: What do I w- the stock. I watch the stock. Weight, count, seal numbers. I can tell you what is in a crate from the noise it makes coming down the ramp and I can tell you if a pallet is two units light from across the bay.

Your response: And the people carrying it?

NPC: What about them? They are hands. I do not- all right, I can see where this is going, and Jones has made this point at me before. No, I could not pick out even one man who has carried a crate through that door this year. Yes, I have been robbed twice, and both times I stood there and watched it happen and gave the provosts nothing worth writing down.

Your response: Because you were looking at the crate.

NPC: Because I was counting the crate. That's my job. Nobody has ever once asked me to look at a face, and if I started, I would miss a short pallet in no time, and somebody in the wastes would run out of ammunition because of it. So no, I do not watch people. I watch numbers, and I'm very good at it.

Your response: That is exactly what she wanted me to hear.

NPC: Then tell her she has made her point and she can stop sending people to make it. Go on, intake is in ten minutes.

NPC: Numbers. Every time. Now let me count.

NPC: Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Go and ask him what he actually looks at.

NPC: What does Corporal Vane watch?

Your response: Numbers. He knows every crate in his depot by weight and count, but he couldn't describe one person who carried one in. He has been robbed twice this year by people he looked directly at.

NPC: Twice that he knows of. It's actually been five times, and he still could not pick any of them out of a line. Now do that for every post in this Base: the gate watches faces, the armory watches badges, the medics watch bodies. Learn the shape of what each of them is not looking at, do your best to become that shape, and people will simply look past you. You will just be standing in the part of the room nobody is responsible for.

NPC: Theory is over. Time for practice. Ready for the part where it is dark and something is already in there?

Your response: Ready. Where am I going?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. The dark is patient. That is rather the point of it.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3, where the recovery sled drops what it drags in. No clean lines, no lit corridors, nothing that behaves like a room. I want you in and out of there. There are things living in there and they do not care how quiet you are, which is exactly the lesson.

Your response: So this is not a stealth exercise.

NPC: It is the other half of one. Sooner or later something sees you, and everything you know about not being seen becomes worthless in the same second. Put down eight of them and come back out. I want to know what you are like after it goes wrong.

NPC: You're still here. The wreck yard in Storage 3. Go.

NPC: So you're back, and in one piece I might add. How far did you get before something noticed you?

Your response: About a third. After that it was just work. I stopped trying to be quiet and started trying to be finished.

NPC: Good. That is how you do it. Most recruits try to do it another way, where they get all the way through untouched. Those recruits are either lying or extremely lucky, and both of those would eventually run out. Next thing to do will be both halves, all in one afternoon. Come back when you have your wind.

NPC: There is a man in this Base selling the result of what I have been trying to teach you. In?

Your response: I'm in. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not be long. He is careful, and careful men get restless.

NPC: Ivo Mattis, CityMercs HQ. He has spent quite some time mapping what every post in this Base fails to look at, and for the last few weeks he has been selling that information to whoever is buying. Not our layout, or our codes, but our blind spots. Somebody walked into the armory level last week on the strength of it.

Your response: Sounds like he is very good at the job you are teaching me.

NPC: He is the best I ever taught. Yes, it was me who taught him. And yes, I am aware of what that makes today. He will know you are there before you are close, so do not waste your afternoon trying to be invisible at a man who knows every trick in the book. Walk up to him. CityMercs HQ. Finish it.

NPC: You have been in the doorway for about five seconds. Come in properly, she taught you better than that. How do I know that? She taught me as well, and now she has taught you, and here we are.

Your response: You have been selling the Base's blind spots.

NPC: I have been selling a lot of work that nobody here would pay me for. I brought her the first survey right at the beginning. Do you know what it got me? Filed. Filed, and a note about my initiative. Every post in this Base is blind in an almost ridiculous way. I can draw that on a page. In fact, I did. But nobody upstairs wanted that page.

Your response: So you sold it to people who came in through the armory last week.

NPC: What I sold is basically a map. What anybody does with it is not my department. And before you say the word: I did not tell them about Hollis, or the sublevel, or any of the other holes this place opens on its own every other week. I only ever wrote down what was already true.

Your response: Two Mercs died on the armory level standing in a spot you drew a circle around.

NPC: Yes. They did. I know both names. I have known them every day since. They hound me every night. And do you know what I do? I keep selling.

NPC: ...

NPC: Mattis is at the CityMercs HQ and he does not sit still forever. Go.

NPC: It is done, then. Did he talk?

Your response: He said he brought you the first survey right at the beginning and it got filed. He knew the names of the two who died in that robbery, and he kept selling anyway.

NPC: He did bring me that survey. I read it, I agreed with every line, and I passed it up. It came back stamped and went in a drawer. And I let it stay in the drawer because I had eleven other things to do. So he is not lying and I do not get to pretend that he is.

Your response: That is not the same as what he did with it.

NPC: No, it's not, and I do not need comforting, thank you very much. He made the choice. I made the filing. Both of those are real, only one of them is a crime, and I have to live in a Base where the second one happens every week.

Your response: So what am I supposed to do differently?

NPC: Know who is looking and at what: that is the craft, and it is yours now. But when you bring somebody the page and they file it, do not go quiet and do not go and sell it. Come back and put it on the desk again, and keep doing that until somebody finally pays attention or throws you out. There is a stealth tool coming your way, so keep training that Pistol Combat and stay somewhere you can stand being invisible. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.
