 229        say:
 230          - "You disappoint me. Faith gives you wings, no matter if your faith is with some deity, or just with one another. These people do the most extraordinary things for each other, and nobody ever tells them so. They go out into the wastes believing they are only worth their contract rate. You do not need to bring them any enlightenment. You need to be able to sustain their trust in one another."

 492        answer:

entries.title: Mission 1: Sample Size
entries.description: Doctor Varga needs specimens and nobody else will collect them. Her sample traps are set through the Supply Depot level of MILITARY BASE SEC-1, down where the shops are - empty %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(collect_samples) of them, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 6 × Growth Sample - Line A
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. There is a woman in Sector 1 with a theory about why the vermin in this Base have got worse this year, and no data, because that would require her to be in two places at once: Collecting some of the data, and processing another part of it. You have her training and, according to your file, patience and an eye for detail. Interested?

Your response: Very. What theory is she trying to prove?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: She will tell you herself. At length, if you let her. What I want from you first is the boring half. She has sample traps set all through the Supply Depot in Sector 1, the shop level downstairs, and nobody has emptied them in months. Bring me six... umm... specimina from the different traps, and pay attention while you do it: size, condition, whether the things in them have been feeding on each other. She needs samples, and she needs somebody who can describe what they saw without decorating it.

Your response: Six traps. That's a rather small sample size, isn't it?

NPC: It is, and you should say so to her face when you get there, because it is the first sensible thing anybody has said about this. The Supply Depot, Sector 1. Go and get me six specimina and an honest description.

NPC: The Supply Depot in Sector 1, six traps, and eyes open. Go.

NPC: So. Six traps emptied. What did you actually see in them?

Your response: They are bigger than the records say and they are not fighting each other over food, which means there is more of it than there should be. Something is feeding them.

NPC: Yeah. That is very close to what Varga has been saying for quite some time now, and I want you to be careful about how pleased that makes you. You will take it to her, next. And when she tells you her theory - and she will, before you have even come to a standstill - remember that you went looking for results she already fully expected.

NPC: So. Ready to go and make a certain person's entire year?

Your response: I guess so. Where do I find her?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. She has waited so long, she can wait another few minutes.

NPC: Doctor Elin Varga, Sector 1. She was doing serious work in the City before she came out here and she has spent six months being told that the sublevel is somebody else's department. Take her the specimens and your description, in that order, and let her do the talking.

Your response: And if she is right?

NPC: Then we have a problem under this Base with a cause, which is better than a problem with a rumor. Sector 1. Go.

NPC: Whatever it is, I am in the middle of- are those from my traps? Those are from my traps! Put them down. Gently! Gently.

Your response: Six of them, out of the Sector 1 line. Mrs. Jones sent me.

NPC: Ugh, for so long I have been asking somebody to collect those samples for me. Every time I was told that vermin are - let me quote - shit, that the aforementioned shit happens, and that it wouldn't be science. Right. Talk to me. Not what you concluded, what you saw.

Your response: They are oversized against the records, and they were not competing over food.

NPC: Not competing? Not competing. That's it, that's exactly it! There is a nutrient load coming into that sector from somewhere and it has been coming in long enough to change the size distribution. Water table, most likely. A cracked waste run feeding it from underneath, and it fits every observation I have made since spring...

Your response: So you were right. What's the matter?

NPC: ...No. No, stop. Listen to what I just said. I had that answer in my head for months, and the first data anybody brings me fits it perfectly. This shouldn't make you feel reaffirmed, it should frighten you. One sector is not a result. It is an anecdote about the behavior of six-legged things, collected by somebody who was told what I was hoping for before they went out there.

Your response: But you didn't tell me. Jones didn't either.

NPC: Then you are a better lab assistant than I could have hoped for, and still, it is not enough. Get me a second set, from a different site with a different water table. If it agrees, I will write it up and put my name on it. Yours too, even, under acknowledgements. If it doesn't, I have been wrong loudly since spring and I will say that just as loudly. Because that is how science is supposed to work. Go on.

NPC: A second site. Different level. Go.

NPC: Varga is in Sector 1 and she has waited six months. Go.

NPC: Well? Was she right?

Your response: Her theory fits every one of the six. Then she took it apart in front of me and said one sector is not a result, it is an anecdote with six legs or something.

NPC: An anecdote with six legs? Right. I like her more every time somebody quotes her at me. That is *so* her: Months of being ignored and the moment somebody hands her the answer she wanted, she is the one who refuses to take it. That is what science is all about, recruit, and most people never manage it once. She will want a second set. Come back when you are ready to go and elate or disappoint her.

NPC: Ready for the second set?

Your response: Ready. Where are they?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. The first sector is already changing while we discuss it.

NPC: The Black Ribbon Bar, far side of the CityMercs HQ. Different ground, different air, different water table, and crucially, not the sector her theory was built on. She talked the Base Commander into letting her set a second line in among the tables, and by now the regulars drink around them. Five will do. Same eyes, same honesty.

Your response: And if the second set says the opposite?

NPC: Then she was wrong for months in public, and she will be the first person to say so. The important part is that this Base will finally know what is actually happening under it. Not a bad afternoon's work. CityMercs HQ, far side, the Black Ribbon Bar. Go.

NPC: The second set of traps, the Black Ribbon Bar on the far side of the CityMercs HQ. Five. Same eyes. Go.

NPC: So. Five from the second set. Did they agree with her?

Your response: Sadly, not at all. Same overgrowth, no water anywhere near it, and the things in them had been competing over food. Whatever is happening, it is not that cracked waste run.

NPC: You wanna know the funny part? Varga already expected your results. She all but withdrew her paper before dinner. As long as you can provide definitive proof, being wrong is just as valuable as being right. Now go and count the people in this Base who would have quietly not mentioned the second set. Most of them outrank her.

Your response: So the lesson isn't about the sublevel at all.

NPC: It never was. Anybody can collect the sample that agrees with them, and out here most people stop there and get promoted for it. Go and get the second set. Every time, especially when the first one made you happy: that is the whole of it, and it is the only thing that separates a scientist from somebody with a strong opinion. There is a research tool coming your way, and Varga insisted on sending that ridiculous toy thing as well. Said that it would amuse you. Keep training that Research. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

entries.title: Mission 1: Shorted
entries.description: Livia Tam has been shorting the Mercs on every crate she moves. Settle it in MILITARY BASE SEC-1, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat Livia Tam
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Everybody assumes your trade is about getting things past people. Yeah, it is not. It is about being the one person in a very long chain that nobody in the chain has a reason to cheat. I have a woman in Sector 1 who never understood that. Interested in her job?

Your response: I'm interested, alright, but what do you mean? What happened to her?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Nothing happened to her, yet. Livia Tam has moved goods for this Base for years and years, and has shorted every single crate by a little. Two units here, a case there, never enough that any one buyer would burn a working route over it. Yeah. But last month the outpost run came up short of ammunition during a contact.

Your response: So nobody caught her in years?

NPC: That is beside the point. Everybody caught her. And everybody decided it was cheaper than finding somebody new, which is exactly what she was counting on. That arithmetic ended when two of my people had to break contact and walk. So she messed up, and now she is paying the price. She is in Sector 1 and she thinks this is another conversation about percentages. Settle it.

NPC: If Jones has sent you about the outpost run, the answer is the same as it was: the manifest is the manifest and shrinkage is shrinkage.

Your response: She did, but not about that. You pinched those last few rounds that would've saved lives.

NPC: Oh yeah. And who tells you that these few rounds would've made a difference, eh? You can look it up, there was never a run with above-average losses, and I defy you to find a mover anywhere between here and the City who does better than-

Your response: You have shorted every crate for years, Livia.

NPC: And every crate arrived. Every. Single. One. In years I have never lost a load, never missed a window, never once been late, and the whole Base has been perfectly happy with the arrangement because the arrangement worked. Nobody complains about a little spillage.

Your response: Actually, they stopped being happy last month. You just didn't notice.

NPC: No, wait. Look at the numbers. Look at the actual numbers, they are right here-

NPC: ...

NPC: Livia Tam is in Sector 1, and she is not expecting anything. Go.

NPC: It is done. Did she understand why, at the end?

Your response: No. She kept explaining the percentages. Right up to the last she thought the numbers were what mattered.

NPC: The numbers never matter. She was cheaper than replacing her for years and then, in one afternoon, she was not, and she never once saw the line move because she was looking at her margin instead of at the people either side of her. Rest. And then, I will show you the part of this job that actually makes you money.

NPC: Ready to learn how goods really leave this Base?

Your response: I am. So who do I talk to?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. Nothing crosses that gate before evening anyway.

NPC: A clerk called Pell at the Military Entrance, who is the guy who decides what leaves this Base. I'm not talking about smuggling. He is the guy who decides. Every crate that goes out either has paper or has a reason, and he is the man who knows which is which. Go and cozy up to him.

Your response: And he will just show me the books, will he?

NPC: He will show you. Because I asked him to, and because he is tired. Do not try to be clever at him, and do not offer him anything. Military Entrance.

NPC: She said you were coming. Stand there, do not touch the book, and pick up whatever I tell you to.

Your response: She said you decide what leaves or enters this Base.

NPC: The paperwork decides what leaves this Base. I decide what the paperwork means, which is a different job. See that crate? Full manifest, three signatures, going nowhere. And that one, no paper at all, goes out at seven.

Your response: Why that way round?

NPC: Because the first one is signed by a man who signed four things last spring that got people killed, and the second is medical stock for an outpost that has been out for nine days and whose requisition is somewhere in a pile in the HQ. One of them is legal. The other one is right. For years, I have been picking the second one and writing the reason in the margin.

Your response: Nobody has ever pulled you up on it?

NPC: Every year somebody new arrives who wants to. Then they read the margins. Everything I have ever waved through went where it needed to be and I can show you the line for all of it, which is the only reason I am still here and not in a cell. I know why you're here - that is what your trade is. It's not about any gap. Your margin note needs to stand up years later.

Your response: And if I ever want a crate through that will not stand up?

NPC: Then you will find I am extremely stupid that evening and cannot read my own handwriting. Now let me handle that crate, it goes out at seven. Tell Jones you were useful.

NPC: Seven o'clock. It goes out on time or it doesn't go out at all.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance and the evening shift is the one worth watching. Go.

NPC: What did the man at the gate teach you?

Your response: That the paperwork is not the system at all, he is. Crates went out with nothing on them but his say-so, and every one of them was going somewhere it needed to be.

NPC: Yep. Years of it, and not one crate that went anywhere it should not have. That is what your trade actually is, recruit: a reputation so solid that nobody bothers checking your crate in the first place. Livia Tam spent four years turning that into two units a run. Come back when you are rested. There is a route to open.

NPC: Ready to earn your first honest crate?

Your response: I'm ready. Where is it going?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. The outpost run has already waited a week on Livia Tam's arithmetic.

NPC: Out to the outposts, through the wreck yard in Military Storage 3, because the surface road is watched and the yard connects to the lower service run. It is the route Pell has been holding open for years and at the moment nothing can use it, because the yard is crawling.

Your response: So the job is not moving the crate.

NPC: The job is never moving the crate. The job is that the route works, and everybody in the chain knows it will work next week, too. So whatever crawls there, eight of them, Storage 3, and then the run goes out. Go.

NPC: The wreck yard in Storage 3 is still crawling, and the run is still sitting at the gate. Go.

NPC: The run went out on time. Full count. What did the yard cost you?

Your response: Some nerves and most of my ammunition. The route is open and it will still be open next week.

NPC: It's been quite a while since a full count went off this Base. Not because of raiders or because of the wastes. Too many people decided a percent was invisible, and too many agreed with them.

Your response: And now everyone in the chain knows the route works.

NPC: Correct, and that is worth more than every crate you will ever move. You can't have a route nobody trusts. Pell has spent years being boringly, tediously reliable and it has made him the most powerful clerk in the wastes, and he could not tell you one clever thing he has ever done.

Your response: So where does the money come from?

NPC: Correct, and that is worth more than every crate you will ever move. You can't have a route nobody trusts. Pell has spent years being boringly, tediously reliable and it has made him the most powerful clerk in the wastes, and he could not tell you one clever thing he has ever done.

Your response: So where does the money come from?

NPC: From being the one nobody checks. That is the whole trade: be so consistently worth trusting that your crate goes through, while everybody else's is being opened. And you never ever spend that trust on something trivial. There is a barter CPU coming your way, so keep training that Barter and remember that the number is never what matters. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

entries.title: Mission 1: Entrance Exam
entries.description: Mrs. Jones wants MILITARY STORAGE 6 cleared out. Put down %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(clear_storage) of the bots and vermin infesting the bay, then report back to her.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 10 × Denizens of Very Easy Military Base dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have read your file. Not just the marksmanship scores, the other columns too. Most recruits here are muscle. I think you might be something more useful. Interested in finding out?

Your response: I'm interested. What did you have in mind?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Simple problem first. I like to watch how people work before I trust them with the complicated kind. Storage went hot when the maintenance units turned on us, and with the housekeeping iron offline, the whole bay has filled up. Rogue bots, and every crawling thing that slipped in behind them. It's a mess. Get into Military Storage 6 and clear it out. Ten of them, I do not much care what: bots, bugs, whatever is moving. Just make the bay quiet again.

Your response: Malfunctioning bots. Anything else I should know?

NPC: Good. Your Nav-Ray will point you to the Storage entrance from anywhere in the Base. Follow it in, clear the bay, then report back to me. Move.

NPC: The bay is still crawling. Finish the job, then report back to me.

NPC: Back in one piece, and the bay is quieter. Tell me one thing: the bots in there, how did they fight?

Your response: Not like malfunctions. Even with all that vermin around them, they moved in a pattern. Coordinated. Like something was giving the orders.

NPC: Coordinated, eh? That is what I was afraid of. Housekeeping bots do not coordinate, and they do not move like that on their own. Somebody reached into their heads. Keep working that Heavy Combat of yours while I pull a service record. You handled yourself well, but well is not good enough out here.

NPC: Ready for the part they do not teach in basic?

Your response: What did the record say?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: The last tech to service those bots signed off a diagnostic patch across the whole fleet. Six hours before they turned. His name is Corporal Vane, and he works out of the Supply Depot. Go have a word with him. Quietly.

Your response: And if he does not want to talk?

NPC: You are not there to shoot him. You are there to make him nervous enough to tell the truth. There is a difference, and you had better learn it. You will find Vane at the Supply Depot.

NPC: If this is about the maintenance backlog, take a number. I am busy.

Your response: No, it's about the patch you pushed to the housekeeping bots. The one that made them open fire.

NPC: That- that was a certified update. The authorization codes were all in order, I checked them myself-

Your response: Bots do not get certified to shoot Mercs, Corporal. Who gave it to you?

NPC: All right. A man paid me. Cash. Said it was a firmware fix. He had real Merc credentials, Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. And he knew things. Gate rotations. Patrol gaps. If he is selling the bots, that isn't all he's selling. Please, I have a family. And listen- if you worked it out, so has he. He will not sit still for this, and the entrance is the only way out of the Base.

Your response: Kessler. Jones needs to hear this.

NPC: Just leave me out of the report. Please.

NPC: We are done here. Get moving.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Vane yet. He is at the Supply Depot. Go.

NPC: You look like you came back with something. Talk.

Your response: Vane was bought. A patch that reads as certified, paid in cash by a man with real Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. Vane says that this guy's been selling more than bots: gate rotations, patrol gaps... and he thinks Kessler already knows we are onto him.

NPC: Kessler. Decorated, and lately the subject of a file I kept telling myself was nothing. Late to muster. Requisitions that did not reconcile. We had our suspicions. Selling the Base's arteries to the scrap-runners is another level entirely. I should've followed my gut. That is on me, but it will not stay that way. Keep that Heavy Combat sharp: the next part is not a conversation.

NPC: This one is not a training exercise, and I won't pretend otherwise. You in?

Your response: I'm in. Where is Kessler?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not take too long. Men like Kessler get nervous, and nervous men run.

NPC: Moving, is where. Somebody put a word in his ear the moment you leaned on Vane, and a man like Kessler does not hang around to explain his paperwork. He is making for the entrance. That is the only way out of this Base, so that is where you take him. Intercept him before he reaches the gate.

Your response: And when it turns?

NPC: When it turns, and it will turn, you do not hesitate. He has had more trigger time than you have had here, so hit first and hit hard. Go. I will be listening.

NPC: Move. I have somewhere to be and no time to discuss it.

Your response: And I'm looking for the man who gave the housekeeping bots a reason to shoot us. Oh. Found him.

NPC: So Vane squealed, huh? Should have known that coward would fold the second someone leaned on him. Anyway. I am walking out of here, and you have got about three seconds to decide not to be standing in the way.

Your response: It's over, Kessler. Stand down.

NPC: Over? Kid, I have buyers who would pay more for you than this Base pays in a year. Nothing personal. You are just standing in the wrong doorway.

NPC: ...

NPC: Kessler is still breathing and still moving. He is at the entrance, on his way out. Finish it before he is gone.

NPC: The entrance checkpoint went quiet, and nobody signed out. That tells me you are standing and he is not. Well?

Your response: Kessler will not be selling anything else. He didn't come quietly.

NPC: Yeah. They never do. You closed a leak today that I did not even realize was open. Questioned a suspect, followed the thread, put the right man in the ground. That is not jarhead work, recruit. That is the other kind.

Your response: So what happens now?

NPC: Now we talk about payment. There is a flamer coming your way - call it a field promotion. And you keep training that Heavy Combat, because a weapon like that is only as good as the hand on it. The Base has plenty of people who can pull a trigger. Very few who can work out who to point it at. I will be in touch.

Your response: I'll be ready.

NPC: I know you will. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

 143        answer:

 145            - "I'm interested. What did you have in mind?"
 146          jones_m1_later:
 147            - "Not right now. Another time?"
 148          jones_dismiss:
 149            - "I'm not interested. Leave me be."
 150

 153          - "The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25."
 154

 156        say:
 157          - "Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice."
 158        answer:
 159          jones_dismiss_confirm:
 160            - "I'm sure."

 162            - "Actually, no. I'll hear you out."

 171            - "On reflection, I'll stay."

 175          - set_flag:
 176              flag: mb_soldier

 182      jones_m1_briefing:
 183        say:
 184          - "Simple problem first. I like to watch how people work before I trust them with the complicated kind. Storage went hot when the maintenance units turned on us, and with the housekeeping iron offline, the whole bay has filled up. Rogue bots, and every crawling thing that slipped in behind them.  185        answer:
 186          jones_m1_go:
 187            - "Malfunctioning bots. Anything else I should know?"

 190        do:
 191          - offer_mission: mb_soldier.mission1
 192        say:
 193          - "Good. Your Nav-Ray will point you to the Storage entrance from anywhere in the Base. Follow it in, clear the bay, then report back to me. Move."

 199            when:
 200              objective_done:
 201                objective: clear_storage

 203

 205        say:
 206          - "The bay is still crawling. Finish the job, then report back to me."
 207        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 208  
 209      jones_m1_report:
 210        say:
 211          - "Back in one piece, and the bay is quieter. Tell me one thing: the bots in there, how did they fight?"
 212        answer:
 213          jones_m1_done:
 214            - "Not like malfunctions. Even with all that vermin around them, they moved in a pattern. Coordinated. Like something was giving the orders."
 215        resume_at: jones_m1_done
 216  
 217      jones_m1_done:
 218        do:
 219          - set_flag:
 220              flag: mb_soldier
 221              value: 1
 222          - complete_objective: report
 223        say:
 224          - "Coordinated, eh? That is what I was afraid of. Housekeeping bots do not coordinate, and they do not move like that on their own. Somebody reached into their heads.  225  
 226      jones_m2_offer:
 227        say:
 228          - "Ready for the part they do not teach in basic?"
 229        answer:
 230          jones_m2_briefing:
 231            - "What did the record say?"
 232          jones_m2_later:
 233            - "Give me a minute."
 234  
 235      jones_m2_later:
 236        say:
 237          - "I'll be here."
 238  
 239      jones_m2_briefing:
 240        say:
 241          - "The last tech to service those bots signed off a diagnostic patch across the whole fleet. Six hours before they turned. His name is Corporal Vane, and he works out of the Supply Depot. Go have a word with him. Quietly."
 242        answer:
 243          jones_m2_go:
 244            - "And if he does not want to talk?"
 245  
 246      jones_m2_go:
 247        do:
 248          - offer_mission: mb_soldier.mission2
 249        say:
 250          - "You are not there to shoot him. You are there to make him nervous enough to tell the truth. There is a difference, and you had better learn it. You will find Vane at the Supply Depot."
 251        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 252  
 253      vane_greeting:
 254        say:
 255          - "If this is about the maintenance backlog, take a number. I am busy."
 256        answer:
 257          vane_certified:
 258            - "No, it's about the patch you pushed to the housekeeping bots. The one that made them open fire."
 259  
 260      vane_certified:
 261        say:
 262          - "That- that was a certified update. The authorization codes were all in order, I checked them myself-"
 263        answer:
 264          vane_confession:
 265            - "Bots do not get certified to shoot Mercs, Corporal. Who gave it to you?"
 266  
 267      vane_confession:
 268        say:
 269          - "All right. A man paid me. Cash. Said it was a firmware fix. He had real Merc credentials, Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. And he knew things. Gate rotations. Patrol gaps. If he is selling the bots, that isn't all he's selling. Please, I have a family. And listen- if you worked it out, so has he. He will not sit still for this, and the entrance is the only way out of the Base."
 270        answer:
 271          vane_leave_me_out:
 272            - "Kessler. Jones needs to hear this."
 273  
 274      vane_leave_me_out:
 275        do:
 276          - complete_objective: question_vane
 277        say:
 278          - "Just leave me out of the report. Please."
 279        resume_at: vane_done
 280  
 281      vane_done:
 282        say:
 283          - "We are done here. Get moving."
 284  
 285      jones_m2_return:
 286        do:
 287          - goto: jones_m2_report
 288            when:
 289              objective_done:
 290                objective: question_vane
 291          - goto: jones_m2_not_done
 292  
 293      jones_m2_not_done:
 294        say:
 295          - "You haven't spoken to Vane yet. He is at the Supply Depot. Go."
 296        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 297  
 298      jones_m2_report:
 299        say:
 300          - "You look like you came back with something. Talk."
 301        answer:
 302          jones_m2_done:
 303            - "Vane was bought. A patch that reads as certified, paid in cash by a man with real Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. Vane says that this guy's been selling more than bots: gate rotations, patrol gaps... and he thinks Kessler already knows we are onto him."
 304        resume_at: jones_m2_done
 305  
 306      jones_m2_done:
 307        do:
 308          - set_flag:
 309              flag: mb_soldier
 310              value: 2
 311          - complete_objective: report
 312        say:
 313          - "Kessler. Decorated, and lately the subject of a file I kept telling myself was nothing. Late to muster. Requisitions that did not reconcile. We had our suspicions. Selling the Base's arteries to the scrap-runners is another level entirely. I should've followed my gut. That is on me, but it will not stay that way. Keep that Heavy Combat sharp: the next part is not a conversation."
 314  
 315      jones_m3_offer:
 316        say:
 317          - "This one is not a training exercise, and I won't pretend otherwise. You in?"
 318        answer:
 319          jones_m3_briefing:
 320            - "I'm in. Where is Kessler?"
 321          jones_m3_later:
 322            - "Give me a moment to gear up."
 323  
 324      jones_m3_later:
 325        say:
 326          - "Do not take too long. Men like Kessler get nervous, and nervous men run."
 327  
 328      jones_m3_briefing:
 329        say:
 330          - "Moving, is where. Somebody put a word in his ear the moment you leaned on Vane, and a man like Kessler does not hang around to explain his paperwork. He is making for the entrance. That is the only way out of this Base, so that is where you take him. Intercept him before he reaches the gate."
 331        answer:
 332          jones_m3_go:
 333            - "And when it turns?"
 334  
 335      jones_m3_go:
 336        do:
 337          - offer_mission: mb_soldier.mission3
 338        say:
 339          - "When it turns, and it will turn, you do not hesitate. He has had more trigger time than you have had here, so hit first and hit hard. Go. I will be listening."
 340        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 341  
 342      kessler_greeting:
 343        say:
 344          - "Move. I have somewhere to be and no time to discuss it."
 345        answer:
 346          kessler_vane_squealed:
 347            - "And I'm looking for the man who gave the housekeeping bots a reason to shoot us. Oh. Found him."
 348  
 349      kessler_vane_squealed:
 350        say:
 351          - "So Vane squealed, huh? Should have known that coward would fold the second someone leaned on him. Anyway. I am walking out of here, and you have got about three seconds to decide not to be standing in the way."
 352        answer:
 353          kessler_attack:
 354            - "It's over, Kessler. Stand down."
 355  
 356      kessler_attack:
 357        do:
 358          - attack
 359        say:
 360          - "Over? Kid, I have buyers who would pay more for you than this Base pays in a year. Nothing personal. You are just standing in the wrong doorway."
 361        resume_at: kessler_silent
 362  
 363      kessler_silent:
 364        say:
 365          - "..."
 366  
 367      jones_m3_return:
 368        do:
 369          - goto: jones_m3_report
 370            when:
 371              objective_done:
 372                objective: eliminate_kessler
 373          - goto: jones_m3_not_done
 374  
 375      jones_m3_not_done:
 376        say:
 377          - "Kessler is still breathing and still moving. He is at the entrance, on his way out. Finish it before he is gone."
 378        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 379  
 380      jones_m3_report:
 381        say:
 382          - "The entrance checkpoint went quiet, and nobody signed out. That tells me you are standing and he is not. Well?"
 383        answer:
 384          jones_m3_debrief:
 385            - "Kessler will not be selling anything else. He didn't come quietly."
 386        resume_at: jones_m3_debrief
 387  
 388      jones_m3_debrief:
 389        say:
 390          - "Yeah. They never do. You closed a leak today that I did not even realize was open. Questioned a suspect, followed the thread, put the right man in the ground. That is not jarhead work, recruit. That is the other kind."
 391        answer:
 392          jones_m3_payment:
 393            - "So what happens now?"
 394  
 395      jones_m3_payment:
 396        say:
 397          - "Now we talk about payment. There is a flamer coming your way - call it a field promotion. And you keep training that Heavy Combat, because a weapon like that is only as good as the hand on it. The Base has plenty of people who can pull a trigger. Very few who can work out who to point it at. I will be in touch."
 398        answer:
 399          jones_m3_done:
 400            - "I'll be ready."
 401  
 402      jones_m3_done:
 403        do:
 404          - set_flag:
 405              flag: mb_soldier
 406              value: 3
 407          - give_item:
 408              item: 8620
 409              quality: 150
 410              slots: 2
 411          - complete_objective: report
 412          - remove
 413        say:
 414          - "I know you will. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs."

 112          - goto: jones_m2_offer
 113            when:
 114              completed: mb_soldier.mission1
 115          - goto: jones_m1_return
 116            when:
 117              active: mb_soldier.mission1
 118          - goto: jones_m1_offer
 119  
 120      jones_not_available:
 121        say:
 122          - "You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense."
 123  
 124      jones_over_qualified:
 125        say:
 126          - "You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?"
 127        answer:
 128          jones_leave_over_qualified:
 129            - "Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones."
 130  
 131      jones_leave_over_qualified:
 132        do:
 133          - set_flag:
 134              flag: mb_soldier
 135              value: 3
 136          - remove
 137        say:
 138          - "Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there."
 139  
 140      jones_m1_offer:
 141        say:
 142          - "Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have read your file. Not just the marksmanship scores, the other columns too. Most recruits here are muscle. I think you might be something more useful. Interested in finding out?"
 143        answer:
 144          jones_m1_briefing:
 145            - "I'm interested. What did you have in mind?"
 146          jones_m1_later:
 147            - "Not right now. Another time?"
 148          jones_dismiss:
 149            - "I'm not interested. Leave me be."
 150  
 151      jones_m1_later:
 152        say:
 153          - "The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25."
 154  
 155      jones_dismiss:
 156        say:
 157          - "Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice."
 158        answer:
 159          jones_dismiss_confirm:
 160            - "I'm sure."
 161          start:
 162            - "Actually, no. I'll hear you out."
 163  
 164      jones_dismiss_confirm:
 165        say:
 166          - "Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good."
 167        answer:
 168          jones_leave:
 169            - "I have thought about it. Goodbye."
 170          start:
 171            - "On reflection, I'll stay."
 172  
 173      jones_leave:
 174        do:
 175          - set_flag:
 176              flag: mb_soldier
 177              value: 3
 178          - remove
 179        say:
 180          - "Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there."
 181  
 182      jones_m1_briefing:
 183        say:
 184          - "Simple problem first. I like to watch how people work before I trust them with the complicated kind. Storage went hot when the maintenance units turned on us, and with the housekeeping iron offline, the whole bay has filled up. Rogue bots, and every crawling thing that slipped in behind them. It's a mess. Get into Military Storage 6 and clear it out. Ten of them, I do not much care what: bots, bugs, whatever is moving. Just make the bay quiet again."
 185        answer:
 186          jones_m1_go:
 187            - "Malfunctioning bots. Anything else I should know?"
 188  
 189      jones_m1_go:
 190        do:
 191          - offer_mission: mb_soldier.mission1
 192        say:
 193          - "Good. Your Nav-Ray will point you to the Storage entrance from anywhere in the Base. Follow it in, clear the bay, then report back to me. Move."
 194        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 195  
 196      jones_m1_return:
 197        do:
 198          - goto: jones_m1_report
 199            when:
 200              objective_done:
 201                objective: clear_storage
 202          - goto: jones_m1_not_done
 203  
 204      jones_m1_not_done:
 205        say:
 206          - "The bay is still crawling. Finish the job, then report back to me."
 207        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 208  
 209      jones_m1_report:
 210        say:
 211          - "Back in one piece, and the bay is quieter. Tell me one thing: the bots in there, how did they fight?"
 212        answer:
 213          jones_m1_done:
 214            - "Not like malfunctions. Even with all that vermin around them, they moved in a pattern. Coordinated. Like something was giving the orders."
 215        resume_at: jones_m1_done
 216  
 217      jones_m1_done:
 218        do:
 219          - set_flag:
 220              flag: mb_soldier
 221              value: 1
 222          - complete_objective: report
 223        say:
 224          - "Coordinated, eh? That is what I was afraid of. Housekeeping bots do not coordinate, and they do not move like that on their own. Somebody reached into their heads. Keep working that Heavy Combat of yours while I pull a service record. You handled yourself well, but well is not good enough out here."
 225  
 226      jones_m2_offer:
 227        say:
 228          - "Ready for the part they do not teach in basic?"
 229        answer:
 230          jones_m2_briefing:
 231            - "What did the record say?"
 232          jones_m2_later:
 233            - "Give me a minute."
 234  
 235      jones_m2_later:
 236        say:
 237          - "I'll be here."
 238  
 239      jones_m2_briefing:
 240        say:
 241          - "The last tech to service those bots signed off a diagnostic patch across the whole fleet. Six hours before they turned. His name is Corporal Vane, and he works out of the Supply Depot. Go have a word with him. Quietly."
 242        answer:
 243          jones_m2_go:
 244            - "And if he does not want to talk?"
 245  
 246      jones_m2_go:
 247        do:
 248          - offer_mission: mb_soldier.mission2
 249        say:
 250          - "You are not there to shoot him. You are there to make him nervous enough to tell the truth. There is a difference, and you had better learn it. You will find Vane at the Supply Depot."
 251        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 252  
 253      vane_greeting:
 254        say:
 255          - "If this is about the maintenance backlog, take a number. I am busy."
 256        answer:
 257          vane_certified:
 258            - "No, it's about the patch you pushed to the housekeeping bots. The one that made them open fire."
 259  
 260      vane_certified:
 261        say:
 262          - "That- that was a certified update. The authorization codes were all in order, I checked them myself-"
 263        answer:
 264          vane_confession:
 265            - "Bots do not get certified to shoot Mercs, Corporal. Who gave it to you?"
 266  
 267      vane_confession:
 268        say:
 269          - "All right. A man paid me. Cash. Said it was a firmware fix. He had real Merc credentials, Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. And he knew things. Gate rotations. Patrol gaps. If he is selling the bots, that isn't all he's selling. Please, I have a family. And listen- if you worked it out, so has he. He will not sit still for this, and the entrance is the only way out of the Base."
 270        answer:
 271          vane_leave_me_out:
 272            - "Kessler. Jones needs to hear this."
 273  
 274      vane_leave_me_out:
 275        do:
 276          - complete_objective: question_vane
 277        say:
 278          - "Just leave me out of the report. Please."
 279        resume_at: vane_done
 280  
 281      vane_done:
 282        say:
 283          - "We are done here. Get moving."
 284  
 285      jones_m2_return:
 286        do:
 287          - goto: jones_m2_report
 288            when:
 289              objective_done:
 290                objective: question_vane
 291          - goto: jones_m2_not_done
 292  
 293      jones_m2_not_done:
 294        say:
 295          - "You haven't spoken to Vane yet. He is at the Supply Depot. Go."
 296        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 297  
 298      jones_m2_report:
 299        say:
 300          - "You look like you came back with something. Talk."
 301        answer:
 302          jones_m2_done:
 303            - "Vane was bought. A patch that reads as certified, paid in cash by a man with real Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. Vane says that this guy's been selling more than bots: gate rotations, patrol gaps... and he thinks Kessler already knows we are onto him."
 304        resume_at: jones_m2_done
 305  
 306      jones_m2_done:
 307        do:
 308          - set_flag:
 309              flag: mb_soldier
 310              value: 2
 311          - complete_objective: report
 312        say:
 313          - "Kessler. Decorated, and lately the subject of a file I kept telling myself was nothing. Late to muster. Requisitions that did not reconcile. We had our suspicions. Selling the Base's arteries to the scrap-runners is another level entirely. I should've followed my gut. That is on me, but it will not stay that way. Keep that Heavy Combat sharp: the next part is not a conversation."
 314  
 315      jones_m3_offer:
 316        say:
 317          - "This one is not a training exercise, and I won't pretend otherwise. You in?"
 318        answer:
 319          jones_m3_briefing:
 320            - "I'm in. Where is Kessler?"
 321          jones_m3_later:
 322            - "Give me a moment to gear up."
 323  
 324      jones_m3_later:
 325        say:
 326          - "Do not take too long. Men like Kessler get nervous, and nervous men run."
 327  
 328      jones_m3_briefing:
 329        say:
 330          - "Moving, is where. Somebody put a word in his ear the moment you leaned on Vane, and a man like Kessler does not hang around to explain his paperwork. He is making for the entrance. That is the only way out of this Base, so that is where you take him. Intercept him before he reaches the gate."
 331        answer:
 332          jones_m3_go:
 333            - "And when it turns?"
 334  
 335      jones_m3_go:
 336        do:
 337          - offer_mission: mb_soldier.mission3
 338        say:
 339          - "When it turns, and it will turn, you do not hesitate. He has had more trigger time than you have had here, so hit first and hit hard. Go. I will be listening."
 340        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 341  
 342      kessler_greeting:
 343        say:
 344          - "Move. I have somewhere to be and no time to discuss it."
 345        answer:
 346          kessler_vane_squealed:
 347            - "And I'm looking for the man who gave the housekeeping bots a reason to shoot us. Oh. Found him."
 348  
 349      kessler_vane_squealed:
 350        say:
 351          - "So Vane squealed, huh? Should have known that coward would fold the second someone leaned on him. Anyway. I am walking out of here, and you have got about three seconds to decide not to be standing in the way."
 352        answer:
 353          kessler_attack:
 354            - "It's over, Kessler. Stand down."
 355  
 356      kessler_attack:
 357        do:
 358          - attack
 359        say:
 360          - "Over? Kid, I have buyers who would pay more for you than this Base pays in a year. Nothing personal. You are just standing in the wrong doorway."
 361        resume_at: kessler_silent
 362  
 363      kessler_silent:
 364        say:
 365          - "..."
 366  
 367      jones_m3_return:
 368        do:
 369          - goto: jones_m3_report
 370            when:
 371              objective_done:
 372                objective: eliminate_kessler
 373          - goto: jones_m3_not_done
 374  
 375      jones_m3_not_done:
 376        say:
 377          - "Kessler is still breathing and still moving. He is at the entrance, on his way out. Finish it before he is gone."
 378        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 379  
 380      jones_m3_report:
 381        say:
 382          - "The entrance checkpoint went quiet, and nobody signed out. That tells me you are standing and he is not. Well?"
 383        answer:
 384          jones_m3_debrief:
 385            - "Kessler will not be selling anything else. He didn't come quietly."
 386        resume_at: jones_m3_debrief
 387  
 388      jones_m3_debrief:
 389        say:
 390          - "Yeah. They never do. You closed a leak today that I did not even realize was open. Questioned a suspect, followed the thread, put the right man in the ground. That is not jarhead work, recruit. That is the other kind."
 391        answer:
 392          jones_m3_payment:
 393            - "So what happens now?"
 394  
 395      jones_m3_payment:
 396        say:
 397          - "Now we talk about payment. There is a flamer coming your way - call it a field promotion. And you keep training that Heavy Combat, because a weapon like that is only as good as the hand on it. The Base has plenty of people who can pull a trigger. Very few who can work out who to point it at. I will be in touch."
 398        answer:
 399          jones_m3_done:
 400            - "I'll be ready."
 401  
 402      jones_m3_done:
 403        do:
 404          - set_flag:
 405              flag: mb_soldier
 406              value: 3
 407          - give_item:
 408              item: 8620
 409              quality: 150
 410              slots: 2
 411          - complete_objective: report
 412          - remove
 413        say:
 414          - "I know you will. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs."

entries.title: Mission 1: The Rifle Construction Kit
entries.description: Mr. Jones wants you to pick up a rifle from Joe Montana in the Smugglers Cave (PEPPER SEC-3).
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Joe Montana
• Talk to Mr. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself. Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

NPC: Ah... nice to see you. Great. Could you spare a moment? I have something that might interest you. And it is a little urgent, if you catch my drift.

Your response: I'm very sorry. I don't have time for you right now.

Your response: What do you want, Mr. Jones?

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself. Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

NPC: Well, this is my concern: I am appointed to do a little job for our faction and I require the proper... tools for the job. You're supposed to help me acquire these tools, since I have other matters to attend.

Your response: And what exactly are we talking about here?

NPC: You will get to know that soon enough. At the moment, I would be grateful if you could go to %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7101). He is at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(1575). Use your Nav-Ray to get there.

Your response: And what am I supposed to tell %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7101)?

NPC: Just tell him that I sent you and that the canaries sang too much again. He will know what's the deal and hand you the tools I need.

Your response: Okay. %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7101) at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(1575) - noted. See you later.

NPC: Good luck.

NPC: Who are you and what do you want from me?

Your response: My name is of no importance. Jones sent me. I'm supposed to tell you that the canaries sang too much again.

NPC: Allright then. Tell him that things are getting way too big for me. I don't want to get involved into this any further. If Jones needs an unmarked gun again, tell him he should either look for someone else or pay me much more moolah.

Your response: A gun..? ...uh... yes... sure. - I'll tell him

NPC: Good. And now, get lost.

NPC: Didn't I tell you to get lost?

NPC: You do not have the kit with you. Come back when you have completed your task successfully.

NPC: Back I see - that was quick. I knew we decided on the right person. Did you fetch me what I need?

Your response: Yes, I have the gun right here in this briefcase...

NPC: Great, great. Um... but how do you know there's a gun in the briefcase?

Your response: Well, %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7101) doesn't talk too much, but he really seems to say too much.

NPC: Apparently. It seems to be the time to look for somebody else I can trust better.

Your response: Oh yes. He said, that things would get too big for him and he wants double his usual fee next time.

NPC: Bastard. The list of people I need to... deal with just seems to get longer and longer.

Your response: Maybe I could help you out?

NPC: I'm sure you could. If I may say so, though: train your Rifle Combat skill - you will surely need it later.

NPC: Back again, I see. Marvelous. As if you could read my mind. I have work for you. You're supposed to do some laundry. Unfortunately, this time, it's a bit dirty. Understand?

Your response: At the moment, all my time is consumed by my own laundry.

Your response: Yes, I do understand. So who is this about?

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great. You remember the gun you fetched for me? I will give it back to you. Just for your own protection, of course. There is a tiny problem I wanted to solve. Unfortunately, some problems cause other bigger problems. As in this case.

Your response: Get to the point...

NPC: We had to get rid of a former co-worker of our faction. Unfortunately, there has been a witness - his name is Mike Carson. And witnesses have this unfortunate habit to talk. So we need to make sure that he will not be able to talk anymore. The man is hiding now though, and we have not yet been able to seek him out.

Your response: And how am I supposed to find him?

NPC: If you would just let me finish. Money can open many doors, and we have lots of money. Luckily for us, people are corrupt. One of Mike Carsons Bodyguards has agreed to give us his current location, if we pay him enough for it.

Your response: And now I am supposed to get that information, right?

NPC: Exactly. And about that payment... use your discretion... hehehe...

Your response: Got that. Where do I find him?

NPC: He goes under the name %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7102) and he is currently at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(5).

NPC: Can I help you?

Your response: Oh yes, I'm sure you can. You are %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7102), right?

NPC: Oh... you are Mr. Jones' contact, I assume? Allright, no sense delaying the inevitable. My client uses the codename %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7103). He changes his location every other day, and has multiple bodyguards doing different shifts.

Your response: But the deal was that you tell me his location, not his codename.

NPC: It doesn't matter. I just don't know his location. But his codename never changes, and your employer will have the necessary resources to find out where he is located.

Your response: I certainly hope that, because he will not be able to send me to you ask you again.

NPC: What... why are you carrying a gun... the deal included... son of a bitch!!!

NPC: Come back when you are finished.

NPC: Nice to see you again. Is that blood on your jacket? Hmmm... I hope you were thorough, at least.

Your response: As thorough as the situation warranted.

NPC: Great - that's how I like it. So, where is Carson hiding?

Your response: I don't know. My contact only knew the codename that he uses now.

NPC: Then you did the right thing by eliminating him. I loathe people who fail to keep meet end of a bargain. Whatever - just tell me what Carsons codename is.

Your response: His new name is %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7103).

NPC: Thanks, it shouldn't take me too long to find out where he is. Now, if you would be so kind to give me back the gun I gave you. Only for your own protection - of course.

Your response: Too bad, I just started to get used to this baby.

NPC: Don't worry, I'll get back to you as soon as I know where %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7103) is. Until then, keep training your Rifle Combat skill. Your next task might not be that easy.

NPC: There you are again. Sooner than expected, but not too soon. Are you ready to help out your faction a little?

Your response: At the moment, I have a few other matters to attend.

Your response: I think I already know what this could be. I'm ready.

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Superb. I knew I could count on you. We could locate %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7103) without too many problems. Your objective in this mission should be well clear by now.

Your response: Of course. Where do I find him?

NPC: %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7103) is at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(1579). I am asking for your discretion. We do not need another witness. That means you should eliminate his bodyguards, too.

Your response: No problem.

NPC: I'm really starting to like you. You might soon go all the way to the top. Trust me. Here, better take that sniper rifle again. It served you well the last time, didn't it? Good luck.

NPC: Now you die!

NPC: Come back when you are finished.

NPC: Carson alias %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7103) is history, yes? Nice work - you are really dependable in such matters. I'm glad that this is finally over.

Your response: It was easy pickings...

NPC: No need to be humble. You did a great job. Unfortunately, other matters call for my attention. You were worth everything, and I do not want to leave that unrewarded. Here - take the gun. I cleared it for permanent usage and you can keep it.

Your response: Thanks, I will put it to good use.

NPC: I'm sure about that. We will surely meet again sometime. Keep training your Rifle Combat Skill, and soon, you will be one of the best. Till then: good luck. Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

entries.title: Mission 1: Help a friend
entries.description: Daniel Fong-Sai is being threatened. Go to PEPPER SEC-1 and make sure nothing happens to him. %SHOWONTARGETSUCCESS(2, Bring the sword to Mr. Jones.)
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Daniel Fong-Sai
• Defeat 3 × Thug
• Talk to Daniel Fong-Sai
• Collect Broken Tsurugaoka-Sword
• Talk to Mr. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself. Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

NPC: Nice to see you. Can you spare some time and do a little work for me? It would be very important to me, and time is short. And even if you are pretty new to our faction, you seem to be the right person for the job.

Your response: Right now, I have other matters to attend.

Your response: Sure, just tell me what you want, and I'll do it.

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself. Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

NPC: Great. Okay, this is the problem. And old friend of mine got me something that is not easy to acquire. I am a little worried about him though. It is not something you can get the legal way and I have lost contact to him days ago.

Your response: And you want me to check if everything is okay?

NPC: Yes, that would be great. I've known him for a long time, and he has always been reliable. I'm afraid he could be in trouble.

Your response: Okay, I will see what I can do.

NPC: His name is %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7111) and he should currently be at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(5). He is asian, so you should be able to identify him when you see him. I think you should equip yourself with a weapon first, in case there is trouble.

NPC: Are you with them? Look, I told you, you cannot have it!

Your response: Jones sent me.

NPC: Ah, that's one reliable guy. I was able to find the Tsurugaoka-Sword, but its blade is broken. Like that stops the bastards trying to take it from me... they have been trailing me for days now.

Your response: You are being followed?

NPC: Followed my ass. These guys aren't playing. I am a trader, not a fighter. Not my domain, know what I'm saying? ...oh shit... Over there. Looks like they'll never give up! You better help me, or the sword will be gone and Jones can scratch one friend!

NPC: There are more of them!!! Help me!!!

NPC: I think Jones sent the right guy... hahaha... We sure showed them!

Your response: That was easy...

NPC: Maybe for you. But this is getting too big for me. Please take the Tsurugaoka-Sword. You're going back to Jones anyway and I don't want to keep taking this risk for a walk.

Your response: I can understand that. I will give it to him.

NPC: Thanks, one huge stone off my chest. It is much safer with you. Send Jones my best greetings and tell him that I still owe him a Sake or two.

NPC: Why are you still here? I already gave you the sword!

NPC: Your job is not done yet.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Did you find %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7111)? Is he okay?

Your response: He's fine. He hopes that you will be able to visit him soon.

NPC: Great. But what was that delay about? Did he even have what I wanted from him?

Your response: He gave me a sword for you. And the reason for the delay was, that some other people wanted to have it too, but I took care of those.

NPC: I figured as much. Where is it? ...but... but it is broken..!

Your response: Yes, I believe he is sorry about that, but there is little to be done about it now.

NPC: Yes... nothing can be done about it... thanks. I guess I will have to look around if I can find someone, who can fix this baby. I will get back to you, you did your job very well. Until then, you should keep training your Melee Combat skill. Nothing went wrong this time, but when you face stronger opponents, you should be ready.

Your response: Thanks for the tip... I'll keep that in mind.

NPC: Good, see you later.

NPC: Ah, right time, right place. I like that. Can you spare some time and do another little job for me?

Your response: Not at the moment, sorry.

Your response: I have enough free time. Shoot.

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great. Remember the sword you fetched for me?

Your response: Yes, the broken blade.

NPC: Exactly... and I aim to change that. I found a blacksmith with the necessary skills to repair such a blade. But believe me - such people are rare now and ask for loads of money.

Your response: Okay... Am I supposed to do errands now to get some money?

NPC: Oh whatever gave you that idea? No, of course not. We already agreed on a price and I paid him. All you need to do is bring him the sword, get it back and bring it to me. Simple as that.

Your response: If it is necessary. Who is this blacksmith and where do I find him?

NPC: His name is %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7113) and he is at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(1555). Good luck and see you later.

NPC: Jones sent you. You bring the Tsurugaoka-Sword.

Your response: Um... yes, that's right. But how do you know that?

NPC: I know many things. And I see many things others cannot see.

Your response: Then I'm sure you see that I'm short on time, right?

NPC: I see impatience. But I will not provoke you. Show me the blade.

Your response: There you go - this is it.

NPC: Oh... indeed. Beautiful. But it isn't just broken, it is splinted. I have to replace some parts.

Your response: Go ahead...

NPC: It's not that easy. I need Shin-Metal. You need to fetch me some.

Your response: It keeps getting better. Where should I get something I have never heard of before?

NPC: %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7114)... He is at %NPC_WORLDFROMID(1575) - He will give you some, when you tell him that I sent you.

Your response: I guess I will be on my way then, so we can get this over with.

NPC: Hurry up. I have other things to do.

NPC: Washap?

Your response: %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7113) sent me... I'm supposed to get Shin-Metal from you.

NPC: Shin-Mefal? Whussat s'posed tah be?

Your response: How am I supposed to know? You are the seller!

NPC: Whaddaya knee id for?

Your response: To repair a blade.

NPC: Oh I shee... that inshane Blackshmish! Uhkay now I know whayou wonz. Shat guy ish jush buying ol' scrap jung of meh.

Your response: Yes, whatever, do you have some now?

NPC: Of coursh... I alwaysh do. Jush Jung. Here, take. 'Sh yoursh, why would ah needid.

Your response: Wow... thanks, I guess.

NPC: No problem, %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7113) paysh me well ushully.

NPC: Whut more you wonz? I haff notheng mor'.

NPC: You do not have the Shin-Metal yet. Go to %NPC_NAMEFROMID(7114) in the %NPC_WORLDFROMID(1575) and then come back to me!

NPC: You have the Shin-Metal.

Your response: Ever thought about the fact that people who know that you know what they are gonna say do not give two shits about your smart-ass comments?

NPC: I knew you would say that. Now give it to me.

Your response: Well, if you ask THAT politely...

NPC: Good. Go - Come back when I'm done.

NPC: The blade isn't finished yet. Come back later.

NPC: The blade is finished.

Your response: Good, I want this to be finally over. Now if you would kindly hand it to me...

NPC: I'm afraid I can't do that.

Your response: W... what? What's that supposed to mean?

NPC: That's supposed to mean that I will not give it to you. This blade is way too nice of a piece. I will not give it away again.

Your response: Have you lost your marbles? Give me the blade, or you will be in a lot of trouble with Jones!

NPC: No, I will not be in trouble with Jones. I will tell him that you took the Tsurugaoka-Sword and took off. He will come to think that you ran away with it.

Your response: Since you always have the answer to anything, explain to me how you plan on stopping me from telling him the real story of your double-cross?

NPC: I will stop you by killing you...

NPC: (The cabinet won't open.)

NPC: (The cabinet opens. You have taken the sword.)

NPC: (The cabinet is empty.)

NPC: Your job isn't done yet!

NPC: Great, here you are again. What took you so long?

Your response: Oh, maybe that I needed to crawl to some slobbering bum in his dark cave to find the necessary metal for the repair. Or that I needed to off your crazy-ass blacksmith because he was sure keen on keeping that blade after he was done with it.

NPC: Oh...

Your response: Yup! Oh!

NPC: I'm sorry that this job took you that much work. But you do have the sword, right?

Your response: Of course I do. Here - take it.

NPC: No, you don't. Go back and get it. He must've hidden it in his apartment.

NPC: Hmmm... marvelous. Unfortunately you can see where it broke. Inevitable I guess. I still owe you my gratitude. You did your job very well. You will surely have learned a lot. Remember to keep training your Melee Combat skill, and you will be very strong in no time.

Your response: What did you think I am doing all the time. Still, thanks.

NPC: I will soon have another job for you. Until then, good luck out there.

NPC: Oh thank god, you're here. I think these bastards followed me.

Your response: Who followed you?

NPC: I don't know. I was with my old friend who gave you the broken blade. Do you remember..?

Your response: Vividly, so? Why are you being followed now?

NPC: He brought me a new Tsurugaoka-Sword. I couldn't get close to the one with the break marks. But now the same goons who have been trying to take the other sword from him seem to follow me now.

Your response: And now you brought these people right here?!? How about collecting something less dangerous? Explosives, poisonous animals or rare viruses maybe?

NPC: Do not mock me. Oh god... I think I heard footsteps. Protect me, I beg you!

NPC: They aren't dead yet!! Attack, dammit!!

NPC: Whew... that was close... I owe you my life. I will never forget that.

Your response: These guys weren't so tough...

NPC: No, you really did great. Take this sword - I have another one now. You seem to know perfectly well how to handle it.

Your response: Wow... thank you... so the entire effort DID pay off for me in the end.

NPC: I'm sorry I cannot give you anything else right now. I gotta take my leave now and go somewhere, where those goons cannot find me. I need to think on how to wipe out this gang.

Your response: Best of luck in that.

NPC: And best of luck to you. I am sure we will meet again. Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!
