entries.title: Mission 2: A Friendly Ear
entries.description: Buy Wren Halasz a drink in the bar in the CANYON FACILITY and listen to what she says about the regulars, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Pest Control
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Wren Halasz
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Now, what am I supposed to make of you? The City would have us believe that killers do it for a fee. I am looking for people who do it for a cause. So I wonder: Which are you?

Your response: I joined the cause, not the mercs, didn't I?

Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: I don't. Please go away.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: That says much less than you think it does. But no matter. We're gonna find out together, anyway. And step one is to see how you work where nobody is watching: In a dark cave. Canyon Cave 2, to be exact. Put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. It's the honest test of a killer.

Your response: Killing vermin in a cave tests my skills as a killer? What do you expect to gain by watching me do that?

NPC: I didn't say anything about your skills. And neither will I be watching you do it. What I will be watching, though, is your attitude about it, and how you behave once you're back. So get going. Canyon Cave 2, eight creepy crawlies.

NPC: Do you honestly want me to report that you came back before the task was finished? Get going!

NPC: So, tell me, honestly: Were you bothered at all by killing those beasts?

Your response: Why would I be bothered by exterminating some pests?

NPC: This is the correct attitude towards a cave full of pests. And it would be the entirely wrong attitude about a person. The difference between those two will determine how good you are at your job. The City will send its goons to kill anyone without ever thinking twice about it. As soon as we do the same, we become just like them. Get back to me soon.

NPC: Last time, I asked you to exterminate a cave full of pests. Wanna learn how the movement picks its targets?

Your response: I'm especially interested in who does the picking.

Your response: Yes, but... hang on.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: There's a regular in our bar. Wren Halasz is the name, drinks in there pretty much every evening, talks a lot and listens a lot. Knows all the regulars on a first name basis, and also knows which ones of them have quietly made their peace with the City. Something the movement calls various things, from collaboration to treason. Not a definition anyone in that bar got to vote on.

Your response: What exactly do you mean? Do the drinkers in there know they are being sorted?

NPC: Of course they don't, that's the whole point. Neither does Halasz, for that matter, and we'd like you to keep it that way. Just buy a round, and listen to what is being said.

NPC: Yes? I am trying to enjoy my beer, thank you very much. But I assume you want something from me.

Your response: Not really. Jones told me that you could use a friendly ear. Let me buy you a drink.

NPC: Jones? Oh, alright, I like her, so I'll like you, especially if you're buyin'. Let me tell you about this bar, and the people walking in and especially out of here. Those who walk out, who still believe in anything, and those- well, those who don't.

Your response: You can tell the difference, simply by watching how they walk out of here?

NPC: If they can still walk, that is. There are those that never complain, and always have something to sell, you know, under the table. Take Tomas, for example. Tomas Bierko. He's quite decent to people, never complains about anything. I'll be damned if he actually believes anything. Those who believe are the ones with loud opinions or spectacular breakdowns. He'd never show either.

Your response: Let's be honest, here. You do realize what just happened, don't you? Why I am here, and what is gonna happen now?

NPC: Please. I am not dense. Of course I know. Doesn't mean that I want to know, or that I am proud of it. Just... don't do it right in front of me, okay?

NPC: (Wren makes a very conscious effort not to notice you again.)

NPC: Wren Halasz in our bar. Don't make me ask again.

NPC: Which name did she land on?

Your response: Tomas Bierko. Really nice guy, apparently. Never complains, gets on well with everybody.

NPC: Bierko. Yeah, I know him. He moves goods here from the City, and does well doing it. His smuggling means that the people he feeds would rather keep him. Getting rid of him would cost us dearly. But leaving him be would incur an even greater cost, an ideological one. And that is a price we can't afford. His fate is decided. Get back to me, and you're gonna seal it.

NPC: I'm not gonna beat around the bush, not gonna soften it for you. This is not a cave full of vermin, but a person, in a room full of people who like him. Are you up to the task?

Your response: If that is what it takes.

Your response: I'll need to think about that, if I'm honest.

NPC: That's a good sign. I won't accept such a task being done half-heartedly. You need to believe.

NPC: Bierko is sitting in the same bar Wren Halasz sits in. Do it right there, do not take him to some back alley. The movement does not hide what it decides.

NPC: What do you think is gonna happen? They're gonna hate you for it, for a while. Especially Wren. But they're gonna turn back to their drinks. That is the cost you will have to pay for your conviction. No sense in me sugar-coating it.

NPC: I see. You want to know what I think? What I did means that people around here stay fed who would otherwise go hungry. Yes, I'm being paid by the City, and I use this money to help the people around here. So tell me: Who exactly have I betrayed?

Your response: I have no answer for you. All I can tell you is that your fate has been decided.

NPC: Right. At least you're being honest about it. Can you say the same about the people who sent you?

NPC: ...

entries.title: Mission 3: In Front of Everyone
entries.description: The movement has ruled on Tomas Bierko, who trades with the City. Carry it out in the bar in the CANYON FACILITY, where everyone can see, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: A Friendly Ear
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat Tomas Bierko
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Now, what am I supposed to make of you? The City would have us believe that killers do it for a fee. I am looking for people who do it for a cause. So I wonder: Which are you?

Your response: I joined the cause, not the mercs, didn't I?

Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: I don't. Please go away.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: That says much less than you think it does. But no matter. We're gonna find out together, anyway. And step one is to see how you work where nobody is watching: In a dark cave. Canyon Cave 2, to be exact. Put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. It's the honest test of a killer.

Your response: Killing vermin in a cave tests my skills as a killer? What do you expect to gain by watching me do that?

NPC: I didn't say anything about your skills. And neither will I be watching you do it. What I will be watching, though, is your attitude about it, and how you behave once you're back. So get going. Canyon Cave 2, eight creepy crawlies.

NPC: Do you honestly want me to report that you came back before the task was finished? Get going!

NPC: So, tell me, honestly: Were you bothered at all by killing those beasts?

Your response: Why would I be bothered by exterminating some pests?

NPC: This is the correct attitude towards a cave full of pests. And it would be the entirely wrong attitude about a person. The difference between those two will determine how good you are at your job. The City will send its goons to kill anyone without ever thinking twice about it. As soon as we do the same, we become just like them. Get back to me soon.

NPC: Last time, I asked you to exterminate a cave full of pests. Wanna learn how the movement picks its targets?

Your response: I'm especially interested in who does the picking.

Your response: Yes, but... hang on.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: There's a regular in our bar. Wren Halasz is the name, drinks in there pretty much every evening, talks a lot and listens a lot. Knows all the regulars on a first name basis, and also knows which ones of them have quietly made their peace with the City. Something the movement calls various things, from collaboration to treason. Not a definition anyone in that bar got to vote on.

Your response: What exactly do you mean? Do the drinkers in there know they are being sorted?

NPC: Of course they don't, that's the whole point. Neither does Halasz, for that matter, and we'd like you to keep it that way. Just buy a round, and listen to what is being said.

NPC: Yes? I am trying to enjoy my beer, thank you very much. But I assume you want something from me.

Your response: Not really. Jones told me that you could use a friendly ear. Let me buy you a drink.

NPC: Jones? Oh, alright, I like her, so I'll like you, especially if you're buyin'. Let me tell you about this bar, and the people walking in and especially out of here. Those who walk out, who still believe in anything, and those- well, those who don't.

Your response: You can tell the difference, simply by watching how they walk out of here?

NPC: If they can still walk, that is. There are those that never complain, and always have something to sell, you know, under the table. Take Tomas, for example. Tomas Bierko. He's quite decent to people, never complains about anything. I'll be damned if he actually believes anything. Those who believe are the ones with loud opinions or spectacular breakdowns. He'd never show either.

Your response: Let's be honest, here. You do realize what just happened, don't you? Why I am here, and what is gonna happen now?

NPC: Please. I am not dense. Of course I know. Doesn't mean that I want to know, or that I am proud of it. Just... don't do it right in front of me, okay?

NPC: (Wren makes a very conscious effort not to notice you again.)

NPC: Wren Halasz in our bar. Don't make me ask again.

NPC: Which name did she land on?

Your response: Tomas Bierko. Really nice guy, apparently. Never complains, gets on well with everybody.

NPC: Bierko. Yeah, I know him. He moves goods here from the City, and does well doing it. His smuggling means that the people he feeds would rather keep him. Getting rid of him would cost us dearly. Your response: If that is what it takes.

Your response: I'll need to think about that, if I'm honest.

NPC: That's a good sign. I won't accept such a task being done half-heartedly. You need to believe.

NPC: Bierko is sitting in the same bar Wren Halasz sits in. Do it right there, do not take him to some back alley. The movement does not hide what it decides.

NPC: I see. You want to know what I think? What I did means that people around here stay fed who would otherwise go hungry. Yes, I'm being paid by the City, and I use this money to help the people around here. So tell me: Who exactly have I betrayed?

Your response: I have no answer for you. All I can tell you is that your fate has been decided.

NPC: ...

entries.title: Mission 1: Brawn First
entries.description: Mrs. Jones wants to see the brawn before anything else. Put down %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(cull_cave) of them in CANYON CAVE 2, then report back to her.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 12 × Denizens of Very Easy Canyon dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The movement is short on people, and has plenty of jobs open for more brawn than brains. The good news is: that means you'll be quite welcome here. The bad news is that, unless I am underestimating you, you won't last long. I want you to prove me wrong. Will you?

Your response: We're gonna have to see, won't we?

Your response: I will, if you just gimme a minute.

Your response: Piss off, won't you.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then first, you need to prove me right, on the brawn at least. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down twelve of whatever is down there. No, you do not get to prove your brains as well on this one.

Your response: Suits me fine, actually.

NPC: Good. And don't you worry: You, I will pay properly for this.

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still a-crawlin'. Don't make me punch your lights out. And don't say 'Oh yeah, I'd like to see you try.'

NPC: And here's your payment. Was this kind of work agreeable to you?

Your response: Uh-huh.

NPC: That was exactly the type of grunt I was hoping to hear. It is also what I had feared. But no matter. Come back to me, once you have restocked and re-whatever'd it is you do.

NPC: You enjoyed your last job, even though it was me sending you into a shithole. Ready for a bigger hole, and bigger shit?

Your response: Uh... how much bigger?

Your response: I will be, just gimme a moment.

NPC: Oh sure, take a moment. Take two.

NPC: You'll see for yourself. It's Canyon Cave 3 this time, and you need to exterminate twelve of them again. Harder ground, bigger critters. Oh, and once again. Good news: I have organized some backup for you. You know, PPUs, equipment, the works. Bad news: It was all reassigned, to something the movement values more than your life, apparently.

Your response: FML. Does it pay well, at least?

NPC: No. ...Oh, you're still here. Let me elaborate: No, with more o's. This will pay less than the last one did, and I'll once again be blunt: The movement won't pay more, because the movement doesn't have to pay more, and that is because you will go in regardless. They know that, I know that, you know that.

NPC: Nice try. Back to Canyon Cave 3 it is.

NPC: Here you go, your payment.

Your response: You weren't kidding, were you. That's all?

NPC: Yes it is, and that's the honest version of what the movement is doing with us. Most people in my position would have beaten around the bush, or hidden it in the paperwork. I'm not gonna pretend otherwise. You do not do this, our cause, for the glamour or the money. There is somebody you need to meet. Get back to me.

NPC: Good news is: It's not a cave this time. Will you take it?

Your response: So what's the bad news?

Your response: Gimme a minute.

NPC: No problem.

NPC: The bad news? Oh, that. Well, the bad news is that you get to off your predecessor. That's the brawn. And you know what that tells you about you being on that job. That's the brains. His name is Dragan Volk - years in the Canyon. Same as you, he has worked out what he was for. It has not stopped him, and now he is a danger to the people around him. Question is, will it stop you?

Your response: But why are you sending me after him? Why not somebody else?

NPC: I had hoped you'd understand that by now. But no matter. You're the reason he is finished. Sending anybody else would be an insult.

NPC: Runner. I know exactly why you are here. And I thank you for this honor.

Your response: So. How long did you have this job before me?

NPC: So many years. I was the one who was sent first through so many doors. Every time, they relied on me to... geez, listen to me, going on about this as if it were some great deed.

Your response: So why did you never stop?

NPC: Listen to me very closely: Being the first through that door was the only thing that ever made me feel worth a damn. I didn't have anything else going for me, but this was the thing they always admired me for.

Your response: And now I'm supposed to be the one always charging first.

NPC: Yes. That is how replaceable I am. And how replaceable you're gonna be one day as well.

NPC: ...

NPC: You still need to take care of Volk.

NPC: You seem somber. That tells me you did it.

Your response: He told me how replaceable he is. And now, I am just as replaceable.

NPC: ...Yes. And I'm not gonna pretend otherwise. I do hope you understand why I sent you, and not some other upstart, though.

Your response: In a couple of years, you're gonna do the same to me, won't you?

NPC: Me? Probably not. One of my successors? Absolutely. You see, I am just as replaceable as you are. The movement will use whatever and whoever it is given, for as long as it benefits the movement. That applies both to you and to me. The only thing I can offer is that I won't sugar-coat it. I'll be honest about it. Dead honest. And that is more than the City can say about the people it uses.

Your response: So I guess there is nothing for me but to accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a sword your way. You've earned it. Keep your Melee Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: Bigger Hole, Less Pay
entries.description: Harder ground, bigger critters and no backup. Put down %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(cull_cave) of them in CANYON CAVE 3, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Brawn First
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 12 × Denizens of Easy Canyon dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 600 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The movement is short on people, and has plenty of jobs open for more brawn than brains. The good news is: that means you'll be quite welcome here. The bad news is that, unless I am underestimating you, you won't last long. I want you to prove me wrong. Will you?

Your response: We're gonna have to see, won't we?

Your response: I will, if you just gimme a minute.

Your response: Piss off, won't you.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then first, you need to prove me right, on the brawn at least. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down twelve of whatever is down there. No, you do not get to prove your brains as well on this one.

Your response: Suits me fine, actually.

NPC: Good. And don't you worry: You, I will pay properly for this.

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still a-crawlin'. Don't make me punch your lights out. And don't say 'Oh yeah, I'd like to see you try.'

NPC: And here's your payment. Was this kind of work agreeable to you?

Your response: Uh-huh.

NPC: That was exactly the type of grunt I was hoping to hear. It is also what I had feared. But no matter. Come back to me, once you have restocked and re-whatever'd it is you do.

NPC: You enjoyed your last job, even though it was me sending you into a shithole. Ready for a bigger hole, and bigger shit?

Your response: Uh... how much bigger?

Your response: I will be, just gimme a moment.

NPC: Oh sure, take a moment. Take two.

NPC: You'll see for yourself. It's Canyon Cave 3 this time, and you need to exterminate twelve of them again. Harder ground, bigger critters. Oh, and once again. Good news: I have organized some backup for you. You know, PPUs, equipment, the works. Bad news: It was all reassigned, to something the movement values more than your life, apparently.

Your response: FML. Does it pay well, at least?

NPC: No. ...Oh, you're still here. Let me elaborate: No, with more o's. This will pay less than the last one did, and I'll once again be blunt: The movement won't pay more, because the movement doesn't have to pay more, and that is because you will go in regardless. They know that, I know that, you know that.

NPC: Nice try. Back to Canyon Cave 3 it is.

NPC: Here you go, your payment.

Your response: You weren't kidding, were you. That's all?

NPC: Yes it is, and that's the honest version of what the movement is doing with us. Most people in my position would have beaten around the bush, or hidden it in the paperwork. I'm not gonna pretend otherwise. You do not do this, our cause, for the glamour or the money. There is somebody you need to meet. Get back to me.

NPC: Good news is: It's not a cave this time. Will you take it?

Your response: So what's the bad news?

Your response: Gimme a minute.

NPC: No problem.

NPC: The bad news? Oh, that. Well, the bad news is that you get to off your predecessor. That's the brawn. And you know what that tells you about you being on that job. That's the brains. His name is Dragan Volk - years in the Canyon. Same as you, he has worked out what he was for. It has not stopped him, and now he is a danger to the people around him. Question is, will it stop you?

Your response: But why are you sending me after him? Why not somebody else?

NPC: I had hoped you'd understand that by now. But no matter. You're the reason he is finished. Sending anybody else would be an insult.

NPC: Runner. I know exactly why you are here. And I thank you for this honor.

Your response: So. How long did you have this job before me?

NPC: So many years. I was the one who was sent first through so many doors. Every time, they relied on me to... geez, listen to me, going on about this as if it were some great deed.

Your response: So why did you never stop?

NPC: Listen to me very closely: Being the first through that door was the only thing that ever made me feel worth a damn. I didn't have anything else going for me, but this was the thing they always admired me for.

Your response: And now I'm supposed to be the one always charging first.

NPC: Yes. That is how replaceable I am. And how replaceable you're gonna be one day as well.

NPC: ...

NPC: You still need to take care of Volk.

NPC: You seem somber. That tells me you did it.

Your response: He told me how replaceable he is. And now, I am just as replaceable.

NPC: ...Yes. And I'm not gonna pretend otherwise. I do hope you understand why I sent you, and not some other upstart, though.

Your response: In a couple of years, you're gonna do the same to me, won't you?

NPC: Me? Probably not. One of my successors? Absolutely. You see, I am just as replaceable as you are. The movement will use whatever and whoever it is given, for as long as it benefits the movement. That applies both to you and to me. The only thing I can offer is that I won't sugar-coat it. I'll be honest about it. Dead honest. And that is more than the City can say about the people it uses.

Your response: So I guess there is nothing for me but to accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a sword your way. You've earned it. Keep your Melee Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 1: Built to Be Abandoned
entries.description: Ask the dealer Ilka Radu in the CANYON FACILITY why the movement drives nothing but wrecks, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Ilka Radu
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. So they tell me you can drive. I hope you realize what that means. The Canyon has no rail and no subway, and our internal logistics is done by hand. So everything the movement has was transported here on chains or wheels, which makes a driver like you one of our supply lines.

Your response: Well, I have seen those vehicles parked outside. They looked rather wrecked for the most important supply line of the Canyon.

Your response: Yes. Give me a moment, though.

Your response: I'm not interested. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Yes. Now why is that? Why does the movement drive decrepit wrecks, when clearly, it could afford better? I will send you to Ilka Radu. Go on and ask that question. You will get the real answer, and I'd much rather have you get it straight from a dealer than from me.

Your response: I'm honestly supposed to walk over to the dealers, only to ask a question that you already know the answer to?

NPC: I hope I am not inconveniencing you. Seriously though. From me, it would only sound like a slogan. From Radu, it will sound like a plain and simple truth. Go.

NPC: Yes? You don't look like the sort of person who could afford anything I have on sale here...

Your response: Jones sent me. Wanted me to ask you why all the vehicles out here seem to be such wrecks.

NPC: Hahaha. Oh emm gee, how clueless. You must be completely new. Do you know how much a new vehicle costs? Do you know how much a run is worth? Do you know how often neither comes back?

Your response: Yes, well, better vehicles would increase the chances of coming back, wouldn't they?

NPC: Marginally, perhaps. Not worth the additional cost, though. It's not like the movement can insure its vehicles, can it? If it is lost, or breaks down and cannot be repaired, the vehicle is gone, and whatever it was worth zeroes. So we only drive what we can afford to abandon at a moment's notice, without running into fiscal trouble due to mounting costs. And I sell these- 'wrecks', as you call them, to anyone who wants one. You probably still can't afford one, but nobody has ever complained about my prices. At least not to my face.

Your response: So you sell to anyone, even those people the movement dislikes?

NPC: Yup. And let me tell you: I don't lose any sleep over it. The road doesn't care what anyone believes. Neither do I.

NPC: If you're not gonna buy anything, move on.

NPC: I know that you haven't spoken to Radu yet.

NPC: Good, you're back. So what did Radu say?

Your response: That a wreck can be abandoned without so much as a second thought, and without anyone being ruined. A good vehicle can't.

NPC: That makes perfect sense, doesn't it? In addition, what Radu left out, because it is none of her business, is this: The movement plans around losing vehicles. Because it has never once been able to plan around keeping them.

NPC: The work never ends. So it's work, this time. Not a lesson.

Your response: Oh yeah? What happened?

Your response: Sure, just gimme a moment.

NPC: Those crates are not going anywhere. I'll be here.

NPC: A freight load is lying scattered across the Canyon and needs picking up. It is what it is, a plain and simple recovery.

Your response: A recovery from what? Whose load was it?

NPC: I'm not gonna beat around the bush: The freight belonged to a City haulage contractor, who now lies dead on the road. Some of our comrades took it, but then got into a fight over the spoils. The movement decided to take it, because the alternative is the Canyon going short on supplies. Yes, that means that you get to play the vulture, picking at the bones. I'm not asking you to feel good about that.

NPC: The crates are still spread across the Facility. Go and get them!

NPC: There's all the crates. Good job. Did you find the manifest as well?

Your response: I did. And I read it. There were many more crates. And that haulage contractor did not just supply the City, but also several wasteland refugee camps.

NPC: Reading the manifest was the right instinct. Any driver worth their salt should, or I'd worry. I will find out about those additional crates. And as for the haulage contractor, let me be blunt: This is what an insurrection eats. Pretending otherwise is how movements like ours start lying to themselves.

NPC: So. There is a good part of the haul which didn't make it to the Canyon. Are you ready to go get it?

Your response: So all those crates are still lying out there in the wastes? Are we sure they're not gone by now?

Your response: I will, but I need a moment first.

NPC: Don't be long. The movement needs those goods, they have already been promised to people who are counting on them.

NPC: Oh, they are, because I sent a recovery crew for them. Unfortunately, when they reached the Canyon, they got too close to Canyon Cave 1, and were attacked by the things in there. Now they refuse to go in there and get the crates back. I shouldn't be angry at them, fighting is not their job. But I have nobody else to send. Except you.

Your response: So what happens if those crates don't come out of there, and need to be declared lost?

NPC: Then our whole promise falls apart. The movement's whole claim is that we can live out here without the City. If we cannot make good on that promise, then it was just a speech. The movement will not fall apart without those crates. But a piece of it will crumble. Too many pieces, and the entire thing falls. So let's not let it come to that.  117      jones_not_available:
 118        say:

 121      jones_over_qualified:
 122        say:
 123          - "You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?"
 124        answer:
 125          jones_leave_over_qualified:
 126            - "Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones."
 127  
 128      jones_leave_over_qualified:
 129        do:
 130          - set_flag:
 131              flag: tg_driver
 132              value: 3
 133          - remove
 134        say:
 135          - "Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."
 136  
 137      jones_m1_offer:
 138        say:
 139          - "Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. So they tell me you can drive. I hope you realize what that means. The Canyon has no rail and no subway, and our internal logistics is done by hand. So everything the movement has was transported here on chains or wheels, which makes a driver like you one of our supply lines."
 140        answer:
 141          jones_m1_briefing:
 142            - "Well, I have seen those vehicles parked outside. They looked rather wrecked for the most important supply line of the Canyon."
 143          jones_m1_later:
 144            - "Yes. Give me a moment, though."
 145          jones_dismiss:
 146            - "I'm not interested. Please leave."
 147  
 148      jones_m1_later:
 149        say:
 150          - "Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25."
 151  
 152      jones_dismiss:
 153        say:
 154          - "Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good."
 155        answer:
 156          jones_dismiss_confirm:
 157            - "Yes, I am sure. Bye, already."
 158          start:
 159            - "Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?"
 160  
 161      jones_dismiss_confirm:
 162        say:
 163          - "Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards."
 164        answer:
 165          jones_leave:
 166            - "Geez. Are you going, or should I?"
 167          start:
 168            - "You know what? I just did."
 169  
 170      jones_leave:
 171        do:
 172          - set_flag:
 173              flag: tg_driver
 174              value: 3
 175          - remove
 176        say:
 177          - "Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."
 178  
 179      jones_m1_briefing:
 180        say:
 181          - "Yes. Now why is that? Why does the movement drive decrepit wrecks, when clearly, it could afford better? I will send you to Ilka Radu. Go on and ask that question. You will get the real answer, and I'd much rather have you get it straight from a dealer than from me."
 182        answer:
 183          jones_m1_go:
 184            - "I'm honestly supposed to walk over to the dealers, only to ask a question that you already know the answer to?"
 185  
 186      jones_m1_go:
 187        do:
 188          - offer_mission: tg_driver.mission1
 189        say:
 190          - "I hope I am not inconveniencing you. Seriously though. From me, it would only sound like a slogan. From Radu, it will sound like a plain and simple truth. Go."
 191        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 192  
 193      radu_greeting:
 194        say:
 195          - "Yes? You don't look like the sort of person who could afford anything I have on sale here..."
 196        answer:
 197          radu_clueless:
 198            - "Jones sent me. Wanted me to ask you why all the vehicles out here seem to be such wrecks."
 199  
 200      radu_clueless:
 201        say:
 202          - "Hahaha. Oh emm gee, how clueless. You must be completely new. Do you know how much a new vehicle costs? Do you know how much a run is worth? Do you know how often neither comes back?"
 203        answer:
 204          radu_abandon:
 205            - "Yes, well, better vehicles would increase the chances of coming back, wouldn't they?"
 206  
 207      radu_abandon:
 208        say:
 209          - "Marginally, perhaps. Not worth the additional cost, though. It's not like the movement can insure its vehicles, can it? If it is lost, or breaks down and cannot be repaired, the vehicle is gone, and whatever it was worth zeroes. So we only drive what we can afford to abandon at a moment's notice, without running into fiscal trouble due to mounting costs. And I sell these- 'wrecks', as you call them, to anyone who wants one. You probably still can't afford one, but nobody has ever complained about my prices. At least not to my face."
 210        answer:
 211          radu_sells_to_anyone:
 212            - "So you sell to anyone, even those people the movement dislikes?"
 213  
 214      radu_sells_to_anyone:
 215        do:
 216          - complete_objective: talk_to_radu
 217        say:
 218          - "Yup. And let me tell you: I don't lose any sleep over it. The road doesn't care what anyone believes. Neither do I."
 219        resume_at: radu_move_on
 220  
 221      radu_move_on:
 222        say:
 223          - "If you're not gonna buy anything, move on."
 224  
 225      jones_m1_return:
 226        do:
 227          - goto: jones_m1_report
 228            when:
 229              objective_done:
 230                objective: talk_to_radu
 231          - goto: jones_m1_not_done
 232  
 233      jones_m1_not_done:
 234        say:
 235          - "I know that you haven't spoken to Radu yet."
 236        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 237  
 238      jones_m1_report:
 239        say:
 240          - "Good, you're back. So what did Radu say?"
 241        answer:
 242          jones_m1_done:
 243            - "That a wreck can be abandoned without so much as a second thought, and without anyone being ruined. A good vehicle can't."
 244        resume_at: jones_m1_done
 245  
 246      jones_m1_done:
 247        do:
 248          - set_flag:
 249              flag: tg_driver
 250              value: 1
 251          - complete_objective: report
 252        say:
 253          - "That makes perfect sense, doesn't it? In addition, what Radu left out, because it is none of her business, is this: The movement plans around losing vehicles. Because it has never once been able to plan around keeping them."
 254  
 255      jones_m2_offer:
 256        say:
 257          - "The work never ends. So it's work, this time. Not a lesson."
 258        answer:
 259          jones_m2_briefing:
 260            - "Oh yeah? What happened?"
 261          jones_m2_later:
 262            - "Sure, just gimme a moment."
 263  
 264      jones_m2_later:
 265        say:
 266          - "Those crates are not going anywhere. I'll be here."
 267  
 268      jones_m2_briefing:
 269        say:
 270          - "A freight load is lying scattered across the Canyon and needs picking up. It is what it is, a plain and simple recovery."
 271        answer:
 272          jones_m2_go:
 273            - "A recovery from what? Whose load was it?"
 274  
 275      jones_m2_go:
 276        do:
 277          - offer_mission: tg_driver.mission2
 278        say:
 279          - "I'm not gonna beat around the bush: The freight belonged to a City haulage contractor, who now lies dead on the road. Some of our comrades took it, but then got into a fight over the spoils. The movement decided to take it, because the alternative is the Canyon going short on supplies. Yes, that means that you get to play the vulture, picking at the bones. I'm not asking you to feel good about that."
 280        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 281  
 282      jones_m2_return:
 283        do:
 284          - goto: jones_m2_report
 285            when:
 286              objective_done:
 287                objective: recover_crates
 288          - goto: jones_m2_not_done
 289  
 290      jones_m2_not_done:
 291        say:
 292          - "The crates are still spread across the Facility. Go and get them!"
 293        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 294  
 295      jones_m2_report:
 296        say:
 297          - "There's all the crates. Good job. Did you find the manifest as well?"
 298        answer:
 299          jones_m2_done:
 300            - "I did. And I read it. There were many more crates. And that haulage contractor did not just supply the City, but also several wasteland refugee camps."
 301        resume_at: jones_m2_done
 302  
 303      jones_m2_done:
 304        do:
 305          - set_flag:
 306              flag: tg_driver
 307              value: 2
 308          - take_item:
 309              item: 8636
 310              count: 6
 311          - complete_objective: report
 312        say:
 313          - "Reading the manifest was the right instinct. Any driver worth their salt should, or I'd worry. I will find out about those additional crates. And as for the haulage contractor, let me be blunt: This is what an insurrection eats. Pretending otherwise is how movements like ours start lying to themselves."
 314  
 315      jones_m3_offer:
 316        say:
 317          - "So. There is a good part of the haul which didn't make it to the Canyon. Are you ready to go get it?"
 318        answer:
 319          jones_m3_briefing:
 320            - "So all those crates are still lying out there in the wastes? Are we sure they're not gone by now?"
 321          jones_m3_later:
 322            - "I will, but I need a moment first."
 323  
 324      jones_m3_later:
 325        say:
 326          - "Don't be long. The movement needs those goods, they have already been promised to people who are counting on them."
 327  
 328      jones_m3_briefing:
 329        say:
 330          - "Oh, they are, because I sent a recovery crew for them. Unfortunately, when they reached the Canyon, they got too close to Canyon Cave 1, and were attacked by the things in there. Now they refuse to go in there and get the crates back. I shouldn't be angry at them, fighting is not their job. But I have nobody else to send. Except you."
 331        answer:
 332          jones_m3_go:
 333            - "So what happens if those crates don't come out of there, and need to be declared lost?"
 334  
 335      jones_m3_go:
 336        do:
 337          - offer_mission: tg_driver.mission3
 338        say:
 339          - "Then our whole promise falls apart. The movement's whole claim is that we can live out here without the City. If we cannot make good on that promise, then it was just a speech. The movement will not fall apart without those crates. But a piece of it will crumble. Too many pieces, and the entire thing falls. So let's not let it come to that. Clear out Canyon Cave 1, and the recovery crew can do the rest."
 340        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 341  
 342      jones_m3_return:
 343        do:
 344          - goto: jones_m3_report
 345            when:
 346              objective_done:
 347                objective: clear_cave
 348          - goto: jones_m3_not_done
 349  
 350      jones_m3_not_done:
 351        say:
 352          - "Canyon Cave 1 is still full, and the recovery crew is still waiting on you to do your job."
 353        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 354  
 355      jones_m3_report:
 356        say:
 357          - "The cave has gone quiet. The recovery crew went in behind you, and the crates have been recovered. Give it to me straight: How bad was it?"
 358        answer:
 359          jones_m3_worth_it:
 360            - "Not too bad, actually. I hope it was worth it."
 361        resume_at: jones_m3_worth_it
 362  
 363      jones_m3_worth_it:
 364        say:
 365          - "17 of our families have food on their table this week. Five of our vehicles could get a long-overdue servicing. Our water reclamation system had one of its parts replaced, one that would surely have broken within the next five weeks. So yes, it was worth it."
 366        answer:
 367          jones_m3_conscience:
 368            - "What about the family of that contractor, or the wasteland refugees? Are they eating, this week?"
 369  
 370      jones_m3_conscience:
 371        say:
 372          - "No. They aren't. And I am quite aware of that. But if the price of continuing our movement out here is a little lost sleep over a nagging conscience, then so be it. It at least tells us that we are still human."
 373        answer:
 374          jones_m3_done:
 375            - "I guess I can accept that."
 376  
 377      jones_m3_done:
 378        do:
 379          - set_flag:
 380              flag: tg_driver
 381              value: 3
 382          - give_item: 8524
 383          - complete_objective: report
 384          - remove
 385        say:
 386          - "Good. I'm gonna send a Quad Key your way. You've earned it. Keep your Vehicle Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."

If it is lost, or breaks down and cannot be repaired, the vehicle is gone, and whatever it was worth zeroes. So we only drive what we can afford to abandon at a moment's notice, without running into fiscal trouble due to mounting costs. And I sell these- 'wrecks', as you call them, to anyone who wants one. entries.title: Mission 1: Four Is Enough
entries.description: Four is all Mrs. Jones can afford to watch a greenhorn be bad at. Take %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(cull_cave) of them in CANYON CAVE 1 with your drone, then report back to her.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 4 × Denizens of Very Easy Canyon dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Listen. The movement is short on people and long on ways to die. So people like you, who fight the good fight from behind a wall, are quite popular among our recruiters, and very much not so among the soldiers. But the work never ends, and I am offering. Are you interested?

Your response: Sure I am. What's the job?

Your response: Let me get back to you.

Your response: No. Honestly, no, not at all. Please go away.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then go into Canyon Cave 1, and kill four of its creepy-crawly denizens. Don't give me that look. Four.

Your response: Are you serious? Four? That's barely worth the walk over there...

NPC: Let me be perfectly clear. Four is what I can afford to watch a greenhorn like you be bad at. You're gonna bump your drone into walls, you're gonna get disoriented, you're gonna lose your drone. That's all part of the learning process, and better it happens now, on my budget, than on a run that actually matters. So get going, and stop complaining.

NPC: I did say four, in Canyon Cave 1, didn't I?

NPC: So? Still flying the same drone, or is there a little pile of scrap in that cave that wasn't there before?

Your response: Four are dead, that's what matters, isn't it?

NPC: Very good. Four done is still done. I've seen people insist on 10, and run out of drones before they could complete their task. Coming back with something small is always better than coming back with nothing at all. Remember that, and get back to me.

NPC: When we met, I told you that your profession is very unpopular among our soldiers. You didn't react to that. Before we get any further, I think you should know why that is.

Your response: Okay, I'll bite. What is it?

Your response: One moment please.

NPC: Sure. The reason isn't going anywhere.

NPC: I'm not gonna tell you. But the drone dealer here in the Canyon will. Goes by the name of Teo Lanz. That's right, he makes a living selling drones to people like you, while thinking that the movement should use neither them nor you.

Your response: How does a dealer argue against their own stock? I'm no expert in economics, but that sounds like bad business.

NPC: It is, and no mistake about it. Lanz is honest, to the point of being bad at his business. You may not like what he has to say. But you should hear it, anyway.

NPC: Welcome. I sell these drones here. Do you want to buy one? Why would you do that?

Your response: Jones sent me. Wants me to hear your objection to my profession.

NPC: My objection? Yeah, I'll give you my objection. We're fighting the good fight against the fascist oppressors in the City. How does it make us look, if we won't stand up for our cause in person? Awesome rebels we are, sending these automatons against theirs. This is not how you get people to believe our cause is just!

Your response: So in your opinion, it's only a proper rebellion if we all die instead?

NPC: ...Look, I- No, of course I don't want us to die. Duh. But- it didn't use to be like this. Used to be that when we went out, we went out ourselves. Stood up for what we believe in.

Your response: So if you abhor drones so much, why do you sell them?

NPC: Because they work, simple as that. I know that my attitude isn't exactly consistent there. I don't wanna lose the people. I just- I just wish it were different. But it isn't. So that's that.

NPC: I have nothing else to say to you.

NPC: You still need to talk to Lanz. You'll find him here in the Canyon.

NPC: You talked to Lanz. Now explain his point to me, calmly and rationally.

Your response: He is in two minds. He believes that a revolution that won't risk bodies has already decided it is going to lose. But he doesn't want to lose the people, either.

NPC: I'll be honest: This kind of claptrap really gets me. The movement can't afford to be romantic about itself! The City can replace everyone it loses, the Canyon can't. We can't borrow the luxury of being willing to spend bodies from an enemy that has ten times as many of them. It's that simple. Digest that, then get back to me.

NPC: As I said, the work never ends, and I have a job for you that proves my point. I assume you are willing.

Your response: I am. What's up?

Your response: Give me a minute, and I'll get back to you.

NPC: Sure. Nobody else is gonna do it in the meantime. That's sort of the whole point.

NPC: What's 'up' is that two scouts went into Canyon Cave 3 and did not come out. These Gnawers in there are what did them in. I want you to make an example of them, and I don't want to risk anyone's life while doing it. Two was already a number we shouldn't have spent. No more. So take your drone, and kill Gnawers in that cave. Three of them. One more of them than they killed of us.

Your response: Why not simply send a squad and exterminate them all?

NPC: Have you been listening? I already sent two, and I have nothing to show for it except two bodies. I'm not gonna make it three, just because one squaddie isn't paying attention. My budget of lives to waste is thoroughly tapped out. Which is why I am risking your drones, not a squad, and not you. That's the kind of arithmetic that people like Lanz refuse to do.

NPC: Those three Gnawers in Canyon Cave 3 won't kill themselves.

NPC: You're back, all in one piece, and the three Gnawers are dead. Tell me you didn't take unnecessary risks.

Your response: I barely set foot into the cave. My drones did the rest.

NPC: Two people, dead. That is the subtotal of doing it how Lanz thinks we should do it. I think I'm gonna tell him just that.

Your response: So Lanz is just plain wrong, then?

NPC: Wrong doesn't quite hit the mark. Deluded, more like. His idea of our movement has principles the real deal simply can't afford. Not to say that his version is unattractive, not even to me. But I'd much rather win this fight than slowly get wiped out because we couldn't let go of some old-fashioned honor-of-the-battlefield principles.

Your response: He makes you angry because you're afraid he might be right, aren't you?

NPC: I'm not afraid. Anyway, I'm gonna send a drone prototype your way. You've earned it. Keep your Remote Control skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: The Dealer's Objection
entries.description: Teo Lanz sells drones and thinks the movement should not use them. Hear him out in the CANYON FACILITY, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Four Is Enough
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Teo Lanz
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience

entries.title: Mission 3: No More Bodies
entries.description: Two scouts went into CANYON CAVE 3 and never came out. Send your drone after the Gnawers that killed them and take %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(kill_gnawers), then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: The Dealer's Objection
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 3 × Canyon Gnawer
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Listen. The movement is short on people and long on ways to die. So people like you, who fight the good fight from behind a wall, are quite popular among our recruiters, and very much not so among the soldiers. But the work never ends, and I am offering. Are you interested?

Your response: No. Honestly, no, not at all. Please go away.

 258        say:
 259          - "My objection? Yeah, I'll give you my objection. We're fighting the good fight against the fascist oppressors in the City. How does it make us look, if we won't stand up for our cause in person? Awesome rebels we are, sending these automatons against theirs. This is not how you get people to believe our cause is just!"
 260        answer:
 261          lanz_not_to_die:
 262            - "So in your opinion, it's only a proper rebellion if we all die instead?"
 263  
 264      lanz_not_to_die:
 265        say:
 266          - "...Look, I- No, of course I don't want us to die. Duh. But- it didn't use to be like this. Used to be that when we went out, we went out ourselves. Stood up for what we believe in."
 267        answer:
 268          lanz_why_sell:
 269            - "So if you abhor drones so much, why do you sell them?"

 272        do:
 273          - complete_objective: talk_to_lanz
 274        say:
 275          - "Because they work, simple as that. I know that my attitude isn't exactly consistent there. I don't wanna lose the people. I just- I just wish it were different. But it isn't. So that's that."

 277

 279        say:
 280          - "I have nothing else to say to you."

 292          - "You still need to talk to Lanz. You'll find him here in the Canyon."
 293        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 294  
 295      jones_m2_report:
 296        say:
 297          - "You talked to Lanz. Now explain his point to me, calmly and rationally."
 298        answer:
 299          jones_m2_done:
 300            - "He is in two minds. He believes that a revolution that won't risk bodies has already decided it is going to lose. But he doesn't want to lose the people, either."
 301        resume_at: jones_m2_done

 304        do:
 305          - set_flag:
 306              flag: tg_droner
 307              value: 2
 308          - complete_objective: report
 309        say:
 310          - "I'll be honest: This kind of claptrap really gets me. The movement can't afford to be romantic about itself! The City can replace everyone it loses, the Canyon can't. We can't borrow the luxury of being willing to spend bodies from an enemy that has ten times as many of them. It's that simple. Digest that, then get back to me."

 313        say:
 314          - "As I said, the work never ends, and I have a job for you that proves my point. I assume you are willing."

 317            - "I am. What's up?"
 318          jones_m3_later:
 319            - "Give me a minute, and I'll get back to you."
 320  
 321      jones_m3_later:
 322        say:
 323          - "Sure. Nobody else is gonna do it in the meantime. That's sort of the whole point."
 324

 327          - "What's 'up' is that two scouts went into Canyon Cave 3 and did not come out. These Gnawers in there are what did them in. I want you to make an example of them, and I don't want to risk anyone's life while doing it. Two was already a number we shouldn't have spent. No more. So take your drone, and kill Gnawers in that cave. Three of them. One more of them than they killed of us."

entries.title: Mission 1: Taking Stock
entries.description: Go through the scrap across the CANYON FACILITY and find %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(collect_couplings) couplings that still work properly, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 6 × Salvaged Coupling
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Your classical engineer training has probably always held all of your work to the highest standards. Well, let me disabuse you of that notion right away. There are no standards out here. If it works, it is good enough. Doesn't matter a bugger to anyone if it still works in 50 years, when it took you six weeks to finish it, while something that lasts a month could have been a five minute job. What does that sound like to you? Like freedom, or like a problem?

Your response: Like interesting new work conditions, but I have always been good at thinking on my feet. What's the assignment?

Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: Words cannot describe how uninterested I am. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: First assignment is to take stock. Having to think on your feet is one thing, not knowing what to work with is another. So go through the scrap across the Canyon, and find us six couplings that are actually still working properly.

Your response: You don't need an engineer for scavenging. What gives?

NPC: Oh, come on. The interesting bit is the telling if a coupling is fused or still working. Find someone to carry them for you, if that is beneath you. Now get out there, and get me those couplings.

NPC: Still waiting on those couplings.

NPC: You got the couplings. So give me an estimate: How much of that scrap out there is still in working condition?

Your response: Honestly? Not much.

NPC: Yeah, that's hardly surprising. Most structures the Canyon relies on are in pretty bad condition, and unfortunately, even most of our own people don't realize that. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So, these couplings. Do you want to know what they are holding together?

Your response: I'm almost afraid to ask...

Your response: Yes, but hang on. I still need a moment.

NPC: Sure. I'll be here.

NPC: Rightly so. Go to Ondrej Vask at the supply depot. The entire Canyon's water supply depends on one machine that came out of a City plant decades ago, and there's nobody left alive who fully understands it. Vask is the guy who comes closest to that.

Your response: That can't be right. Why did nobody write it all down, back then?

NPC: Let me put it this way: The movement's founding claim is that people can live free out here. Writing down how many parts of our machines come from the City, and only the City... well, it could be seen as a written confession that this claim is less than true. Still. Get as much information out of Vask as you can.

NPC: Yeah, what do you want? The water plant is working fine, thank you very much!

Your response: Calm down, I'm not here to file anything. Jones sent me.

NPC: Alright then. You want some straight shootin', then? Keeping this machine alive, by now, has become more of a ritual than actual repair work. We go through motions handed down through the years, without any idea why we do what we do, imitating what we observed from people long dead by now.

Your response: More straight shootin', please. In your honest opinion, what's the first part that's likely to fail soon?

NPC: It's the anti-radiation regulator. I've been nursing it for months, now. I've also tried to put my ear to the ground, but there is no replacement to be taken from anywhere in the wastes. Only the City has these parts, and I don't have to explain to you why that is not an option for us.

Your response: So why haven't you raised this topic higher up?

NPC: You mean an escalation? An escalation would become an admission, an admission that the Canyon cannot sustain itself. I won't have that. No, I'll manage to keep the old part working. Somehow.

NPC: Leave me be, I have stuff to attend to that I barely understand myself.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Vask yet.

NPC: So what did Vask admit to?

Your response: The anti-radiation regulator is failing, probably only has weeks still in it. And no amount of wishful thinking from him is gonna fix that.

NPC: Once again, I suspected as much. That's the most fragile part of the entire machinery, and it already didn't look that good anymore last year. So far, I have raised this through the discreet channels inside the movement that are available to me, but to no avail. We may need to evaluate alternative arrangements. Give me a moment to make a few calls, then get back to me again.

NPC: Alright. I have found a way to procure the required item. It will allow us to keep operating. And as long as neither you nor I blab about it, our ideology stays intact. Can I rely upon your discretion?

Your response: I'm not going to like this, am I? Just tell me where.

Your response: Can I... think about this for a minute?

NPC: Alright, but make your mind up. The machine is not waiting for anybody's conscience.

NPC: No one official will approve any requisitioning, because doing so would be admitting failure. That's how they think. But I have been made to understand that if I were to somehow magically come up with that part, nobody would ask any uncomfortable questions. There is a smuggler in the Canyon - goes by the name of Ilka Radu. She has confirmed that she could procure such a part for us. From the City, I'd imagine. And at a Smuggler's price.

Your response: So we're doing now exactly what the movement condemns? And you're keeping clean by sending me?

NPC: Absolutely. Make no mistake about it. You and me, we are gonna be the ones that will make the idea of the Canyon live on, and nobody will thank us for it. Nobody will even want to know. The Canyon's independence is bought from the very system it hates much more often than it would care to admit. Now, go to Radu and get that part. Take a shower after, if you must, with the water you ensured that we're gonna keep having.

NPC: Radu's the name, and... oh. You're the one Jones sent, hmm? Not so conceited about pure ideology now, is she? Heh heh heh.

Your response: Less gloating, more anti-radiation regulator giving, please.

NPC: Oh, I don't mean to be cruel about all this. It's just refreshing not to have people look down their noses at me for a change. In your own story, you're probably the hero who does what needs to be done, aren't you? Well, without me and what I do, there's no heroism to be had. So where does that leave me?

Your response: You do it for the money. And I bet you exploit our vulnerability in these matters regularly.

NPC: You know what? This part is dirt cheap in the City. But Jones is gonna wire me 5,000 NC for it. And like all the others from the Command Center, she won't thank me, yet she knows my name. They all do. Ask yourself how that could be.

Your response: I'd rather not. I'll have that regulator now, thank you.

NPC: Here you go. Just think: Which one of us is actually keeping the Canyon alive?

NPC: You're still here. Back to acting all better-than-thou?

NPC: We still need that regulator from Radu.

NPC: You got the part, while I got Radu's hefty bill. Did she say anything worth repeating?

Your response: She asked me to think about which one of us is actually keeping the Canyon alive.

NPC: Here's what's gonna happen. The movement will fix the water plant, tell nobody where that part came from, and go on making pretty little speeches about self-sufficiency. Our burden of knowledge is having peeked behind the curtain, and knowing that these speeches are really just that.

Your response: And that doesn't bother you at all?

NPC: It does, and having vultures like Radu gloat about it does not make it more agreeable. I do believe in the idea of the Canyon, however. And that is worth a few sleepless nights.

Your response: I guess I can live with that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Construction Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Construction skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: The Water Machine
entries.description: The Canyon's water depends on one machine nobody fully understands. Find out from Ondrej Vask at the supply depot in the CANYON FACILITY what is about to fail, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Taking Stock
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Ondrej Vask
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. If it works, it is good enough. Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: Words cannot describe how uninterested I am. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 3: Bought From the Enemy
entries.description: The failing regulator cannot be requisitioned. Buy it from the smuggler Ilka Radu in the CANYON FACILITY, keep quiet about where it came from, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: The Water Machine
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Ilka Radu
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Your classical engineer training has probably always held all of your work to the highest standards. Well, let me disabuse you of that notion right away. There are no standards out here. If it works, it is good enough. Doesn't matter a bugger to anyone if it still works in 50 years, when it took you six weeks to finish it, while something that lasts a month could have been a five minute job. Your response: Like interesting new work conditions, but I have always been good at thinking on my feet. What's the assignment?

Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: Words cannot describe how uninterested I am. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

We go through motions handed down through the years, without any idea why we do what we do, imitating what we observed from people long dead by now."

 267          vask_regulator:
 268            - "More straight shootin', please. In your honest opinion, what's the first part that's likely to fail soon?"
 269  
 270      vask_regulator:
 271        say:
 272          - "It's the anti-radiation regulator. I've been nursing it for months, now. I've also tried to put my ear to the ground, but there is no replacement to be taken from anywhere in the wastes. Only the City has these parts, and I don't have to explain to you why that is not an option for us."
 273        answer:
 274          vask_no_escalation:
 275            - "So why haven't you raised this topic higher up?"
 276

 279          - complete_objective: question_vask
 280        say:

 297        say:
 298          - "You haven't spoken to Vask yet."
 299        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 300

 302        say:
 303          - "So what did Vask admit to?"
 304        answer:

 306            - "The anti-radiation regulator is failing, probably only has weeks still in it. And no amount of wishful thinking from him is gonna fix that."

 312              flag: tg_engineer

 316          - "Once again, I suspected as much. That's the most fragile part of the entire machinery, and it already didn't look that good anymore last year. So far, I have raised this through the discreet channels inside the movement that are available to me, but to no avail. We may need to evaluate alternative arrangements. Give me a moment to make a few calls, then get back to me again."

 319        say:
 320          - "Alright. I have found a way to procure the required item. It will allow us to keep operating. And as long as neither you nor I blab about it, our ideology stays intact. Can I rely upon your discretion?"

 322          jones_m3_briefing:
 323            - "I'm not going to like this, am I? Just tell me where."
 324          jones_m3_later:
 325            - "Can I... think about this for a minute?"
 326  
 327      jones_m3_later:
 328        say:
 329          - "Alright, but make your mind up. The machine is not waiting for anybody's conscience."
 330  
 331      jones_m3_briefing:
 332        say:
 333          - "No one official will approve any requisitioning, because doing so would be admitting failure. That's how they think. But I have been made to understand that if I were to somehow magically come up with that part, nobody would ask any uncomfortable questions. There is a smuggler in the Canyon - goes by the name of Ilka Radu. She has confirmed that she could procure such a part for us. From the City, I'd imagine. And at a Smuggler's price."

 335          jones_m3_go:
 336            - "So we're doing now exactly what the movement condemns? And you're keeping clean by sending me?"
 337

 339        do:
 340          - offer_mission: tg_engineer.mission3
 341        say:
 342          - "Absolutely. Make no mistake about it. You and me, we are gonna be the ones that will make the idea of the Canyon live on, and nobody will thank us for it. Nobody will even want to know. The Canyon's independence is bought from the very system it hates much more often than it would care to admit. Now, go to Radu and get that part. Take a shower after, if you must, with the water you ensured that we're gonna keep having."
