entries.title: Mission 1: Still Sterile
entries.description: A supply drom burst its crates in a narrow passage on the lower level of the CANYON FACILITY. Recover %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(collect_dressings) dressing packs that are still usable, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 6 × Spilled Dressing Pack
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. You are trained in treating casualties. Most of the people in need of treating around here aren't casualties at all. Interested in finding out what I mean by that?

Your response: That probably sounded better in your head. But I'll take it.

Your response: In a minute.

Your response: Ugh. No. Not at all. Please leave. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: First things first: Some medical supplies came off a supply drom that panicked in a narrow passage on the lower level of the Canyon. The crates burst, and scattered their contents all over that passage. Get me six of the dressing packs that were inside, before people start quietly pocketing them.

Your response: Come on. You don't need a medic for this kind of work.

NPC: Yes I do. A medic is the only one who will bother checking which packs are still sterile, instead of just counting them up, and proudly presenting me with a bunch of unusable trash. So get down there, and get me those packs.

NPC: I still need those packs. Get them, before they're gone.

NPC: You got them. So how much of the stuff lying about was still usable?

Your response: Well, most of the usable stuff has been pocketed by now. The stuff that was strewn across the floor clearly already had been gone through a couple of times.

NPC: That's the entire Canyon's medical supply situation right there: Nothing arrives reliably, and everything that does arrive gets rationed by whoever is standing closest. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So. I already told you that most people treated around here aren't casualties at all. Do you want to know what they get treated for, or what they don't get treated for, and then die of?

Your response: I do.

Your response: Yes, but hang on. Not ready yet.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: Then head over to Doc Sarn in the Barracks, in HQ. He has been treating people in the Canyon longer than the movement has held it. The answer will become clear.

Your response: So what am I supposed to expect, down there?

NPC: That it is actually not the fighting that accounts for most deaths around here. Well, at least not directly. But you don't need to hear second-hand information from me. Go directly to the source, Doc Sarn.

NPC: No grave external injuries. Take a seat, I'll be right with you. Actually, you don't look injured at all. Why are you taking up space here?

Your response: Jones sent me. I'm a medic as well, although not nearly as experienced as you are.

NPC: Oh, you are of the trade as well? I could use the extra hands, sure. You see, there are so many people to treat here, cave wounds, heat, and above all injuries that were survivable a year ago and were never treated back then.

Your response: You know, I cannot help but notice that a lot of those people you treat around here do not seem to be of our movement at all...

NPC: Oh, less than half, make no mistake about it. Everyone within a day's walk comes here if they get injured, simply because there is nowhere else. And me, well, I have never asked anyone what they believe in before I treat them. And neither should you.

Your response: I didn't even know the guards at the gate would let people in, just like that. Does nobody object to what you're doing?

NPC: They have started to, recently. The more people come here, the bigger the problem some people seem to have with it. But I'm not in the habit of turning people away, so anyone who has a problem with that can just come up to me and say it to my face. That's all I have to say about it.

NPC: I must get back to my patients.

NPC: You need to speak to Doc Sarn in the Barracks.

NPC: So. Doc Sarn's patients. Anything about them that you'd notice?

Your response: He's mostly treating people suffering from cave injuries, heatstroke or untreated old injuries, barely any recent combat casualties. And about half of the people he's treating aren't even from our movement at all.

NPC: I know. And I have been getting asked from above about this more and more, recently. Take a breather, then get back to me. Unfortunately, the position of the movement on matters like these is quite clear.

NPC: I have spent some time trying to come up with ways of dressing this up like a lesson. But it's not. So I'm gonna stop pretending that it is. This is an order, plain and simple. You're going to deliver it and Doc Sarn is going to obey it. And that's that.

Your response: I'm not going to like this, am I. What is it?

Your response: Uh, I'm gonna need a moment.

NPC: Take that moment. I'd much rather have you do this reluctantly than cheerfully.

NPC: It's precisely what you already guessed. Doc Sarn is to stop treating people aligned with the City. Our medical supplies are finite, and the movement will not spend them on people who would hand the Canyon back to the City tomorrow.

Your response: This goes against everything I stand for. I can't imagine you agree with that order.

NPC: The point of an order is that it comes from people you don't get to overrule. I don't get to overrule them, and you don't get to overrule me. And Sarn doesn't get to overrule you. That he gets that order from a fellow medic is the modicum of comfort I can offer him.

NPC: No. Don't say it. Don't say anything. You're forbidding me from treating people not of the Canyon, aren't you.

Your response: You are hereby ordered to stop treating people aligned with the City. Our supplies are finite, and we cannot spend them on people who might come back in the next attack wave against us.

NPC: I bet you rehearsed that line in your head over and over again on your way here. Unfortunately for you, I've been expecting this to happen for some time, and I've had time to prepare myself, too. So let me ask you one simple question of procedure: How exactly am I supposed to make out a patient's politics with blood gushing from their open wounds and them screaming and crying for their mothers?

Your response: I... have no procedure to offer you about that.

NPC: Figures. They never even thought this through, did they? Headful of ideology, and no practical considerations ever spent. But if they want ideology, here's one for them: As soon as we start doing triage by loyalty rather than by severity of injury, this becomes just another installation of the same system the City is running, and the movement will have lost the only thing it can honestly claim to be better at.

Your response: I don't know what to say to you. What do you expect me to report back, now?

NPC: You want something to report back? Here goes, and do take note, so you get the wording exactly right: Fuck the lot of you. There you go, report that. I will not have someone bleeding out under my care because some people deem them not ideologically pure enough. I'm not scared of you, I'm not scared of that bitch Jones, and I'm certainly not scared of the chief ideologists who think they actually run this place. ...Actually, I'm gonna take that 'bitch' back. I know Jones, and honestly, I don't think she really wants me to obey that order.

NPC: You don't want me to obey that order either. That's plain as day. So I'll be going back to work now, if you don't mind.

NPC: You still need to deliver that order. It's not gonna get easier by procrastinating.

NPC: So. How'd it go? Did he tell you where you can shove that order?

Your response: He asked me to relay his reply word for word, and it was: 'Fuck the lot of you.'

NPC: I expected no less. ...Sorry. You probably expected me to know what to do now. The truth is: I don't.

Your response: He raised the good point of how to find out the politics of someone with blood gushing out of them, and them crying for their mommies. Maybe that helps?

NPC: It may. I will do the only thing I can do, which is the same thing you did: I will report that refusal upward, along with that very valid question. No editing, no mincing words. They can have that problem sit on their plate and stare at their faces. I have spent years justifying everything the movement asks. But this is one I just can't. And I will not insult a medic by trying to.

Your response: Does that change anything for you? Or me?

NPC: No. I still believe in the movement. People fail, the idea doesn't. If the idea collapses on one doctor refusing an order to stop treating people, it won't survive the City's onslaught, either. I'm gonna send a Healing Module your way. You've earned it. Keep your Passive Psi Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: Not Casualties
entries.description: Find Doc Sarn in the TG HQ - BARRACKS and see who he actually treats, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Still Sterile
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Doc Sarn
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience

entries.title: Mission 3: Triage by Loyalty
entries.description: Deliver the order to Doc Sarn in the TG HQ - BARRACKS: no more treatment for people aligned with the City. Then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: Not Casualties
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Doc Sarn
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

 187            - "Come on. You don't need a medic for this kind of work."
 188  
 189      jones_m1_go:
 190        do:
 191          - offer_mission: tg_fieldmedic.mission1
 192        say:
 193          - "Yes I do. A medic is the only one who will bother checking which packs are still sterile, instead of just counting them up, and proudly presenting me with a bunch of unusable trash. So get down there, and get me those packs."
 194        resume_at: jones_m1_return

 197        do:
 198          - goto: jones_m1_report
 199            when:
 200              objective_done:
 201                objective: collect_dressings
 202          - goto: jones_m1_not_done

 205        say:
 206          - "I still need those packs. Get them, before they're gone."
 207        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 208  
 209      jones_m1_report:
 210        say:
 211          - "You got them. So how much of the stuff lying about was still usable?"
 212        answer:
 213          jones_m1_done:
 214            - "Well, most of the usable stuff has been pocketed by now. The stuff that was strewn across the floor clearly already had been gone through a couple of times."
 215        resume_at: jones_m1_done

 218        do:
 219          - set_flag:
 220              flag: tg_fieldmedic
 221              value: 1
 222          - take_item:
 223              item: 8638
 224              count: 6
 225          - complete_objective: report
 226        say:
 227          - "That's the entire Canyon's medical supply situation right there: Nothing arrives reliably, and everything that does arrive gets rationed by whoever is standing closest. Take five, then get back to me."
 228  
 229      jones_m2_offer:
 230        say:
 231          - "So. I already told you that most people treated around here aren't casualties at all. Do you want to know what they get treated for, or what they don't get treated for, and then die of?"
 232        answer:
 233          jones_m2_briefing:
 234            - "I do."
 235          jones_m2_later:
 236            - "Yes, but hang on. Not ready yet."
 237  
 238      jones_m2_later:
 239        say:
 240          - "I'll be here."
 241  
 242      jones_m2_briefing:
 243        say:
 244          - "Then head over to Doc Sarn in the Barracks, in HQ. He has been treating people in the Canyon longer than the movement has held it. The answer will become clear."
 245        answer:
 246          jones_m2_go:
 247            - "So what am I supposed to expect, down there?"
 248  
 249      jones_m2_go:
 250        do:
 251          - offer_mission: tg_fieldmedic.mission2
 252        say:
 253          - "That it is actually not the fighting that accounts for most deaths around here. Well, at least not directly. But you don't need to hear second-hand information from me. Go directly to the source, Doc Sarn."
 254        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 255  
 256      sarn_greeting:
 257        say:
 258          - "No grave external injuries. Take a seat, I'll be right with you. Actually, you don't look injured at all. Why are you taking up space here?"
 259        answer:
 260          sarn_patients:
 261            - "Jones sent me. I'm a medic as well, although not nearly as experienced as you are."
 262  
 263      sarn_patients:
 264        say:
 265          - "Oh, you are of the trade as well? I could use the extra hands, sure. You see, there are so many people to treat here, cave wounds, heat, and above all injuries that were survivable a year ago and were never treated back then."
 266        answer:
 267          sarn_no_questions:
 268            - "You know, I cannot help but notice that a lot of those people you treat around here do not seem to be of our movement at all..."
 269  
 270      sarn_no_questions:
 271        say:
 272          - "Oh, less than half, make no mistake about it. Everyone within a day's walk comes here if they get injured, simply because there is nowhere else. And me, well, I have never asked anyone what they believe in before I treat them. And neither should you."
 273        answer:
 274          sarn_objections:
 275            - "I didn't even know the guards at the gate would let people in, just like that. Does nobody object to what you're doing?"
 276  
 277      sarn_objections:
 278        do:
 279          - complete_objective: talk_to_sarn
 280        say:
 281          - "They have started to, recently. The more people come here, the bigger the problem some people seem to have with it. But I'm not in the habit of turning people away, so anyone who has a problem with that can just come up to me and say it to my face. That's all I have to say about it."
 282        resume_at: sarn_back_to_patients
 283  
 284      sarn_back_to_patients:
 285        say:
 286          - "I must get back to my patients."
 287

 291            when:
 292              objective_done:
 293                objective: talk_to_sarn
 294          - goto: jones_m2_not_done
 295  
 296      jones_m2_not_done:
 297        say:
 298          - "You need to speak to Doc Sarn in the Barracks."
 299        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 300  
 301      jones_m2_report:
 302        say:
 303          - "So. Doc Sarn's patients. Anything about them that you'd notice?"
 304        answer:
 305          jones_m2_done:
 306            - "He's mostly treating people suffering from cave injuries, heatstroke or untreated old injuries, barely any recent combat casualties. And about half of the people he's treating aren't even from our movement at all."
 307        resume_at: jones_m2_done
 308  
 309      jones_m2_done:
 310        do:
 311          - set_flag:
 312              flag: tg_fieldmedic
 313              value: 2
 314          - complete_objective: report
 315        say:
 316          - "I know. And I have been getting asked from above about this more and more, recently. Take a breather, then get back to me. Unfortunately, the position of the movement on matters like these is quite clear."
 317  
 318      jones_m3_offer:
 319        say:
 320          - "I have spent some time trying to come up with ways of dressing this up like a lesson. But it's not. So I'm gonna stop pretending that it is. This is an order, plain and simple. You're going to deliver it and Doc Sarn is going to obey it. And that's that."
 321        answer:
 322          jones_m3_briefing:
 323            - "I'm not going to like this, am I. What is it?"
 324          jones_m3_later:
 325            - "Uh, I'm gonna need a moment."
 326  
 327      jones_m3_later:
 328        say:
 329          - "Take that moment. I'd much rather have you do this reluctantly than cheerfully."
 330  
 331      jones_m3_briefing:
 332        say:
 333          - "It's precisely what you already guessed. Doc Sarn is to stop treating people aligned with the City. Our medical supplies are finite, and the movement will not spend them on people who would hand the Canyon back to the City tomorrow."
 334        answer:
 335          jones_m3_go:
 336            - "This goes against everything I stand for. I can't imagine you agree with that order."
 337  
 338      jones_m3_go:
 339        do:
 340          - offer_mission: tg_fieldmedic.mission3
 341        say:
 342          - "The point of an order is that it comes from people you don't get to overrule. I don't get to overrule them, and you don't get to overrule me. And Sarn doesn't get to overrule you. That he gets that order from a fellow medic is the modicum of comfort I can offer him."
 343        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 344  
 345      sarn_refusal:
 346        say:
 347          - "No. Don't say it. Don't say anything. You're forbidding me from treating people not of the Canyon, aren't you."
 348        answer:
 349          sarn_procedure:
 350            - "You are hereby ordered to stop treating people aligned with the City. Our supplies are finite, and we cannot spend them on people who might come back in the next attack wave against us."
 351  
 352      sarn_procedure:
 353        say:
 354          - "I bet you rehearsed that line in your head over and over again on your way here. Unfortunately for you, I've been expecting this to happen for some time, and I've had time to prepare myself, too. So let me ask you one simple question of procedure: How exactly am I supposed to make out a patient's politics with blood gushing from their open wounds and them screaming and crying for their mothers?"
 355        answer:
 356          sarn_triage:
 357            - "I... have no procedure to offer you about that."
 358  
 359      sarn_triage:
 360        say:
 361          - "Figures. They never even thought this through, did they? Headful of ideology, and no practical considerations ever spent. But if they want ideology, here's one for them: As soon as we start doing triage by loyalty rather than by severity of injury, this becomes just another installation of the same system the City is running, and the movement will have lost the only thing it can honestly claim to be better at."
 362        answer:
 363          sarn_reply:
 364            - "I don't know what to say to you. What do you expect me to report back, now?"
 365

 367        do:
 368          - complete_objective: deliver_order
 369        say:
 370          - "You want something to report back? Here goes, and do take note, so you get the wording exactly right: Fuck the lot of you. There you go, report that. I will not have someone bleeding out under my care because some people deem them not ideologically pure enough. I'm not scared of you, I'm not scared of that bitch Jones, and I'm certainly not scared of the chief ideologists who think they actually run this place. ...Actually, I'm gonna take that 'bitch' back. I know Jones, and honestly, I don't think she really wants me to obey that order."
 371        resume_at: sarn_back_to_work
 372  
 373      sarn_back_to_work:
 374        say:
 375          - "You don't want me to obey that order either. That's plain as day. So I'll be going back to work now, if you don't mind."
 376

 378        do:
 379          - goto: jones_m3_report
 380            when:
 381              objective_done:
 382                objective: deliver_order

 386        say:
 387          - "You still need to deliver that order. It's not gonna get easier by procrastinating."
 388        resume_at: jones_m3_return

 391        say:
 392          - "So. How'd it go? Did he tell you where you can shove that order?"
 393        answer:
 394          jones_m3_no_answer:
 395            - "He asked me to relay his reply word for word, and it was: 'Fuck the lot of you.'"
 396        resume_at: jones_m3_no_answer
 397  
 398      jones_m3_no_answer:
 399        say:
 400          - "I expected no less. ...Sorry. You probably expected me to know what to do now. The truth is: I don't."
 401        answer:
 402          jones_m3_report_upward:
 403            - "He raised the good point of how to find out the politics of someone with blood gushing out of them, and them crying for their mommies. Maybe that helps?"
 404  
 405      jones_m3_report_upward:
 406        say:
 407          - "It may. I will do the only thing I can do, which is the same thing you did: I will report that refusal upward, along with that very valid question. No editing, no mincing words. They can have that problem sit on their plate and stare at their faces. I have spent years justifying everything the movement asks. But this is one I just can't. And I will not insult a medic by trying to."
 408        answer:
 409          jones_m3_done:
 410            - "Does that change anything for you? Or me?"

 414          - set_flag:
 415              flag: tg_fieldmedic
 416              value: 3
 417          - give_item:
 418              item: 8556
 419              quality: 150
 420              slots: 3
 421          - complete_objective: report
 422          - remove
 423        say:
 424          - "No. I still believe in the movement. People fail, the idea doesn't. Keep your Passive Psi Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."

entries.title: Mission 1: Nothing to Hack
entries.description: Find the analyst Adela Prosk in the TG HQ - INTELLIGENCE CENTER and learn how City data reaches the Canyon, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Adela Prosk
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Now, good news first: This place is virtually impossible to hack. The bad news: That's because there is almost no technical infrastructure that could be hacked. Which limits your options somewhat. But the movement wants you anyway. Know why that is?

Your response: This does not start promising. But I'm interested.

Your response: Let me get back to you on that.

Your response: No I don't, nor have I the slightest interest in finding out. Now leave my apartment, please.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then head over to our Intelligence Center. Talk to Adela Prosk, and learn how City data actually reaches the Canyon, because it is not over any wire. Or WiFi, for that matter.

Your response: So all the data arrives physically?

NPC: I can neither confirm nor deny that. Just talk to Prosk. It will change your perception of what your skill is for out here. The Intelligence Center can be found inside HQ. There's a hatch.

NPC: Just put the latest discs over there, would y- what? A hacker? What are you doing here?

Your response: Jones sent me. Asked me to learn how data actually gets here.

NPC: Ah, I see. Well, it's simple, really. Nothing arrives here over any network. If it did, anything coming in would be accompanied by ten times as much data going out. So all the data arrives in someone's coat. That's 'coat' if we are lucky. The Canyon's entire intelligence capacity is people willing to walk the distance, and smuggle data out the old-fashioned way.

Your response: And what does the movement do with that data?

NPC: We publish it, mostly. It's the City's own propaganda, spun against itself, aimed at City workers who may not yet be fully indoctrinated.

Your response: Does that even work at all?

NPC: I'll be honest: Most of our numbers are guesstimates, and even those are low. But actually, that's not our concern around here. What we do is make sure that what gets published and what is being stolen remains the same - if that makes any sense at all to you.

NPC: Back to stacks of data discs to go through.

NPC: You need to speak to Prosk in the Intelligence Center before we can continue.

NPC: You're back. So what did Prosk show you?

Your response: Loads of physical media, a story about couriers, and the fact that the movement's real output appears to be respun City propaganda rather than intelligence.

NPC: You got that exactly right. And here is the political point: The movement does not steal City data to know things, it steals City data so that people in the City have to know things they have arranged their lives around not knowing. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So, I have a job for you. It may or may not be a little more up your street. What do you say?

Your response: I'm gonna say: I'm in.

Your response: I'm gonna say: Hang on a moment.

NPC: I'll be here. Don't know if the job will still be, though.

NPC: So, one of those couriers who was supposed to carry loads of data into our Intelligence Center? Yeah, he arrived running for his life, dropping half of his haul all over the place. He was running because City agents were waiting on his route. Recover these data cubes from all around the Canyon, five at least.

Your response: Hold up, this doesn't exactly sound like a chance encounter.

NPC: We're thinking the same thought, then. Maybe the data on those cubes will tell us. I do have a suspicion, though. But I won't say it out loud before we've had a look at that data.

NPC: You still need to retrieve those cubes.

NPC: I assume you had a look at that data by now. I'd ask you to get out of my sight if you hadn't.

Your response: All the files on those cubes had very recent access timestamps. That data was read, even before I did.

NPC: So this data was read, possibly even manipulated, before it even reached us, and the City knew the route of our courier. Quite obviously, despite our precautions, data is leaving the Canyon after all. Something out here is connected. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: I have good news and bad. The good news is that this time, the job IS a hack. Are you in?

Your response: Yes I am. I assume that the bad news is what it is that you need hacked?

Your response: You asked for a moment, now I still need one.

NPC: Hurry up, then. That open connection needs to close as soon as possible.

NPC: Not exactly, but the bad news is that we have confirmed that there is an open connection leading here, into the Canyon. We've traced the signal, and it is leading right into the Canyon Facility, but we couldn't pinpoint its exact location. So you're gonna have to look for it, I guess. Some terminal, data interface, something that looks out of place. And it is definitely in the Canyon itself, not in some cave or building. Find it, break its encryption, and get its log files.

Your response: How could such a line be open without anyone in the Canyon knowing about it?

NPC: It couldn't. Or at least, that's what I suspect. But we won't know for sure until you get us these logs. So hurry up and get them!

NPC: Get me those log files! The connection leads somewhere inside the Canyon Facility!

NPC: Did you find it? What do the logs say?

Your response: I could only read the header info. The log itself is heavily encrypted. I think the line had already existed before the movement set up shop in this Canyon. Forgotten infrastructure.

NPC: Yes. That would be a classic attack vector: Nobody is aware that the old infrastructure even still exists, so it is not actively monitored and not secured. But it works, and the attacker exploits it.

Your response: You got that right. I can't even count how many systems I entered myself using similar techniques. Old, unmonitored parts of a system are the easiest to compromise.

NPC: This is exactly why we make do without any connection to the outside. Not by choice, but by sheer necessity. This line was found by an outside attacker - in this case, City agents - and has been exploited against us for who knows how long. So keep this as a warning example: Don't open a connection to the outside from here. Not even for five minutes.

Your response: Bit difficult to work under these conditions, but I guess I'll manage.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Hacking Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Hacking skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Nothing to Hack
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 5 × Courier Data Cube
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience

entries.title: Mission 3: The Open Line
entries.description: Somewhere in the CANYON FACILITY, a data line nobody knew about is still live. Find it, hack it and recover its log, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: The Courier Ran
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect Data Line Log
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

entries.title: Mission 1: What Comes Back
entries.description: Find the handler Marek Toth in the TG HQ - BARRACKS and hear what happens to the people he sends into the City, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Marek Toth
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Every recruit that specializes in the field of infiltration we've ever gotten thought that 'getting in' is the difficult part of the job. It isn't. Let me tell you: We have never once lost anybody on the way in. Where we lose them comes after. Are you willing to learn?

Your response: I am, but I find it hard to believe that you never lost anyone on the way in.

Your response: Yes, but I'll need a moment, first.

Your response: This is a joke, right? If you've never lost anyone on the way in, you're aiming at the wrong targets. I can't learn anything from you. I'm out.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: So I may have exaggerated slightly for emphasis. That's not important. I'm gonna send you to Marek Toth in the Barracks. He's been running people into the City for years. And whatever comes back, he's the one who has to deal with that, as well.

Your response: What do you mean, 'whatever comes back'?

NPC: Oh, you will find out, believe you me. Talk to Toth. What he will tell you will be the most honest answer to that question possible, since he's the one who has to look at them.

NPC: That's close enough. What makes you come here? Are you reporting for infiltration duty?

Your response: No, at least not yet, I guess. Jones sent me.

NPC: I see. So she wants me to explain what we do around here. We put our people into the City is what it is. We create the best covers for them we can afford, hope that they last slightly longer than the previous guy did, and lament how little support we can give them.

Your response: I had come to believe that some of them do come back?

NPC: Oh, they do. The coming back is not the issue. Well, sometimes we just lose contact. Most people come back, no problem. But, you see, they're never quite the same when they do. They're getting a taste of the 'sweet life' that the City uses to pacify its populace. And let me tell you: That siren song is strong. So the failures aren't the ones who get caught. The ones who settle in are the problem. You can never tell if what they have is a good cover, or... well, a life.

Your response: So how can you tell the difference?

NPC: That's the problem right there. I can't. There are just the ones I worry about, and they are the ones that do not in fact complain. I mean, have you ever met anyone who has nothing to complain about? ...I think I've said all I can, really. Probably more than I should have.

NPC: I have nothing more to say to you. At least for now.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Toth yet. He's in the Barracks.

NPC: You look thoughtful. What did Toth tell you?

Your response: Funny thing is, getting people out never even came up. Not once. His problem is the opposite: the longer they stay in the City, the less they're themselves. They stop complaining and start building a life there. We're losing them, basically.

NPC: That's the problem right there. The City is comfortable. Rebelling against it from some stony Canyon... isn't. And that's fine, while you haven't actually experienced the comfort. But once you do, the politics slowly start ebbing away. That's the one weapon the enemy has, to which the movement has no counter. We'll get back to that.

NPC: You're back, good. This time, there is a practical problem I'm gonna task you with resolving, instead of a lecture about the problems with infiltration we currently have.

Your response: Sounds good. What is it?

Your response: In a moment.

NPC: Makes no difference, I guess. The problem doesn't resolve itself.

NPC: Here's the thing: When we actually do exfiltrate people from the City, we can't lead them through the Canyon entrance. Virtually all of the City's eyes are pointed at that gate. So we lead them through Canyon Cave 3. Only problem: That cave is very popular among the wildlife, and it's time to decimate it again. Kill eight of whatever has moved into there, so that our exfiltration route is usable again.

Your response: That sounds pressing. How many people are currently depending on that route being open?

NPC: Relax. So far, it's only five people waiting, and they haven't waited long, yet. But let's not let that number get bigger, and that waiting time longer, shall we?

NPC: The route through Canyon Cave 3 is still not clear.

NPC: Good work. The route is open again. In fact, one of the people who needed it has used it already.

Your response: That's good to hear. Who was it that used the route?

NPC: Yeah. About him. His name is Cass Roeder, has been inside the City for years. His debrief was flawless, he said all the right things. Given what you heard from Toth, that's precisely what should worry us. Get your breath back, then talk to me again.

NPC: So. This one will be ugly, I won't pretend otherwise. I also won't pretend that the evidence is conclusive, or that we can be absolutely certain. But we have to do it anyway. In, or out. Tell me.

Your response: In.

Your response: Can I... get some time to think about this?

NPC: Oh yes, absolutely. Think about it properly, since I am asking you to act on a judgment rather than a proof.

NPC: Then let me lay it out for you plainly: Roeder was not turned, was not paid, and he has betrayed nothing. His 'crime' is liking it in there. And he has started describing the City life in a way that is starting to spread through the Canyon.

Your response: Well, that's hardly treason, is it?

NPC: It is not. If it were, I would not have to ask you to deal with him, but put him in front of a tribunal. We have to consider the ongoing survival of our movement, though. And an honest man describing a comfortable life with the enemy will empty the Canyon faster than any City operation ever could. So go deal with a threat to our continued existence.

NPC: My friend! Great to meet another infiltrator, I'm really pleased! Wanna go for a couple of cold ones, and exchange war stories from behind enemy lines?

Your response: Sure, but first, tell me: What is it really like, over there in the City?

NPC: Oh, let me tell you, if they send you there, that's gonna be the best assignment of your life. The food, the quiet... no one I met over there is any kind of monster, they're actually really nice people!

Your response: So why did you come back at all, and not stay with your new friends?

NPC: I got the communication to report back, so I did, but then I'm gonna head back- Wait just a minute! I see now where this conversation is going. Let's get this over with, then.

NPC: ...

NPC: Roeder is still in the Facility, still talking too much.

NPC: I can see by the look on your face that the deed is done. What did he say, in the end?

Your response: He talked about the food and the quiet, said that nobody he met in the City was a monster, and that if I were ever sent there, it would be the best assignment I'd ever be on.

NPC: That's exactly what we feared. So at least we weren't wrong in our suspicions. So it had to be done. Doesn't mean we have to like it.

Your response: Do you think he was right, though? About the City, and the life there?

NPC: He probably was. But that is beside the point. A golden cage is still a cage. The people in the City are leading comfy lives, but they are not free. And we intend to free them. That is the good fight we are fighting.

Your response: Yeah, I guess I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Stealth Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Pistol Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: The Way Out
entries.description: The exfiltration route runs through CANYON CAVE 3, and the wildlife has moved back in. Clear %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(clear_cave) of them out, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: What Comes Back
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 8 × Denizens of Easy Canyon dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Every recruit that specializes in the field of infiltration we've ever gotten thought that 'getting in' is the difficult part of the job. It isn't. Let me tell you: We have never once lost anybody on the way in. Where we lose them comes after. Are you willing to learn?

Your response: I am, but I find it hard to believe that you never lost anyone on the way in.

Your response: Yes, but I'll need a moment, first.

Your response: This is a joke, right? If you've never lost anyone on the way in, you're aiming at the wrong targets. I can't learn anything from you. I'm out.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: So I may have exaggerated slightly for emphasis. That's not important. I'm gonna send you to Marek Toth in the Barracks. He's been running people into the City for years. And whatever comes back, he's the one who has to deal with that, as well.

Your response: What do you mean, 'whatever comes back'?

NPC: Oh, you will find out, believe you me. Talk to Toth. What he will tell you will be the most honest answer to that question possible, since he's the one who has to look at them.

NPC: That's close enough. What makes you come here? Are you reporting for infiltration duty?

Your response: No, at least not yet, I guess. Jones sent me.

NPC: I see. So she wants me to explain what we do around here. We put our people into the City is what it is. We create the best covers for them we can afford, hope that they last slightly longer than the previous guy did, and lament how little support we can give them.

Your response: I had come to believe that some of them do come back?

NPC: Oh, they do. The coming back is not the issue. Well, sometimes we just lose contact. Most people come back, no problem. But, you see, they're never quite the same when they do. They're getting a taste of the 'sweet life' that the City uses to pacify its populace. And let me tell you: That siren song is strong. So the failures aren't the ones who get caught. The ones who settle in are the problem. You can never tell if what they have is a good cover, or... well, a life.

Your response: So how can you tell the difference?

NPC: That's the problem right there. I can't. There are just the ones I worry about, and they are the ones that do not in fact complain. I mean, have you ever met anyone who has nothing to complain about? ...I think I've said all I can, really. Probably more than I should have.

NPC: I have nothing more to say to you. At least for now.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Toth yet. He's in the Barracks.

NPC: You look thoughtful. What did Toth tell you?

Your response: Funny thing is, getting people out never even came up. Not once. His problem is the opposite: the longer they stay in the City, the less they're themselves. They stop complaining and start building a life there. We're losing them, basically.

NPC: That's the problem right there. The City is comfortable. Rebelling against it from some stony Canyon... isn't. And that's fine, while you haven't actually experienced the comfort. But once you do, the politics slowly start ebbing away. That's the one weapon the enemy has, to which the movement has no counter. We'll get back to that.

NPC: You're back, good. This time, there is a practical problem I'm gonna task you with resolving, instead of a lecture about the problems with infiltration we currently have.

Your response: Sounds good. What is it?

Your response: In a moment.

NPC: Makes no difference, I guess. The problem doesn't resolve itself.

NPC: Here's the thing: When we actually do exfiltrate people from the City, we can't lead them through the Canyon entrance. Virtually all of the City's eyes are pointed at that gate. So we lead them through Canyon Cave 3. Only problem: That cave is very popular among the wildlife, and it's time to decimate it again. Kill eight of whatever has moved into there, so that our exfiltration route is usable again.

Your response: That sounds pressing. How many people are currently depending on that route being open?

NPC: Relax. So far, it's only five people waiting, and they haven't waited long, yet. But let's not let that number get bigger, and that waiting time longer, shall we?

NPC: The route through Canyon Cave 3 is still not clear.

NPC: Good work. The route is open again. In fact, one of the people who needed it has used it already.

Your response: That's good to hear. Who was it that used the route?

NPC: Yeah. About him. His name is Cass Roeder, has been inside the City for years. His debrief was flawless, he said all the right things. Given what you heard from Toth, that's precisely what should worry us. Get your breath back, then talk to me again.

NPC: So. This one will be ugly, I won't pretend otherwise. I also won't pretend that the evidence is conclusive, or that we can be absolutely certain. But we have to do it anyway. In, or out. Tell me.

Your response: In.

Your response: Can I... get some time to think about this?

NPC: Oh yes, absolutely. Think about it properly, since I am asking you to act on a judgment rather than a proof.

NPC: Then let me lay it out for you plainly: Roeder was not turned, was not paid, and he has betrayed nothing. His 'crime' is liking it in there. And he has started describing the City life in a way that is starting to spread through the Canyon.

Your response: Well, that's hardly treason, is it?

NPC: It is not. If it were, I would not have to ask you to deal with him, but put him in front of a tribunal. We have to consider the ongoing survival of our movement, though. And an honest man describing a comfortable life with the enemy will empty the Canyon faster than any City operation ever could. So go deal with a threat to our continued existence.

NPC: My friend! Great to meet another infiltrator, I'm really pleased! Wanna go for a couple of cold ones, and exchange war stories from behind enemy lines?

Your response: Sure, but first, tell me: What is it really like, over there in the City?

NPC: Oh, let me tell you, if they send you there, that's gonna be the best assignment of your life. The food, the quiet... no one I met over there is any kind of monster, they're actually really nice people!

Your response: So why did you come back at all, and not stay with your new friends?

NPC: I got the communication to report back, so I did, but then I'm gonna head back- Wait just a minute! I see now where this conversation is going. Let's get this over with, then.

NPC: ...

NPC: Roeder is still in the Facility, still talking too much.

NPC: I can see by the look on your face that the deed is done. What did he say, in the end?

Your response: He talked about the food and the quiet, said that nobody he met in the City was a monster, and that if I were ever sent there, it would be the best assignment I'd ever be on.

NPC: That's exactly what we feared. So at least we weren't wrong in our suspicions. So it had to be done. Doesn't mean we have to like it.

Your response: Do you think he was right, though? About the City, and the life there?

NPC: He probably was. But that is beside the point. A golden cage is still a cage. The people in the City are leading comfy lives, but they are not free. And we intend to free them. That is the good fight we are fighting.

Your response: Yeah, I guess I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Stealth Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Pistol Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 3: The Sweet Life
entries.description: Cass Roeder came back from the City, and he liked it there. Deal with him in the CANYON FACILITY, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: The Way Out
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat Cass Roeder
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Every recruit that specializes in the field of infiltration we've ever gotten thought that 'getting in' is the difficult part of the job. It isn't. Let me tell you: We have never once lost anybody on the way in. Where we lose them comes after. Are you willing to learn?

Your response: I am, but I find it hard to believe that you never lost anyone on the way in.

Your response: Yes, but I'll need a moment, first.

Your response: This is a joke, right? If you've never lost anyone on the way in, you're aiming at the wrong targets. I can't learn anything from you. I'm out.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: So I may have exaggerated slightly for emphasis. That's not important. I'm gonna send you to Marek Toth in the Barracks. He's been running people into the City for years. And whatever comes back, he's the one who has to deal with that, as well.

Your response: What do you mean, 'whatever comes back'?

NPC: Oh, you will find out, believe you me. Talk to Toth. What he will tell you will be the most honest answer to that question possible, since he's the one who has to look at them.

NPC: That's close enough. What makes you come here? Are you reporting for infiltration duty?

Your response: No, at least not yet, I guess. Jones sent me.

NPC: I see. So she wants me to explain what we do around here. We put our people into the City is what it is. We create the best covers for them we can afford, hope that they last slightly longer than the previous guy did, and lament how little support we can give them.

Your response: I had come to believe that some of them do come back?

NPC: Oh, they do. The coming back is not the issue. Well, sometimes we just lose contact. Most people come back, no problem. But, you see, they're never quite the same when they do. They're getting a taste of the 'sweet life' that the City uses to pacify its populace. And let me tell you: That siren song is strong. So the failures aren't the ones who get caught. The ones who settle in are the problem. You can never tell if what they have is a good cover, or... well, a life.

Your response: So how can you tell the difference?

NPC: That's the problem right there. I can't. There are just the ones I worry about, and they are the ones that do not in fact complain. I mean, have you ever met anyone who has nothing to complain about? ...I think I've said all I can, really. Probably more than I should have.

NPC: I have nothing more to say to you. At least for now.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Toth yet. He's in the Barracks.

NPC: You look thoughtful. What did Toth tell you?

Your response: Funny thing is, getting people out never even came up. Not once. His problem is the opposite: the longer they stay in the City, the less they're themselves. They stop complaining and start building a life there. We're losing them, basically.

NPC: That's the problem right there. The City is comfortable. Rebelling against it from some stony Canyon... isn't. And that's fine, while you haven't actually experienced the comfort. But once you do, the politics slowly start ebbing away. That's the one weapon the enemy has, to which the movement has no counter. We'll get back to that.

NPC: You're back, good. This time, there is a practical problem I'm gonna task you with resolving, instead of a lecture about the problems with infiltration we currently have.

Your response: Sounds good. What is it?

Your response: In a moment.

NPC: Makes no difference, I guess. The problem doesn't resolve itself.

NPC: Here's the thing: When we actually do exfiltrate people from the City, we can't lead them through the Canyon entrance. Virtually all of the City's eyes are pointed at that gate. So we lead them through Canyon Cave 3. Only problem: That cave is very popular among the wildlife, and it's time to decimate it again. Kill eight of whatever has moved into there, so that our exfiltration route is usable again.

Your response: That sounds pressing. How many people are currently depending on that route being open?

NPC: Relax. So far, it's only five people waiting, and they haven't waited long, yet. But let's not let that number get bigger, and that waiting time longer, shall we?

NPC: The route through Canyon Cave 3 is still not clear.

NPC: Good work. The route is open again. In fact, one of the people who needed it has used it already.

Your response: That's good to hear. Who was it that used the route?

NPC: Yeah. About him. His name is Cass Roeder, has been inside the City for years. His debrief was flawless, he said all the right things. Given what you heard from Toth, that's precisely what should worry us. Get your breath back, then talk to me again.

NPC: So. This one will be ugly, I won't pretend otherwise. I also won't pretend that the evidence is conclusive, or that we can be absolutely certain. But we have to do it anyway. In, or out. Tell me.

Your response: In.

Your response: Can I... get some time to think about this?

NPC: Oh yes, absolutely. Think about it properly, since I am asking you to act on a judgment rather than a proof.

NPC: Then let me lay it out for you plainly: Roeder was not turned, was not paid, and he has betrayed nothing. His 'crime' is liking it in there. And he has started describing the City life in a way that is starting to spread through the Canyon.

Your response: Well, that's hardly treason, is it?

NPC: It is not. If it were, I would not have to ask you to deal with him, but put him in front of a tribunal. We have to consider the ongoing survival of our movement, though. And an honest man describing a comfortable life with the enemy will empty the Canyon faster than any City operation ever could. So go deal with a threat to our continued existence.

NPC: My friend! Great to meet another infiltrator, I'm really pleased! Wanna go for a couple of cold ones, and exchange war stories from behind enemy lines?

Your response: Sure, but first, tell me: What is it really like, over there in the City?

NPC: Oh, let me tell you, if they send you there, that's gonna be the best assignment of your life. The food, the quiet... no one I met over there is any kind of monster, they're actually really nice people!

Your response: So why did you come back at all, and not stay with your new friends?

NPC: I got the communication to report back, so I did, but then I'm gonna head back- Wait just a minute! I see now where this conversation is going. Let's get this over with, then.

NPC: ...

NPC: Roeder is still in the Facility, still talking too much.

NPC: I can see by the look on your face that the deed is done. What did he say, in the end?

Your response: He talked about the food and the quiet, said that nobody he met in the City was a monster, and that if I were ever sent there, it would be the best assignment I'd ever be on.

NPC: That's exactly what we feared. So at least we weren't wrong in our suspicions. So it had to be done. Doesn't mean we have to like it.

Your response: Do you think he was right, though? About the City, and the life there?

NPC: He probably was. But that is beside the point. A golden cage is still a cage. The people in the City are leading comfy lives, but they are not free. And we intend to free them. That is the good fight we are fighting.

Your response: Yeah, I guess I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Stealth Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Pistol Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 1: Benefit of the Doubt
entries.description: The Canyon distrusts Monks. Start earning its trust by putting down %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(clear_cave) of whatever crawls around CANYON CAVE 2, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 8 × Denizens of Very Easy Canyon dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The Canyon distrusts Monks. That can't possibly be a surprise to you, given the history between our movement and the tyranny of the Monks. So you're gonna have to earn our trust by being useful. Until then, best I can do is give you the benefit of the doubt. Will you take that chance?

Your response: I intend to prove myself, ten times over.

Your response: I will. You're gonna have to give me a moment, though.

Your response: I'm going to prove myself, alright. But not to you. Please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then let's start with something straightforward. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. If you cannot fight, you are just a liability, another mouth to feed. So let's see how you handle that.

Your response: Is that really all there is to it?

NPC: For now? Yes. After that? Well, let's see. The job I actually want you for isn't one I'm gonna describe to someone I haven't watched work.

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still crawling. Prove yourself to me.

NPC: That was a satisfactory performance. So aren't you going to ask me what I have been assessing you for?

Your response: *sigh* What have you been assessing me for?

NPC: Let me explain part of the problem: We have no courts. No judges. No prisons. At most, we can convene a tribunal, for the very few cases where one can actually do any good around here. What we do have, though, is people trained to ask questions, and people trained to give believable answers. More details when you get back to me.

NPC: Right. So, there is an accusation on my desk. I need you to look into the case.

Your response: Who is it that is being accused here? And of what?

Your response: I will, just give me five minutes.

NPC: Yeah. Accusations don't go stale, they keep. Surprisingly well.

NPC: To learn that, I'm going to send you straight to the source: Reva Sikora is the person who made the accusation. And I want to be perfectly clear, here: I want the accuser assessed as much as their accusation.

Your response: Understood. But what is the charge?

NPC: The charge is nothing of the usual sort, like theft or treason. It is that Emilia Bracha has quietly stopped believing. That's all. But perhaps you should let Sikora put it in her own words.

NPC: Emilia Bracha has stopped believing in the cause of the Canyon! Why won't somebody do something about her spreading falsehoods?! The movement cannot afford to suffer the likes of her!

Your response: Alright, I'm listening. What did she actually do?

NPC: She did what? What she did? Well, nothing! It's what she has been saying, and who she has been saying it to!

Your response: So explain to me where the crime is.

NPC: Why won't anybody take this seriously?! Belief is the only thing that holds this movement together! Someone quietly dissolving it is doing more damage to us than even the worst of City agents ever could!

Your response: What's your game? What do you get out of this accusation, personally?

NPC: What do you mean? Why would you ask a thing like that?! I don't have to stand here and take this abuse! Maybe your own beliefs are wearing thin too, huh? How about that!

NPC: I have nothing further to say to the likes of you!

NPC: You still need to hear Sikora out first.

NPC: So you talked to Sikora. What's your read on her?

Your response: Hard to tell how much of her accusation is true, but she clearly has something to gain by making it.

NPC: Most accusers have their own reasons. That much is not surprising. But, and this may be uncomfortable to you: That the accusation is made in self-interest does not make it false. So take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So. The next part is what you might call 'the job itself'. Nobody else in the Canyon wants it, and you're uniquely qualified to deal with it. So what do you say? Will you take it?

Your response: What does taking the job mean, exactly?

Your response: Let me prepare for this, first.

NPC: You need to be sure about what you're doing, because I'm giving you all the leeway. I will not review the outcome. It's all up to you.

NPC: You are to question Bracha yourself, and then act on what you conclude. There will be no tribunal, and no appeal afterwards. There will be a judge, a jury, and an executioner. And it will all be you.

Your response: So what if I conclude that she is innocent?

NPC: Then nothing happens, and Sikora will be furious. It will be up to you. It may not be what the movement expects. But don't let that make you waver.

NPC: I can guess why you're here. I have been expecting this. At least ask me properly.

Your response: Emilia Bracha, do you still believe in the movement?

NPC: I do not. I think the movement is misguided, and that it is trying to save people from something they do not wish to be saved from. My husband was an infiltrator. When he came back here from his assignments, he described the fulfilled, content lives the people in the City live. And the movement couldn't have that, so he was killed. And I will never forgive them for it.

Your response: So this is what you have been telling people around here?

NPC: I have. I'd much rather be honest with people than keep them in for a cause that has lost all its credibility to me. So what is it you're going to do about it?

Your response: I was prepared to give you what I was given recently: The benefit of the doubt. But I see that you are beyond salvation.

NPC: Salvation? There is no salvation! And when you realize that, in maybe a year, remember me!

NPC: ...

NPC: You still need to question Bracha.

NPC: You still need to deliver the verdict on Bracha.

NPC: So what did Bracha say? Did you ask her properly?

Your response: Her husband turned, when he infiltrated the City. And when he was brought to justice for it, she lost her conviction.

NPC: That is a serious reason, not to be dismissed easily. The siren song of the City is strong. And that's precisely why the movement wanted a Monk like you to deal with this situation. You'd be willing to listen to the reason, first.

Your response: I was prepared to give her what you gave me: The benefit of the doubt. But she didn't deserve it. Even though the accusation seemed so flimsy.

NPC: No less flimsy than my earlier accusation that your kind would not be trustworthy, simply because of a tyranny that ended quite some time ago. The benefit of the doubt is a good thing to give, and a better thing to withdraw, when doubt turns into certainty. Even though that would usually be a job for courts. We have none, so that's all there is to it.

Your response: I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send an Attack Module your way. You've earned it. Keep your Aggressive Psi Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: The Accuser
entries.description: Reva Sikora claims Emilia Bracha has stopped believing. Hear her out in the CANYON FACILITY, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Benefit of the Doubt
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Reva Sikora
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The Canyon distrusts Monks. That can't possibly be a surprise to you, given the history between our movement and the tyranny of the Monks. So you're gonna have to earn our trust by being useful. Until then, best I can do is give you the benefit of the doubt. Will you take that chance?

Your response: I intend to prove myself, ten times over.

Your response: I will. You're gonna have to give me a moment, though.

Your response: I'm going to prove myself, alright. But not to you. Please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then let's start with something straightforward. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. If you cannot fight, you are just a liability, another mouth to feed. So let's see how you handle that.

Your response: Is that really all there is to it?

NPC: For now? Yes. After that? Well, let's see. The job I actually want you for isn't one I'm gonna describe to someone I haven't watched work.

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still crawling. Prove yourself to me.

NPC: That was a satisfactory performance. So aren't you going to ask me what I have been assessing you for?

Your response: *sigh* What have you been assessing me for?

NPC: Let me explain part of the problem: We have no courts. No judges. No prisons. At most, we can convene a tribunal, for the very few cases where one can actually do any good around here. What we do have, though, is people trained to ask questions, and people trained to give believable answers. More details when you get back to me.

NPC: Right. So, there is an accusation on my desk. I need you to look into the case.

Your response: Who is it that is being accused here? And of what?

Your response: I will, just give me five minutes.

NPC: Yeah. Accusations don't go stale, they keep. Surprisingly well.

NPC: To learn that, I'm going to send you straight to the source: Reva Sikora is the person who made the accusation. And I want to be perfectly clear, here: I want the accuser assessed as much as their accusation.

Your response: Understood. But what is the charge?

NPC: The charge is nothing of the usual sort, like theft or treason. It is that Emilia Bracha has quietly stopped believing. That's all. But perhaps you should let Sikora put it in her own words.

NPC: Emilia Bracha has stopped believing in the cause of the Canyon! Why won't somebody do something about her spreading falsehoods?! The movement cannot afford to suffer the likes of her!

Your response: Alright, I'm listening. What did she actually do?

NPC: She did what? What she did? Well, nothing! It's what she has been saying, and who she has been saying it to!

Your response: So explain to me where the crime is.

NPC: Why won't anybody take this seriously?! Belief is the only thing that holds this movement together! Someone quietly dissolving it is doing more damage to us than even the worst of City agents ever could!

Your response: What's your game? What do you get out of this accusation, personally?

NPC: What do you mean? Why would you ask a thing like that?! I don't have to stand here and take this abuse! Maybe your own beliefs are wearing thin too, huh? How about that!

NPC: I have nothing further to say to the likes of you!

NPC: You still need to hear Sikora out first.

NPC: So you talked to Sikora. What's your read on her?

Your response: Hard to tell how much of her accusation is true, but she clearly has something to gain by making it.

NPC: Most accusers have their own reasons. That much is not surprising. But, and this may be uncomfortable to you: That the accusation is made in self-interest does not make it false. So take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So. The next part is what you might call 'the job itself'. Nobody else in the Canyon wants it, and you're uniquely qualified to deal with it. So what do you say? Will you take it?

Your response: What does taking the job mean, exactly?

Your response: Let me prepare for this, first.

NPC: You need to be sure about what you're doing, because I'm giving you all the leeway. I will not review the outcome. It's all up to you.

NPC: You are to question Bracha yourself, and then act on what you conclude. There will be no tribunal, and no appeal afterwards. There will be a judge, a jury, and an executioner. And it will all be you.

Your response: So what if I conclude that she is innocent?

NPC: Then nothing happens, and Sikora will be furious. It will be up to you. It may not be what the movement expects. But don't let that make you waver.

NPC: I can guess why you're here. I have been expecting this. At least ask me properly.

Your response: Emilia Bracha, do you still believe in the movement?

NPC: I do not. I think the movement is misguided, and that it is trying to save people from something they do not wish to be saved from. My husband was an infiltrator. When he came back here from his assignments, he described the fulfilled, content lives the people in the City live. And the movement couldn't have that, so he was killed. And I will never forgive them for it.

Your response: So this is what you have been telling people around here?

NPC: I have. I'd much rather be honest with people than keep them in for a cause that has lost all its credibility to me. So what is it you're going to do about it?

Your response: I was prepared to give you what I was given recently: The benefit of the doubt. But I see that you are beyond salvation.

NPC: Salvation? There is no salvation! And when you realize that, in maybe a year, remember me!

NPC: ...

NPC: You still need to question Bracha.

NPC: You still need to deliver the verdict on Bracha.

NPC: So what did Bracha say? Did you ask her properly?

Your response: Her husband turned, when he infiltrated the City. And when he was brought to justice for it, she lost her conviction.

NPC: That is a serious reason, not to be dismissed easily. The siren song of the City is strong. And that's precisely why the movement wanted a Monk like you to deal with this situation. You'd be willing to listen to the reason, first.

Your response: I was prepared to give her what you gave me: The benefit of the doubt. But she didn't deserve it. Even though the accusation seemed so flimsy.

NPC: No less flimsy than my earlier accusation that your kind would not be trustworthy, simply because of a tyranny that ended quite some time ago. The benefit of the doubt is a good thing to give, and a better thing to withdraw, when doubt turns into certainty. Even though that would usually be a job for courts. We have none, so that's all there is to it.

Your response: I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send an Attack Module your way. You've earned it. Keep your Aggressive Psi Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.
