entries.title: Mission 3: Judge, Jury and Executioner
entries.description: Question Emilia Bracha outside the Rodriguez Barracks in the CANYON FACILITY and act on what you conclude. Nobody will review your verdict. Then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: The Accuser
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Emilia Bracha
• Defeat Emilia Bracha
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The Canyon distrusts Monks. That can't possibly be a surprise to you, given the history between our movement and the tyranny of the Monks. So you're gonna have to earn our trust by being useful. Until then, best I can do is give you the benefit of the doubt. Will you take that chance?

Your response: I intend to prove myself, ten times over.

Your response: I will. You're gonna have to give me a moment, though.

Your response: I'm going to prove myself, alright. But not to you. Please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then let's start with something straightforward. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. If you cannot fight, you are just a liability, another mouth to feed. So let's see how you handle that.

Your response: Is that really all there is to it?

NPC: For now? Yes. After that? Well, let's see. The job I actually want you for isn't one I'm gonna describe to someone I haven't watched work.

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still crawling. Prove yourself to me.

NPC: That was a satisfactory performance. So aren't you going to ask me what I have been assessing you for?

Your response: *sigh* What have you been assessing me for?

NPC: Let me explain part of the problem: We have no courts. No judges. No prisons. At most, we can convene a tribunal, for the very few cases where one can actually do any good around here. What we do have, though, is people trained to ask questions, and people trained to give believable answers. More details when you get back to me.

NPC: Right. So, there is an accusation on my desk. I need you to look into the case.

Your response: Who is it that is being accused here? And of what?

Your response: I will, just give me five minutes.

NPC: Yeah. Accusations don't go stale, they keep. Surprisingly well.

NPC: To learn that, I'm going to send you straight to the source: Reva Sikora is the person who made the accusation. And I want to be perfectly clear, here: I want the accuser assessed as much as their accusation.

Your response: Understood. But what is the charge?

NPC: The charge is nothing of the usual sort, like theft or treason. It is that Emilia Bracha has quietly stopped believing. That's all. But perhaps you should let Sikora put it in her own words.

NPC: Emilia Bracha has stopped believing in the cause of the Canyon! Why won't somebody do something about her spreading falsehoods?! The movement cannot afford to suffer the likes of her!

Your response: Alright, I'm listening. What did she actually do?

NPC: She did what? What she did? Well, nothing! It's what she has been saying, and who she has been saying it to!

Your response: So explain to me where the crime is.

NPC: Why won't anybody take this seriously?! Belief is the only thing that holds this movement together! Someone quietly dissolving it is doing more damage to us than even the worst of City agents ever could!

Your response: What's your game? What do you get out of this accusation, personally?

NPC: What do you mean? Why would you ask a thing like that?! I don't have to stand here and take this abuse! Maybe your own beliefs are wearing thin too, huh? How about that!

NPC: I have nothing further to say to the likes of you!

NPC: You still need to hear Sikora out first.

NPC: So you talked to Sikora. What's your read on her?

Your response: Hard to tell how much of her accusation is true, but she clearly has something to gain by making it.

NPC: Most accusers have their own reasons. That much is not surprising. But, and this may be uncomfortable to you: That the accusation is made in self-interest does not make it false. So take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So. The next part is what you might call 'the job itself'. Nobody else in the Canyon wants it, and you're uniquely qualified to deal with it. So what do you say? Will you take it?

Your response: What does taking the job mean, exactly?

Your response: Let me prepare for this, first.

NPC: You need to be sure about what you're doing, because I'm giving you all the leeway. I will not review the outcome. It's all up to you.

NPC: You are to question Bracha yourself, and then act on what you conclude. There will be no tribunal, and no appeal afterwards. There will be a judge, a jury, and an executioner. And it will all be you.

Your response: So what if I conclude that she is innocent?

NPC: Then nothing happens, and Sikora will be furious. It will be up to you. It may not be what the movement expects. But don't let that make you waver.

NPC: I can guess why you're here. I have been expecting this. At least ask me properly.

Your response: Emilia Bracha, do you still believe in the movement?

NPC: I do not. I think the movement is misguided, and that it is trying to save people from something they do not wish to be saved from. My husband was an infiltrator. When he came back here from his assignments, he described the fulfilled, content lives the people in the City live. And the movement couldn't have that, so he was killed. And I will never forgive them for it.

Your response: So this is what you have been telling people around here?

NPC: I have. I'd much rather be honest with people than keep them in for a cause that has lost all its credibility to me. So what is it you're going to do about it?

Your response: I was prepared to give you what I was given recently: The benefit of the doubt. But I see that you are beyond salvation.

NPC: Salvation? There is no salvation! And when you realize that, in maybe a year, remember me!

NPC: ...

NPC: You still need to question Bracha.

NPC: You still need to deliver the verdict on Bracha.

NPC: So what did Bracha say? Did you ask her properly?

Your response: Her husband turned, when he infiltrated the City. And when he was brought to justice for it, she lost her conviction.

NPC: That is a serious reason, not to be dismissed easily. The siren song of the City is strong. And that's precisely why the movement wanted a Monk like you to deal with this situation. You'd be willing to listen to the reason, first.

Your response: I was prepared to give her what you gave me: The benefit of the doubt. But she didn't deserve it. Even though the accusation seemed so flimsy.

NPC: No less flimsy than my earlier accusation that your kind would not be trustworthy, simply because of a tyranny that ended quite some time ago. The benefit of the doubt is a good thing to give, and a better thing to withdraw, when doubt turns into certainty. Even though that would usually be a job for courts. We have none, so that's all there is to it.

Your response: I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send an Attack Module your way. You've earned it. Keep your Aggressive Psi Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 1: The Recruiter
entries.description: Find the recruiter Halina Brecht in the TG HQ - BARRACKS and hear what she promises the people who come to the gates, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Halina Brecht
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me state the problem plainly: We are not fighting the City for territory or resources, we are fighting over people. And while we live in this Canyon, the people in the City have jobs and are mostly fine. So do you think we can argue someone out of being comfortable?

Your response: Intriguing. Do go on.

Your response: I may need to get back to you on that.

Your response: This is so far beneath me, honestly, it is insulting. Please leave my apartment. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: First, I'm going to send you to Halina Brecht in the Barracks. She is the one responsible for the recruitment of our movement. You should ask her what it is that she promises those willing to listen.

Your response: Are her promises truthful, or does she peddle falsehoods?

NPC: Talk to her. She will answer your question better than I ever could. Pay close attention to what she says, but even closer to the parts she doesn't mention. Go.

NPC: Welcome, my friend, to the Canyon! You will quickly understand what our movement is all about, and equally quick in joining up, once you... wait a minute, that's not why you're here, are you?

Your response: Jones sent me. I mean to hear what you tell those people who come to our gates.

NPC: This is what I tell them: You're here because deep down, you know the promises of the City to be false. It took your life, then rented it back to you, a bed, a wage and a number. And then it taught you to say 'thank you' for it, instead of wondering what happens when you ask the wrong question. Here, in the Canyon, nobody counts you, and nobody decides for you where to stand when the shooting starts. The City has a place for you: replaceable, fed, forgotten. We offer you a purpose, and people who will know your name!

Your response: Great rhetoric. So how much of all that survives the first month, here?

NPC: What do you think? What people who arrive here experience day to day, even when their heads are filled with ideas to the brim, is bad pay, worse food, and things crawling out of the caves to terrorize them at night. More than three quarters of our recruits disappear here and magically reappear in the City within half a year, telling tall tales of being abducted.

Your response: That's not a great success quota for your speech then, is it.

NPC: I'm not lying about what life in the Canyon is like. All I'm making is a claim about what we're all here for. In my personal opinion, that's the more important argument, and I absolutely stand by it, one hundred percent.

NPC: That's really all I have to say about it.

NPC: You have not spoken to Brecht yet. She is in the Barracks.

NPC: So what did you learn? Is her speech truthful, or a lie? Is it good, or bad? Is it successful, or failing?

Your response: Her rhetoric is flawless, and she manages not to say one falsehood. But her success rate leaves something to be desired. About three quarters of the recruits are back in the City within half a year.

NPC: That is a big number, make no mistake about it. But you assume that the best speech in the world would achieve a success rate of ten out of ten. My experience says that it doesn't. But you'll draw your own conclusions, anyway. Which is good. Get back to me in a bit.

NPC: So. Your next job will be unpleasant and administrative. But I need a preacher to do it, not a clerk. Will you do it?

Your response: For certain, but you have failed to tell me what it is, yet.

Your response: I will not falter. But you will need to give me a moment.

NPC: Sure. This matter has waited that long, it can wait a bit longer.

NPC: There are some lockers in HQ. We have no organized system here, people just set up their locker somewhere safe, put their stuff in it, then padlock it. Some of our dead sisters and brothers still have their locker up in HQ. They need to be cleared. Clear at least five of them, then bring me their contents, all the personal effects they left in there.

Your response: First you make me learn about Canyon propaganda, then you make me do a clerk's job. What am I supposed to make of this?

NPC: Nothing, yet. But a clerk would just bring five boxes with stuff in them, and a preacher will bring back five names with stories behind them. And that will be the only material you're ever going to work with. So go to HQ, and clear those lockers out.

NPC: You still need to clear those lockers.

NPC: Did you read the names on the labels? Have you read the stories behind the personal effects?

Your response: I did. And when I did, I noticed a name I glimpsed earlier, but it was listed as active. Might be a relative, perhaps. The name was 'Ruz'.

NPC: That would be Peter Ruz who's dead, and Stefan Ruz, who's still alive. That makes sense, and I think Stefan already knows. He's been going on about how our cause isn't worth it. And people are listening. So you may already guess what I expect next from you. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: The last job is a conversation. Plain and simple, and yet it will be the hardest thing I could ask of you. Are you ready?

Your response: I assume I am going to talk Stefan into not abandoning the movement.

Your response: Not yet.

NPC: Take your time, get ready, and then talk to me again.

NPC: That's exactly right. You are going to take his brother's effects to him personally, and you are going to make him believe all the more in the movement, not less.

Your response: So I am supposed to take his grief, twist it, and then turn him around, all the way.

NPC: Absolutely. And I won't pretend that it is anything other than that, I am fully aware what I am asking of you. The City buries its dead quietly and hopes their family stays quiet, too. The movement will call out its losses, by name. It will weep, it will mourn. And it will be stronger for it.

NPC: ...so why do we keep fighting a fight that we cannot possibly win? It is this simple truth... hang on. What are you carrying there? Oh no. Oh no. Please, don't show me. If this is what I think it is, I don't want to know.

Your response: Son, these are the earthly effects of your brother. May he rest in peace.

NPC: This... this is his picture of us two, on a drom hunt as little kids. And this... oh no, I cannot... Oh geez...

Your response: Your brother, Peter Ruz, fought the good fight, and he died a hero to our people. We will mourn his death together.

NPC: Thanks... Honestly, thank you. He was such a good person, always believed in the good cause. What am I supposed to do without my brother? He always knew what to do.

Your response: He always believed in the cause of our movement. And where he dropped the torch, you're going to pick it up, and carry it further, further than it's ever been. To honor his memory.

NPC: Yes. Yes, I will. And I have been telling people that our fight is pointless. Oh no, what have I done? Guys! Come back! I've made a terrible mistake! Our cause is just! Please, listen to me! We need to...

NPC: Please! I need to undo some of the damage I did!

NPC: You still need to carry the personal effects of Peter Ruz to his brother.

NPC: Ruz took the personal effects of his brother, I assume. So how did it go down?

Your response: He remembered how his brother always believed in the good cause. And that made him see the error of his ways.

NPC: That one concession is worth more than a hall full of people cheering. I hope you realize what a great service you have done to us. This is how the movement is held together.

Your response: Your turn to answer truthfully: Do you feel anything at all about how this was actually accomplished?

NPC: I do, absolutely. There is a whole rainbow of emotions going through me right now. And unless you can say the same about yourself, you're of no use to me.

Your response: I can.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send two modules your way, an aggressive and a passive one. I assume you understand the symbolism. You've earned them. Keep your Psi skills well trained, you're gonna need them. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: Names and Stories
entries.description: Clear %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(clear_lockers) sets of personal effects out of the fallen comrades' lockers in the TG HQ - BARRACKS, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: The Recruiter
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 5 × Personal Effects
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me state the problem plainly: We are not fighting the City for territory or resources, we are fighting over people. And while we live in this Canyon, the people in the City have jobs and are mostly fine. So do you think we can argue someone out of being comfortable?

Your response: Intriguing. Do go on.

Your response: I may need to get back to you on that.

Your response: This is so far beneath me, honestly, it is insulting. Please leave my apartment. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: First, I'm going to send you to Halina Brecht in the Barracks. She is the one responsible for the recruitment of our movement. You should ask her what it is that she promises those willing to listen.

Your response: Are her promises truthful, or does she peddle falsehoods?

NPC: Talk to her. She will answer your question better than I ever could. Pay close attention to what she says, but even closer to the parts she doesn't mention. Go.

NPC: Welcome, my friend, to the Canyon! You will quickly understand what our movement is all about, and equally quick in joining up, once you... wait a minute, that's not why you're here, are you?

Your response: Jones sent me. I mean to hear what you tell those people who come to our gates.

NPC: This is what I tell them: You're here because deep down, you know the promises of the City to be false. It took your life, then rented it back to you, a bed, a wage and a number. And then it taught you to say 'thank you' for it, instead of wondering what happens when you ask the wrong question. Here, in the Canyon, nobody counts you, and nobody decides for you where to stand when the shooting starts. The City has a place for you: replaceable, fed, forgotten. We offer you a purpose, and people who will know your name!

Your response: Great rhetoric. So how much of all that survives the first month, here?

NPC: What do you think? What people who arrive here experience day to day, even when their heads are filled with ideas to the brim, is bad pay, worse food, and things crawling out of the caves to terrorize them at night. More than three quarters of our recruits disappear here and magically reappear in the City within half a year, telling tall tales of being abducted.

Your response: That's not a great success quota for your speech then, is it.

NPC: I'm not lying about what life in the Canyon is like. All I'm making is a claim about what we're all here for. In my personal opinion, that's the more important argument, and I absolutely stand by it, one hundred percent.

NPC: That's really all I have to say about it.

NPC: You have not spoken to Brecht yet. She is in the Barracks.

NPC: So what did you learn? Is her speech truthful, or a lie? Is it good, or bad? Is it successful, or failing?

Your response: Her rhetoric is flawless, and she manages not to say one falsehood. But her success rate leaves something to be desired. About three quarters of the recruits are back in the City within half a year.

NPC: That is a big number, make no mistake about it. But you assume that the best speech in the world would achieve a success rate of ten out of ten. My experience says that it doesn't. But you'll draw your own conclusions, anyway. Which is good. Get back to me in a bit.

NPC: So. Your next job will be unpleasant and administrative. But I need a preacher to do it, not a clerk. Will you do it?

Your response: For certain, but you have failed to tell me what it is, yet.

Your response: I will not falter. But you will need to give me a moment.

NPC: Sure. This matter has waited that long, it can wait a bit longer.

NPC: There are some lockers in HQ. We have no organized system here, people just set up their locker somewhere safe, put their stuff in it, then padlock it. Some of our dead sisters and brothers still have their locker up in HQ. They need to be cleared. Clear at least five of them, then bring me their contents, all the personal effects they left in there.

Your response: First you make me learn about Canyon propaganda, then you make me do a clerk's job. What am I supposed to make of this?

NPC: Nothing, yet. But a clerk would just bring five boxes with stuff in them, and a preacher will bring back five names with stories behind them. And that will be the only material you're ever going to work with. So go to HQ, and clear those lockers out.

NPC: You still need to clear those lockers.

NPC: Did you read the names on the labels? Have you read the stories behind the personal effects?

Your response: I did. And when I did, I noticed a name I glimpsed earlier, but it was listed as active. Might be a relative, perhaps. The name was 'Ruz'.

NPC: That would be Peter Ruz who's dead, and Stefan Ruz, who's still alive. That makes sense, and I think Stefan already knows. He's been going on about how our cause isn't worth it. And people are listening. So you may already guess what I expect next from you. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: The last job is a conversation. Plain and simple, and yet it will be the hardest thing I could ask of you. Are you ready?

Your response: I assume I am going to talk Stefan into not abandoning the movement.

Your response: Not yet.

NPC: Take your time, get ready, and then talk to me again.

NPC: That's exactly right. You are going to take his brother's effects to him personally, and you are going to make him believe all the more in the movement, not less.

Your response: So I am supposed to take his grief, twist it, and then turn him around, all the way.

NPC: Absolutely. And I won't pretend that it is anything other than that, I am fully aware what I am asking of you. The City buries its dead quietly and hopes their family stays quiet, too. The movement will call out its losses, by name. It will weep, it will mourn. And it will be stronger for it.

NPC: ...so why do we keep fighting a fight that we cannot possibly win? It is this simple truth... hang on. What are you carrying there? Oh no. Oh no. Please, don't show me. If this is what I think it is, I don't want to know.

Your response: Son, these are the earthly effects of your brother. May he rest in peace.

NPC: This... this is his picture of us two, on a drom hunt as little kids. And this... oh no, I cannot... Oh geez...

Your response: Your brother, Peter Ruz, fought the good fight, and he died a hero to our people. We will mourn his death together.

NPC: Thanks... Honestly, thank you. He was such a good person, always believed in the good cause. What am I supposed to do without my brother? He always knew what to do.

Your response: He always believed in the cause of our movement. And where he dropped the torch, you're going to pick it up, and carry it further, further than it's ever been. To honor his memory.

NPC: Yes. Yes, I will. And I have been telling people that our fight is pointless. Oh no, what have I done? Guys! Come back! I've made a terrible mistake! Our cause is just! Please, listen to me! We need to...

NPC: Please! I need to undo some of the damage I did!

NPC: You still need to carry the personal effects of Peter Ruz to his brother.

NPC: Ruz took the personal effects of his brother, I assume. So how did it go down?

Your response: He remembered how his brother always believed in the good cause. And that made him see the error of his ways.

NPC: That one concession is worth more than a hall full of people cheering. I hope you realize what a great service you have done to us. This is how the movement is held together.

Your response: Your turn to answer truthfully: Do you feel anything at all about how this was actually accomplished?

NPC: I do, absolutely. There is a whole rainbow of emotions going through me right now. And unless you can say the same about yourself, you're of no use to me.

Your response: I can.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send two modules your way, an aggressive and a passive one. I assume you understand the symbolism. You've earned them. Keep your Psi skills well trained, you're gonna need them. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 3: Grief, Turned Around
entries.description: Take Peter Ruz's effects to his brother Stefan in the CANYON FACILITY and turn him back toward the movement, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: Names and Stories
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Stefan Ruz
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me state the problem plainly: We are not fighting the City for territory or resources, we are fighting over people. And while we live in this Canyon, the people in the City have jobs and are mostly fine. So do you think we can argue someone out of being comfortable?

Your response: Intriguing. Do go on.

Your response: I may need to get back to you on that.

Your response: This is so far beneath me, honestly, it is insulting. Please leave my apartment. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: First, I'm going to send you to Halina Brecht in the Barracks. She is the one responsible for the recruitment of our movement. You should ask her what it is that she promises those willing to listen.

Your response: Are her promises truthful, or does she peddle falsehoods?

NPC: Talk to her. She will answer your question better than I ever could. Pay close attention to what she says, but even closer to the parts she doesn't mention. Go.

NPC: Welcome, my friend, to the Canyon! You will quickly understand what our movement is all about, and equally quick in joining up, once you... wait a minute, that's not why you're here, are you?

Your response: Jones sent me. I mean to hear what you tell those people who come to our gates.

NPC: This is what I tell them: You're here because deep down, you know the promises of the City to be false. It took your life, then rented it back to you, a bed, a wage and a number. And then it taught you to say 'thank you' for it, instead of wondering what happens when you ask the wrong question. Here, in the Canyon, nobody counts you, and nobody decides for you where to stand when the shooting starts. The City has a place for you: replaceable, fed, forgotten. We offer you a purpose, and people who will know your name!

Your response: Great rhetoric. So how much of all that survives the first month, here?

NPC: What do you think? What people who arrive here experience day to day, even when their heads are filled with ideas to the brim, is bad pay, worse food, and things crawling out of the caves to terrorize them at night. More than three quarters of our recruits disappear here and magically reappear in the City within half a year, telling tall tales of being abducted.

Your response: That's not a great success quota for your speech then, is it.

NPC: I'm not lying about what life in the Canyon is like. All I'm making is a claim about what we're all here for. In my personal opinion, that's the more important argument, and I absolutely stand by it, one hundred percent.

NPC: That's really all I have to say about it.

NPC: You have not spoken to Brecht yet. She is in the Barracks.

NPC: So what did you learn? Is her speech truthful, or a lie? Is it good, or bad? Is it successful, or failing?

Your response: Her rhetoric is flawless, and she manages not to say one falsehood. But her success rate leaves something to be desired. About three quarters of the recruits are back in the City within half a year.

NPC: That is a big number, make no mistake about it. But you assume that the best speech in the world would achieve a success rate of ten out of ten. My experience says that it doesn't. But you'll draw your own conclusions, anyway. Which is good. Get back to me in a bit.

NPC: So. Your next job will be unpleasant and administrative. But I need a preacher to do it, not a clerk. Will you do it?

Your response: For certain, but you have failed to tell me what it is, yet.

Your response: I will not falter. But you will need to give me a moment.

NPC: Sure. This matter has waited that long, it can wait a bit longer.

NPC: There are some lockers in HQ. We have no organized system here, people just set up their locker somewhere safe, put their stuff in it, then padlock it. Some of our dead sisters and brothers still have their locker up in HQ. They need to be cleared. Clear at least five of them, then bring me their contents, all the personal effects they left in there.

Your response: First you make me learn about Canyon propaganda, then you make me do a clerk's job. What am I supposed to make of this?

NPC: Nothing, yet. But a clerk would just bring five boxes with stuff in them, and a preacher will bring back five names with stories behind them. And that will be the only material you're ever going to work with. So go to HQ, and clear those lockers out.

NPC: You still need to clear those lockers.

NPC: Did you read the names on the labels? Have you read the stories behind the personal effects?

Your response: I did. And when I did, I noticed a name I glimpsed earlier, but it was listed as active. Might be a relative, perhaps. The name was 'Ruz'.

NPC: That would be Peter Ruz who's dead, and Stefan Ruz, who's still alive. That makes sense, and I think Stefan already knows. He's been going on about how our cause isn't worth it. And people are listening. So you may already guess what I expect next from you. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: The last job is a conversation. Plain and simple, and yet it will be the hardest thing I could ask of you. Are you ready?

Your response: I assume I am going to talk Stefan into not abandoning the movement.

Your response: Not yet.

NPC: Take your time, get ready, and then talk to me again.

NPC: That's exactly right. You are going to take his brother's effects to him personally, and you are going to make him believe all the more in the movement, not less.

Your response: So I am supposed to take his grief, twist it, and then turn him around, all the way.

NPC: Absolutely. And I won't pretend that it is anything other than that, I am fully aware what I am asking of you. The City buries its dead quietly and hopes their family stays quiet, too. The movement will call out its losses, by name. It will weep, it will mourn. And it will be stronger for it.

NPC: ...so why do we keep fighting a fight that we cannot possibly win? It is this simple truth... hang on. What are you carrying there? Oh no. Oh no. Please, don't show me. If this is what I think it is, I don't want to know.

Your response: Son, these are the earthly effects of your brother. May he rest in peace.

NPC: This... this is his picture of us two, on a drom hunt as little kids. And this... oh no, I cannot... Oh geez...

Your response: Your brother, Peter Ruz, fought the good fight, and he died a hero to our people. We will mourn his death together.

NPC: Thanks... Honestly, thank you. He was such a good person, always believed in the good cause. What am I supposed to do without my brother? He always knew what to do.

Your response: He always believed in the cause of our movement. And where he dropped the torch, you're going to pick it up, and carry it further, further than it's ever been. To honor his memory.

NPC: Yes. Yes, I will. And I have been telling people that our fight is pointless. Oh no, what have I done? Guys! Come back! I've made a terrible mistake! Our cause is just! Please, listen to me! We need to...

NPC: Please! I need to undo some of the damage I did!

NPC: You still need to carry the personal effects of Peter Ruz to his brother.

NPC: Ruz took the personal effects of his brother, I assume. So how did it go down?

Your response: He remembered how his brother always believed in the good cause. And that made him see the error of his ways.

NPC: That one concession is worth more than a hall full of people cheering. I hope you realize what a great service you have done to us. This is how the movement is held together.

Your response: Your turn to answer truthfully: Do you feel anything at all about how this was actually accomplished?

NPC: I do, absolutely. There is a whole rainbow of emotions going through me right now. And unless you can say the same about yourself, you're of no use to me.

Your response: I can.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send two modules your way, an aggressive and a passive one. I assume you understand the symbolism. You've earned them. Keep your Psi skills well trained, you're gonna need them. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 1: What the Doc Sees
entries.description: Find Doc Sarn in the TG HQ - BARRACKS and learn what the people of the Canyon are actually getting sick with, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Doc Sarn
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me be perfectly clear. Nobody around here funds 'interesting research', and the only science happening around here is done by people with no equipment, and on problems the City has no reason to care about. And this is the point where you either lose all interest, or where your interest is actually piqued.

Your response: Piqued, definitely.

Your response: Give me a moment to consider.

Your response: Oh, I believe there is interesting research here, you're just not offering it. So please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then let's begin with some fact finding. Go see Doc Sarn in the Barracks. Find out what the people in this Canyon actually present with. I don't want to just trust my impression of it.

Your response: What you're expecting might be important, though.

NPC: I'm not going to tell a researcher what to expect. That's how you get the answer you wanted, not necessarily the right one. Let's see what answer you come up with on your own, and then we can compare notes.

NPC: Pull a number and take a seat, I'll be with you shortly.

Your response: I'm not here about that. I want to know what people around here are presenting with.

NPC: Do you? That's unusual. Nobody asks, normally. But anyway, I treat mostly wounds from battle with the City or from cave critters, and more and more infectious diseases.

Your response: Those infectious diseases are what interests me, does the infection pattern follow any particular group?

NPC: Not so much by social group or faction. It's more along regional lines. Basically, it's where people sleep. Some parts of the Canyon seem to lead to more infections. Cause unknown.

Your response: That sounds bad. Why have you never reported this?

NPC: What makes you think I haven't? In fact, I did! Twice! And nothing came of it. They said they'd look into this, and that was that. You asking is actually the first sign I ever saw that somebody seems to be looking into this.

NPC: I must get back to my patients. Too many sick, too little time worrying about why they're getting sick.

NPC: You still need to talk to Doc Sarn in the Barracks.

NPC: So you talked to Sarn. What did he observe?

Your response: There seems to be a cluster of infectious diseases going on based on where people live, or spend the night, rather than on what they do.

NPC: And the pattern that follows where people live and not what they do points at either parasites, or something everybody is drinking. I had hoped for someone qualified to say that out loud. Thank you. Give me some minutes to do some communications, then get back to me.

NPC: If we want to turn this problem into something that's certain not to be waved away, we need some field work done.

Your response: Alright, what do you need?

Your response: Hang on a moment.

NPC: If I am right, the water is not going to get better while we think about it.

NPC: What I need is eight samples from the water sampling points set across every level of the Facility. Not just one level, or our case goes straight out the window and will be dismissed. We need to be able to compare sites.

Your response: What do you mean? Who will be doing the dismissing?

NPC: That is a very good question. But before you've gotten the results, better not to burden you with the politics behind it all. So get going.

NPC: Do take a look at those sampling points, now.

NPC: You've succeeded. What do the samples say?

Your response: I wanted to draw up a chart on where the water seems to be most contaminated. But as it turns out, there is just one source. Look.

NPC: I know that site. There's a fuel and chemical dump there. Has been there since before the Canyon was properly settled, really. That's not- Hmmm. Get back to me on that one.

NPC: These results need to go up. I'd take it myself, but I'd say it's probably better if it is brought up by the person who took the samples. Will you do that?

Your response: And why would that be better?

Your response: Give us a moment, please.

NPC: Don't sit on it too long. Sitting on findings is how they turn into somebody else's decision.

NPC: What you will report is a legitimate finding. Anything I report immediately becomes part of the politics. This needs to be addressed. So go to the Intelligence Center in HQ, and talk to Commissar Ledek in there.

Your response: What should I expect Ledek to do?

NPC: I honestly do not know. My advice is to give him those numbers straight, and not to negotiate on them. They are facts, and should be treated as such.

NPC: Welcome to the Intelligence Center, comrade. What can I do for you? I hear that you have made a certain discovery. Am I correct in believing that you are here to report your findings?

Your response: Yes, you are. The old fuel and chemical dump seems to have corroded its way into the local water pipes, and the people living in that part of the Canyon are getting sick from it.

NPC: Let me see those findings of yours - yes, that is unequivocal, isn't it. Those numbers make for grim, but clear reading, and your analysis is flawless.

Your response: So what's going to happen to my findings now?

NPC: What do you mean? Your findings are not in question here. The science does not lie. There is however a political dimension that I cannot afford to ignore. Our whole movement is based on the claim that we can live freely out here. Any story that casts doubt on our self-reliance immediately makes our numbers of new recruits drop, and the City has eyes and ears everywhere. A proper reaction to these findings would be an immediate quarantine of the area, and that is something we cannot do.

Your response: But you can't ignore my findings either! If people get sick around here, that won't exactly be a recruitment slogan either, will it?

NPC: No, it won't. Make no mistake: I was not prepared to sweep this under the rug. But our reaction will not be as expeditious as it would be without this political dimension. We will clean that area of the Canyon up, fix the pipes, the whole works. But slowly, quietly. That will mean that until the work is finished, more people will get sick. That is unfortunate, but sadly, cannot be helped. You are to be commended for a great service to the Canyon, however. Please do accept my sincere thanks. The Canyon is glad to have bright minds like yours among its ranks.

NPC: Do not let me keep you.

NPC: You still need to deliver your findings. Ledek is in the Intelligence Center, in HQ.

NPC: Your face tells me that Ledek reacted exactly the way I had feared.

Your response: He says quickly cleaning it up would lead to bad PR, so they're gonna do it, but slowly and quietly.

NPC: I won't defend his decision. I have watched the movement do this before. It seemed quite wrong then, and it seems quite wrong now. I have no other words for that.

Your response: Are you going to fight this?

NPC: The best I can do is make sure that those numbers do not get lost. In fact, now that you have raised them, I will raise them again, and again, regularly. That's not the same as fighting, I have to admit. I hope you can find solace in the fact that your findings are true, they're yours, and no one can take that away from you.

Your response: I'm a scientist. What am I supposed to do with that?

NPC: Your job. Keep taking samples, keep the record honest - and sometimes, just outlast the people who would rather not know. I'm gonna send a Research Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Research skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 2: Every Level
entries.description: Take %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(take_samples) water samples from the sampling points across every level of the CANYON FACILITY, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: What the Doc Sees
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 8 × Canyon Water Sample
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me be perfectly clear. Nobody around here funds 'interesting research', and the only science happening around here is done by people with no equipment, and on problems the City has no reason to care about. And this is the point where you either lose all interest, or where your interest is actually piqued.

Your response: Piqued, definitely.

Your response: Give me a moment to consider.

Your response: Oh, I believe there is interesting research here, you're just not offering it. So please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then let's begin with some fact finding. Go see Doc Sarn in the Barracks. Find out what the people in this Canyon actually present with. I don't want to just trust my impression of it.

Your response: What you're expecting might be important, though.

NPC: I'm not going to tell a researcher what to expect. That's how you get the answer you wanted, not necessarily the right one. Let's see what answer you come up with on your own, and then we can compare notes.

NPC: Pull a number and take a seat, I'll be with you shortly.

Your response: I'm not here about that. I want to know what people around here are presenting with.

NPC: Do you? That's unusual. Nobody asks, normally. But anyway, I treat mostly wounds from battle with the City or from cave critters, and more and more infectious diseases.

Your response: Those infectious diseases are what interests me, does the infection pattern follow any particular group?

NPC: Not so much by social group or faction. It's more along regional lines. Basically, it's where people sleep. Some parts of the Canyon seem to lead to more infections. Cause unknown.

Your response: That sounds bad. Why have you never reported this?

NPC: What makes you think I haven't? In fact, I did! Twice! And nothing came of it. They said they'd look into this, and that was that. You asking is actually the first sign I ever saw that somebody seems to be looking into this.

NPC: I must get back to my patients. Too many sick, too little time worrying about why they're getting sick.

NPC: You still need to talk to Doc Sarn in the Barracks.

NPC: So you talked to Sarn. What did he observe?

Your response: There seems to be a cluster of infectious diseases going on based on where people live, or spend the night, rather than on what they do.

NPC: And the pattern that follows where people live and not what they do points at either parasites, or something everybody is drinking. I had hoped for someone qualified to say that out loud. Thank you. Give me some minutes to do some communications, then get back to me.

NPC: If we want to turn this problem into something that's certain not to be waved away, we need some field work done.

Your response: Alright, what do you need?

Your response: Hang on a moment.

NPC: If I am right, the water is not going to get better while we think about it.

NPC: What I need is eight samples from the water sampling points set across every level of the Facility. Not just one level, or our case goes straight out the window and will be dismissed. We need to be able to compare sites.

Your response: What do you mean? Who will be doing the dismissing?

NPC: That is a very good question. But before you've gotten the results, better not to burden you with the politics behind it all. So get going.

NPC: Do take a look at those sampling points, now.

NPC: You've succeeded. What do the samples say?

Your response: I wanted to draw up a chart on where the water seems to be most contaminated. But as it turns out, there is just one source. Look.

NPC: I know that site. There's a fuel and chemical dump there. Has been there since before the Canyon was properly settled, really. That's not- Hmmm. Get back to me on that one.

NPC: These results need to go up. I'd take it myself, but I'd say it's probably better if it is brought up by the person who took the samples. Will you do that?

Your response: And why would that be better?

Your response: Give us a moment, please.

NPC: Don't sit on it too long. Sitting on findings is how they turn into somebody else's decision.

NPC: What you will report is a legitimate finding. Anything I report immediately becomes part of the politics. This needs to be addressed. So go to the Intelligence Center in HQ, and talk to Commissar Ledek in there.

Your response: What should I expect Ledek to do?

NPC: I honestly do not know. My advice is to give him those numbers straight, and not to negotiate on them. They are facts, and should be treated as such.

NPC: Welcome to the Intelligence Center, comrade. What can I do for you? I hear that you have made a certain discovery. Am I correct in believing that you are here to report your findings?

Your response: Yes, you are. The old fuel and chemical dump seems to have corroded its way into the local water pipes, and the people living in that part of the Canyon are getting sick from it.

NPC: Let me see those findings of yours - yes, that is unequivocal, isn't it. Those numbers make for grim, but clear reading, and your analysis is flawless.

Your response: So what's going to happen to my findings now?

NPC: What do you mean? Your findings are not in question here. The science does not lie. There is however a political dimension that I cannot afford to ignore. Our whole movement is based on the claim that we can live freely out here. Any story that casts doubt on our self-reliance immediately makes our numbers of new recruits drop, and the City has eyes and ears everywhere. A proper reaction to these findings would be an immediate quarantine of the area, and that is something we cannot do.

Your response: But you can't ignore my findings either! If people get sick around here, that won't exactly be a recruitment slogan either, will it?

NPC: No, it won't. Make no mistake: I was not prepared to sweep this under the rug. But our reaction will not be as expeditious as it would be without this political dimension. We will clean that area of the Canyon up, fix the pipes, the whole works. But slowly, quietly. That will mean that until the work is finished, more people will get sick. That is unfortunate, but sadly, cannot be helped. You are to be commended for a great service to the Canyon, however. Please do accept my sincere thanks. The Canyon is glad to have bright minds like yours among its ranks.

NPC: Do not let me keep you.

NPC: You still need to deliver your findings. Ledek is in the Intelligence Center, in HQ.

NPC: Your face tells me that Ledek reacted exactly the way I had feared.

Your response: He says quickly cleaning it up would lead to bad PR, so they're gonna do it, but slowly and quietly.

NPC: I won't defend his decision. I have watched the movement do this before. It seemed quite wrong then, and it seems quite wrong now. I have no other words for that.

Your response: Are you going to fight this?

NPC: The best I can do is make sure that those numbers do not get lost. In fact, now that you have raised them, I will raise them again, and again, regularly. That's not the same as fighting, I have to admit. I hope you can find solace in the fact that your findings are true, they're yours, and no one can take that away from you.

Your response: I'm a scientist. What am I supposed to do with that?

NPC: Your job. Keep taking samples, keep the record honest - and sometimes, just outlast the people who would rather not know. I'm gonna send a Research Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Research skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 3: Slowly, Quietly
entries.description: Report the contamination to Commissar Ledek in the TG HQ - INTELLIGENCE CENTER, then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: Every Level
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Commissar Ledek
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me be perfectly clear. Nobody around here funds 'interesting research', and the only science happening around here is done by people with no equipment, and on problems the City has no reason to care about. And this is the point where you either lose all interest, or where your interest is actually piqued.

Your response: Piqued, definitely.

Your response: Give me a moment to consider.

Your response: Oh, I believe there is interesting research here, you're just not offering it. So please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then let's begin with some fact finding. Go see Doc Sarn in the Barracks. Find out what the people in this Canyon actually present with. I don't want to just trust my impression of it.

Your response: What you're expecting might be important, though.

NPC: I'm not going to tell a researcher what to expect. That's how you get the answer you wanted, not necessarily the right one. Let's see what answer you come up with on your own, and then we can compare notes.

NPC: Pull a number and take a seat, I'll be with you shortly.

Your response: I'm not here about that. I want to know what people around here are presenting with.

NPC: Do you? That's unusual. Nobody asks, normally. But anyway, I treat mostly wounds from battle with the City or from cave critters, and more and more infectious diseases.

Your response: Those infectious diseases are what interests me, does the infection pattern follow any particular group?

NPC: Not so much by social group or faction. It's more along regional lines. Basically, it's where people sleep. Some parts of the Canyon seem to lead to more infections. Cause unknown.

Your response: That sounds bad. Why have you never reported this?

NPC: What makes you think I haven't? In fact, I did! Twice! And nothing came of it. They said they'd look into this, and that was that. You asking is actually the first sign I ever saw that somebody seems to be looking into this.

NPC: I must get back to my patients. Too many sick, too little time worrying about why they're getting sick.

NPC: You still need to talk to Doc Sarn in the Barracks.

NPC: So you talked to Sarn. What did he observe?

Your response: There seems to be a cluster of infectious diseases going on based on where people live, or spend the night, rather than on what they do.

NPC: And the pattern that follows where people live and not what they do points at either parasites, or something everybody is drinking. I had hoped for someone qualified to say that out loud. Thank you. Give me some minutes to do some communications, then get back to me.

NPC: If we want to turn this problem into something that's certain not to be waved away, we need some field work done.

Your response: Alright, what do you need?

Your response: Hang on a moment.

NPC: If I am right, the water is not going to get better while we think about it.

NPC: What I need is eight samples from the water sampling points set across every level of the Facility. Not just one level, or our case goes straight out the window and will be dismissed. We need to be able to compare sites.

Your response: What do you mean? Who will be doing the dismissing?

NPC: That is a very good question. But before you've gotten the results, better not to burden you with the politics behind it all. So get going.

NPC: Do take a look at those sampling points, now.

NPC: You've succeeded. What do the samples say?

Your response: I wanted to draw up a chart on where the water seems to be most contaminated. But as it turns out, there is just one source. Look.

NPC: I know that site. There's a fuel and chemical dump there. Has been there since before the Canyon was properly settled, really. That's not- Hmmm. Get back to me on that one.

NPC: These results need to go up. I'd take it myself, but I'd say it's probably better if it is brought up by the person who took the samples. Will you do that?

Your response: And why would that be better?

Your response: Give us a moment, please.

NPC: Don't sit on it too long. Sitting on findings is how they turn into somebody else's decision.

NPC: What you will report is a legitimate finding. Anything I report immediately becomes part of the politics. This needs to be addressed. So go to the Intelligence Center in HQ, and talk to Commissar Ledek in there.

Your response: What should I expect Ledek to do?

NPC: I honestly do not know. My advice is to give him those numbers straight, and not to negotiate on them. They are facts, and should be treated as such.

NPC: Welcome to the Intelligence Center, comrade. What can I do for you? I hear that you have made a certain discovery. Am I correct in believing that you are here to report your findings?

Your response: Yes, you are. The old fuel and chemical dump seems to have corroded its way into the local water pipes, and the people living in that part of the Canyon are getting sick from it.

NPC: Let me see those findings of yours - yes, that is unequivocal, isn't it. Those numbers make for grim, but clear reading, and your analysis is flawless.

Your response: So what's going to happen to my findings now?

NPC: What do you mean? Your findings are not in question here. The science does not lie. There is however a political dimension that I cannot afford to ignore. Our whole movement is based on the claim that we can live freely out here. Any story that casts doubt on our self-reliance immediately makes our numbers of new recruits drop, and the City has eyes and ears everywhere. A proper reaction to these findings would be an immediate quarantine of the area, and that is something we cannot do.

Your response: But you can't ignore my findings either! If people get sick around here, that won't exactly be a recruitment slogan either, will it?

NPC: No, it won't. Make no mistake: I was not prepared to sweep this under the rug. But our reaction will not be as expeditious as it would be without this political dimension. We will clean that area of the Canyon up, fix the pipes, the whole works. But slowly, quietly. That will mean that until the work is finished, more people will get sick. That is unfortunate, but sadly, cannot be helped. You are to be commended for a great service to the Canyon, however. Please do accept my sincere thanks. The Canyon is glad to have bright minds like yours among its ranks.

NPC: Do not let me keep you.

NPC: You still need to deliver your findings. Ledek is in the Intelligence Center, in HQ.

NPC: Your face tells me that Ledek reacted exactly the way I had feared.

Your response: He says quickly cleaning it up would lead to bad PR, so they're gonna do it, but slowly and quietly.

NPC: I won't defend his decision. I have watched the movement do this before. It seemed quite wrong then, and it seems quite wrong now. I have no other words for that.

Your response: Are you going to fight this?

NPC: The best I can do is make sure that those numbers do not get lost. In fact, now that you have raised them, I will raise them again, and again, regularly. That's not the same as fighting, I have to admit. I hope you can find solace in the fact that your findings are true, they're yours, and no one can take that away from you.

Your response: I'm a scientist. What am I supposed to do with that?

NPC: Your job. Keep taking samples, keep the record honest - and sometimes, just outlast the people who would rather not know. I'm gonna send a Research Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Research skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.title: Mission 1: Don't Ask
entries.description: Clear out %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(clear_drops) drops from around the CANYON FACILITY and bring back what is in them, unopened. Then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Collect 5 × Sealed Drop Package
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Your trade is considered a crime in the City. Around here, it is considered 'the economy'. A person who gets you what you need can go far around here. Can you?

Your response: Given time, yes. Didn't have much time to organize a distribution network, though.

Your response: If you'll give me a moment first, sure.

Your response: Not for you. I'll do quite fine on my own. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: For your first task, you won't need one. We're starting off with a simple pickup: We have dead drops, spread across the Canyon. Clear five of them out and bring me their contents. And don't ask what's in them.

Your response: So what's in them?

NPC: Very funny. I will not tell you. And you will not risk a peek, either. I will not accept opened merchandise. Get used to that. Out here, the person carrying the stuff often doesn't know what it is that they're carrying. So get going.

NPC: You still need to clear out those five drops.

NPC: So. Did you peek?

Your response: I didn't need to. By the weight, and the way they felt, I'm pretty sure I already know what's inside. And that makes me wonder who actually agreed my price.

NPC: I did, and you're in no position to negotiate. Not if you want to work for us, anyway. You're right, though. The much more interesting question is who sets the price on the far end. Take five, then get back to me, and you're gonna find out that that person is not in the Command Center.

NPC: You're back. So, do you want to meet the person who actually decides how much the Canyon can afford?

Your response: Sure. Who is that?

Your response: Could you give us a moment, please?

NPC: Oh, sure. She will still be setting the prices tomorrow.

NPC: Bara Tesar is the name. You will find her by the wasteland traders. Tesar knows the price of everything that crosses into this Canyon. And who fixes each price.

Your response: That seems like a weird arrangement. Why does the movement put up with that?

NPC: We put up with it, because the alternative is nothing arriving at all. But I will let Tesar explain the mathematics behind all that.

NPC: What have we here? A fellow trader. And one who knows how to get things, but doesn't know how the prices around here work yet, I'd wager.

Your response: Yes, about that. How *do* the prices work here, actually?

NPC: You know what a new, pristine water purifier costs in the City? Around 30 K. You know what that thing costs here? About 100 K. And make no mistake: I know how indecent that gap is. But everyone along the line gets their cut, their hazard pay, and so on.

Your response: Who does, besides you?

NPC: The people I made the arrangement with. The operator within the City, the guy who keeps my route free, and the guy who runs the route. Plus: There's no alternative. So everyone takes a monopoly markup. Yes, myself included. Nobody is arguing about those margins.

Your response: Has anyone tried?

NPC: Oh yes. But sooner or later, they stopped. Because mine is the only way in. Well, the only feasible one, that is.

NPC: I have said all I'm gonna say to you.

NPC: You still need to talk to Tesar.

NPC: Yeah. I can see it in your face that you have now understood the barrel she has us over.

Your response: She said that there's the guy in the City, guy who cleans the route, guy who runs the route and her. Each taking their cut, their hazard pay and a monopoly margin.

NPC: Honestly, this makes me so mad that it is difficult for me to keep my composure. We threw off a government, only to let one person with a monopoly on the only route become another quasi-government, with all taxes and no representation. Because I sure as hell did not vote for this woman.

Your response: The only feasible route, that is.

NPC: What do you mean? Did she say that? If there is another route, we must use it. And if it is unfeasible, we need to make it feasible. Let me make a few calls, then get back to me.

NPC: There *is* a second route in. And no matter what Tesar says, it is feasible. It just collapsed and had some critters move into the remains. I had someone clear out the debris, and someone else move stuff from a passing trader into there. Now I need you to prove that this new route will work end to end. You in?

Your response: Absolutely. I'd love to wipe that smirk off Tesar's face.

Your response: Hang on, let me get my stuff.

NPC: Hurry up. Those caches will not sit there indefinitely. And my patience with the current arrangement is stretched to the limit as well.

NPC: The end of the route goes through Canyon Cave 1. Carry three consignments out of there from the caches, and we can finally undercut this choking monopoly.

Your response: What will happen to the people whose prices we break?

NPC: They lose parts of their margins, not their lives. This is no time to be hesitant. Go into that cave and get the goods!

NPC: Canyon Cave 1. Go!

NPC: It worked. You got the consignments out of there. How did the route hold up?

Your response: The beasts in there are a bit of a nuisance, but nothing that can't be handled.

NPC: Then the old monopoly has just crumbled. Prices are gonna drop hard for a lot of stuff that is normally difficult to come by out here.

Your response: Are they, though? Or are you planning to be the new monopoly, and I do the runs for you?

NPC: No. I made sure that will never happen. I already told several people about the new route. Now I will just confirm that it is fully open. This will not be a secret, but common knowledge. We won't get held over a barrel again. It's great when people like you can get you what you need. But if they run a monopoly on half the Canyon's needs, we cannot accept that.

Your response: Fair enough, I guess.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send an Experimental Barter CPU your way. You've earned it. Keep your Bartering skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: The people I made the arrangement with. The operator within the City, the guy who keeps my route free, and the guy who runs the route. Plus: There's no alternative. So everyone takes a monopoly markup. Yes, myself included. Nobody is arguing about those margins.

Your response: Has anyone tried?

NPC: Oh yes. But sooner or later, they stopped. Because mine is the only way in. Well, the only feasible one, that is.

NPC: I have said all I'm gonna say to you.

NPC: You still need to talk to Tesar.

NPC: Yeah. I can see it in your face that you have now understood the barrel she has us over.

Your response: She said that there's the guy in the City, guy who cleans the route, guy who runs the route and her. Each taking their cut, their hazard pay and a monopoly margin.

NPC: Honestly, this makes me so mad that it is difficult for me to keep my composure. We threw off a government, only to let one person with a monopoly on the only route become another quasi-government, with all taxes and no representation. Because I sure as hell did not vote for this woman.

Your response: The only feasible route, that is.

NPC: What do you mean? Did she say that? If there is another route, we must use it. And if it is unfeasible, we need to make it feasible. Let me make a few calls, then get back to me.

NPC: There *is* a second route in. And no matter what Tesar says, it is feasible. It just collapsed and had some critters move into the remains. I had someone clear out the debris, and someone else move stuff from a passing trader into there. Now I need you to prove that this new route will work end to end. You in?

Your response: Absolutely. I'd love to wipe that smirk off Tesar's face.

Your response: Hang on, let me get my stuff.

NPC: Hurry up. Those caches will not sit there indefinitely. And my patience with the current arrangement is stretched to the limit as well.

NPC: The end of the route goes through Canyon Cave 1. Carry three consignments out of there from the caches, and we can finally undercut this choking monopoly.

Your response: What will happen to the people whose prices we break?

NPC: They lose parts of their margins, not their lives. This is no time to be hesitant. Go into that cave and get the goods!

NPC: Canyon Cave 1. Go!

NPC: It worked. You got the consignments out of there. How did the route hold up?

Your response: The beasts in there are a bit of a nuisance, but nothing that can't be handled.

NPC: Then the old monopoly has just crumbled. Prices are gonna drop hard for a lot of stuff that is normally difficult to come by out here.

Your response: Are they, though? Or are you planning to be the new monopoly, and I do the runs for you?

NPC: No. I made sure that will never happen. I already told several people about the new route. Now I will just confirm that it is fully open. This will not be a secret, but common knowledge. We won't get held over a barrel again. It's great when people like you can get you what you need. But if they run a monopoly on half the Canyon's needs, we cannot accept that.

Your response: Fair enough, I guess.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send an Experimental Barter CPU your way. You've earned it. Keep your Bartering skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.
