entries.title: Mission 1: Nobody Makes You
entries.description: Clear %OBJECTIVE_COUNT(clear_cave) of them out of CANYON CAVE 1. Nobody is going to check your count. Then report back to Mrs. Jones.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 10 × Denizens of Very Easy Canyon dungeons
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. People around here like to call themselves soldiers, but they're volunteers who showed up when they liked, and they can leave whenever they like. So self-references aside, this is no army. Can you work under these conditions?

Your response: Yes, ma'am.

Your response: I can, I just need a moment.

Your response: May I invite you to leave my barrack room. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Then the first thing I will send you out to deal with is Canyon Cave 1. Clear out ten of whatever critters have moved in there. And in case you're wondering: Yes, this is a test, not a crisis intervention.

Your response: So what is it that I am being tested for?

NPC: I am testing whether you finish a tedious job that nobody makes you finish. That is the only kind of discipline I have access to. So get going, clear out ten of them from Canyon Cave 1, and then come back. Or, you know, don't come back.

NPC: Canyon Cave 1 is not cleared out yet, and yet here you are.

NPC: You killed the full ten, didn't you? Had it ever occurred to you to stop at six, and just claim it was ten? I wouldn't have had any way to check.

Your response: That would have been dishonest.

NPC: That's all we rely upon out here. In the City, you can bet that somebody would have checked, honesty be damned. That is the trade the movement made out here, and it costs us more than people think. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: Ah, there you are. I'd like you to spend some time with the person who trains the Canyon's fighters.

Your response: That makes sense.

Your response: I will, but I need a moment, first.

NPC: Sure. Vada is not going anywhere.

NPC: Then go and meet Ilinca Vada here in the Canyon. Be sure to ask her what she is actually allowed to make anybody do around here.

Your response: Given what I've heard so far, I assume she is allowed very little?

NPC: Close to nothing, more like, and yet, Vada gets results anyway. So that is definitely a trick worth learning.

NPC: Come here, join the training. We're right in the middle, but you'll catch on quickly enough.

Your response: Jones sent me. She wants me to ask you what you can actually order anyone to do.

NPC: Ha! Order? That's a good one. Everyone here is a volunteer, and can walk out of my session and out of the Canyon at any time. I won't rely on orders, I can't and I don't need to.

Your response: Then how do you get anything done?

NPC: Oh, quite simple. I make people want to be the person who didn't leave. I make them take pride in what they do, and not want to endure the shame of having failed. There is no other way.

Your response: And what do you do if it fails?

NPC: Then I lose the person I have worked with, try to learn what I could have done differently and better, and then I move on to the next. And for them, there is no punishment detail, no stockade. That is how our movement operates, and it does well like that.

NPC: I need to get on with the training.

NPC: You still need to speak with Vada.

NPC: Have you learned what Vada does instead of giving orders?

Your response: She makes people take pride in what they do, and they don't want to fail. Slower than an order, and more personal, but effective.

NPC: Exactly right. A City sergeant can produce obedience in a week, and yet a frightened City soldier may still desert. Vada needs months, but after that, our soldiers fight to the death without fear. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So remember what you learned from Vada? Good, because this is a bit of an embarrassment: we haven't had a failure like this in months. Unfortunately, as you discovered, I am not able to deal with this - how shall I put it? - the easy way. At least not right away. I'm gonna ask you to deal with it.

Your response: What's the matter?

Your response: In a minute, hang on.

NPC: We're in a bit of a hurry here, so hurry, too. Please.

NPC: One of our guards, Niko Prey, has left his guard post. Simply walked off, and it is one that matters. Now he hangs out in the bar and is getting drunk instead. In an army, this would be a simple case for disciplinary action. Here, it is not.

Your response: Disciplinary action? Leaving your post on duty is desertion, the guy should be shot!

NPC: Probably, yes. But - and I'm not gonna give you any twaddle about motivation, there - shooting him would prove the City's account of what the Twilight Guardian is. I'm not going to hand them that PR victory over one man's failure of character. I hate it myself, but I'm going to ask you to go to him, and talk him into going back on duty.

NPC: Yeah? Yeah! I'm not at my post, and I'm drinkin'. In fact, I'm drunk. What'chu gonna do about it, huh? Nothing. So shove off!

Your response: Soldier, why are you not at your post?

NPC: Why would I? What difference does it make? They sent my buddy, Rex, to guard some broken down City transport until our reclamation teams could get the goods. Yeah, when they got there, the goods were gone, and Rex was perforated like a sieve. They sent one man. Of course he wasn't going to survive that!

Your response: That does seem like really bad judgment, I'll give you that.

NPC: You don't understand, you- wait, what? You're agreeing with me? Well, agreeing won't change anything. If this is how they waste the people on guard duty around here, what's the point? Huh? What's the point?

Your response: It's not about duty. You never guard a thing, or a post. You guard for your fellow people, so that they can get the goods, so that they are not shot and killed by surprise. You always guard with your life. Some posts are just more dangerous than others. But no guarding is wasted. Rex was defending all of us. We should be thankful and honor his memory.

NPC: Jones sent you, didn't she. Well, you can tell her that she sent no idiot. Finishing my drink now. And then you can report that I am back on guard. The fresh air will sober me right up.

NPC: I am on my way back out there, now.

NPC: Niko Prey is still in the bar instead of at his post.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Flamer your way. You've earned it. Keep your Heavy Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

 100                    name: tg_soldier
 101                    ge: 3
 102                - completed: tg_soldier.mission3
 103          - goto: jones_m3_return
 104            when:
 105              active: tg_soldier.mission3
 106          - goto: jones_m3_offer
 107            when:

 116            when:
 117              active: tg_soldier.mission1

 119  
 120      jones_not_available:
 121        say:
 122          - "You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense."
 123  
 124      jones_over_qualified:
 125        say:
 126          - "You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?"
 127        answer:
 128          jones_leave_over_qualified:
 129            - "Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones."
 130  
 131      jones_leave_over_qualified:
 132        do:
 133          - set_flag:
 134              flag: tg_soldier
 135              value: 3
 136          - remove
 137        say:
 138          - "Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."
 139  
 140      jones_m1_offer:
 141        say:
 142          - "Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. People around here like to call themselves soldiers, but they're volunteers who showed up when they liked, and they can leave whenever they like. So self-references aside, this is no army. Can you work under these conditions?"
 143        answer:
 144          jones_m1_briefing:
 145            - "Yes, ma'am."
 146          jones_m1_later:
 147            - "I can, I just need a moment."
 148          jones_dismiss:
 149            - "May I invite you to leave my barrack room. Now."
 150  
 151      jones_m1_later:
 152        say:
 153          - "Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25."
 154  
 155      jones_dismiss:
 156        say:
 157          - "Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good."
 158        answer:
 159          jones_dismiss_confirm:
 160            - "Yes, I am sure. Bye, already."
 161          start:
 162            - "Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?"
 163  
 164      jones_dismiss_confirm:
 165        say:
 166          - "Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards."
 167        answer:
 168          jones_leave:
 169            - "Geez. Are you going, or should I?"
 170          start:
 171            - "You know what? I just did."
 172  
 173      jones_leave:
 174        do:
 175          - set_flag:
 176              flag: tg_soldier
 177              value: 3
 178          - remove
 179        say:
 180          - "Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."
 181  
 182      jones_m1_briefing:
 183        say:
 184          - "Then the first thing I will send you out to deal with is Canyon Cave 1. Clear out ten of whatever critters have moved in there. And in case you're wondering: Yes, this is a test, not a crisis intervention."
 185        answer:
 186          jones_m1_go:
 187            - "So what is it that I am being tested for?"
 188  
 189      jones_m1_go:
 190        do:
 191          - offer_mission: tg_soldier.mission1
 192        say:
 193          - "I am testing whether you finish a tedious job that nobody makes you finish. That is the only kind of discipline I have access to. So get going, clear out ten of them from Canyon Cave 1, and then come back. Or, you know, don't come back."
 194        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 195  
 196      jones_m1_return:
 197        do:
 198          - goto: jones_m1_report
 199            when:
 200              objective_done:
 201                objective: clear_cave
 202          - goto: jones_m1_not_done
 203  
 204      jones_m1_not_done:
 205        say:
 206          - "Canyon Cave 1 is not cleared out yet, and yet here you are."
 207        resume_at: jones_m1_return
 208  
 209      jones_m1_report:
 210        say:
 211          - "You killed the full ten, didn't you? Had it ever occurred to you to stop at six, and just claim it was ten? I wouldn't have had any way to check."
 212        answer:
 213          jones_m1_done:
 214            - "That would have been dishonest."
 215        resume_at: jones_m1_done
 216  
 217      jones_m1_done:
 218        do:
 219          - set_flag:
 220              flag: tg_soldier
 221              value: 1
 222          - complete_objective: report
 223        say:
 224          - "That's all we rely upon out here. In the City, you can bet that somebody would have checked, honesty be damned. That is the trade the movement made out here, and it costs us more than people think. Take five, then get back to me."
 225  
 226      jones_m2_offer:
 227        say:
 228          - "Ah, there you are. I'd like you to spend some time with the person who trains the Canyon's fighters."
 229        answer:
 230          jones_m2_briefing:
 231            - "That makes sense."
 232          jones_m2_later:
 233            - "I will, but I need a moment, first."
 234  
 235      jones_m2_later:
 236        say:
 237          - "Sure. Vada is not going anywhere."
 238  
 239      jones_m2_briefing:
 240        say:
 241          - "Then go and meet Ilinca Vada here in the Canyon. Be sure to ask her what she is actually allowed to make anybody do around here."
 242        answer:
 243          jones_m2_go:
 244            - "Given what I've heard so far, I assume she is allowed very little?"
 245  
 246      jones_m2_go:
 247        do:
 248          - offer_mission: tg_soldier.mission2
 249        say:
 250          - "Close to nothing, more like, and yet, Vada gets results anyway. So that is definitely a trick worth learning."
 251        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 252  
 253      vada_training:
 254        say:
 255          - "Come here, join the training. We're right in the middle, but you'll catch on quickly enough."
 256        answer:
 257          vada_orders:
 258            - "Jones sent me. She wants me to ask you what you can actually order anyone to do."
 259  
 260      vada_orders:
 261        say:
 262          - "Ha! Order? That's a good one. Everyone here is a volunteer, and can walk out of my session and out of the Canyon at any time. I won't rely on orders, I can't and I don't need to."
 263        answer:
 264          vada_pride:
 265            - "Then how do you get anything done?"
 266  
 267      vada_pride:
 268        say:
 269          - "Oh, quite simple. I make people want to be the person who didn't leave. I make them take pride in what they do, and not want to endure the shame of having failed. There is no other way."
 270        answer:
 271          vada_failure:
 272            - "And what do you do if it fails?"
 273  
 274      vada_failure:
 275        do:
 276          - complete_objective: train_with_vada
 277        say:
 278          - "Then I lose the person I have worked with, try to learn what I could have done differently and better, and then I move on to the next. And for them, there is no punishment detail, no stockade. That is how our movement operates, and it does well like that."
 279        resume_at: vada_done
 280  
 281      vada_done:
 282        say:
 283          - "I need to get on with the training."
 284  
 285      jones_m2_return:
 286        do:
 287          - goto: jones_m2_report
 288            when:
 289              objective_done:
 290                objective: train_with_vada
 291          - goto: jones_m2_not_done
 292  
 293      jones_m2_not_done:
 294        say:
 295          - "You still need to speak with Vada."
 296        resume_at: jones_m2_return
 297  
 298      jones_m2_report:
 299        say:
 300          - "Have you learned what Vada does instead of giving orders?"
 301        answer:
 302          jones_m2_done:
 303            - "She makes people take pride in what they do, and they don't want to fail. Slower than an order, and more personal, but effective."
 304        resume_at: jones_m2_done
 305  
 306      jones_m2_done:
 307        do:
 308          - set_flag:
 309              flag: tg_soldier
 310              value: 2
 311          - complete_objective: report
 312        say:
 313          - "Exactly right. A City sergeant can produce obedience in a week, and yet a frightened City soldier may still desert. Vada needs months, but after that, our soldiers fight to the death without fear. Take five, then get back to me."
 314  
 315      jones_m3_offer:
 316        say:
 317          - "So remember what you learned from Vada? Good, because this is a bit of an embarrassment: we haven't had a failure like this in months. Unfortunately, as you discovered, I am not able to deal with this - how shall I put it? - the easy way. At least not right away. I'm gonna ask you to deal with it."
 318        answer:
 319          jones_m3_briefing:
 320            - "What's the matter?"
 321          jones_m3_later:
 322            - "In a minute, hang on."
 323  
 324      jones_m3_later:
 325        say:
 326          - "We're in a bit of a hurry here, so hurry, too. Please."
 327  
 328      jones_m3_briefing:
 329        say:
 330          - "One of our guards, Niko Prey, has left his guard post. Simply walked off, and it is one that matters. Now he hangs out in the bar and is getting drunk instead. In an army, this would be a simple case for disciplinary action. Here, it is not."
 331        answer:
 332          jones_m3_go:
 333            - "Disciplinary action? Leaving your post on duty is desertion, the guy should be shot!"
 334  
 335      jones_m3_go:
 336        do:
 337          - offer_mission: tg_soldier.mission3
 338        say:
 339          - "Probably, yes. But - and I'm not gonna give you any twaddle about motivation, there - shooting him would prove the City's account of what the Twilight Guardian is. I'm not going to hand them that PR victory over one man's failure of character. I hate it myself, but I'm going to ask you to go to him, and talk him into going back on duty."
 340        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 341  
 342      prey_drunk:
 343        say:
 344          - "Yeah? Yeah! I'm not at my post, and I'm drinkin'. In fact, I'm drunk. What'chu gonna do about it, huh? Nothing. So shove off!"
 345        answer:
 346          prey_rex:
 347            - "Soldier, why are you not at your post?"
 348  
 349      prey_rex:
 350        say:
 351          - "Why would I? What difference does it make? They sent my buddy, Rex, to guard some broken down City transport until our reclamation teams could get the goods. Yeah, when they got there, the goods were gone, and Rex was perforated like a sieve. They sent one man. Of course he wasn't going to survive that!"
 352        answer:
 353          prey_whats_the_point:
 354            - "That does seem like really bad judgment, I'll give you that."
 355  
 356      prey_whats_the_point:
 357        say:
 358          - "You don't understand, you- wait, what? You're agreeing with me? Well, agreeing won't change anything. If this is how they waste the people on guard duty around here, what's the point? Huh? What's the point?"
 359        answer:
 360          prey_back_on_guard:
 361            - "It's not about duty. You never guard a thing, or a post. You guard for your fellow people, so that they can get the goods, so that they are not shot and killed by surprise. You always guard with your life. Some posts are just more dangerous than others. But no guarding is wasted. Rex was defending all of us. We should be thankful and honor his memory."
 362  
 363      prey_back_on_guard:
 364        do:
 365          - complete_objective: talk_prey_back
 366        say:
 367          - "Jones sent you, didn't she. Well, you can tell her that she sent no idiot. Finishing my drink now. And then you can report that I am back on guard. The fresh air will sober me right up."
 368        resume_at: prey_done
 369  
 370      prey_done:
 371        say:
 372          - "I am on my way back out there, now."
 373  
 374      jones_m3_return:
 375        do:
 376          - goto: jones_m3_report
 377            when:
 378              objective_done:
 379                objective: talk_prey_back
 380          - goto: jones_m3_not_done
 381  
 382      jones_m3_not_done:
 383        say:
 384          - "Niko Prey is still in the bar instead of at his post."
 385        resume_at: jones_m3_return
 386  
 387      jones_m3_report:
 388        say:
 389          - "Niko Prey is back at his post, albeit swaying slightly. What did you say to him?"
 390        answer:
 391          jones_m3_debrief:
 392            - "I reminded him that he stands guard for his fellow people. His grievance was legitimate, though. Sending one person out to guard a downed transport is a waste of a good life. And in this case, it was his personal friend."
 393        resume_at: jones_m3_debrief
 394  
 395      jones_m3_debrief:
 396        say:
 397          - "That's what happened? I agree that this was a gross oversight. I will look into that matter, you have my word."
 398        answer:
 399          jones_m3_restraint:
 400            - "Would you really have had him shot, if I hadn't convinced him?"
 401  
 402      jones_m3_restraint:
 403        say:
 404          - "I want to, and I make no bones about it. Every single time something like this happens, I do. I haven't yet, though. And so far, it has never become necessary. Let's just hope it stays that way. I don't want the movement to turn into the very thing it fights, but that restraint comes with a price tag of uncovered posts, and there is only so much we can afford."
 405        answer:
 406          jones_m3_done:
 407            - "I guess I can accept that."
 408  
 409      jones_m3_done:
 410        do:
 411          - set_flag:
 412              flag: tg_soldier
 413              value: 3
 414          - give_item:
 415              item: 8620
 416              quality: 150
 417              slots: 2
 418          - complete_objective: report
 419          - remove
 420        say:
 421          - "Good. I'm gonna send a Flamer your way. You've earned it. Keep your Heavy Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there."

entries.title: Mission 1: A quick combat test!
entries.description: Go and finish off five drones at the Drone Racetrack, speak to Mrs. Jones afterwards.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Defeat 5 × Assault Drone
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner.  Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Although Tech Haven is a dedicated technocracy, we do keep a small contingent of specialists who are able to take... practical measures to ensure Tech Haven's safety.

Your response: I'm not exactly what you'd call 'muscle'.

NPC: No. However, we have an opening for an agent with the skills to neutralise threats covertly. Looking at your profile, I believe you may be what I'm looking for.

Your response: You're talking about a Hit-Man?

NPC: No - that implies a lack of finesse. We're looking for professional - someone who can eliminate calmly and efficiently, and then disappear...

Your response: Alright - I'm interested.

NPC: Good. Firstly, I want to run you through a quick combat test. We've established drones at the Drone Racetrack for you to fight. Take down 5 of them and report back to me.

NPC: Go and finish off the drones, and then we'll talk.

NPC: Excellent. I was concerned that your time in stasis may have interfered with your weapon skills. It appears that is not the case.

Your response: That's good to know, what next?

NPC: I think it's time we give you something a little more realistic and see how you do. Talk to me again, once you're ready.

NPC: Am I right to assume you wish to continue with your mission?

NPC: Are you ready to press on?

NPC: It's time to continue your training!

Your response: Let's do this!

Your response: I'll come back to you.

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me.

NPC: We've had reports of a Neocron recon team in the area. They've split up into individuals and they seem to be watching our movements.

Your response: Want me to go and take them all out?

NPC: Not quite - we already have other operatives assigned to all but one member of the recon team - he will be your target.

Your response: Point me in the right direction...

NPC: Enthusiasm. Good. Head to Tech Haven Sec-3, near the entrance to Energy Core 6.

NPC: Go and finish off this Spy, and then we'll talk!

NPC: Well done out there. Although we're not officially at war with Neocron, they continue to make our lives difficult. It's important that we don't allow that.

Your response: What next?

NPC: I have one more task for you. Speak to me when you are ready.

NPC: Are you ready for your last task?

NPC: One more task, are you ready?

Your response: Sure, might as well finish this!

Your response: I'll come back to you!

NPC: Very well, I shall wait here for you!

NPC: We've been studying your combat analysis, and we think we have just the thing to complement your new role. Go back to the Drone Racetrack and speak with Jordan King. He has a treat for you.

NPC: Ah, you're our new operative, I see. I am Jordan King - a member of Tech Haven's Research and Development division. We've just finished testing a new marksman's rifle, and I'd like to see how it performs in the real world.

Your response: *click

NPC: Take this weapon and use it. Try and break it, in fact. Based on your feedback, we may take it to production. Now, head back to Jones.

NPC: Go back to your apartment and speak with Mrs. Jones!

NPC: Jordan King is waiting for you.

NPC: Ah, I heard that King has given you a new toy? May I see it?

Your response: Sure!

NPC: You don't want to show me your new toy?

NPC: My my, this is an interesting piece of hardware. I trust you will put it to good use?

Your response: King told me to break it - so I'll do my best.

NPC: A good man that King. He's not happy with his weapons seeing the field until he knows they're reliable. You've done well - I'm sure I will hear your name in the future.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner.  Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Although Tech Haven is a dedicated technocracy, we do keep a small contingent of specialists who are able to take... practical measures to ensure Tech Haven's safety.

Your response: I'm not exactly what you'd call 'muscle'.

NPC: No. However, we have an opening for an agent with the skills to neutralise threats covertly. Looking at your profile, I believe you may be what I'm looking for.

Your response: You're talking about a Hit-Man?

NPC: No - that implies a lack of finesse. We're looking for professional - someone who can eliminate calmly and efficiently, and then disappear...

Your response: Alright - I'm interested.

NPC: Good. Firstly, I want to run you through a quick combat test. We've established drones at the Drone Racetrack for you to fight. Take down 5 of them and report back to me.

NPC: Go and finish off the drones, and then we'll talk.

NPC: Excellent. I was concerned that your time in stasis may have interfered with your weapon skills. It appears that is not the case.

Your response: That's good to know, what next?

NPC: I think it's time we give you something a little more realistic and see how you do. Talk to me again, once you're ready.

NPC: Am I right to assume you wish to continue with your mission?

NPC: Are you ready to press on?

NPC: It's time to continue your training!

Your response: Let's do this!

Your response: I'll come back to you.

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me.

NPC: We've had reports of a Neocron recon team in the area. They've split up into individuals and they seem to be watching our movements.

Your response: Want me to go and take them all out?

NPC: Not quite - we already have other operatives assigned to all but one member of the recon team - he will be your target.

Your response: Point me in the right direction...

NPC: Enthusiasm. Good. Head to Tech Haven Sec-3, near the entrance to Energy Core 6.

NPC: Go and finish off this Spy, and then we'll talk!

NPC: Well done out there. Although we're not officially at war with Neocron, they continue to make our lives difficult. It's important that we don't allow that.

Your response: What next?

NPC: I have one more task for you. Speak to me when you are ready.

NPC: Are you ready for your last task?

NPC: One more task, are you ready?

Your response: Sure, might as well finish this!

Your response: I'll come back to you!

NPC: Very well, I shall wait here for you!

NPC: We've been studying your combat analysis, and we think we have just the thing to complement your new role. Go back to the Drone Racetrack and speak with Jordan King. He has a treat for you.

NPC: Ah, you're our new operative, I see. I am Jordan King - a member of Tech Haven's Research and Development division. We've just finished testing a new marksman's rifle, and I'd like to see how it performs in the real world.

Your response: *click

NPC: Take this weapon and use it. Try and break it, in fact. Based on your feedback, we may take it to production. Now, head back to Jones.

NPC: Go back to your apartment and speak with Mrs. Jones!

NPC: Jordan King is waiting for you.

NPC: Ah, I heard that King has given you a new toy? May I see it?

Your response: Sure!

NPC: You don't want to show me your new toy?

NPC: My my, this is an interesting piece of hardware. I trust you will put it to good use?

Your response: King told me to break it - so I'll do my best.

NPC: A good man that King. He's not happy with his weapons seeing the field until he knows they're reliable. You've done well - I'm sure I will hear your name in the future.

NPC: Ah Runner, welcome to Tech Haven. I've been reading your notes, and it appears that you are quite handy in a fight. I have something for you, if you're interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Good. Now, you've been in MC5 for some time, and I want to make sure none of your motor-functions are impaired. We've set up some training bots at the Drone Racetrack - go and kill 5 of them.

Your response: Are you sure I shouldn't start on sewer rats or something?

NPC: Very funny. Get going.

NPC: Go and finish off the drones, and then we'll talk!

NPC: Welcome back runner. That was better than a sewer, wasn't it?

Your response: Marginally. What's next?

NPC: Well, that weapon you're using isn't really up to the job. Let's sort you out with something a little better. Speak with me again, when you're ready.

NPC: Right - I've had word that the geek... erm... Scientists have come up with some kind of new polymer.

Your response: Okay...

NPC: It's extremely light, but very strong. Head to Tech Haven Sec-3's Retail Area and speak with Jared Hanson. Retrieve some of the polymer for me - I have an idea.

NPC: Yes, can I help you?

Your response: Jones sent me, about the polymer you're working on.

NPC: Ah yes, it's quite remarkable. We've taken a standard ultradence polycarbide, and increased its tensile strength by...

Your response: Uh huh. Look, I don't really care. I'm just here for the polymer, pal.

NPC: Oh. Oh no, that's not really possible, you see this...

entries.title: Mission 3: Work with the polymer!
entries.description: Bring Cory Weyland, at the Droner Racetrack, the polymer you got from Mrs. Jones and talk with him.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: Polymer!
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Corey Weyland
• Collect Finished Sword
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

entries.title: Mission 1: Meeting!
entries.description: Talk with Sean Burton at the ASG in sector F_07.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Sean Burton
• Collect ATV components
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner. I am Mrs. Jones. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Glad to hear it. As you're likely aware, Tech Haven is situated quite comfortably in a mountain range, half way between the Dome of York and Neocron City.

Your response: Uh huh.

NPC: Although this affords us security and a necessary amount of solitude, it also raises logistical issues.

Your response: Yeah, I bet. Go on.

NPC: We rely on drivers to transport both supplies and personnel safely across the toxic wastes. This is where you come in. We're working on a new all-terrain vehicle, which should make transport equipment and personnel more efficient, and we'd like you to test it.

Your response: Amazing - how do I start?

NPC: I'm a big believer in drivers understanding their vehicles. With that in mind, you're going to assist in the building of the prototype, and the construction of the vehicle. So first, head over to Sean Burton at the ASG in sector F07. He's in the process of breaking down a number of vehicles, and has some parts you will require.

NPC: Oh, for pity's sake! Not more garbage. Put it over there with the rest.

Your response: Actually, I'm making a collection, not a delivery. Jones said you have some parts for an ATV?

NPC: Thank goodness. I kept getting brought trash - I've got a pile of it bigger than me... well, you know - it's pretty big. Anyway. Yes, here are the components you'll need.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: You need to go and speak with Sean Burton. Come back when you have.

NPC: You got nothing for me...?

NPC: There you are! How are you?

Your response: That wasn't an easy task, but I walked over to Sean Burton and carried those parts back like a true champion.

NPC: Very funny. Now give me a moment to double-check these. Speak with me again when you're ready to proceed.

NPC: Okay - time to fit those parts. Head out and speak with Dana Ord, she will guide you. Don't let her age fool you - she might be a youngster, but she's one hell of a mechanic. It's like machines speak to her.

Your response: Hey, as long as she can do the job, I'm happy

NPC: That's the spirit. She's waiting for you at the 'Hacker's Delight' bar at the Drone Racetrack.

NPC: Hiya, I'm Dana. I heard you have parts for George.

Your response: George?

NPC: Oh... sorry - that's what I called the quad. Ahem. Anyway, pass them here and I'll get them fitted.

Your response: Make sure you don't hurt George.

NPC: There we go - and he ticks over as well! Shiny!

Your response: Wow, that was impressively fast!

NPC: Aww thanks! Okay, now we know that this little guy runs, take the production datacube back to Jones. She knows what to do.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Don't keep Dana waiting, or she'll deconstruct the air vents again...

NPC: Did you enjoy meeting Dana?

Your response: Oh yeah... she's something else.

NPC: I need the datacube!

NPC: Isn't she just. She can strip an engine faster than I can tie my shoes. Hand me the production datacube.

Your response: Here you go!

NPC: Great. Now, all we need to do is get the schematics off for production. Let's talk again when you have time to do that.

NPC: Alright - final part. I've sent the schematics through to Jase Cubbon in Tech Haven Sec-1 - he usually hangs around near the Gravity Lifts. Go and check on the production of these things.

NPC: What do you want?

Your response: Jones sent me about plans - she said we're ready for a test run.

NPC: Oh did she now? Well, that's just great. I'm up to my eyeballs here and she sends you sauntering in and... Fine. Fine. Let's see what she sent me... Hmm, actually, this isn't a bad design. I see what they've done here... clever.

Your response: It sounds like we're good to go then, right?

NPC: Sure. Actually, it looks like my assistance already started the run, and one's ready - take it to Jones.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: Go and speak with Jase and check on production.

NPC: Ah you're back. I hope Cubbon didn't give you any trouble.

Your response: Nothing I couldn't handle - but he did give me this.

NPC: I thought Cubbon gave you something?

NPC: Ah, fantastic. This will allow you to retrieve one of the test quads from an ASG station. I'll tell you what, you keep hold of that - as payment for your help.

Your response: Hey thanks, I'll try not to break it.

NPC: Actually, it wouldn't be a bad thing if you did break it. We'd learn from the experience and make improvements. Anyway, I have things to tend to. Take care.

entries.title: Mission 2: Production Datacube!
entries.description: Talk with Dana Ord at the Hackers Delight Bar at the Drone Racetrack.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Meeting!
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Dana Ord
• Collect ATV Schematics
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner. I am Mrs. Jones. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Glad to hear it. As you're likely aware, Tech Haven is situated quite comfortably in a mountain range, half way between the Dome of York and Neocron City.

Your response: Uh huh.

NPC: Although this affords us security and a necessary amount of solitude, it also raises logistical issues.

Your response: Yeah, I bet. Go on.

NPC: We rely on drivers to transport both supplies and personnel safely across the toxic wastes. This is where you come in. We're working on a new all-terrain vehicle, which should make transport equipment and personnel more efficient, and we'd like you to test it.

Your response: Amazing - how do I start?

NPC: I'm a big believer in drivers understanding their vehicles. With that in mind, you're going to assist in the building of the prototype, and the construction of the vehicle. So first, head over to Sean Burton at the ASG in sector F07. He's in the process of breaking down a number of vehicles, and has some parts you will require.

NPC: Oh, for pity's sake! Not more garbage. Put it over there with the rest.

Your response: Actually, I'm making a collection, not a delivery. Jones said you have some parts for an ATV?

NPC: Thank goodness. I kept getting brought trash - I've got a pile of it bigger than me... well, you know - it's pretty big. Anyway. Yes, here are the components you'll need.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: You need to go and speak with Sean Burton. Come back when you have.

NPC: You got nothing for me...?

NPC: There you are! How are you?

Your response: That wasn't an easy task, but I walked over to Sean Burton and carried those parts back like a true champion.

NPC: Very funny. Now give me a moment to double-check these. Speak with me again when you're ready to proceed.

NPC: Okay - time to fit those parts. Head out and speak with Dana Ord, she will guide you. Don't let her age fool you - she might be a youngster, but she's one hell of a mechanic. It's like machines speak to her.

Your response: Hey, as long as she can do the job, I'm happy

NPC: That's the spirit. She's waiting for you at the 'Hacker's Delight' bar at the Drone Racetrack.

NPC: Hiya, I'm Dana. I heard you have parts for George.

Your response: George?

NPC: Oh... sorry - that's what I called the quad. Ahem. Anyway, pass them here and I'll get them fitted.

Your response: Make sure you don't hurt George.

NPC: There we go - and he ticks over as well! Shiny!

Your response: Wow, that was impressively fast!

NPC: Aww thanks! Okay, now we know that this little guy runs, take the production datacube back to Jones. She knows what to do.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Don't keep Dana waiting, or she'll deconstruct the air vents again...

NPC: Did you enjoy meeting Dana?

Your response: Oh yeah... she's something else.

NPC: I need the datacube!

NPC: Isn't she just. She can strip an engine faster than I can tie my shoes. Hand me the production datacube.

Your response: Here you go!

NPC: Great. Now, all we need to do is get the schematics off for production. Let's talk again when you have time to do that.

NPC: Alright - final part. I've sent the schematics through to Jase Cubbon in Tech Haven Sec-1 - he usually hangs around near the Gravity Lifts. Go and check on the production of these things.

NPC: What do you want?

Your response: Jones sent me about plans - she said we're ready for a test run.

NPC: Oh did she now? Well, that's just great. I'm up to my eyeballs here and she sends you sauntering in and... Fine. Fine. Let's see what she sent me... Hmm, actually, this isn't a bad design. I see what they've done here... clever.

Your response: It sounds like we're good to go then, right?

NPC: Sure. Actually, it looks like my assistance already started the run, and one's ready - take it to Jones.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: Go and speak with Jase and check on production.

NPC: Ah you're back. I hope Cubbon didn't give you any trouble.

Your response: Nothing I couldn't handle - but he did give me this.

NPC: I thought Cubbon gave you something?

NPC: Ah, fantastic. This will allow you to retrieve one of the test quads from an ASG station. I'll tell you what, you keep hold of that - as payment for your help.

Your response: Hey thanks, I'll try not to break it.

NPC: Actually, it wouldn't be a bad thing if you did break it. We'd learn from the experience and make improvements. Anyway, I have things to tend to. Take care.

Mrs. Jones

One time

1

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner. I am Mrs. Jones. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Glad to hear it. As you're likely aware, Tech Haven is situated quite comfortably in a mountain range, half way between the Dome of York and Neocron City.

Your response: Uh huh.

NPC: Although this affords us security and a necessary amount of solitude, it also raises logistical issues.

Your response: Yeah, I bet. Go on.

NPC: We rely on drivers to transport both supplies and personnel safely across the toxic wastes. This is where you come in. We're working on a new all-terrain vehicle, which should make transport equipment and personnel more efficient, and we'd like you to test it.

Your response: Amazing - how do I start?

NPC: I'm a big believer in drivers understanding their vehicles. With that in mind, you're going to assist in the building of the prototype, and the construction of the vehicle. So first, head over to Sean Burton at the ASG in sector F07. He's in the process of breaking down a number of vehicles, and has some parts you will require.

NPC: Oh, for pity's sake! Not more garbage. Put it over there with the rest.

Your response: Actually, I'm making a collection, not a delivery. Jones said you have some parts for an ATV?

NPC: Thank goodness. I kept getting brought trash - I've got a pile of it bigger than me... well, you know - it's pretty big. Anyway. Yes, here are the components you'll need.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: You need to go and speak with Sean Burton. Come back when you have.

NPC: You got nothing for me...?

NPC: There you are! How are you?

Your response: That wasn't an easy task, but I walked over to Sean Burton and carried those parts back like a true champion.

NPC: Very funny. Now give me a moment to double-check these. Speak with me again when you're ready to proceed.

NPC: Okay - time to fit those parts. Head out and speak with Dana Ord, she will guide you. Don't let her age fool you - she might be a youngster, but she's one hell of a mechanic. It's like machines speak to her.

Your response: Hey, as long as she can do the job, I'm happy

NPC: That's the spirit. She's waiting for you at the 'Hacker's Delight' bar at the Drone Racetrack.

NPC: Hiya, I'm Dana. I heard you have parts for George.

Your response: George?

NPC: Oh... sorry - that's what I called the quad. Ahem. Anyway, pass them here and I'll get them fitted.

Your response: Make sure you don't hurt George.

NPC: There we go - and he ticks over as well! Shiny!

Your response: Wow, that was impressively fast!

NPC: Aww thanks! Okay, now we know that this little guy runs, take the production datacube back to Jones. She knows what to do.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Don't keep Dana waiting, or she'll deconstruct the air vents again...

NPC: Did you enjoy meeting Dana?

Your response: Oh yeah... she's something else.

NPC: I need the datacube!

NPC: Isn't she just. She can strip an engine faster than I can tie my shoes. Hand me the production datacube.

Your response: Here you go!

NPC: Great. Now, all we need to do is get the schematics off for production. Let's talk again when you have time to do that.

NPC: Alright - final part. I've sent the schematics through to Jase Cubbon in Tech Haven Sec-1 - he usually hangs around near the Gravity Lifts. Go and check on the production of these things.

NPC: What do you want?

Your response: Jones sent me about plans - she said we're ready for a test run.

NPC: Oh did she now? Well, that's just great. I'm up to my eyeballs here and she sends you sauntering in and... Fine. Fine. Let's see what she sent me... Hmm, actually, this isn't a bad design. I see what they've done here... clever.

Your response: It sounds like we're good to go then, right?

NPC: Sure. Actually, it looks like my assistance already started the run, and one's ready - take it to Jones.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: Go and speak with Jase and check on production.

NPC: Ah you're back. I hope Cubbon didn't give you any trouble.

Your response: Nothing I couldn't handle - but he did give me this.

NPC: I thought Cubbon gave you something?

NPC: Ah, fantastic. This will allow you to retrieve one of the test quads from an ASG station. I'll tell you what, you keep hold of that - as payment for your help.

Your response: Hey thanks, I'll try not to break it.

NPC: Actually, it wouldn't be a bad thing if you did break it. We'd learn from the experience and make improvements. Anyway, I have things to tend to. Take care.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I hear you're interested in using Drones. We could use someone with that talent, if you're interested?

Your response: I'm interested.

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: The drone can take a little bit of getting used to - some droners feel sick when they first interface with the drone's cameras. Other feel a dizziness when breaking the connection. We hope to reduce the discomfort. We've set up a little introduction at the Drone Racetrack. Head down there and speak with Jackie Gnu. She'll guide you through the basics.

NPC: Hello, I am Jackie - the Drone Instructor. Do you have any questions before we start?

Your response: What do I need to know about drone movement?

Your response: What do I need to know about attacking and defending?

Your response: No, I just want to practice flying.

Your response: I think I know it all, can I skip the flying lessons? (Skip tutorial)

NPC: Okay - so I gather you've already learned how to launch and fly the drone. So a refresher - you adjust your vertical elevation using [space] and [ctrl] by default. Your pitch and yaw are controlled via your mouse. You control your forward and backwards movement with [W] and [S] by default. If you fly into things like the ceiling or the floor, your drone might bounce if you're going too quickly. Generally, this won't damage the drone, but it could lead it to taking extra damage from any enemies in the area due to your momentary loss of control.

Your response: Alright, got it.

NPC: I think that covers the basics - do you have any other questions?

Your response: Yeah, could you go over the movement basics again?

Your response: Let's move onto combat

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Hello Runner, I am Mrs. Jones. I represent the Administration of Tech Haven. I understand that you are an Engineer. Would you be interested in some work?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

One time

1

• Complete Mission 2: Constructing-time!

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Morag Harris
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Hello Runner, I am Mrs. Jones. I represent the Administration of Tech Haven, and I have use of an individual with your professional interests. Are you interested?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now.  Another time?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: No doubt you are already aware - Tech Haven is mostly a self-sufficient sanctuary for the scientific minds of the Fallen Angels. However, there are certain materials and supplies which cannot be produced here. For these items, we rely on trade caravans from the waste lands. Recently, one such caravan came under attack - its occupants mostly wiped out.

Your response: What attacked them?

NPC: Of that, I am not currently sure. The bodies have been recovered, and are being investigated by Doctor Tyrell outside of Tech Haven in E07 - she will be near the ramp. If you speak with her, she should be able to shed more details on the situation.

NPC: Ah, you must be the Runner that Jones sent - she just contacted me to say that you were coming. I see you are a Monk... you are too late to save these people.

Your response: Jones mentioned that you might have some information on the cause of death?

NPC: Quite so. We have completed the autopsy. There are significant wounds on each body - they had all been shot. But that's not all: Each of them was found to have chemical burns to their lungs. We believe that, and not the gunshots, was the cause of death. However, we would need a fresher sample to determine the nature of the chemicals used.

Your response: But why would you bother wasting ammunition by shooting a dead body? It makes no sense.

NPC: I'd wager that they were attempting to cover up the true nature of the attack - the gunshots would be sufficient to fool a casual observer. Please, take my findings back to Jones. She will decide what to do next.

NPC: Please return to Mrs. Jones at your apartment to report these findings.

NPC: You need to speak with Dr. Tyrell regarding the autopsy report!

NPC: Ah Runner - what did you discover?

Your response: Dr. Tyrell advised that the caravan appears to have been attacked with a type of chemical agent, and that the bodies were shot afterwards as a coverup.

NPC: And the type of chemical are we talking about?

Your response: Unknown - she said we'd require a fresh sample to determine that.

NPC: I see. This is peculiar. I will see if I can find any more information for myself. I will be in touch soon.

NPC: Ah, perfect timing, I have another task for you. Are you interested?

Your response: Not right now, I will be back though.

Your response: Of course - what do you need?

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me.

NPC: There are security measures at the entrance to Tech Haven, turrets, put in place to prevent intrusion. I have had a report that they have come online just now and killed someone attempting to enter the facility. Call this intuition, but it seems strange that this has occurred so soon after the attack on the traders. Go to Tech Haven Sec-1 - near the bottom of the Gravity Lifts and see what you can find.

NPC: (After searching the body, you find a canister and a technical diagram of Tech Haven's ventilation systems. It seems that the plan was to use the contents of the canister attack the inhabitants of Tech Haven. However, there are no signs as to whom the individual is working for. This should be reported to Jones at once.)

NPC: (You can't find any more information here.)

NPC: You should know what to do!

NPC: Come back to me with whatever you find.

NPC: You're back. What did you find?

Your response: A corpse, a canister, and a diagram of our ventilation systems. Here, take a look.

NPC: What?! This is an outrage! I need to contact the Administration with these findings, and ensure that that appropriate measures are taken. Please, take this reward, and speak with me shortly. You have done a very good job today.

NPC: Your assistance has been invaluable to us so far. Are you ready for one last task?

Your response: Of course, how can I help?

Your response: I have other things to do. I will be back though.

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me.

NPC: I need you to take the canister straight to Dr. Carylon Thoran at the Fallen Angels Tech Core's Medical Room. She is ready to analyse the contents, so that we know what we're dealing with.

NPC: Ah, greetings Runner. Jones told me all about it. Give me the canister, and we'll see what we're working with...

Your response: Yeah, sure!

NPC: I need the canister if you want me to continue.

NPC: Now, let me just feed a sample into the analyser...

Your response: So how long is this gonna take?

NPC: Oh, this will likely take a few hours. Please return to Mrs. Jones and let her know that I will contact her once I know the nature of the contents - and I have a suitable plan for neutralising their usage.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: Take the canister to Dr. Thoran at the Fallen Angels HQ's Medical Room.

NPC: Runner, your assistance has been invaluable. Soon, Dr. Thoran will have a counter-measure in place against any more attempted attacks.

Your response: That's good to know!

NPC: The administration has given me this to pass to you - as a token of their appreciation. Keep up the good work - Tech Haven can use someone with your potential.

entries.title: Mission 1: Data-corruption!
entries.description: Access the Hacknet Terminal in Tech Haven Sec-2 and then access the ALPHA TERMINAL.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Alpha Terminal
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah Runner, welcome to Tech Haven. It says here that you have network security experience. I have use of your skills, if you're interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Good to hear it. As you probably already know, Tech Haven has one of the most sophisticated networks in the world - and has access to both Neocron and the Dome of York's networks.

Your response: If I understand it correctly, Tech Haven is a hub, and also keeps a lot of the uplinks in the wastelands going.

NPC: Something like that. I'm not a tech-specialist. However, as you can appreciate, being at the top also paints a large target on our backs. So we have to routinely monitor network security.

Your response: Let me guess, that's where I come in right?

NPC: Exactly. Head to the Small Database Link terminal in Tech Haven Sec-2 - you'll find it near the tools and parts traders. Access the ALPHA TERMINAL inside there, and run this program. Come back when it's done.

NPC: E R R O R  4 0 1  - - -  A B O R T  - - -  N O   I N P U T   F O U N D

NPC: (The scanner whirls away for a few moments, and then identifies that a number of ports have been opened recently. Checking the logs, it appears that they were all done by the same person. It feels unusual. This should be reported to Jones.)

NPC: Go and complete the security scan, and we will talk.

NPC: Welcome back runner. I trust everything is in order?

Your response: Actually, I've spotted something which I think you should take a look at.

NPC: Hmm. This is very peculiar. All of these ports correspond with some very sensitive material. It looks like these changes might have been internal as well.

Your response: You mean someone in Tech Haven did this? Do you have any idea who?

NPC: Not yet. Give me a moment to think, and we will discuss this further!

NPC: It's my understanding that we have a secondary system which logs all access to our networks. It uses a form of internal authentication to prevent external changes.

Your response: I'm assuming that this system has some form of logging procedure. So, we can find out who made the changes?

NPC: That's the plan. The secondary system isn't something we publicise, so there's a very good chance our friend wasn't aware their actions were recorded. Head back to the same Hacknet Terminal in Sector 2 and access BETA TERMINAL within!

NPC: (It appears that the system has indeed taken a full log of the security breach. Jones would be interested in seeing this.)

NPC: Connection terminated!

***Access Denied!***


***Authorisation required from Agent Jones to access***

NPC: Come back with the security logs.

NPC: You're back, and with the security logs. Let me see.

Your response: Here they are.

NPC: Oh my. Not good. Did you read these?

Your response: Yes, I did. All the ports were opened by one employee - Harrington, G.

NPC: Agreed. I will begin a search for Mr. Harrington. Speak with me in a moment, and we can proceed.

NPC: Alright, I've located Harrington. He's in Energy Core 1. The entrance to that is located within Tech Haven Sec-1 - I want you to question him.

Your response: Why not just send security?

NPC: I don't want to scare him off. See what you can learn, then return to me.

NPC: Yes? Can I help you?

Your response: George Harrington, I have a couple of questions for you.

NPC: I'm sorry, I really don't have time to chat right now.

Your response: I recommend that you make time, this is about a security breach in Tech Haven's network.

NPC: W-what? No. I d-don't know anything about that.

Your response: I pulled logs from another system which recorded your access credentials, and the changes that were made.

NPC: Oh... No. That wasn't me. S-someone must have used my password!

Your response: Then why are you sweating so much? Listen, answer my questions, or I'll call security. Co-operate and I'll see what can be done for you!

NPC: No, please. Don't. Okay, look. I admit that I opened the ports. I needed the money, and I thought I could sell some research projects or something.

Your response: You were trying to sell out the whole of Tech Haven for a few credits? That's pretty low.

NPC: You don't understand. I owe money to the kinds of people you don't want to owe anything to. This was my last chance to get clean, now I have nothing.

Your response: Okay. Look, the only thing I can suggest is we take you in - place you in custody, so they cannot get to you.

NPC: And let Tech Haven security have their way with me instead? No way.

Your response: What's it gonna be, then?

NPC: I'm a dead man now - but I can still go on my own terms! (Before you have time to react, Harrington pulls out a pistol, places it in his mouth and pulls the trigger. You should let Jones know about this.)

NPC: Don't come back until you've spoken with Harrington.

NPC: Did you deal with Harrington?

Your response: Yeah - he iced himself.

NPC: What? He's dead? Did you have a chance to speak with him?

Your response: Briefly, before he ate his own pistol. He said he was working alone - selling data to cover some debts.

NPC: Selfish idiot. He risked lives over something so trivial?

Your response: He did. What happens now?

NPC: I'll set a team plugging any remaining security holes. I'm going to go and check Harrington's apartment and make sure he was working alone. Here, take this - I think we might speak again in the future.

entries.description: Access the Hacknet Terminal in Tech Haven Sec-2 and then access the BETA TERMINAL.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 1: Data-corruption!
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Beta Terminal
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 2,000 credits
• 2,000 experience

entries.title: Mission 3: Data-corruption!
entries.description: Interrogate Harrington, he's located in Tech Haven Sec-1, Energy Core 1.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

POSSIBLE PREREQUISITES
• Complete Mission 2: Data-corruption!
Other conditions may also apply.

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Harrington
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 3,000 credits
• 3,000 experience

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah Runner, welcome to Tech Haven. It says here that you have network security experience. I have use of your skills, if you're interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Constance Wong
• Collect Picture box
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah Runner, welcome to Tech Haven. It's my understanding that you have experience of investigation and espionage? I need help with something - interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Excellent. There is a breed of drugs being introduced into Tech Haven. Addictive and nasty. I want to find out who the supplier is.

Your response: Okay, any leads?

NPC: Constance Wong, one of the Command Centre's administrators has been admitted to the Medical Room at the Fallen Angels Tech Core - we believe she was under the influence. Speak with her and find out what she knows.

Your response: And if I find out where the drugs are coming from?

NPC: Report back to me. Where-ever there are drugs, there is danger - I'd rather plan properly than risk sending you in alone.

NPC: (Constance glances up. Her pupils are wide, and she is sweating, despite the room's coolness.)

Your response: Constance, my name is %PLAYER_NAME(). We think that you've taken something. Can you tell me about it?

NPC: I wasss out with friendsss. A party. We met a guy who bought me some drinksss. Then I woke up here. I never took nothing - I swear!

Your response: Any idea who that person is?

NPC: (Constance shakes her head slowly, and her eyes start to close.)

Your response: Stay with me, Constance. Can you give me a description of him?

NPC: No. Wait... picturesss. There's picturesss on this.

Your response: Okay Constance, that's great. Look, I need to borrow this - but I'll make sure you get it back.

NPC: So many picturesss!

NPC: You got nothing for me...?

NPC: Speak with Constance Wong, then we'll talk.

NPC: Any luck with Constance?

Your response: She was pretty out of it, but she said there are pictures on this.

NPC: I've read her medical reports. From what I gather, she was close to comatose when she was found. She's lucky they brought her back around.

Your response: Here, Jones, I think I found a picture of the guy we're looking for. Is he familiar?

NPC: Not really - but I have a facial recognition program I can use. Speak with me in a moment and we'll see what it says.

NPC: Okay, it looks like our lead is from out of town - a city Runner called Jase Dunn. Find out what he knows.

Your response: Any idea where he is?

NPC: I'd try the bar at the Drone Racetrack - there's a good chance he'll be hanging around there.

NPC: Yeah, what the fuck do you want?

Your response: I need to talk to you about Constance Wong.

NPC: Who? Never heard of her...

Your response: I have a photo which proves you were together last night, before she was slipped a drug. She nearly died.

NPC: Whoa - no way. Look, I admit, I slipped her the drug. But they told me it would just put her in the mood to party. Nothing more, I swear.

Your response: You're sick. Tell me where you got it from, or I am going to seriously fuck your day up!

NPC: Okay! Okay! I got it from Fast Eddy. Please - don't hurt me!

Your response: You're lucky I've got more important things to do. Fuck off, before I change my mind.

NPC: Alright! I'm going!

NPC: I told you everything!

NPC: Come back when you've spoken with our mystery man.

NPC: Did you find anything out from our 'friend'.

Your response: I learned he's a scumbag wanna-be rapist.

NPC: I see. Don't worry about that, I'll make sure he is picked up and 'dealt with'. What else did you discover?

Your response: He got the drugs from a guy called Fast Eddy. Does the name ring any bells?

NPC: Unfortunately, yes. Let me check the security net and see where he is. Speak with me again in a moment.

NPC: Okay, it appears that Fast Eddy is loitering in Tech Haven Sec-3, near the bottom of the stairway. Go and see what he has to say. He has a history of violence, so make sure you're armed before you go.

Your response: So much for not sending me into harm's way...

NPC: I don't like it either, but I think you can handle him. Come back when you've sorted Eddy out.

NPC: Hey, you - you in the market for a good time? I can hook you up.

Your response: Some of the stuff you have been peddling has been sending some of those girls straight to the infirmary. Please stop what you're doing, before one of them ends up in the morgue.

Your response: You are going to stop peddling that shit of yours, or I'm gonna take all those pills from you and shove them straight up your ass. Let's see how your body deals with that.

NPC: Boo fuckin' hoo. And why should I care about those bitches?

Your response: You either stop peddling that shit, or you end up dealing with TH security!

NPC: Yeah? Is that so? And who's going to call security if I take you out?

NPC: Hah! I'd like to see you try, motherfucker!

NPC: ...

NPC: Don't come back until you've spoken with Eddy.

NPC: Did you deal with Eddy?

Your response: Yeah - he won't be peddling that shit any more.

NPC: Well, that's one less scumbag to worry about at least. Did you recover anything from him?

Your response: No, he wasn't carrying the stash on him...

NPC: Shame. Oh well, it should be rather trivial to track down. Eddy was never a smart person, after all.

Your response: So, what happens now?

NPC: I'm going to shake down a couple of his known haunts - I'm sure I'll find his drugs there. You did well - I have a feeling we'll speak again.

Your response: Yeah. Let me know if I can be of assistance in the future.

NPC: Naturally. Oh, and before I go, take this. You'll find it will come in useful for future endeavours.

NPC: Okay, it appears that Fast Eddy is loitering in Tech Haven Sec-3, near the bottom of the stairway. Go and see what he has to say. He has a history of violence, so make sure you're armed before you go.

entries.title: Mission 1: Wasteland Invasion!
entries.description: Speak with Declan Swan inside the Fallen Angels Tech Core.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Mrs. Jones

REPEAT
One time

DIFFICULTY
1

OBJECTIVES
• Talk to Declan Swan
• Talk to Mrs. Jones

REWARDS
• 1,000 credits
• 1,000 experience
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Ah, runner. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I have a task that I need assistance with, if you are interested.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: First: Although Tech Haven is a dedicated technocracy, I do want to assure you that you are welcome here.

Your response: Reassuring - I thought you'd look down on a PSI Monk.

NPC: We are reasonable and logical - we learned difficult lessons from your predecessors, but we do not hold those experiences against you personally.

Your response: Fine - what about this task you mentioned?

NPC: We have an agreement of sorts with settlers in the area. We trade equipment made here for supplies they bring in from the outside world. However, we have reason to believe they are attempting to spread an alien influence within Tech Haven.

Your response: What sort of influence are you referring to?

NPC: We're unsure at the moment. They have been limiting key resources - releasing them only when we agree to supply weapons - something which they have not previously requested.

Your response: Protecting yourself in the wastes isn't suspicious.

NPC: No, but the frequency and volume is. We need to ensure that they are not distributing them to Neocron - or to any other unsavoury party

Your response: Okay, and where do you recommend I start looking?

NPC: Go ahead and speak with Declan Swan inside the Fallen Angels Tech Core. He's their primary handler and might be able to give you some insight on where to begin looking.

NPC: Yes? How can I help? Keep it brief.

Your response: Jones sent me about the unusual demands being made by local traders.

NPC: Ah yes... that. They've begun to request weapons, ammunition, clothing, and other supplies. All in much larger volumes than a settlement of their size could require.

Your response: Do you have any idea why that is?

NPC: I only asked once, and their response was quite disagreeable. I understand that they are expecting an influx of new occupants in the near future.

Your response: I wonder where they might be coming from. There are only so many folks in the wastes.

NPC: Honestly, I couldn't say. We've left them encamped outside the city as a precaution, but I understand one of their lieutenants is currently outside the Command Centre, waiting for a meeting.

Your response: Thanks for the info, Declan.

NPC: You should head back to Jones and let her know about this...

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Come back once you've spoken with Declan.

NPC: Welcome back - did Declan give you anything useful?

Your response: Not really. He thinks that the traders are preparing for a sudden settlement expansion.

NPC: Peculiar. I'm not aware of any groups in the area which would be large enough to require this amount of equipment. What else did he say?

Your response: One of their leaders is currently in front of the Fallen Angels Tech Core, waiting for a meeting.

NPC: Ah yes, I seem to remember hearing about that. Let me check on the reason for the meeting - speak to me again in a moment.

NPC: Am I right to assume you wish to continue with your mission?

Your response: Let's do this!

Your response: I've got other things to do. Speak soon?

NPC: Very well, I shall wait here for you.
