   2  -- Script  : FOA_NC_TG.LUA
   3  -- Author  : Nick "Nidhogg" Milner
   4  -- Date    : 30-JUL-04
   5  -- Version : 1.0
   6  -- Description:
   7  
   8  -- This is the dialog for the Twilight Guardian Faction Office Assistant.
   9  
  10  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  11  -- Change History:
  12  -- Date           Author  Description
  13  -- 07-JUN-04  NM      Heavily modified U-Turn's original and added dialog text
  14  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  15  
  16  -- Faction ID definitions
  17  facid_CA	= 1
  18  facid_DRE	= 2
  19  facid_NXT	= 3
  20  facid_TT	= 4
  21  facid_BT	= 5
  22  facid_PP	= 6
  23  facid_TS	= 8
  24  facid_BD	= 9
  25  facid_CS	= 10
  26  facid_CM	= 11
  27  facid_FA	= 14
  28  facid_TG	= 15
  29  
  30  
  31  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  32  -- Function    : HELP
  33  -- Description : Calls other NPCs in the area to attack the runner
  34  -- Inputs      : none
  35  -- Side-effects: none
  36  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  37  function HELP()
  38  	--actions 
  39  	-- 4 - help
  40  	if (node==state) then
  41  		SendScriptMsg("npcaction", dialogclass, 4)
  42  	end
  43  end
  44  
  45  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  46  -- Function    : CANDOEPICRUN
  47  -- Description : Checks to see if the runner is able to perform the given
  48  --               mission of the given faction's epic run
  49  -- Inputs      : factionid - the ID of the faction (as given above)
  50  --               missionid - the mission number within the run (0 base)
  51  -- Side-effects: result modified
  52  --                 -1 = the runner is unable to perform that mission
  53  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  54  function CANDOEPICRUN(factionid, missionid)
  55  
  56    if (node==state) then
  57  
  58      SendScriptMsg("candoepicrun", dialogclass, factionid, missionid)
  59  
  60    end -- if
  61  
  62  end -- function CANDOEPICRUN()
  63  
  64  
  65  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  66  -- Function    : CHECKFACTION
  67  -- Description : Checks to see if the runner is of the given faction
  68  -- Inputs      : facid - The ID of the faction to check for
  69  -- Side-effects: result modified
  70  --                 0 = not in the given faction
  71  --                 1 = in the given faction
  72  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  73  function CHECKFACTION(facid)
  74  
  75    if (node==state) then
  76  
  77      -- If the runner can do the epic run then s/he must be in this faction
  78      CANDOEPICRUN(facid,0) 
  79  
  80      if (result==-1) then
  81  
  82        -- Can't do the mission
  83        result = 0
  84  
  85      else
  86  
  87        -- Can do the mission
  88        result = 1
  89  
  90      end -- if
  91  
  92    end -- if
  93  
  94  end -- function CHECKFACTION()
  95  
  96  
  97  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  98  -- Function    : DIRECTJUMP
  99  -- Description : Jumps to a different place in the dialog.  When that
 100  --               completes it returns back to the original place.
 101  -- Inputs      : The node ID of the dialog to jump to
 102  -- Side-effects: None
 103  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 104  function DIRECTJUMP(newnode)
 105  
 106    if (node==state) then
 107  
 108      -- Remember where we are in the dialog right now
 109      local savestate = state
 110  
 111      -- Move to the new point in the dialog
 112      state = newnode
 113  
 114      -- Run the dialog from the new point
 115      DIALOG()
 116  
 117      -- Go back to where we were
 118      state = savestate
 119  
 120    end -- if
 121  
 122  end -- function DIRECTJUMP()
 123  
 124  
 125  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 126  -- Function    : DIALOG
 127  -- Description : Controls the flow of the FOA's dialog with the runner
 128  -- Inputs      : None
 129  -- Side-effects: None
 130  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 131  function DIALOG()
 132  
 133    -- Set the result to a default value
 134    result = 0;
 135  
 136    -- Start here
 137    NODE(0)
 138  
 139      -- Is the runner TG?
 140      CHECKFACTION(facid_TG)
 141  
 142      if (result==1) then
 143  
 144        -- Runner is TG so talk nicely
 145        DIRECTJUMP(100) 
 146  
 147      else
 148  
 149        -- Runner is not TG
 150        DIRECTJUMP(50) 
 151  
 152      end -- if
 153  
 154    -- Dialog end point
 155    NODE(1)
 156  
 157      SAY("Go in freedom.")
 158      
 159      -- The end
 160      ENDDIALOG()
 161  
 162    -- Nasty dialog end point
 163    NODE(2)
 164  
 165      -- Nasty goodbye
 166      SAY("Come back when you have the guts to stand up for your beliefs.  You make me sick! ")
 167      
 168      -- The end
 169      ENDDIALOG()
 170  
 171    -- Runner is not TG
 172    NODE(50)
 173  
 174      -- Find out what this runner's TG faction sympathy is
 175      GETFACTIONSYMPATHY(facid_TG)
 176  
 177      -- Is the runner a member of a friendly faction?
 178      if (result>=0) then
 179  
 180        -- This runner is friendly
 181        DIRECTJUMP(51) 
 182  
 183      else
 184  
 185        -- This runner is an enemy!
 186        DIRECTJUMP(76) 
 187  
 188      end -- if
 189  
 190    -- Runner is friendly but not TG
 191    NODE(51)
 192  
 193      SAY("Who told you about this place?  Why are you here? ")
 194  
 195      ANSWER("I wish to join the Twilight Guardian and help destroy the corruption within Neocron! ",60)
 196      ANSWER("I wanted to see what you bozos were up to.  Frankly I am not impressed and would not join you if you paid me. ",2)
 197  
 198    -- How to join
 199    NODE(60)
 200  
 201      SAY("For security reasons we cannot accept memberships here.  Please go to our headquarters within the Dome and talk to one of our recruiters there. ")
 202      ENDDIALOG()
 203  
 204    -- Runner is an enemy
 205    NODE(76)
 206  
 207      SAY("You have a fucking nerve coming here?  You like repression?  I'm going to repress your ability to breathe... ")
 208  
 209      -- Call for help
 210      HELP()
 211      ENDDIALOG()
 212  
 213    -- Deliver the full FOA dialog
 214    NODE(100)
 215  
 216      SAY("Welcome.  How can I help you? ")
 217      ANSWER("What can you tell me about this place? ",150)
 218      ANSWER("What can you tell me about the faction counsil? ",200)   
 219      ANSWER("Ah, never mind.  Thanks for your time. ",1)
 220  
 221        -- Describe the offices generally
 222    NODE(150)
 223  
 224      SAY("The Twilight Guardian offices are quite simply where the big decisions are taken - the decisions that will remove the corrupt government from Neocron.  All Twilight Guardian runners may find sanctuary here.  We have a supply depot, a faction office, a main office and a regeneration area. ")
 225      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the supply depot? ",155)
 226      ANSWER("What can you tell me about the faction office? ",160)
 227      ANSWER("The main office sounds important.  What can you tell me about that? ",165)
 228      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the regeneration area? ",170)
 229      ANSWER("Great.  Thanks for the information. ",1)
 230      
 231    -- Talk about the supply depot
 232    NODE(155)
 233  
 234      SAY("The supply depot is run by the Resource Supply Manager and sells virtually everything that you will need.  You also qualify for a 10 percent discount. ")
 235      ANSWER("What can you tell me about the faction office? ",160)
 236      ANSWER("The main office sounds important.  What can you tell me about that? ",165)
 237      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the regeneration area? ",170)
 238      ANSWER("Thanks for the information. ",1)
 239      
 240    -- Talk about the faction office
 241    NODE(160)
 242  
 243      SAY("The faction office is where you can find the central counsil chamber.  It's where the counsil gather to strategise how to remove the City Admin from power. ")
 244      ANSWER("What is the faction counsil? ",200)
 245      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the supply depot you mentioned earlier? ",155)
 246      ANSWER("The main office you mentioned sounds important.  What can you tell me about that? ",165)
 247      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the regeneration area? ",170)
 248      ANSWER("Thanks.  That's all I needed to know. ",1)
 249      
 250    -- Talk about the main office
 251    NODE(165)
 252  
 253      SAY("The main office is where people who have become tired with the constant abuse, harassment and torture perpetrated by this government come to help put a stop to it.  Prospective new members of the Twilight guardian may talk to recruiters there. ")
 254  
 255      ANSWER("What is the faction counsil? ",200)
 256      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the supply depot you mentioned earlier? ",155)
 257      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the regeneration area? ",170)
 258      ANSWER("Thanks.  I have no more questions. ",1)
 259      
 260    -- Talk about the regeneration area
 261    NODE(170)
 262  
 263      SAY("The regeneration area provides medical treatment to our brave soldiers.  A wide variety of medical drugs are also on offer here. ")
 264  
 265      ANSWER("Can you tell me about the supply depot please? ",155)
 266      ANSWER("What can you tell me about the faction office? ",160)
 267      ANSWER("The main office sounds important.  What can you tell me about that? ",165)
 268      ANSWER("What is the faction counsil all about then? ",200)
 269      ANSWER("Thanks for all your information. ",1)
 270      
 271    -- Describe the faction counsil
 272    NODE(200)
 273  
 274      SAY("The Twilight Guardian counsil are the policy makers and commanders of all TG runners and clans.  In order to be effective against the City Admin scum we must communicate and co-ordinate and *that* is the job of the counsil. ")
 275  
 276      ANSWER("Who gets to sit on the counsil? ",210)
 277      ANSWER("What else can you tell me about? ",150)
 278      ANSWER("Thanks for all your help. ",1)
 279      
 280    -- Describe who makes up the counsil
 281    NODE(210)
 282  
 283      SAY("Each Twilight Guardian clan can choose a member to be elected to the counsil.  All Twilight Guardian runners are then elligible to vote and the winners are duly elected. ")
 284  
 285      ANSWER("What else can you tell me about? ",150)
 286      ANSWER("Thanks for all your help. ",1)
 287      
 288  end -- TG FOA Dialog

entries.details:
CONTACT
Faction Office Assistant

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sayonara.

NPC: Ahondara ya de!

NPC: Nan da kor' ya?  What are you doing here?  Who told you about this place?

Your response: That's not important.  What *is* important is that I want to join Tsunami.  I can be useful to you.

Your response: Er, I'm just leaving.

NPC: Do I look like a pencil-pushing personnel officer?  Go see our guys in the dome if you wish to discover honour within yourself.  Tell them I sent you.

NPC: Nan da yo? Omae aho ya de!

NPC: You better have a good reason for being here.

Your response: What is going on here?

Your response: I want to know how we can use the counsil to fight back at our enemies.

Your response: Just looking.

NPC: The key thing you need to know is that this place is for Tsunami only.  If it gets out that you told *anyone* about this location I wil burn your life down.  Clear?  Our faction office is located here and here only.  Also, feel free to use the supply depot and the regeneration area.

Your response: Please can you tell me about the supply depot?

Your response: What can you tell me about the faction office?

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?

Your response: Thanks for your help.

NPC: The supply depot is run by the Resource Supply Manager and contains many useful pieces of equipment.  You can get a 10 percent discount on all goods.

Your response: What can you tell me about the faction office?

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?

Your response: Thanks for your help.

NPC: The faction office is where the Tsunami counsil resides, hidden here deep within the heart of our enemies.

Your response: What is the faction counsil?

Your response: Can you tell me about the supply depot you mentioned earlier?

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?

Your response: Thanks.  That's all I needed to know.

NPC: The regeneration area can be used to rest and heal yourself should you be involved in any trouble outside.

Your response: Can you tell me about the supply depot please?

Your response: What can you tell me about the faction office?

Your response: What is the faction counsil all about then?

Your response: Thanks for all your information.

NPC: The counsil provides direction and control for all Tsunami.  They can be very generous but they are *always* unforgiving so it is probably best not to get too well known.

Your response: Who gets to sit on the counsil?

Your response: What else can you tell me about?

Your response: Thanks for all your help.

NPC: Every Tsunami clan has the right to nominate a member to reside on the counsil.  Every Tsunami runner can then vote to decide who wins.

Your response: What else can you tell me about?

Your response: Thanks for all your help.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Faction Office Assistant

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Be safe, runner.

NPC: Welcome to the security of Tangent Technologies.  How may I help?

Your response: Could you tell me how I might join Tangent?

Your response: Thanks, maybe some other time, eh?

NPC: Tangent Technologies is *the* premier provider of peace of mind and it might be possible for you to join us if you think you are up to the task.  Please visit an H.R. Director over in the main office.

NPC: You are here to view our merchandise eh?  Let me arrange a demonstration right away...

NPC: Good day.  I am the Tangent Technologies Faction Office Assistant.  How can I help you today?

Your response: What can you tell me about this place?

Your response: Do you have a counsil, like the other factions?

Your response: Thanks but I have no more questions to ask.

NPC: Tangent Technologies employees enjoy wealth and security here in the faction offices.  We have a supply depot containing many examples of the most advanced weaponry the world has ever seen, a faction office, a main office for admin and a regeneration area, should you have an unfortunate run in with one of your own products.

Your response: Please can you tell me about the supply depot?  Sounds like there are some cool gadgets!

Your response: What can you tell me about the faction office?

Your response: I'm interested in finding out more about the main office.  It just sounds so *main*!

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?  I think I could do with a lie down.

Your response: Thanks for your help.

NPC: The Resource Supply Manager heads up the supply depot and always holds the most breathtaking weapons in stock (literally).  You also automatically qualify for a generous 10 percent discount on all items purchased.

Your response: What can you tell me about the faction office?

Your response: I was wondering what the main office is for?

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?

Your response: What does the Faction Supply Manager do?

Your response: Thanks for your help.

NPC: The Faction Supply Manager provides sophisticated hi-tech items that can only be used by Tangent employees.  Very neat stuff.

Your response: What can you tell me about the faction office?

Your response: What can you tell me about the main office?

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?

Your response: Thanks for the information.

NPC: The most important thing to know about the faction office is that is where you can find the central counsil chamber.  This is the place where all security and product decisions are taken.

Your response: Can you tell me more about the faction counsil?

Your response: Can you tell me about the supply depot you mentioned earlier?

Your response: The main office?

Your response: Can you tell me about the regeneration area?

Your response: Thanks.  I have no more questions.

NPC: The main office is where people who wish to join our great company sign up.  Naturally security is high there.  Actually, security is high *everywhere*.

Your response: What is the faction counsil?

  47  function bitvalue(pos)
  48  	if (pos==-1) then return 0 end
  49  	if (pos==0) then return 1 end
  50  	if (pos==1) then return 2 end
  51  	if (pos==2) then return 4 end
  52  	if (pos==3) then return 8 end
  53  	if (pos==4) then return 16 end
  54  	if (pos==5) then return 32 end
  55  	if (pos==6) then return 64 end
  56  	if (pos==7) then return 128 end
  57  	if (pos==8) then return 256 end
  58  	if (pos==9) then return 512 end
  59  	if (pos==10) then return 1024 end
  60  	if (pos==11) then return 2048 end
  61  	if (pos==12) then return 4096 end
  62  	if (pos==13) then return 8192 end
  63  	if (pos==14) then return 16384 end
  64  	if (pos==15) then return 32768 end
  65  end

  67  -- makes ordinal out of float (positive only)
  68  function trunc(val)
  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;
  71  	while (testval<val) and (testval+1<val) do
  72  		if (testval+bitvalue(testbit)>val) then
  73  			testval = testval + bitvalue(testbit-1) 
  74  			testbit = 0
  75  		else
  76  			testbit = testbit + 1
  77  		end
  78  		if (testbit>15) then
  79  			return -1
  80  		end
  81  	end
  82  	return testval
  83  end
  84  
  85  -- makes modular
  86  function mod(val,divider)
  87  	return val - (trunc(val/divider) * divider)
  88  end

  67  -- makes ordinal out of float (positive only)
  68  function trunc(val)
  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;
  71  	while (testval<val) and (testval+1<val) do
  72  		if (testval+bitvalue(testbit)>val) then
  73  			testval = testval + bitvalue(testbit-1) 
  74  			testbit = 0
  75  		else
  76  			testbit = testbit + 1
  77  		end
  78  		if (testbit>15) then
  79  			return -1
  80  		end
  81  	end
  82  	return testval
  83  end

  68  function trunc(val)
  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;
  71  	while (testval<val) and (testval+1<val) do
  72  		if (testval+bitvalue(testbit)>val) then
  73  			testval = testval + bitvalue(testbit-1) 
  74  			testbit = 0

  77  		end

  80  		end
  81  	end
  82  	return testval
  83  end

  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;

  81  	end
  82  	return testval

 173  function JOBRAND(jobs, level)
 174  	--  get one not at beginning or end
 175  	RAND(jobs - 2)
 176  	mitte = result
 177  	jobchoose1 = mitte + 11
 178  	--  get one left of the middle one
 179  	RAND(mitte + 1)
 180  	jobchoose2 = result + 10
 181  	-- get one right of the middle one
 182  	RAND(jobs - mitte)
 183  	jobchoose3 = 9 + jobs - result
 184  	
 185  	return jobchoose1, jobchoose2, jobchoose3

  67  -- makes ordinal out of float (positive only)
  68  function trunc(val)
  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;
  71  	while (testval<val) and (testval+1<val) do
  72  		if (testval+bitvalue(testbit)>val) then
  73  			testval = testval + bitvalue(testbit-1) 
  74  			testbit = 0
  75  		else

  77  		end

  80  		end
  81  	end
  82  	return testval
  83  end

 169  -- JOB randomizer 
 170  -- random through the jobs and get 3
 171  -- TAKE CARE!! function assumes your jobs start with 10  NOT with 0 !!!
 172  
 173  function JOBRAND(jobs, level)
 174  	--  get one not at beginning or end
 175  	RAND(jobs - 2)
 176  	mitte = result
 177  	jobchoose1 = mitte + 11
 178  	--  get one left of the middle one
 179  	RAND(mitte + 1)
 180  	jobchoose2 = result + 10
 181  	-- get one right of the middle one
 182  	RAND(jobs - mitte)
 183  	jobchoose3 = 9 + jobs - result
 184  	
 185  	return jobchoose1, jobchoose2, jobchoose3
 186  	
 187  end

  49  	if (pos==0) then return 1 end

  51  	if (pos==2) then return 4 end

  67  -- makes ordinal out of float (positive only)
  68  function trunc(val)
  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;
  71  	while (testval<val) and (testval+1<val) do
  72  		if (testval+bitvalue(testbit)>val) then
  73  			testval = testval + bitvalue(testbit-1) 
  74  			testbit = 0
  75  		else
  76  			testbit = testbit + 1
  77  		end
  78  		if (testbit>15) then
  79  			return -1
  80  		end
  81  	end
  82  	return testval
  83  end

  67  -- makes ordinal out of float (positive only)
  68  function trunc(val)
  69  	testval = 0 ;
  70  	testbit = 0 ;

  74  			testbit = 0

  80  		end
  81  	end
  82  	return testval

entries.details:
CONTACT
Frank Ferguson

ITEMS THE NPC MAY ASK FOR
• code snippets reg: #0122-VGPX

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• It is about the acquisition of code snippets out of the Tech Haven Bridge. I need them realy urgent and I am looking for somebody who is sneaky enough to do this run fast and without getting too much attention. Have I found the right one?

• That's right, chummer, you can only win. The code snippets should be findable in the repository of the infected storages of Tech Haven Bridge. Be carefull! I heard that there are some defect defence programs twangig around, so it can be hot there...

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: (angry) I already gave you the access to the secret repository. What else do you want? Piss off!

NPC: Hey Chummer!

Your response: Who? Me? What do you want from me?

NPC: You really need to learn a little bit more before you can help me. Come back when you _really_ can call yourself a hacker.

NPC: Hey you! Yes, you! Are interested in a run? I am sure it will be worth the effort, chummer.

Your response: That depends on what it is...

Your response: Nope, thank you.

NPC: It is about the acquisition of code snippets out of the Tech Haven Bridge. I need them realy urgent and I am looking for somebody who is sneaky enough to do this run fast and without getting too much attention. Have I found the right one?

Your response: Maybe... But what would I get out of this?

Your response: Nah, I am usually like a bull in a china shop, find someone else.

NPC: Well, then you better return to your ranch...

NPC: Hmm... If you get these code snippets for me, I can grant you access to some secret Phoenix NC databases, which include some interesting and - even more important - valuable data.

Your response: Okay, that sounds really tantalizing, but... why do _you_ have the possibility to give me access to these databases? What is your connection to Phoenix NC?

Your response: I am sorry, but I don't think that I am interested in that. But thanks for that offer.

NPC: That's beside the point, chummer. Just trust me. Get me five 'Code Snippets Reg:#0122-VGPX' and that's the deal. Just give it a try and you will see it is worth your while, chummer.

Your response: Okay, I think I have nothing to loose here. Where can I find these code snippets?

NPC: That's right, chummer, you can only win. The code snippets should be findable in the repository of the infected storages of Tech Haven Bridge. Be carefull! I heard that there are some defect defence programs twangig around, so it can be hot there...

Your response: No problem, I can take care of myself. Time to go, I guess.

NPC: Fine, fine... But don't become a sensation inside the net, understood? See ya later, chummer.

NPC: Great work, chummer! Exactly the code snippets I need. Okay, I will grant you the access to the secret Phoenix NC databases, but keep your mouth shut who did it for you, or I will show you my other side!

Your response: No need for that, you can trust me.

NPC: What are you doing here? Why aren't you in the net to get me these code snippets? Didn't I tell you that I need it urgent? Should I spell it for you? U R G E N T! So move your ass!

NPC: *does some typing, but you can't see exactly what he is typing* Argh... typo *does it again* Okay, now you have access to the databases. Use it wise. They say that these databases also contain some super rare fragments of the stolen data from the Tangent High Security Mainframe.

Your response: Interesting! So, where can I find these databases?

NPC: The databases are not to be found at a glance and I can't tell you where exactly they are. Watch out for repositories which are linked with the customer registration of the local companies. One of them is containing the data you are looking for.

Your response: Will do so. Let's hope that the whole story was worth the trouble I had.

NPC: It will be profitable, chummer. Believe me. So.. move out now, please, I have some things to do.

Your response: One more thing.

NPC: Shoot. I really got stuff to do.

Your response: What are those data fragments you mentioned?

NPC: Oh, that I can tell you. The data fragments are part of a larger data packet. If you recycle several fragments, you will receive the blueprints for a few of Tangent Technologies' weapon prototypes. The databases I just gave you access to contain a few fragments, but there are more out there.

Your response: Interesting. Where can I find the rest of the fragments?

NPC: I don't know for sure. I heard that some fragments may be obtainable from Corrupt ICMP Ping Packets and Intrusion Countermeasure Daemons. The Phoenix CPU probably plays some role too. But I'm not really into that underground hacking stuff anymore, that's way out of my league. Well, I really gotta go now. Take care, Chummer!

entries.conversation:
NPC: Welch ein wunderschöner Tag an dem ich Dich, meinen Freund, in meine Arme schließen kann. Ich möchte das Du statt der Ringe diesen Trank nimmst. Er ist etwas ganz besonderes. Hüte ihn gut und bewahre unsere Freundschaft immer in Deinem Herzen.

Your response: Danke Mann. Das ist ja cool. Mach Dir keine Sorgen. Ich werde Dich nicht vergessen und weiter für Eure Sache kämpfen.

NPC: Crahn sei mit, O Freund des Zargerus. Kämpfer für das Gute. Was kann ich für Dich tun

Your response: Ich möchte Euch helfen. Mitkämpfen!

Your response: Ich möchte mit für Eure Sache kämpfen!

Your response: Gibt es nichts was ich für Dich tun kann?

Your response: Du machst einen glücklichen Eindruck, gibt es nichts was ich für Dich tun kann?

Your response: Was macht Ihr hier? Eine Gruppe von Mönchen mitten in der Wildnis.

NPC: Crahn sei mit Dir. Was kann ich für Dich tun?

Your response: Kann ich mich an Eurem Kampf beteiligen?

Your response: Ich möchte etwas für Dich tun. Ganz speziell für DICH. Gibt es da nichts was Dir Freude machen würde?

Your response: Was macht Ihr hier? Eine Gruppe von Mönchen mitten in der Wildnis.

NPC: Mit Kampf habe ich nichts zu tun. Ich folge meinem Mentor und Vorbild Bruder Leitus wohin er seinen Schritt auch wenden mag. Wenn Du kämpfen willst solltest Du Dich an unseren Bruder Zargerus wenden. Er ist ein starker Krieger. Lass Dich von seiner harten Schale nicht abschrecken. In seinem Innersten ist er ein Herzensguter, der dem Ziel der Erfüllung und des Guten nachstrebet.

Your response: Hmm... Also für Dich kann ich nichts tun?

NPC: Da gibt es schon dieses oder jenes. Mein innigster Wunsch ist es, dem großen Bruder Leitus Freude zu machen. Wenn Du für mich in die Stadt gehen könntest und von %NPC_NAME(0) das Päckchen mit köstlichen Spezialitäten abholen und mir überbrigen würdest, wäre ich der glücklichste Mensch auf der Erde. Ich könnte Bruder Leitus dann endlich wieder ein Festmal bereiten welches seiner Größe würdig ist.

Your response: Wenns weiter nichts ist. Ich hol Dir Dein Päckchen. Ich hoffe ich bekomme unterwegs keinen Hunger...

NPC: Fevle nicht mein Br....

Your response: Keine Sorge, keine Sorge. War ja nur ein Witz. Aber wo finde ich %NPC_NAME(0)?

Your response: Eh Alterchen. Glaubst Du wirklich das ich für ein Packet Fressalien ganz in die Stadt laufe?

NPC: Er bevorugt es sich in %NPC_WORLD(0) aufzuhalten. Er ist ein Mundschenk... Barkeeper sagt man wohl..., jedoch auch Liebhaber guter Küche und Freund von Leitus und seinen Brüdern. Gehe hin und kehre zurück schnell wie auf des Windes Flüglen.

NPC: Ich verstehe. Es ist ein weiter Weg. Eines Tages wird ein Runner kommen der mir die ersehnten Köstlichkeiten bringt. Lebe wohl.

NPC: Wir haben eine heilige Mission. Wir überwarfen uns mit den anderen Brüdern unseres Ordens... Jedoch, wenn Du mehr zu erfahren trachtest, sprich mit Bruder Leitus, dem Kopf und dem Herz unserer Mission. Er ist wahrhaft groß.

Your response: Ich sehe schon, Du bist Deinem Bruder Leitus sehr ergeben. Aber gibt es nichts was ich für DICH tun kann?

NPC: So geh den hin, Edelmütiger. Gehe hin und trachte nach dem Guten. Ich hoffe Du wirst uns in der Zukunft wieder mit Deinem Besuch beglücken.

NPC: Hey kennst Du den schon: Kommt ein Pferd in die Bar. Sagt der Barkeeper: Hey warum so ein langes Gesicht. Hahaha..ha.. Na was willst Du trinken?

Your response: Gib mir einen Wiskey. Ich habe einen langen Weg hinter mir, ich verdurste. Aber keinen sytetischen!

Your response: Sorry aber kein Bedarf. Ich bin schließlich im Namen des Herrn unterwegs. Kennst Du Bruder Aurelius?

NPC: Bei uns gibts nur Reallife Whiskey. Hier eine Flasche von dem Besten!

Your response: Danke. Aurelius wird schon nichts dagegen haben wenn ich mir einen kleinen genemige.

NPC: Wo ist die Kohle. Der Whiskey kostet 99 NC

Your response: Hmm... Mist! Ich hab kein Geld dabei. Aurelius hätte mir mal nen Vorschuß geben sollen.

NPC: AURELIUS? Bruder Aurelius? Der alt Halunke. Was macht er so? Er hat sich damals einfach aus dem Staub gemacht.

Your response: Er lebt zusammen mit ein par anderen Mönchen in den Wastelands und kämpft für einen gute Sache. Das heißt, eigentlich kämpfen die Andern. Ich glaube er kocht lieber. Ich soll hier ein Päckchen mit Spezialitäten abholen. Weißt Du davon?

NPC: Kochen. Das kann ich mir vorstellen. Wir sind damals, bevor er dem Crahnorden beigetreten ist, hier in Neocron auf die Kochschule gegangen. Ich kann ihm shon was zusammenstellen. Gehe ich recht in der Annahme das er kein Geld mitgegeben hat? Er ist notorisch pleite.

Your response: Richtig. Ich hoffe das ist kein Problem. Ich möchte nicht unverichteter Dinge wieder umkehren.

NPC: Nein, nein. Er soll bekommen was er sich wünscht. Warte..... Hier nimm. Und grüße die alte Schwallnase schön von mir. Ich habe noch nie jemanden erlebt der so geschwollen reden kann.... Hahaha...

NPC: Beeile Dich. Aurelius wartet doch. Die Sachen verderben sonst.

NPC: Eile mein Freund! Ich benötige besagte Spezereien. %NPC_NAME(0) ist mein Freund. Er wird sie Dir aushändigen.

NPC: Du bist ein warer Freund. Jetzt kann ich Bruder Leitus endlich ein gebürendes Mahl bereiten und er muß nicht mehr diese... ...essen. Ich möchte mich Dir erkenntlich zeigen.

Your response: Kein Problem. Rück einfach ein par adäquate Piepen rüber.

NPC: Ich hatte keinen schnöden Mammon im Sinn. Ich möchte Dir etwas geben. Etwas persönliches. Etwas, das Dich meiner Freundschaft versichert. Nimm diesen Ring und bewahre ihn gut. In manchen Fällen bin ich in der Lage, mich besonders guten Freunden gegenüber erkenntlich zu zeigen.

Your response: Einen Ring? Na ja. Her damit. Ich werd ihn schon nicht versetzten.

NPC: So ziehe denn hin und beehre mich wieder wenn Du in diese Gegend kommst.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Welch ein wunderschöner Tag an dem ich Dich, meinen Freund, in meine Arme schließen kann. Ich möchte das Du statt der Ringe dieses Geschenk nimmst. Es ist etwas ganz besonderes. Hüte es gut und bewahre unsere Freundschaft immer in Deinem Herzen.

Your response: Danke Mann. Das ist ja cool. Mach Dir keine Sorgen. Ich werde Dich nicht vergessen und weiter für Eure Sache kämpfen.

NPC: Crahn sei mit, O Freund des Zargerus. Kämpfer für das Gute. Was kann ich für Dich tun

Your response: Ich möchte Euch helfen. Mitkämpfen!

Your response: Gibt es nichts was ich für Dich tun kann?

Your response: Was macht Ihr hier? Eine Gruppe von Mönchen mitten in der Wildnis.

NPC: Crahn sei mit Dir. Was kann ich für Dich tun?

Your response: Kann ich mich an Eurem Kampf beteiligen?

Your response: Ich möchte etwas für Dich tun. Ganz speziell für DICH. Gibt es da nichts was Dir Freude machen würde?

Your response: Was macht Ihr hier? Eine Gruppe von Mönchen mitten in der Wildnis.

NPC: Mit Kampf habe ich nichts zu tun. Ich folge meinem Mentor und Vorbild Bruder Leitus wohin er seinen Schritt auch wenden mag. Wenn Du kämpfen willst solltest Du Dich an unseren Bruder Zargerus wenden. Er ist ein starker Krieger. Lass Dich von seiner harten Schale nicht abschrecken. In seinem Innersten ist er ein Herzensguter, der dem Ziel der Erfüllung und des Guten nachstrebet.

Your response: Hmm... Also für Dich kann ich nichts tun?

NPC: Da gibt es schon etwas. Obwohl wir eigentlich alle Brücken zu der Brotherhood of Crahn abgebrochen haben, habe ich dennoch noch einige treue Freunde in der Abtei. %NPC_NAME(0) lebt dort und ich halte noch etwas sehr persönliches von ihm, das er unbedingt wiederbekommen muß, in meinen Händen. Möglicherweise ist er in dem Glauben, ich sein ein Verräter und beschmutze meine Hände durch das entwenden mir nicht eigener Dinge. Der Grund ist jedoch ein fehlender, meines Vertrauens würdiger der den Gegenstand überbringen könnte. Würdest Du diese Aufgabe übernehmen?

Your response: Ich bin zwar eigentlich kein Bote aber da es Dir so am Herzen liegt... Ich werde es tun. Kannst Du mir genauer sagen wo ich ihn finde?

Your response: Tut mir leid aber ich bin kein Bote.

NPC: Er bevorugt es sich in %NPC_WORLD(0) aufzuhalten. Gehe hin und wasche mich und mein Gewissen rein.

NPC: Ich verstehe. Es ist ein weiter Weg. Eines Tages wird ein Runner kommen... Lebe wohl.

NPC: Wir haben eine heilige Mission. Wir überwarfen uns mit den anderen Brüdern unseres Ordens... Jedoch, wenn Du mehr zu erfahren trachtest, sprich mit Bruder Leitus, dem Kopf und dem Herz unserer Mission. Er ist wahrhaft groß.

Your response: Ich sehe schon, Du bist Deinem Bruder Leitus sehr ergeben. Aber gibt es nichts was ich für DICH tun kann?

NPC: So geh den hin, Edelmütiger. Gehe hin und trachte nach dem Guten. Ich hoffe Du wirst uns in der Zukunft wieder mit Deinem Besuch beglücken.

NPC: Bruder. Was führt Dich zu mir?

Your response: Du erinnerst Dich an Aurelius?

NPC: Aurelius? Sprich diesen Namen nie wieder aus. Er hat mich hintergangen. Er hat mich beraubt. Er hat mir sehr Persönliches... gestohlen!

Your response: Er bedauert die ganze Geschichte schrecklich. Er ist mit einer Gruppe gleichgesinnter auf einer Mission in den Wastelands draußen. Er meint es gut. Er gab mir das hier für Dich.

NPC: Was ist das? Nach all der Zeit? Ich kann es nicht glauben... Sollte ich mich in ihm getäuscht haben? Warum erst jetzt....?

Your response: Er hat niemanden gefunden dem er das Päckchen anvertrauen wollte. Ich hab übrigens keine Ahnung was drin ist.

NPC: Verlasse mich und treibe keinen Schindluder mit meinen Gefühlen

NPC: Es handelt sich um mein Tagebuch in dem ich damals die Geschichte der Beziehung zu Aurelius verarbeitet und aufgeschreiben habe. Ich danke Dir von Herzen Runner. Bitte richte Aurelius meine Grüße aus und... Crahn ist groß!

Your response: Schon gut. Ich sags ihm wenn ich ihn sehe

NPC: Dank, Dank Dir, Runner. Sag ihm, ich vergebe ihm.

NPC: Berichte Aurelius von meiner Freude.

NPC: Überbringe das Paket. Eile mein Freund!

NPC: Erzähle. Was waren seine Reaktionen? Hat er mich vergessen?

Your response: Na zuerst war er richtig sauer. Er wollte nicht mal Deinen Namen hören. Es war wie Du gesagt hast. Er hat sich hintergangen gefühlt.

NPC: Ist das das Ende? Das rührt mein Herz zu Tränen...

Your response: Moment! Als ich ihm das Tagebuch gegeben habe war er wie ausgewechselt. Er hat sich gefreut und vergibt Dir.

NPC: WIRKLICH?! Oh danke, danke. Diese Kunde läßt mein Herz jubeln. Ich werde in Zukunft mit leichteem Schritt auf meinen Weg fortschreiten. Zum Dank diesen Ring als Zeichen meiner Freundschaft. Bewahre ihn und ich werde mich irgendwann erkenntlich zeigen.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Hullo there, you look like one of those Runners to me.

NPC: Whut? Speak up, I am not the youngest any more.

Your response: Sorry to disappoint you, I was just leaving.

Your response: Quite curious to see somebody like you out here.

NPC: Show me these! Have you gotten all those rings from me? All three of them? I would surely have remembered that.

Your response: Indeed I did. What is your point?

NPC: Good, good, then you will not be able to disrupt my work. Go now.

NPC: Well, what are you waiting for, go, go, go!

NPC: Why that? I am just an old professor who likes to make some scientific radiation readings out here in the desert.

NPC: I am just making a few experiments out here to support my theories.

Your response: Very nice but I am not interested in that kind of scientific stuff.

Your response: What do you need these experiments here for?. Is it something interesting?

NPC: Since you have done a lot for me in the past, I am prepared to make a special gift to you. Its a little something I prepared as a side effect for my experiments.

Your response: Yes of course, I am always open for gifts.

Your response: A gift? For me? What is it?

NPC: I can offer you the choice between two teenie little items, the fabulous armor of p-speed or the Weapon of Noob?

Your response: Give me the p-speed armor! Yes, I want the armor.

Your response: I'd like the weapon, the weapon!

NPC: Here you are my friend, but I cannot give you any more... . Goodbye!

Your response: No need for more, thank you.

NPC: Here you are, take this weapon and be happy.

Your response: Thank you very much, indeed.

NPC: It really is quite complicated to be honest. It is all about certain particles that exist in the air and that can be ionized. Can you follow me?

Your response: Errm, not really, no. Can't you just give me a job or something?

Your response: Of course. It is all described in great detail in the CERES documents isn't it?

NPC: You surprise me. The CERES documents indeed have information on this topic but only somewhat limited applications and no descriptions of machinery that uses this effect.

Your response: ...

NPC: In addition I suspect that those particles exist not only in the atmosphere but also in space. This would mean a revolution for space travel.

Your response: Errm ... it is already very late, I have to go now. Goodbye.

Your response: Please continue.

NPC: I am not completely sure yet, but I believe that I can develop some kind of engine from that knowledge. Ultimately I can only win.

Your response: Interesting. Are you finished now?

NPC: Yes, I have an old friend with the name of %NPC_NAME(1), he is residing in the %NPC_WORLD(1) district and is specialising in rare mechanical spare parts. Would you please go to him and bring back a package he should already have prepared for me?

Your response: It shall be done presently.

Your response: No, not another delivery job. I'm gone. Goodbye.

NPC: Excellent, I am expecting you in a short time, yes?

NPC: You have my package, no? You don't have my package, yes? Please get it for me.

NPC: You get me my package and I give you a token of friendship, yes?.

NPC: Finally, I can repair my mechanical mechanisms and continue with my research. As promised, here is a token of my friendship. Keep it safe, for I can be rather generous to friends.

Your response: Is that all? Just a token of friendship? No money?

Your response: All right. Thank you anyway... . Goodbye.

NPC: Fine. Here. But don't drink all that money away.

Your response: Goodbye.

NPC: Wohoo, I don't think I want business with you.

NPC: Who do we have here? A runner? And what can I do for you?

NPC: What may you want from me, ey?

Your response: I came to pick up a delivery. Something the professor wants.

Your response: I... oh yes, I would like you to give me that package for the professor,

NPC: Hah, but how then do I know, that you are really here because the professor sent you?

Your response: Because otherwise I would not know about the package, right?

Your response: Because ... because I ... well, he did send me!

NPC: You seem to be a clever one. Now, tell me what kind of research does the professor do?

Your response: It is rather complex and I do not have the nerve to tell all that complicated stuff to somebody who can't tell his right from his left hand.

Your response: He does some experiments on ionized particles, I believe.

NPC: Hrrmph, I suppose I can give the package to you. here you go. Better hurry.

Your response: Quite curious to see somebody like you out here.

NPC: Show me these! Have you gotten all those rings from me? All three of them? I would surely have remembered that.

Your response: Indeed I did. What is your point?

NPC: Good, good, then you will not be able to disrupt my work. Go now.

NPC: Well, what are you waiting for, go, go, go!

NPC: Why that? I am just an old professor who likes to make some scientific radiation readings out here in the desert.

NPC: I am just making a few experiments out here to support my theories.

Your response: Very nice but I am not interested in that kind of scientific stuff.

Your response: What do you need these experiments here for?. Is it something interesting?

NPC: Since you have done a lot for me in the past, I am prepared to make a special gift to you. Its a little something I prepared as a side effect for my experiments.

Your response: Yes of course, I am always open for gifts.

Your response: A gift? For me? What is it?

NPC: I can offer you the choice between two teenie little items, the fabulous armor of p-speed or the Weapon of Noob?

Your response: Give me the p-speed armor! Yes, I want the armor.

Your response: I'd like the weapon, the weapon!

NPC: Here you are my friend, but I cannot give you any more... . Goodbye!

Your response: No need for more, thank you.

NPC: Here you are, take this weapon and be happy.

Your response: Thank you very much, indeed.

NPC: It really is quite complicated to be honest. It is all about certain particles that exist in the air and that can be ionized. Can you follow me?

Your response: Errm, not really, no. Can't you just give me a job or something?

Your response: Of course. It is all described in great detail in the CERES documents isn't it?

NPC: You surprise me. The CERES documents indeed have information on this topic but only somewhat limited applications and no descriptions of machinery that uses this effect.

Your response: ...

NPC: In addition I suspect that those particles exist not only in the atmosphere but also in space. This would mean a revolution for space travel.

Your response: Errm ... it is already very late, I have to go now. Goodbye.

Your response: Please continue.

NPC: I am not completely sure yet, but I believe that I can develop some kind of engine from that knowledge. Ultimately I can only win.

Your response: Interesting. Are you finished now?

NPC: Yes, I have an old friend with the name of %NPC_NAME(1), he is residing in the %NPC_WORLD(1) district and is specialising in rare mechanical spare parts. Would you please go to him and bring back a package he should already have prepared for me?

Your response: It shall be done presently.

Your response: No, not another delivery job. Goodbye.

NPC: Excellent, I am expecting you in a short time, yes?

NPC: You have my package, no? You don't have my package, yes? Please get it for me.

NPC: You get me my package and I give you a token of friendship, yes?.

NPC: Finally, I can repair my mechanical mechanisms and continue with my research. As promised, here is a token of my friendship. Keep it safe, for I can be rather generous to friends.

Your response: Is that all? Just a token of friendship? No money?

Your response: All right. Thank you anyway... . Goodbye.

NPC: Fine. Here. But don't drink all that money away.

Your response: Goodbye.

NPC: Wohoo, I don't think I want business with you.

NPC: Who do we have here? A runner? And what can I do for you?

NPC: What may you want from me, ey?

Your response: I came to pick up a delivery. Something the professor wants.

Your response: I... oh yes, I would like to give me that package for the professor,

NPC: I fear I cannot give it to you, Runner. I do not have it.

Your response: How can that be? Is there maybe another possibility where I can get those parts?

Your response: Oh, yeah? Thanks for nothing.

NPC: I am really sorry, but the delivery came late. Goodbye.

NPC: Yes, but its a slim one. I once had a co owner of my supply company. %NPC_NAME(2). He might still be in the business, though. Look in the %NPC_WORLD(2) district.

Your response: Thank you. I will try.

NPC: Hello and where do I know you from?

NPC: Less gawking more shopping, I say, can I interest you in anything?

Your response: I am interested in some rare spare mechanical spare parts.

NPC: You have come to the right person then. I sell all of that and more... But that what you request is very rare indeed. It might be very expensive.

Your response: Expensive? How expensive? I was just expected to get something for the professor.

NPC: I don't even know your professor. Tell you what, I'll make a special price only for you. 500 credits! Sounds good, ey?

Your response: 500 credits?! I wanted to buy some spare parts not your entire job.

Your response: Holy camoly! That is outrageous but it seems that you have the upper hand here. I will buy it.

NPC: You are a wise man, my friend. May you enjoy your spare parts.

NPC: I see reason behind your words and if you are to poor to afford such affordable generously priced spare parts. I will offer them to you for only 480 credits.

Your response: NO! No way! 150 I say.

NPC: You want to ruin me, 450!

Your response: NO! Not more than 170.

NPC: You are no better than a thief, 400 credits!

Your response: Its not worth that much and you know it! 200 credits!

NPC: You want to ruin me, 350, that is my last word.

Your response: Bah, I am sure I would find somebody who sells it for a lower price, 220.

Your response: Alright, Alright, here you have your 350 credits. Now give me the package.

NPC: You are a tough negotiator. Goodbye.

NPC: 320 and that is my last word.

Your response: 225!

NPC: 300 is my last word.

Your response: 230 and thats it!

NPC: 280!

Your response: 230!

NPC: 260!!!

Your response: 230!

NPC: 240!

Your response: 240, alright, your hand on it!

Your response: 230 and that is really my last word on this.

NPC: You are as tough as a bone my friend. Come by and we will haggle again sometime!

NPC: I cannot help you then, that is not enough for me. Visit again, sometime.

NPC: I have no more business with you for now.

Your response: Is that all? Just a token of friendship? No money?

Your response: Goodbye.

NPC: What? What do you say, the delivery boy is coming to pick up the delivery.

Your response: You guessed it.

Your response: Yep, thats me.

NPC: Right! Here take the package. On your way back, could you please tell a friend of mine that I want to speak to him in private, soon? %NPC_NAME(2) is his name and you can find him in the %NPC_WORLD(2) district.

Your response: Of course, if I have to.

NPC: Hey, Runner, do I know you? No?

Your response: A friend of yours. %NPC_NAME(1). He wanted me to tell you that he wants to see you in private.

NPC: Oh, shit! I'm in deep trouble here. Say! That is a very nice package! I smell sweet food in there. Man, I am ever so hungry.

Your response: That is your problem pal.

NPC: Wait! Ahh... no... its all right. Just go on. Its nothing.

NPC: What do you still want from me?

Your response: Did you steal my package? You son of a ...

NPC: All right, all right! Please don't hurt me. I was so hungry. Here take it, take it and go ...

NPC: I am sorry, but I have given you your package already.

entries.details:

Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

• Backpack

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• If you don't want to work, you'll soon find yourself in Pepper Park, roaming through the alleys and dreaming of beautiful colors. You'll see!

entries.conversation:
NPC: Hi friend! I have a little job for a tough guy. Are you interested?

NPC: Hey! Want a quick job?

NPC: Hi! In search for work?

NPC: You there! What about a quick and easy job?

Your response: Yes!

Your response: What the hell, sure!

Your response: Hmm... why not?

Your response: Well, what is it about?

Your response: No thanks.

Your response: Not now.

Your response: Naah... not right now.

NPC: Ok, let me fill you in. Take this packet and deliver it to %NPC_NAME(0) of the %FRACTION_NAME(%NPC_TYPE(0)) faction in %NPC_WORLD(0). Come back to me afterwards to claim your reward. Will you accept?

Your response: It's as good as done.

Your response: Ok. I'm up to it.

Your response: No... rather not.

Your response: Pah! Do I look like a delivery boy to you?

NPC: Ok, here is the packet I told you about. Take good care of it!

NPC: Take this then and be careful!

NPC: Sorry, but I can't talk right now. I'm really very, very busy.

NPC: Go away. I'm waiting for an urgent delivery.

NPC: Please leave me alone. Try talking to one of our service employees.

NPC: I'm not a member of the serviceteam. For questions about our faction or similar subjects, please refer to those who are.

Your response: But I have a packet for you from %NPC_NAME(4).

Your response: If you don't want the packet I was told to bring you, I'll sell it to someone else.

Your response: I just wanted to deliver something, but hey, if you are this busy... forget it.

NPC: Ah, the delivery! Finally. Thank you very much. Go back to %NPC_NAME(4) to receive your reward.

NPC: At last. Why did this take you so long? Hmpf. In my opinion you don't deserve it at all, but don't forget to return to %NPC_NAME(4) to claim your money.

NPC: So you do? Where is it then?

NPC: Says you. I can't see it.

NPC: How could you give something to me if you don't have it with you?

NPC: No you don't! Liar.

NPC: Hurry up, deliver the packet ASAP!

NPC: Thank you for doing this job so well. Here is your reward. Our faction always has a place for smart people like you.

NPC: Here, take your money. You deserve it. Come back anytime, there is always work around here for someone like you.

NPC: Suit yourself, somebody else will surely do it.

NPC: Come back if you change your mind.

NPC: If you don't want to work, you'll soon find yourself in Pepper Park, roaming through the alleys and dreaming of beautiful colors. You'll see!

NPC: I'll find someone else then.

NPC: You are a con man! %NPC_NAME(4) would never give such an important thing to someone like you.

NPC: Pah, I don't belive anything you tell me. You'd better leave now before I alert security.

NPC: Hey Alter. Das ist ein etwas heikeler Auftrag der sich auch etwas außerhalb der gestzlichen Vorgaben abspielt. Wir vergeben ihn auch nur an loyale Freunde von %FRACTION_NAME( %NPC_TYPE(4)).

Your response: Kein Problem. Ich bin Ihr Mann.

Your response: Sorry aber ich halte mich immer an die Gesetzte.

NPC: OK Mann. Es geht um folgendes: %FRACTION_NAME( %NPC_TYPE(1)) hat uns ein Päckchen mit einer wichtigen Erfindung entwendet. Sie würden das natürlich abstreiten und behaupten es wäre Ihre.

Your response: Klar. Aber....

NPC: Ich war noch nicht fertig. Es ist äußerst wichtig dieses Päckchen zurück zu holen. Allerdings gibt es keine gesicherten Informationen wer es zur Zeit in seinem Besitz hat. Es kann sein, das %NPC_NAME(0) etwas weiß. Er sollte sich in %NPC_WORLD(1) aufhalten. Komme nicht ohne das Packet wieder. Wenn Du es schaffst bekommst Du reichlichen Lohn.

Your response: OK. Ich bin schon unterwegs.

Your response: Ich bin doch nicht verrückt und klaue für Euch. Darauf steht in Neocron schließlich die Todesstrafe.

NPC: Beeil Dich. Es ist wichtig!

NPC: Schade dann werden wir jemand anderen suchen müssen.

NPC: Was gibt's?

Your response: Ich bin auf der Suche nach einem ominösen Päckchen das %FRACTION_NAME( %NPC_TYPE(4)) gestohlen worden ist.

NPC: Gestohlen? Das ich nicht lache! Aber wenn Du den Typen glauben willst... Die Info kostet Dich 150.

Your response: OK. Hier. Schieß los.

Your response: Nöpe. Vergisses.

NPC: OK. Soweit ich weiß, und ich weiß alles, ist das Päckchen, wem es auch gehören mag in Händen von %NPC_NAME(1)

Your response: Und wo kann ich den finden?

NPC: Sorry aber damit kannst Du Dir die Info nicht leisten.

NPC: Dafür hast Du nicht bezahlt... Na ich will mal nicht so sein. Gehe mal in %NPC_NAME(1). Da solltest Du ihn finden können. Und jetzt mach das Du wegkommst und überstrapaziere nicht meine Geduld!

NPC: Ist auch besser und für Dich sicherer wenn Du Dich da raushälst.

NPC: Zisch ab. Mehr infos wirst Du von mir nicht bekommen. Ich will mir auch nicht die Finger verbrennen!

NPC: Was wollen Sie?

Your response: ...*ich muss ihn irgendwie ablenken*...Guten Tag. Wie gehts denn so?..

NPC: Was soll die Frage. Ich mache hier meinen Job als Sicherheitschef. Gehen Sie jetzt bitte weiter.

Your response: Ich habe gehört das es hier größere Sicherheitsmängel gibt. Das ist wohl kein Wunder bei einem solchen Chef. Ich bin ein Gutachter zur Erstellung und Beurteilung von Wachsystemen und werde mich mal gut umschauen.

NPC: WAS? E..entschuldigen Sie. Das war nicht so gemeint... K..kann ich irgendwie be...behilflich sein..?

Your response: ...*Jetzt oder nie! Die Gelegenheit ist günstig*.. Was ist denn zum Beispiel mit den Selbstschussanlagen? Werden die regelmäßig gewartet? Und die Viedoüberwachung - dort drüben?

Your response: ...*die Sache ist mir zu heiß..scheiße ich hau ab*.. Ich werde mich erst mal mit Ihrem Vorgesetzten unterhalten!

NPC: Wo? Wir haben gar keine...

Your response: ...*oh oh - hat er was gemerkt?* Ja - BITTE!?

NPC: Du hast es hier mit dem Sicherheitschef zu tun! Ich laß mich doch nicht einfach beklauen!!

NPC: ...Selbstschußanlagen.

Your response: ...*piuhh* Ein Grund mehr den Leiter hier zu sprechen! Unglaublich!

NPC: Bitte. Ich brauche meinen Job. Ich habe Kinder....

NPC: Bitte... Sie haben doch nicht..? Sie werden doch nicht...?

NPC: Ah, wunderbar! Finally. Du hast Dir Deine Belohnung verdient und uns einen großen  Dienst erwiesen.

NPC: Ich sagte doch: Komm wieder wenn der Auftrag erledigt ist!

NPC: Hi friend! I've got a job for a tough guy. Interested?

NPC: Hello! This is an important and perhaps a little dangerous job. Are you ready to face it?

NPC: Hey. Are you able to handle secret mission?

Your response: Of course!

Your response: Sure! This is my opportunity to prove my loyalty to the faction!

Your response: I'm your man. Shoot.

Your response: I don't want to be involved into such business.

Your response: Sorry but I'm not ready for that yet.

Your response: Sorry. Not right now.

NPC: Ok. But you really have to handle this top secret. The life of %NPC_NAME(0) depends on it.

Your response: Why does his life depends on that?

Your response: His life? Who is he?

NPC: %NPC_NAME(0) is a loyal member of our faction. He has infiltrated the %FRACTION_NAME(%NPC_TYPE(0)) to investigate their inner structures.

Your response: I see. But what do you need me for?

Your response: That explains a lot. But what's my part in this game?

Your response: Stop! Before you tell me more... I don't want to hear it. I'm not ready for this.

Your response: I don't believe anything of what you're telling me. I'm out of here.

NPC: We need you to bring this special decoding machine to him so he can investigate the most important structures of their network. Do you think you can handle that?

Your response: Yes. I think so.

Your response: OK. I'll do it.

Your response: Sorry but this one is yet to difficult for me.

Your response: Ask someone else. I can't do that.

NPC: Ok here is the decoder. Take care.

NPC: So take the decoder and be careful! Remember, don't talk to anyone about it.

Your response: Ok. But where can I find him?

Your response: Ok. But isn't there anything else I should know?

NPC: That's true. I almost forgot. You can find him in %NPC_WORLD(0)... and... come back to me, when you're done, to get your reward. We'll pay you %REWARD_MONEY() NC.

Your response: OK. Keep your money ready. I'll be right back.

Your response: I don't do this for money but only to prove %FRACTION_NAME(%NPC_TYPE(4)) my loyalty.

NPC: Yeah, yeah... Hurry up now, please!

NPC: I don't talk to %FRACTION_NAME(%NPC_TYPE(4)) pigs. Move on or I'll call the security!

NPC: Go away. We don't like your sort here. You shouldn't be here.

Your response: %NPC_NAME(4) gave me this to bring it to you...I think you might want to have it...

Your response: If you don't want it I'll sell it to someone else.

Your response: I just wanted to deliver something but if you are that uncooperative... forget it.

NPC: Quiet!...*whisper*... I see. What do you know about me?...

NPC: Man!...*whisper*... Nobody should hear this or...*whisper*...Thanks. Do you know much about my...mission?...

Your response: ...*whisper*...Not much...and to be honest...I don't want to...

Your response: ...*whisper*..I just do this for %FRACTION_NAME(%NPC_TYPE(4)). So spare me from details...

NPC: ...*whisper*...Finally! Thank you. It's better if you do not know too much... Go back to receive your reward.

NPC: ...*whisper*...Thanks... Leave now. They are lookin' already...

NPC: ...*whisper*...Where is it?...

NPC: ...*whisper*...Don't fool around with me. It's really important...

NPC: Come on! You know how important this mission is! Don't return without having the machine delivered.

NPC: Thanks for doing the job so well. This is a nice strategic advantage for us. Here is your money.

NPC: With your excellent work we have gained a strong position against %FRACTION_NAME(%NPC_TYPE(0)) now. Take your money. You deserve it.

NPC: I'm sorry about that. We'll find somebody else.

NPC: Come back if you change your mind.

NPC: If you know somebody who can help us out, send them to me!

NPC: ...*whisper*...You are a con man! %NPC_NAME(4) would never give such an important job to someone like you...

Your response: Nothing...

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

ITEMS THE NPC MAY ASK FOR
• Delivery Bag

ITEMS THE NPC MAY GIVE
• Delivery Bag
• Renegade Armor Parts

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: What are you doing here? Don't you know how dangerous it is here?

NPC: For your own health, get the hell outta here! It's hitting the fan!

NPC: Dude, no offense, but you should get out! It's dangerous as hell here!

Your response: Calm down. I'm being sent.

Your response: What? Why? What is this here?

Your response: Already gone!

NPC: What?

Your response: Yes, I was sent here by a Psi Monk. I have to get some Renegade Armour Parts for him! He gave me these Papers here...

NPC: *shrug* Here, I have some! C'mon, take 'em. And now do me a favour and leave! I don't want any trouble!

NPC: *shrug* Here, I have some! C'mon, take 'em. And now do me a favour and leave! I don't want any trouble!

NPC: *shrug* Here, I have some! C'mon, take 'em. And now do me a favour and leave! I don't want any trouble!

NPC: *shrug* Here, I have some! C'mon, take 'em. And now do me a favour and leave! I don't want any trouble!

NPC: Haha, you old kidder! For a second, I almoste believed you. Almost! Oh well, no harm done. But now vamoose.

NPC: This is the Gaya Mine! The Psi Monks let people dig for some ore here, back when they ruled Neocron. This Ore had some really bad side effects though!

Your response: Do tell. What kind of sideeffects?

NPC: Well, any Machine that was brought down here went completely nuts. The gathering robots became terrible monsters. And it all started from one second to the other, everyone was gathering ore, when all of a sudden all electronics go completely crazy.

Your response: Oh. Not good.

NPC: You can say that again. And good ol' Reza couldn't just believe the tales, of course. No, he had to be sure. He had to send some Copbots down here to check things out. As those stopped reporting and didn't come back, he sent STORM Bots. Never heard from them again, either. About the same with the human soldiers he sent down here then, which could only report being killed by Rezas bots before the com went down.

Your response: Ah yes, most interesting... hmm, the Psi Monks, you say? Interesting, because I am sent by one!

NPC: Good.

NPC: Ok.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Hello!

NPC: Hi!

NPC: Hi there!

NPC: What can I do for ya?

Your response: I got  a few questions.

NPC: Heh, no kidding. How can I help?

Your response: You do have a database with the archives of our knowledge, right?

NPC: Of course, all the knowledge from the Ceres Disks, plus all that had to be added since.

Your response: Great! May I use it?

NPC: No, sorry, access is restricted to NCPD employees.

Your response: Allright, I ask, you enter?

NPC: I don't think you understood me! Access is not allowed to civillians!

Your response: Hmm I understand... Isn't it boring to stand around here all day?

NPC: What are you driving at?

Your response: Well... are you being paid enough?

NPC: Are you trying to bribe me?

Your response: Bribe is such an ugly word... Let's put it this way: You do me a favour, I do you a favour!

NPC: You DO know where you are right here, right?

Your response: Yes, I do. Are you interested or not?

NPC: Thousand.

Your response: WHOA! Don't you think that's a little...

NPC: Maybe I should just call the Copbots instead?

Your response: Damn you!... Allright, allright. You can have the money.

NPC: Thanks. A pleasure doing business with you.

Your response: Are you gonna help me now?

NPC: Good. Then go and get it, I'll wait here.

NPC: Sure! What do you want to know?

Your response: Please do a Word-search for 'Job' and restrict the results to mythology meanings.

NPC: Okay, hold on for a bit... Ah, here it comes...

Your response: And? What does it say?

NPC: This: 'Job, also Hiob, lat. Iob, central persona of the Book of Job in the old Testament of the Bible of Christianity, a training poem; it is about the maintaining of uprightness in times of trial; important part of the old world literature. Job's news, Bad news'. Doesn't say any more.

Your response: Hmm... Job's news... Bad news... The pieces are starting to fit.

NPC: Something else?

Your response: Yes. What's this 'lat. Iob' supposed to mean?

NPC: Well, it's like this: Back when this Bible-Book has been written, people spoke a different language than back when the Ceres Discs were made, that was also different from our language today. The most common language back then in which the Book was written, too,  was called 'Latin'. In this language, the name of this guy was 'Iob'.

Your response: I understand. Hmm. Could you do a search for 'latin words' in general?

NPC: One second... Hmm it just says: 'Words of the latin language, noteable are its notations that are different from todays language, like the usage of the character V instead of U, or I instead of J.'

Your response: Now this is getting interesting. What are cross totals supposed to be?

NPC: 'The sum you get by adding the positions of the different letters in the alphabet.' Hehe, this Computer always has a reply.

NPC: Why do I always get the nutcases...

entries.conversation:
NPC: No time!

NPC: I am busy!

NPC: Not now!

NPC: I have to ask you to leave, we got problems to deal with!

Your response: Problems? I am not the slightest bit surprised. A hacking attack?

NPC: How do you know?! Did you do it?!

Your response: No, it wasn't me. But this is not the first time they hacked something.

NPC: What else did they hack?

Your response: The Tangent mainframe, among other things. But I don't have time to tell stories. What happened?

NPC: We wished we would know. Somehow a back door Trojan was installed, our own hackers don't even comprehend fully. This is one mean program, each time we delete it, it appears at two other places all the more aggressive.

Your response: What does it do?

NPC: It overwrites our data! It places a single saying everywhere: 'Read the map like a book, from bottom to top, and IOB will lead you to the goal. At the end of the path the position of his words will point at the right way.'

Your response: That fits in. I can't explain everything now, but I think the hackers are giving us clues to their location all the time.

NPC: Why do you think that?

Your response: As I already said, I've picked up several of their clues already. At a different site they left an excerpt from aforesaid Iob, Hiob or also Job. Three names, the same thing. I don't know if it comforts you, but you seem to have been attacked for nothing but a symbolic reason.

NPC: Symbolic or not, I don't give a shit. I want my business to run again. I want the hackers tracked down. And above all I want to know how they did it!

Your response: Well, then help me. The sooner I track them down, the sooner it is gonna stop.

NPC: That's fine by me. How can I help?

Your response: Mental exercise. What could 'Read the map like a book, from bottom to top' mean?

NPC: Well, I suppose it means sectors. You can read them from left to right or line for line. But I guess you have to read them bottom to top. Probably meaning only accessible sectors.

Your response: Hmm... yes, that makes sense... and IOB...

NPC: I don't understand that part...

Your response: I do. The tip I got from the NCPD is useful after all. I 0 and B. 26, that's... the Foster Uplink. That matches.

NPC: Sure you don't want to tell me what this is all about?

Your response: Pretty sure, yes. But if you really want your business to run again, you better help me now.

NPC: Ok ok. What else do you want to know?

Your response: 'At the end of the path the position of his words will point at the right way.' Any idea?

NPC: Nope! What do you expect me to come up with? YOU are the one having collected clues of them already.

Your response: Well, as I said, they left an excerpt at a different site... The excerpt stems from a book, the book Job, and is from chapter 3, paragraph 19.

NPC: 3 and 19... that doesn't really help. It could mean anything, 3 steps north and 19 west maybe... or east. Could also mean sub sectors. Or maybe 319 degrees. Or 22? I haven't got a clue!

Your response: Interesting ideas. Well, I suppose I gonna get going.

NPC: Do as you please. But put an end to this spook soon.

NPC: This can't be true!

Your response: I heard about it... bad stuff! Who was it?

Your response: What?

NPC: Weren't you here already?... yes you were. And I said leave.

NPC: Don't you read the Newspapers? We have been hacked!

Your response: Hacked? By who?

NPC: No idea. We were not able to trace back the attack! They just left us some kind of saying in the Logfiles!

Your response: A saying? How does it go?

NPC: It's a strange quote: 'The small and the great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.'

Your response: Do you know what it is supposed to mean?

NPC: No, of course not! If we did, we would have a trace, right? What are we supposed to do with some kind of religious saying?

Your response: Well, maybe you should ask those that are religious?

NPC: Listen, Buddy, if you want to waste your time, then go ahead and try to find out, no skin off my nose. But PLEASE, don't get on our nerves with this!

Your response: As you like... I will follow this lead allright! It's just that...

NPC: What is it NOW?!

Your response: Maybe I could have a copy of those Logfiles? So I could show them to others...

NPC: Okay, whatever. Here you go. And now leave!

NPC: May Crahn bless you, runner!

Your response: May Crahn be with you. I need your help brother!

Your response: Hello. I got a question.

NPC: Speak my friend. I shall do everything in my power to help you.

Your response: Evil men did great mischief, I want to administer the deserved justice!

NPC: An honorable cause. How may I assist you??

Your response: Well, they left a clue; an excerpt, which seems to be of religious nature!

NPC: Let me see it friend, do you have it on you?

Your response: Sure, here you are!

NPC: Hmm... 'The small and the great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.' I think I know this excerpt, but I don't remember its origin...

Your response: So it's not an excerpt of Crahns teachings?

NPC: No, but... Oh, Crahn enlightens me!

Your response: Speak!

NPC: This excerpt is really of religious nature, but none of Crahns teachings! It's part of the old religions, which were followed before the cleansing fire

Your response: Go on...

NPC: I think the religion was called 'bible' and this excerpt is from the book 'Christianity'. Might be the other way around. But I recall that I studied that book once.

Your response: Can you recall the context of the excerpt my wise friend?

NPC: If my memory serves me right, it was a tale about a man named Job. His faith was to be tested by hardship.

Your response: A really strange clue this is!

NPC: Indeed! The sense escapes me. Maybe there are other clues?

Your response: Good idea! Say, do you know the exact position of the verse in that book?

NPC: Sorry. My recollections are too loose for such questions!

Your response: How unfortunate. Allow me to ask if there might be someone which I could contact in regard to this question??

NPC: That will not be necessary. Come back to me at a later date! I will contact the brothers of my order, they will be able to assist me!

Your response: Thank you for your generous help my friend!

NPC: To follow the path of justice is a privilege. You don't have to thank me.

NPC: A question? Go ahead!

Your response: Some hackers hacked Tangent and left a saying which somehow sounds religious to me. I wanted to ask you if you know this saying.

NPC: Well, show me the saying

Your response: There you go!

NPC: Hmm... 'The small and the great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.' I think I know this excerpt, but I fail to recollect its origin...

Your response: Then strain your brain a bit!

NPC: My friend, I am a peaceful Man, but you really start to annoy me! However I recollect where the excerpt is from.

Your response: Where from?

NPC: Well, before the cleansing fire there were several religions in the old culture. This excerpt originates in the teachings of one of the old religions.

Your response: And, what is that supposed to tell me?

NPC: The story of this excerpt is about a man named Job, which faith was to be proven by grave torment.

Your response: Man, the folks back then sure were spaced out...

NPC: Many things were rather peculiar, with that I have to agree.

Your response: Ok, but how does this help me?

NPC: That you have to know yourself, I told you everything I know.

Your response: What a bunch of fuc... sh..

NPC: Leave and spare me from your outbursts!

NPC: I was indeed. One of my brothers found the book - it is called 'bible' by the way and not Christianity, which is the name of the religion that it depicts - in our library. He looked up the chapter we needed.

Your response: This is great news!

NPC: Don't be pleased early my friend, so I don't disappoint you. We couldn't find out much.

Your response: I quite believe it, but every little counts.

NPC: That might be right. Well, the excerpt is indeed from the bible part called the book of Job. Chapter 3, paragraph 18 is the wanted excerpt.

Your response: Is there anything more?

NPC: Not much. The chapter is about a  man who faithfully served his god and because of that was a minion of luck. But his god put him to the test by taking everything that was dear to him away.

Your response: A scry story. What happened to the poor man?

NPC: He kept his faith, and his god rewarded him with more than ever.

Your response: That's interesting. But I am asking myself, what could be the meaning of the excerpt...

NPC: The excerpt itself is from a part of the story, in which Job quarreled with his fate and cursed the day he was born.

Your response: I am confused...

NPC: Neither can I understand why someone would leave an excerpt like this as a clue to a crime. But maybe there is a chance...

Your response: Tell me, my wisdom welling friend!

NPC: The town of Neocron, which was build by Crahn long ago, owns a huge knowledge data base. It resorts to the old Ceres-disks. Maybe you will find hints there

Your response: A brilliant idea! How can I possibly thank you?

NPC: At our last meeting, I already told you there is no need to thank me. To aid justice is a privilege not a service. Have long life, and may Crahn be with you!

NPC: Hello Runner, how can I help you?

Your response: I was told I could learn about the Construction Device here.

Your response: Is it true that you can teach me how to use the Research Device?

Your response: I'd like to know how to use the Recycling and Salvaging Tools.

Your response: Please explain how the Repair Tool works.

Your response: I have an Implanting Device here. I'd like to know more about it.

Your response: Sorry, but I have to go.

NPC: Are you already familiar with the basic functionality? Or do I have to explain the basics too?

Your response: That would be nice. I'm new to this business.

Your response: No, no. I'm fairly familiar with it. I'd like to know how I can get started.

NPC: Okay. From the beginning then: The Construction Device allows qualified Runners to build items, from weapons to drugs, themselves. The tools exist in different models. They differ in the maximum techlevel of items that can be built with them. You'll see that the high level tools are pretty expensive.

Your response: So you have to invest quite a lot if you want to build complex things.

NPC: But that's not all. Your 'Construction' skill must be higher than the techlevel of the item to be built. And you need additional items.

Your response: What items?

NPC: Well, of course you need a Blueprint of the item, from which the Construction Device will read the required data. Additionally, the Processor needs a certain amount of 'Construction Grease', depending on the complexity of the item you want to build. The grease must be in your inventory for the tool to use it.

Your response: Ah, 'Construction Grease' ...

NPC: Lastly, the Construction Device obviously can't build items out of thin air. You'll need all the required item parts. In your inventory, if you access the Blueprint's context menu with your right mouse button and select 'SHOW INFO', you'll see among other things a full list of the required item parts.

Your response: It seems like you need a lot of items. Where do I get all that stuff?

NPC: Well, if you want to establish yourself as a Constructor, there are different ways. You can buy everything at Cryton Tech Tools, the chain of stores that sells all these items. However, that's pretty bad for your profit margin. So it's pretty good to work together with a few other budding specialists. People who recycle junk to make base materials or people with a Research Tool to provide Blueprints and so forth. You could share the profits. It is always advisable to keep on good terms with other people.

Your response: Can't I do all that myself? I mean recycle or research?

NPC: That might work to begin with, but for more complex items, you have to specialize. The processes are too different and complex to master them all.

Your response: You could be right there. So what do you suggest now?

NPC: I'd go to %NPC_NAME(0) in %NPC_WORLD(0) first and learn about processes, prices, etc.
