entries.details:
CONTACT
Detective Noah

ITEMS THE NPC MAY GIVE
• BLUEPRINT- 30 TB Capacity:

POSSIBLE COST
• 3,000 credits (depends on choice)

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• Not the Twister in Pepper Park. I mean the good Twister. In the Wastes in Sector I09. The one where the women are so drugged, it does not matter what you do with them.

• They did not. But earlier Sterling mentioned to Cyril where he hid it. He said it was in a lock box in Sector I10 in front of some old lab he found.

• Her name is Kylan Chambers. She has a tracking bracelet on her while the case is open. It shows she is currently in the Chez Sypher in Viarosso Sector 3. Follow any leads you deem necessary. If you need assistance, ask me or Officer Jenna in the NCPD HQ. Run along then. I have more files to sort.

• Some of the contractors from the wastelands who built her apartment took and hid the armor parts.
They either built in safeguards to sneak in after she moved in, or figured out her security while installing it.
I found one of the antiques in a hiding spot out in the Wastelands.

• Nowhere in any of the civilized parts of the city. All of the Anarchy Breed and their sympathizers I hear about come from the old Jailhouse in Outzone Sector 8.

• It says to meet her in the Old Jailhouse in Outzone Sector 8, outside the bar. Do you need backup? I can send Charlie here to assist.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: I have no case for you, Detective, I'm sorry.

NPC: You should talk to Tracy Callahan first.

NPC: How? How can there be this many files? There cannot be enough memory in our computer banks to store this many files!

What? Who are you? Did you come to bring me more files? I HAVE NO MORE SPACE!

Your response: Nope. I have no files. I will just be leaving. Sorry for bothering you.

Your response: Actually, the receptionist up front told me to come see you if I was looking for some work.
She seemed to think that I could be of some help since I am part of the NCPD Special Unit.

NPC: Take care!

NPC: Hrm. If you are a part of the Special Unit, than you might just be able to help me. See, I have this problem. It is called lack of resources.

Your response: *click*

NPC: I have dozens of cold cases that have gone unsolved and no personnel to help work the cases. Ever since the battle of DoY, all the members of the unit have been reassigned to high risk areas. All that I have now is me and Charlie over there; and he is nothing but a distraction.

Your response: *click*

NPC: So, if you were maybe willing to help me with some of these cases, my file log will dwindle, and you could collect some reward money for solving them. It would be completely legit too.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Since you are not officially an employee of the NCPD you can collect reward money, but since you have an official rank you can still work the cases. It is a win-win! What do you say?

Your response: Yeaahhh. That seems a bit shady. I will just leave you to your Copbot. Take care now.

Your response: Wow! That is a loophole if I have ever seen one, but as long as I get paid, I am up for some detective work.

NPC: Wonderful! So, what to give you for a first assignment? Let me have a look...

Your response: *click*

NPC: Yes. Here is a good one. A business woman in Viarosso claims to have had some antiques stolen from her apartment. It looks like they were parts to an old suit of armor.
All available evidence pointed to her staging the theft herself, which she still denies. She was never arrested since you cannot steal something you already own.

How about you go talk with her and see if you can get a confession from her so we can get this pointless case closed.

Your response: Sounds easy enough. What is her name, and where can I find her?

NPC: Her name is Kylan Chambers. She has a tracking bracelet on her while the case is open. It shows she is currently in the Chez Sypher in Viarosso Sector 3. Follow any leads you deem necessary. If you need assistance, ask me or Officer Jenna in the NCPD HQ. Run along then. I have more files to sort.

NPC: Hey bud. What you need? You know I have it. Just say the word and it is all yours. Your own altered reality in a vial. Just 15,000nc.

Your response: Are you Dylan Gooden from Gooden Contracting?

Your response: Sorry, no drugs for me today.

NPC: Cya!

NPC: Um, why whatever do you mean? I do not know of this Dylan Gooden you speak of.

Your response: Really? Because the 'Hello, my name is Dylan Gooden. How may I serve your needs today?' on your name tag says you do know who he is.

NPC: Dammit! I forgot about the name tag. Fuck! Ok, what do you want?

Your response: So I take it you are not a high end contractor?

NPC: Yes and No. I did have my contracting license, but competition was just too high. I was not getting the good business I needed.

Your response: *click*

NPC: So, I hired a good hacker and programmer to give my online profiles a little boost. After that business went crazy. I could not keep up with the requests.

Your response: *click*

NPC: I got a few jobs done, with some hired vagrants and lowlifes, but eventually I just could not fill the orders. So I turned in my license and started working here at my favorite watering hole.

Your response: Do you remember an apartment construction job for a Viarosso business woman named Kylan Chambers?

NPC: Oh boy do I remember her! She had legs that went on for miles. I showed up to that construction site in person quite a few times... just to see the sites, if you know what I mean.

Your response: So you did not actually work the construction yourself?

NPC: Of course not. That is what I hired people for.

Your response: Do you remember who you hired for that particular job?

NPC: I could not tell you who I hired for any particular job. I went out to the Twister Bar and asked if anybody needed some extra credits. Got a few drunks to work for cheap which, in turn allowed me to maximize profits.

Your response: The Twister has been closed for a while. You would not have been able to go there to get workers.

NPC: Not the Twister in Pepper Park. I mean the good Twister. In the Wastes in Sector I09. The one where the women are so drugged, it does not matter what you do with them.

Your response: You are a sick fuck. This info had better be good. If it is not, I am coming back to bring a world of pain on you.

NPC: Hey, the info is legit. If you are looking for one of those workers, this is the best I can do for you. They are around there, or somebody who works there knows where to find them. Go see for yourself.

NPC: It's all I have to say... Talk to Esperanza at the Twister Bar.

NPC: Hey there stranger. You look like you need a stiff drink. What can I get ya?

Your response: Actually, what I could really use is some information on your patrons.

Your response: I am just here for the view.

NPC: You should talk to Dylan Gooden!

NPC: Enjoy!

NPC: Fuck You! Damn city cops coming out here to our Wastes trying to shake down simple folk. Get the hell out of here!

Your response: I am not a cop, but yes, I am from Neocron City. A man named Dylan Gooden sent me out here to get some info on some of his former employees.

NPC: Ah. Dylan, that fucking sleezebag. Yeah, if you are doing business with him, you are certainly not a cop. If he did not tip so well I would have shoved my stiletto heels in his eyes years ago.

Your response: So, do you know of anybody from around here that Dylan might have hired?

NPC: Dylan hired almost everybody around at one point or another. He paid a well enough wage, and did not do much of a background check if you know what I mean.

Your response: This particular group would have worked on building an apartment for some of the high class of Neocron City.
Maybe they mentioned finding weaknesses in security that allowed them to do a little snatch and grab job after the construction was complete.

NPC: Well, I do hear a lot of stories. And the drunker the patrons get, the more willing they are to spill any information.

Your response: Have you heard any spill some information about this specific story?

NPC: I am not sure. My mind seems a bit fuzzy. Maybe 3000nc could help clear up my memory.

Your response: You must be crazy. I am not paying you 3000nc when I do not even know if you have any information that I need.

NPC: Have you ever met a bar wench? Do you know how much we hear on a daily basis? Tongues get really loose, and we always have an open ear. Some of that information can be repeated; for those that can pay that is.

Your response: Fine, I will pay. You had better know something though, and that something had better be worth it.

Your response: Sorry, I will not pay when I do not know if you even have any information.

NPC: Than that is your loss. No information is free around here. Head back to your civilized city and enjoy the clean life again. You do not belong out here.

NPC: You are a smart one. I know of the folks you were talking about. There were three of them. Two of them were regulars. Sterling and Cyril. They came in bragging one night that they were able to get an old armor part off of an uppity sap in Neocron City.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Come back, when you have the money!

NPC: They built the apartment, and knew how to get inside without triggering any security. Those two definitely were not the brains of that heist though. The third one must have been the mastermind. She came to the bar one night and ended up killing Sterling and Cyril.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Apparently they hid the part and wanted more pay before they would tell the boss woman where it was. She did not take kindly to it. Cleaned up brain matter for a week.

Your response: Great. So two of the three are dead. Did they tell the boss where the parts were before she offed them?

NPC: They did not. But earlier Sterling mentioned to Cyril where he hid it. He said it was in a lock box in Sector I10 in front of some old lab he found.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Side note: The lady did not seem like one of us Wastelanders either. She had white teeth and brushed hair. Defiantly nobody I had seen before.

Your response: Well, that is more information I had then when I arrived here. Thanks for your help.

NPC: If you need any more information, just drop by with some nc, and I will be glad to help.

NPC: If you need any more information, just drop by with some nc, and I will be glad to help.

NPC: It is about time you came back. I was beginning to think you had given up on this little mission. Did you find some evidence that Ms. Chambers staged the robbery herself?

Your response: Not given up. Just following leads all over. I actually discovered that Ms. Chambers was, in fact, robbed. She has been truthful this whole time.

NPC: You're coming back without any evidence?

NPC: You should talk to Kylan Chambers and follow her leads.

NPC: Go ahead.

Your response: Some of the contractors from the wastelands who built her apartment took and hid the armor parts.
They either built in safeguards to sneak in after she moved in, or figured out her security while installing it.
I found one of the antiques in a hiding spot out in the Wastelands.

NPC: Well, that is something. I wonder how two thugs from the Wastes could beat our DNA scanners at the crime scene. That is not something that can just be faked. Everybody leaves DNA on everything they touch.

Your response: That is a mission for a different time. As for the mission at hand, should I be receiving my reward or something?

NPC: You should, and you will. The reward is 5000nc for one of the parts or 15000nc for the pair. Here is your reward. I will let Ms. Chambers know we have one of her antiques. Come see me again if you want to pursue this case some more.

NPC: Ah. You came back for more. I figured you would be up for completing this case. So, are you interested in finding that last part?

Your response: No. You are incorrect. Detective work is a waste of my time.

Your response: I am. I was thinking about the contractors that got killed.
Maybe they broke in with the third person who killed them.
There is the possibility some DNA was left that the original investigative crew did not find.

I was thinking about scanning around the area myself.

NPC: Sad to hear that, if you change your mind, come back to me.

NPC: Sounds like a good plan. If you want to do that, you will have to speak with Officer Jenna to check out a DNA scanner. Also, since you are not actually a detective, you will have to get permission from Ms. Chambers to gain access to her apartment.

Your response: Very well. I will do that. I will return when I get some results.

NPC: Understood.

NPC: Officer Jenna is waiting!

NPC: START: SCANNNING...

SCAN COMPLETE...

DNA result stored...

NPC: NO SCANNER DETECTED!


ABORT...

NPC: ALREADY SCANNED.

NPC: Hello. Welcome to the N.C.B.R.L. That is the current acronym we are using instead of saying Neocron Biological Research Laboratory; which I just said anyway, therefore rendering the acronym useless.

Your response: *click*

NPC: You should talk to Officer Jenna first!

NPC: This whole greeting seems to be a waste of valuable time. Perhaps we should just program a computer to speak with visitors. Yes. I shall submit the appropriate paper work to create an N.C.B.R.L.A.P. That would be the acronym for Neocron Biological Research Laboratory Assistance Program. Thank you for your assistance. You have been a great asset to the N.C.B.R.L.

Your response: Um, do I need to be here for any of this? I came as a representative of the NCPD to get this DNA Scanner processed.

NPC: Oh yes! Something other than scanning sewer rats. Those things get boring. Also, sorry about the mess in the foyer. There was... something... that went wrong. So yeah, a scanner huh? That will do just fine. We really do enjoy our contract with the NCPD.

Your response: *click*

NPC: It is also a good thing we have the gag order on anything we find with NCPD equipment. There are so many amazing stories I could tell you. Like the time we were brought a bag of goo...

Your response: Did you not just mention a gag order?
That does mean you are not allowed to talk about this, correct?

NPC: Absolutely! I am glad you are here to remind me. So what is it I can do for you today?

Your response: The DNA Scanner?

NPC: Fantastic! Hand it here. Uh huh. Hrm. It is a good device. Five samples. That should take me about 15 minutes or so. Come back in a bit and I should have the results ready.

Your response: Very well.

NPC: Don't tell me you've lost the Scanner?

NPC: Alright, talk to you in about 15 minutes.

NPC: Tremendous! You are just in time. The final result is in. Here are the results. It seems like all of the DNA strands found are in the central NC database. Kylan Chambers, Sterling Figgis, Dylan Gooden, Cyril Archer, and Colton Oppelt. Do not know any of them myself. But, unless they were cellar snakes, chances are I would not know them anyway.

Your response: That is wonderful information. Thank you for your help.
Just send the bill to Officer Jenna at the NCPD and you will be taken care of.

NPC: You are back already? Patience for fucks sake! You are asking too much out of me! I cannot handle the pressure! Fuck! I messed up. Now I have to start over. Thanks, asshole.

NPC: Will do! Enjoy your results runner.

NPC: I'll send the bill to Officer Jenna. Have a good day, runenr!

NPC: Welcome back. How did the DNA scanning go?

Your response: Quite well. I found five DNA matches. Apparently all are in the database.

NPC: You got nothing? Really?

NPC: Well, let us have a look. Ok, we have Kylan Chambers, which is obvious. This one is from Dylan Gooden. Records show he was the contractor for the construction of her apartment. You mentioned that some of the contract workers were the ones that stole the other armor part. Do you think he is involved?

Your response: Dylan Gooden is shady and a pervert, but it does not seem like robbery is his avenue.

NPC: Very well. The other three names are all records who have not had an update in quite some time. That either means they went off the grid in the Wastes, or they are dead. The computer shows two of the names, Sterling Figgis and Cyril Archer are known Anarchy Breed.

Your response: *click*

NPC: They are wanted in connection to over a dozen crimes.The last one, Colton Oppelt is listed as an Anarchy Breed sympathizer, but is currently 'Whereabouts Unknown'.

Your response: You can go ahead and update the records for Sterling Figgis and Cyril Archer.
Those are the 2 contractors that stole the first armor part.
A third member of their group showed up and killed them for the part after they got a bit greedy.

NPC: I wonder if the third member was this Colton Oppelt guy.

Your response: No. The third person from that group was a female according to the eye witness.
This Oppelt guy is the only puzzle piece that is not fitting.
Any thoughts on where somebody like him would hide out?

NPC: Nowhere in any of the civilized parts of the city. All of the Anarchy Breed and their sympathizers I hear about come from the old Jailhouse in Outzone Sector 8.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Maybe someone around knows where to find him. Doubtful that any of them will speak with you. Hell, they will probably shoot you for showing up on their turf.

Your response: If that is where I need to go, than that is where I am going. I will just make sure my gun is bigger than theirs when I show up.

NPC: Sounds good to me.

NPC: You are back, and hopefully with some more good news?

Your response: Yes. Good news. You can throw Colton Oppelt on the dead list.

NPC: What about Colton Oppelt?

NPC: I never realized you would come with such a body count following you. At least they are all people who will not be missed. We might have a bit less crime without them around as well.

Your response: Probably. But that is not even the good news.
I found the other part that was stolen from Ms. Chambers.

NPC: OUTSTANDING! We can close one of these damn cases. Now that is what I call results. Officer Jenna told me it was a bad idea to recruit you. I am glad we have proven her wrong.

Your response: Well, do not go gloating to her yet. There was this encrypted datacube on his body too. He mentioned it had the locations of four more parts.
It seems like Ms. Chambers' relatives had some parts stolen from them too.

NPC: You cannot be serious. There are no filed reports on any other missing antiques. Hand over the datacube and I will get it analyzed. We can still call this case closed. If a new case happens to open up because of the datacube, it will not be under my jurisdiction.

Your response: *click*

NPC: You've got the encrypted datacube?

NPC: And because of that, I do not care.

Your response: Here you go. Let me know if you need any more help in the future. This has been an entertaining experience.

NPC: Where is the antique part?

NPC: Will do. It seems you have earned the full reward for retrieving both of Ms. Chambers' parts. Here is an additional 10,000nc to add to the original reward. Do you want to break the news to Ms. Chambers? I bet she would love to hear it from you.

NPC: You already talked to Mrs. Chambers?

NPC: Welcome back. Looking for another job already?

Your response: Sure. It seems like I cannot get away from the rush.

Your response: No. Just wanted to drop in to see Charlie here.

NPC: Charlie is the best indeed!

NPC: Good. I was hoping you would drop in. We looked into Ms. Chambers' extended family. Both of her aunts had a will and each one stated that upon her death the next oldest living relative would get ownership of her set of armor parts.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Ms. Chambers is the last living relative in the family according to the records. We contacted her to inform her of this information and she asked us to open a case to find the last four parts.

Your response: So just decrypt the datacube I gave you.
Colton Oppelt said it had the locations of the parts on it.

NPC: I believe that is the plan. Since this is officially a new case, I am not in charge of it. Officer Jenna is running point on this one. She mentioned she could use your specific set of skills in her investigation.

Your response: My set of skills?

NPC: Yes. She took an interest in your ability to go beyond the normal terms of the law. Go have a chat with her and see what she needs. Ms. Chambers is offering a pretty hefty sum for the reward this time. 10,000nc per part, or 50,000nc for the lot. Officer Jenna agreed to forward you the reward once these are found just like our agreement.

Your response: Thank you for the information. I will go by and see Officer Jenna.

NPC: Officer Jenna is already waiting for you.

NPC: Officer Jenna is waiting!

NPC: You did a great job so far. Want to proceed?

Your response: Yeah, sure!

Your response: Not now. Sorry.

NPC: If you change your mind, talk to me.

NPC: Officer Jenna is waiting for you, have a chat with her!

NPC: Officer Jenna is waiting for you, have a chat with her!

NPC: Hello there, Detective! What do you think about your new rank?

Your response: I am beyond amazed. Thank you very much for all you have done for me.

NPC: Thank you for the help you have given us. I was tasked with letting Ms. Chambers know the rest of her antiques have been located, but I thought it would be a good idea for you to tell her. She would like to hear it from you.

Your response: Of course. That will not be a problem.

NPC: Oh, yeah. Before you go. I received this message on a private terminal.
It is from a Lady C who wants to speak with you. She says it is regarding the family armor suit, and she has some important information for you.

Your response: Lady C? She is the one who was heading up this whole operation.
Maybe she is going to try to steal it back again. I am going to have to go armed and armored to meet this one.
Where does she want to meet me?

NPC: It says to meet her in the Old Jailhouse in Outzone Sector 8, outside the bar. Do you need backup? I can send Charlie here to assist.

Your response: No thanks. Charlie seems to be comfortable right where he is.
I should be able to handle this lady myself.

NPC: Good Luck, Detective.

NPC: I just got a message from Ms. Chambers. She was so excited she could barely talk. She told me to transfer full ownership off all the parts to you for your assistance in this case.
Seems strange she would go through all this trouble to get the antiques back just to give them away in the end.

Your response: Yeah. I guess just knowing that they are not in the wrong hands is enough for her. I am humbled that she would offer something of such great value to me.

NPC: Don't you have work in OZ8 to do, Detective?

NPC: Well, you earned them. Here are your antiques, Detective.

Your response: Thank you. I guess this is goodbye, until the next cold case.

NPC: Maybe we meet again, Detective!

Stone of the Hurler King

• **Just an ordinary stone. You've already seen millions of them in the wastelands.**

entries.conversation:
NPC: **You get a strange feeling about this stone... somehow - maybe it's magic? - it is able to get your full attention.**

Your response: - Leave the stone alone

Your response: - Touch the stone

NPC: **Just an ordinary stone. You've already seen millions of them in the wastelands.**

NPC: **The strange feeling disappears and you realize that this stone is just an ordinary one. You've already seen millions of them in the wastelands.**

NPC: **It is a comfortable feeling, these vibrations in your hands. Suddenly you hear some words in your mind... Hurler King... Keeper of the Hurler King... Crystal...**

Your response: - Release stone

NPC: **The strange feeling disappears and you realize that this stone is just an ordinary one. You've already seen millions of them in the wastelands. But these words... There is another strange feeling about an abandoned building next to a mountain right north from here**

NPC: Hey stranger! I only meet somebody so far out here once in a moon! So, what are you doing?

Your response: Greetings! I am just on my way from here *points in one direction* to there *points in another direction* But something strange just happened to me!

NPC: I see, you're a runner! Tell me about this strange happening!

Your response: I just touched a stone I found in this sector and while it was vibrating some words appeared in my mind - Hurler King, Keeper of the Hurler King and crystal... Uh man, I tell ya, really strange stuff! But hey, aren't you this Keeper of the Hurler King??

NPC: *cough* Uh! I have to go, sorry!

Your response: Stop! Wait!! Please!

NPC: *sigh* Well, yes, I am the the Keeper of the Hurler King. I hoped this shit stopped finally...

Your response: Shit?

NPC: I guess you know that stuff with destiny and so on... Well, my destiny is to stay here all my life and wait for runners like you who touched this dman stone! And know you want this 'Strange Crystal' right? To call the Hurler King, right?

Your response: Hmm, well, that sound interesting. Yes, why not? Give me one of these 'Strange Crystals' to call the Hurler King, please.

NPC: See? Just what I expected! But this time it will be not that easy! This time I want something in return! I can not give the crystal out for free everytime! This poor man needs to make his life as well!

Your response: Okay okay! I can understand that man, and as long as it is not too expensive it is okay for me.

NPC: Nah, I just want some 'Extract of Quercus Ilicifolia'. That's a kind of oak brush you can usually find near Tech Haven. Just recently I saw a brush near the entrance in sector F_07. Perhaps it is still there.

Your response: I think I can do that. I'll be back soon, don't move!

NPC: Don't worry. As soon as I have this extract I can brew my special mixture based on herbs. *smiles*

NPC: **A Quercus Ilicifolia plant**

Your response: - Get some extract

NPC: **You get some extract**

NPC: **There is nothing you would have use for anymore**

NPC: Ah, there you are! Do you have the extract?

Your response: Yes, I have. Here, take this gluey stuff...

NPC: So, where is the extract? Not with you, I think! Go look around near Tech Haven!

NPC: Great! Thank you very much!

Your response: No problem. So where is my crystal?

NPC: Ah right, here take this damn thing. I think you know what you have to do with that. I have to take care about my mixture made from herbs. Good luck! YOu will need it, especially if you really think you can call the Hurler King on your own! YOu really should ask some friends for some help if you go there.

NPC: What do you want from me? You already have that damn crystal!

NPC: **The 'Strange Crystal' starts to vibrate again as you are getting closer**

Your response: - Examine stone

NPC: **Nothing happens. Maybe it is just a stone?**

NPC: **You see an indentation and the 'strange crystal' seems to fit in there quite perfectly**

Your response: - Put 'Strange Crystal' into the indentation

NPC: **Now the stone even starts to rumble and as it gets stronger and louder the Hurler King appears in front of you - together with his Butchee bodyguards!**

NPC: **The stone starts to vibrate heavily again to finally release the 'Hurler King Knuckles'**

Your response: - Take 'Hurlerking Knuckles'

NPC: **Again a vison shoots through your head...Defeat the Hurlerking...Finish what you have begun...**

NPC: **You take the 'Hurlerking Knuckles'**

NPC: **Nothing happens. Maybe it is just a stone?**

Hata Mari

CONDITIONS FOUND

entries.conversation:
NPC: Psst Runner! I'm looking for a trustworthy member of the Guardian. Are you interested?

Your response: Who are you?

NPC: You don't belong to the Guardians. Move out!

NPC: I don't think you are experienced enough to work for me. Get some training and come back when you can stand on your own feet! (level 20)

NPC: My name is Hata Mari and I'm working for the TGIS.

Your response: The TGIS? Never heard of it.

NPC: The Twilight Guardian Intelligence Service. My current mission is to recruit loyal members of our faction who are willing to take on a secret mission.

Your response: A secret mission? That sounds pretty dangerous.

Your response: No sorry, I don't think that this is something I want to do.

NPC: No, it's an easy mission. One of our agents is in NC City at the moment. His mission is to identify members of the Neocron Citycouncil, to gain their trust and to collect information about the regime. He recently asked for assistance.

Your response: You want me to support an undercover agent on enemy territory? This doesn't sound like an easy mission. I don't think that this is want I wanna do.

NPC: This job is really not very difficult. We are only talking about basic support duties, but further details can only be provided by our agent on site.

Your response: hmmm hmmm. I don't know.

NPC: It is an honour to serve your faction! We really need your help and will of course pay an adequate reward once you have finished your tasks.

Your response: Okay okay. I will give it a try. Where can I find the contact person?

NPC: The agents name is Bames Jond and he usually stays in Industrial Sector 1 in Neocrons outskirts. Since we do not know his exact position, you will have to search for it.

Your response: Yes ma'am. On my way to Neocron City.

NPC: Deliver this suitcase to Mr. Jond and make sure you don't lose it.

NPC: You can find Mr. Jond in Industrial 1 in Neocron City.

NPC: Who are you and what do you want?

Your response: I think that you are waiting for me. What is your name, Sir?

NPC: Where is my suitcase ? I'm not going to talk to you if you don't have it.

NPC: My name is Jond. Bames Jond. I'm not going to ask this a third time: Who are you and want do you want?

Your response: Hata Mari assigned me to this mission. I'm here to assist you and serve our faction as best I can.

NPC: *smiles* ... to serve our faction. How sweet. Agent Mari has been quite busy for the last weeks. I'm sure that you will serve MY faction very very well, as did your predecessors.

Your response: Sir? What are you talking about? My predecessors? YOUR faction?

NPC: Yes, my faction. The City Administration. I'm a member of the 00-Section of the NCSS. The Neocron City Secret Service. Do you know what's so special about the 00-section? It's members hold the licence to kill.

Your response: City Administration? The licence to kill? That means, you are going to .......

NPC: .... kill you. Yes. Exactly the same way as I killed all the other Guardians Hata Mari sent to me.

Your response: This is a trap? For what? What are you trying to achieve?

NPC: Isn't this quite obvious? Agent Mari recruits the most promising young Guardians, sends them to me and I kill them in order to weaken our worst enemy sustainably.

Your response: This is murder! And you are nothing but a dirty murderer!

NPC: No, my friend, this is war! Any last words?

Your response: STOP! Please don't kill me. Can't we find a peaceful solution?

NPC: I'm afraid we can't.

NPC: My fellow agents are still attacking you! I don't think you have the time to talk to me right now.

NPC: Umm, it looks like this went outta control. You were supposed to die ......

Your response: HANDS UP and DONT MOVE!

NPC: Calm down please. I'm sure we can find a peaceful solution.

Your response: A PEACEFUL SOLUTION? Now you want a peaceful solution? When I asked for it you tried to fucking kill me!

NPC: The NCSS is a very powerful organisation. Do you really think, you can kill one of their agents without being punished for it? Hata Mari knows who you are. They will hunt you and your whole family and finally kill you all.

Your response: I don't think that you are in the position to threaten me right now. Your are DEAD MEAT, asshole!

NPC: Listen. You seem to be a smart person. Why not save your and your families lives and also add a considerable sum of money to your account?

Your response: You want to pay for your life? That's really pathetic.

NPC: No. Your life, your family members lives plus money in exchange for my life. That sounds quite fair to me. If you are willing to accept this proposal, you will have to meet my supervisor, Agent M, at Via Rosso 3.

Your response: Your supervisor? It is YOUR life we are talking about, not your supervisors.

NPC: I'm neither allowed to sign deals with enemies, nor to give out money. You'll have to deal with Agent M, if you are interested.

Your response: You better contact this person and explain this to her before I arrive at ViaRosso 3. Don't try to cheat on me. I know who you are. I'll make your face and your name public otherwise.

NPC: This datacube provides all the information Agent M needs. Leave me alone now.

NPC: Deliver the datacube to Agent M in Via Rosso 3.

NPC: Yes?

Your response: One of your 00-agents was begging for mercy when I kicked his ass an hour ago. He sent me to you in order to reach an agreement. Here I am and here is the datacube.

NPC: Who are you? I'm not the person you are looking for.

NPC: Bames was begging for mercy? I don't think so. *laughs* So you are the little rebel who managed to get one of my best agents in hot water? Not bad, really, not bad.

Your response: Yes it's me.  You better spare me your compliments and name the conditions for our agreement.

NPC: I need the datacube!

NPC: Alright, here we go: you return to your dirty canyon and refrain from talking to anybody about this and from unmasking Hata Mari and Bames Jond. You even forget that they exist!

Your response: Why should I do that?

NPC: If you agree, you and your family members are safe, our recruitment mission in the canyon will be stopped immediately, plus I will pay you 6000nc. If not... well, you know what's going to happen if you do not agree or break our agreement....

Your response: How can I be sure that the NCSS abides by the agreement?

NPC: You can't. You have to trust me just like I have to trust you.

Your response: Okay! Give me my money now!

NPC: Here it is. If you ever come to the idea of working for the City Administration, you know where I am!

Your response: That is never going to happen, bitch!

NPC: Good bye

NPC: Never mind. Good bye.

CONTACT
Commander Hopkins

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at least 55; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• For unknown reasons we have lost the signal from our relay station in sector C_11 . We are in urgent need of the daily report from our recon group. Your next task is to contact Signal Intelligence Officer Isabelle Renard at our relay station in sector C_11 and get todays report ASAP. Do not let me find out you've stopped to play with the Droms on your way there. Now move out!

• We observed an increased amount of Warbots in sector I_10. They are getting too close to Twilight Guardian facilities. We have to take care of this situation now! YOU have to take care of this! Go to sector I_10 and kill at least 50 of these WarBot killing machines! It would be a good idea to get a back up team, this is not an easy task. But I am sure you will not disappoint me, soldier!

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.

NPC: I don't deal with you pathetic Reza followers. Get the hell out of here now!

NPC: By the looks of you, you wouldn't be able to handle working with me. Get some more training and come back when you can stand on your own two feet!

NPC: Ahh, great! You're here just in time, soldier!

Your response: I'm sorry to disappoint you, but I don't have any time to spare chatting with you right now.

Your response: Err.. whaazzzup?

Your response: Sir, yes, Sir!

NPC: Well done, soldier! I see you've already mastered the Canyon Challenge. Go on and keep up the good work! If we only had more soldiers like you, we would have won the war already. Dismissed!

NPC: Well, then get out of my sight! Now!

NPC: Hmm, somehow you don't look like a real soldier... Have you ever had a weapon in your hands? have you ever used it against another human being?

Your response: Err... well, when I was a child I used to visit the shooting stand on the annual fair. I loved that!

NPC: Well, I think you should go back to picking flowers, you loser! Move out!

NPC: At ease soldier. First I need to test to see if you are suitable for this special mission I have. Right outside of the canyon there are some dangerous wasteland beasts which are attacking our freedom fighters. I want you to put a stop to that! Go out and reduce the number of dangerous fire creatures. 50 of either Doomreaper, Terror Leaper, Terror Raptor, Grim Chaser or Grim Persecutor should be enough. When you are finished come back to the base.

Your response: Hmm, I don't I'm tough enough for for that. I have to go.

Your response: Sir, consider those beasts as good as dead, Sir!

NPC: YOU LOUSY WUSS!!! Get the hell out of my face!!

NPC: That's what I like to hear, soldier! I would be glad if every soldier was as dutiful as you. We would have already won the war! Now move out!

NPC: ah, you are back! Good job, soldier! You really surprised me. I think you are ready for a more difficult task.

Your response: Sir, thanks, Sir! Sir, yes, Sir!

Do not let me find out you've stopped to play with the Droms on your way there. Now move out!

NPC: What the hell are you doing here! You have a mission to complete! Now move out and complete your task! Now!

NPC: Let me see... Hm, that is not good, really! Hmm...

Your response: Sir?

NPC: Did Commander Hopkins send you? Finally! You're late!

Your response: Mam, I was delayed. I am sorry!

NPC: It's okay, you are here now. Here take this report of our reconnaissance straight to Commander Hopkins. Move out, soldier!

NPC: Why are you still here? Don't waste our time, soldier! Commander Hopkins needs this report!

NPC: We observed an increased amount of Warbots in sector I_10. They are getting too close to Twilight Guardian facilities. We have to take care of this situation now! YOU have to take care of this! Go to sector I_10 and kill at least 50 of these WarBot killing machines! It would be a good idea to get a back up team, this is not an easy task. But I am sure you will not disappoint me, soldier!

Your response: Sir, it is an honor to work for you! I will not disappoint you, Sir!

NPC: Great! Dismissed!

NPC: I am impressed, soldier! Your doing a really great job! All those WarBots are scrap metal now! We are proud to have you on our side!

Your response: Sir, thanks, Sir! I just contribute my part.

NPC: What the hell are you doing here! You have a mission to complete! Now move out and complete your task! Now!

NPC: Words alone wouldn't do your accomplishments justice soldier! I want to award for valiant actions you've done under the banner of the Twilight Guardians with the 'Canyon Challenge Medal of Valor'!

Your response: Sir, I am honored, Sir!

NPC: Additionally I proudly present you with this 'Freedom Fighter CPU'. This is the brand new tactical implant for fighters created by our biomedical specialists. I am sure it will be of great value in your future fights.

Your response: Sir, I am at loss for words!

NPC: Your work for the Twilight Guardian is exemplary! Keep it up! Now I have to get back to my regular duties. Dismissed!

NPC: Without the suitcase we can't proceed!

NPC: I want Bob dead!

NPC: This is exciting!
We should proceed!
Just give me a quick moment to celebrate!

NPC: Okay, my final offer: Really: Wyatt Earp and 100k - Take it or leave it.

Your response: No... I can't effort that, sorry!

Your response: Oh man... Yes, I accept your offer!

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

ITEMS THE NPC MAY GIVE
• Enh. 7.62mm Sniper Rounds

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• I'm sure about that. We will surely meet again sometime. Keep training your Rifle Combat Skill, and soon, you will be one of the best. Till then: good luck.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

• Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: You know where to find me.

NPC: Ah... nice to see you. Great. Could you spare a moment? I have something that might interest you. And it is a little urgent, if you catch my drift.

Your response: I'm very sorry. I don't have time for you right now.

Your response: What do you want, Mr. Jones?

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Well, this is my concern: I am appointed to do a little job for our faction and I require the proper... tools for the job. You're supposed to help me acquire these tools, since I have other matters to attend.

Your response: And what exactly are we talking about here?

NPC: Just tell him that I sent you and that the canaries sang too much again. He will know what's the deal and hand you the tools I need.

NPC: Good luck.

NPC: Back I see - that was quick. I knew we decided on the right person. Did you fetch me what I need?

Your response: Yes, I have the gun right here in this briefcase...

NPC: You do not have the kit with you. Come back when you have completed your task successfully.

NPC: Great, great. Um... but how do you know there's a gun in the briefcase?

NPC: Apparently. It seems to be the time to look for somebody else I can trust better.

Your response: Oh yes. He said, that things would get too big for him and he wants double his usual fee next time.

NPC: Bastard. The list of people I need to... deal with just seems to get longer and longer.

Your response: Maybe I could help you out?

NPC: I'm sure you could. If I may say so, though: train your Rifle Combat skill - you will surely need it later.

NPC: Who are you and what do you want from me?

Your response: My name is of no importance. Jones sent me. I'm supposed to tell you that the canaries sang too much again.

NPC: Allright then. Tell him that things are getting way too big for me. I don't want to get involved into this any further. If Jones needs an unmarked gun again, tell him he should either look for someone else or pay me much more moolah.

Your response: A gun..? ...uh... yes... sure. - I'll tell him

NPC: Good. And now, get lost.

NPC: Didn't I tell you to get lost?

NPC: Back again, I see. Marvelous. As if you could read my mind. I have work for you. You're supposed to do some laundry. Unfortunately, this time, it's a bit dirty. Understand?

Your response: At the moment, all my time is consumed by my own laundry.

Your response: Yes, I do understand. So who is this about?

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great. You remember the gun you fetched for me? I will give it back to you. Just for your own protection, of course. There is a tiny problem I wanted to solve. Unfortunately, some problems cause other bigger problems. As in this case.

Your response: Get to the point...

NPC: We had to get rid of a former co-worker of our faction. Unfortunately, there has been a witness - his name is Mike Carson. And witnesses have this unfortunate habit to talk. So we need to make sure that he will not be able to talk anymore. The man is hiding now though, and we have not yet been able to seek him out.

Your response: And how am I supposed to find him?

NPC: If you would just let me finish. Money can open many doors, and we have lots of money. Luckily for us, people are corrupt. One of Mike Carsons Bodyguards has agreed to give us his current location, if we pay him enough for it.

Your response: And now I am supposed to get that information, right?

NPC: Exactly. And about that payment... use your discretion... hehehe...

Your response: Got that. Where do I find him?

NPC: Nice to see you again. Is that blood on your jacket? Hmmm... I hope you were thorough, at least.

Your response: As thorough as the situation warranted.

NPC: Come back when you are finished.

NPC: Great - that's how I like it. So, where is Carson hiding?

Your response: I don't know. My contact only knew the codename that he uses now.

NPC: Then you did the right thing by eliminating him. I loathe people who fail to keep meet end of a bargain. Whatever - just tell me what Carsons codename is.

NPC: Thanks, it shouldn't take me too long to find out where he is. Now, if you would be so kind to give me back the gun I gave you. Only for your own protection - of course.

Your response: Too bad, I just started to get used to this baby.

NPC: Can I help you?

Your response: But the deal was that you tell me his location, not his codename.

NPC: It doesn't matter. I just don't know his location. But his codename never changes, and your employer will have the necessary resources to find out where he is located.

Your response: I certainly hope that, because he will not be able to send me to you ask you again.

NPC: What... why are you carrying a gun... the deal included... son of a bitch!!!

NPC: There you are again. Sooner than expected, but not too soon. Are you ready to help out your faction a little?

Your response: At the moment, I have a few other matters to attend.

Your response: I think I already know what this could be. I'm ready.

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

Your response: Of course. Where do I find him?

Your response: No problem.

NPC: I'm really starting to like you. You might soon go all the way to the top. Trust me. Here, better take that sniper rifle again. It served you well the last time, didn't it? Good luck.

Your response: It was easy pickings...

NPC: Come back when you are finished.

NPC: No need to be humble. You did a great job. Unfortunately, other matters call for my attention. You were worth everything, and I do not want to leave that unrewarded. Here - take the gun. I cleared it for permanent usage and you can keep it.

Your response: Thanks, I will put it to good use.

NPC: I'm sure about that. We will surely meet again sometime. Keep training your Rifle Combat Skill, and soon, you will be one of the best. Till then: good luck.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

NPC: Now you die!

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: You know where to find me.

NPC: Nice to see you. Can you spare some time and do a little work for me? It would be very important to me, and time is short. And even if you are pretty new to our faction, you seem to be the right person for the job.

Your response: Right now, I have other matters to attend.

Your response: Sure, just tell me what you want, and I'll do it.

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great. Okay, this is the problem. And old friend of mine got me something that is not easy to acquire. I am a little worried about him though. It is not something you can get the legal way and I have lost contact to him days ago.

Your response: And you want me to check if everything is okay?

NPC: Yes, that would be great. I've known him for a long time, and he has always been reliable. I'm afraid he could be in trouble.

Your response: Okay, I will see what I can do.

Your response: He's fine. He hopes that you will be able to visit him soon.

NPC: Your job is not done yet.

NPC: Great. But what was that delay about? Did he even have what I wanted from him?

Your response: He gave me a sword for you. And the reason for the delay was, that some other people wanted to have it too, but I took care of those.

NPC: I figured as much. Where is it? ...but... but it is broken..!

Your response: Yes, I believe he is sorry about that, but there is little to be done about it now.

NPC: Yes... nothing can be done about it... thanks. I guess I will have to look around if I can find someone, who can fix this baby. I will get back to you, you did your job very well. Until then, you should keep training your Melee Combat skill. Nothing went wrong this time, but when you face stronger opponents, you should be ready.

Your response: Thanks for the tip... I'll keep that in mind.

NPC: Good, see you later.

NPC: Are you with them? Look, I told you, you cannot have it!

Your response: Jones sent me.

NPC: Ah, that's one reliable guy. I was able to find the Tsurugaoka-Sword, but its blade is broken. Like that stops the bastards trying to take it from me... they have been trailing me for days now.

Your response: You are being followed?

NPC: Followed my ass. These guys aren't playing. I am a trader, not a fighter. Not my domain, know what I'm saying? ...oh shit... Over there. Looks like they'll never give up! You better help me, or the sword will be gone and Jones can scratch one friend!

NPC: I think Jones sent the right guy... hahaha... We sure showed them!

Your response: That was easy...

NPC: There are more of them!!! Help me!!!

NPC: Maybe for you. But this is getting too big for me. Please take the Tsurugaoka-Sword. You're going back to Jones anyway and I don't want to keep taking this risk for a walk.

Your response: I can understand that. I will give it to him.

NPC: Thanks, one huge stone off my chest. It is much safer with you. Send Jones my best greetings and tell him that I still owe him a Sake or two.

NPC: Why are you still here? I already gave you the sword!

NPC: Ah, right time, right place. I like that. Can you spare some time and do another little job for me?

Your response: Not at the moment, sorry.

Your response: I have enough free time. Shoot.

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great. Remember the sword you fetched for me?

Your response: Yes, the broken blade.

NPC: Exactly... and I aim to change that. I found a blacksmith with the necessary skills to repair such a blade. But believe me - such people are rare now and ask for loads of money.

Your response: Okay... Am I supposed to do errands now to get some money?

NPC: Oh whatever gave you that idea? No, of course not. We already agreed on a price and I paid him. All you need to do is bring him the sword, get it back and bring it to me. Simple as that.

Your response: If it is necessary. Who is this blacksmith and where do I find him?

NPC: Great, here you are again. What took you so long?

Your response: Oh, maybe that I needed to crawl to some slobbering bum in his dark cave to find the necessary metal for the repair. Or that I needed to off your crazy-ass blacksmith because he was sure keen on keeping that blade after he was done with it.

NPC: Your job isn't done yet!

NPC: Oh...

Your response: Yup! Oh!

NPC: I'm sorry that this job took you that much work. But you do have the sword, right?

Your response: Of course I do. Here - take it.

NPC: Hmmm... marvelous. Unfortunately you can see where it broke. Inevitable I guess. I still owe you my gratitude. You did your job very well. You will surely have learned a lot. Remember to keep training your Melee Combat skill, and you will be very strong in no time.

Your response: What did you think I am doing all the time. Still, thanks.

NPC: I will soon have another job for you. Until then, good luck out there.

NPC: Jones sent you. You bring the Tsurugaoka-Sword.

Your response: Um... yes, that's right. But how do you know that?

NPC: I know many things. And I see many things others cannot see.

Your response: Then I'm sure you see that I'm short on time, right?

NPC: I see impatience. But I will not provoke you. Show me the blade.

Your response: There you go - this is it.

NPC: Oh... indeed. Beautiful. But it isn't just broken, it is splinted. I have to replace some parts.

Your response: Go ahead...

NPC: It's not that easy. I need Shin-Metal. You need to fetch me some.

Your response: It keeps getting better. Where should I get something I have never heard of before?

Your response: I guess I will be on my way then, so we can get this over with.

NPC: Hurry up. I have other things to do.

NPC: You have the Shin-Metal.

Your response: Ever thought about the fact that people who know that you know what they are gonna say do not give two shits about your smart-ass comments?

NPC: I knew you would say that. Now give it to me.

Your response: Well, if you ask THAT politely...

NPC: Good. Go - Come back when I'm done.

NPC: The blade is finished.

Your response: Good, I want this to be finally over. Now if you would kindly hand it to me...

NPC: The blade isn't finished yet. Come back later.

NPC: I'm afraid I can't do that.

Your response: W... what? What's that supposed to mean?

NPC: That's supposed to mean that I will not give it to you. This blade is way too nice of a piece. I will not give it away again.

Your response: Have you lost your marbles? Give me the blade, or you will be in a lot of trouble with Jones!

NPC: No, I will not be in trouble with Jones. I will tell him that you took the Tsurugaoka-Sword and took off. He will come to think that you ran away with it.

Your response: Since you always have the answer to anything, explain to me how you plan on stopping me from telling him the real story of your double-cross?

NPC: I will stop you by killing you...

NPC: Washap?

NPC: Shin-Mefal? Whussat s'posed tah be?

Your response: How am I supposed to know? You are the seller!

NPC: Whaddaya knee id for?

Your response: To repair a blade.

NPC: Oh I shee... that inshane Blackshmish! Uhkay now I know whayou wonz. Shat guy ish jush buying ol' scrap jung of meh.

Your response: Yes, whatever, do you have some now?

NPC: Of coursh... I alwaysh do. Jush Jung. Here, take. 'Sh yoursh, why would ah needid.

Your response: Wow... thanks, I guess.

NPC: Whut more you wonz? I haff notheng mor'.

NPC: Cabinet open. You have taken the sword.

NPC: Cabinet closed.

NPC: The cabinet is empty.

NPC: Oh thank god, you're here. I think these bastards followed me.

Your response: Who followed you?

NPC: I don't know. I was with my old friend who gave you the broken blade. Do you remember..?

Your response: Vividly, so? Why are you being followed now?

NPC: He brought me a new Tsurugaoka-Sword. I couldn't get close to the one with the break marks. But now the same goons who have been trying to take the other sword from him seem to follow me now.

Your response: And now you brought these people right here?!? How about collecting something less dangerous? Explosives, poisonous animals or rare viruses maybe?

NPC: Do not mock me. Oh god... I think I heard footsteps. Protect me, I beg you!

NPC: Whew... that was close... I owe you my life. I will never forget that.

Your response: These guys weren't so tough...

NPC: They aren't dead yet!! Attack, dammit!!

NPC: No, you really did great. Take this sword - I have another one now. You seem to know perfectly well how to handle it.

Your response: Wow... thank you... so the entire effort DID pay off for me in the end.

NPC: I'm sorry I cannot give you anything else right now. I gotta take my leave now and go somewhere, where those goons cannot find me. I need to think on how to wipe out this gang.

Your response: Best of luck in that.

NPC: And best of luck to you. I am sure we will meet again.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

NPC: You're a dangerous enemy. I'll make sure to stay on my toes with you!

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• It's like this: You can only use vehicles outside the city, otherwise the city would be all clogged up. You will find a big terminal next to most city exits to the wastelands. So called 'Carports'. There you can get your vehicle, if you have the proper key.

• I'm sure of that. Anyway - I'm gonna have to leave now. Other matters require my attention. Maybe we will meet again sometime. Best of luck until then. I'm not needed anymore. Watch yourself.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

• Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: You know where to find me.

NPC: Good to see you. Feel at home yet? Yes? Well, it's good that you're here. We have a small problem, that you could help us solve...

Your response: No thanks, not at the moment.

Your response: Tell me what it is.

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Well, I want you to start a construction plant for vehicles again. The machine was sabotaged, is broken, was mistreated... whatever. I just want to see it running again so production is no longer delayed.

Your response: And how am I supposed to do that?

NPC: Ah, there you are again... Very good - I got to know that everything runs smoothly now. I am very happy that our faction has members that are as highly skilled as you are.

Your response: Thanks, but it wasn't really that hard.

NPC: The machine isn't repaired yet. Come back when you finished your job.

NPC: No need to be humble. You're doing great. I advise you to use your gained knowledge to train your Vehicle Usage skill. After all, that's what you want to do, right?

Your response: Yes, thanks for the advice.

NPC: My pleasure. If you can spare some time, please talk to me, I will surely have more jobs for you.

NPC: Yes, what is it? My day is fuckin' packed, so talk already.

Your response: Nothing. Wrong guy.

Your response: Jones sent me. I'm supposed to get a replacement part for a machine.

NPC: Sure. I have too much work anyway.

NPC: What the hell?! You're a godsend! That POS is causing problems since weeks and now it finally broke completely. I didn't think, that Jones would send help that quickly. All the better - here it is. Put that part in and check if everything works fine again. Then you should go right back to Jones.

Your response: Uh, sure. But where is that broken machine anyway?

NPC: Hmm? What do you want? You have the replacement part already.

NPC: S Y S T E M   D I S O P E R A T I O N A L

NPC: P A R T   N O T   F O U N D   P L E A S E   R E P E A T

NPC: S Y S T E M   O P E R A T I O N S   R E S T O R E D

NPC: Oh, hello. Great timing that you ask me now. Nice appartment, by the way. Well, I have another small job for you. Interested?

Your response: No, I don't have time at the moment.

Your response: Of course. What is it?

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

Your response: And what am I supposed to do? Get that mini-prototype for you?

NPC: There you are. What took you so long?

Your response: I had to play the vermin exterminator, because you didn't send one...

NPC: You do not have the prototype? Well, come back when you do.

NPC: A vermin exterminator..? ...oh... oh yes... right. I'm very sorry about that. I completely forgot about that with all that work I have to do. But it's nice to see you doing the work for your faction so enthusiastically.

Your response: Yeah... but I would still rather drive something than playing the vermin exterminator and carry around toy cars. By the way, here it is.

NPC: Wonderful. But be patient. This 'toy car' is way more than that. I think I can further involve you into this matter and, of course, reward you properly. So if you want to drive something bigger, you should keep training your Vehicle Usage skill.

Your response: Yes, thank you. I'll be sure to remember that.

NPC: Good. I have further jobs to finish. Come back to me when you are ready.

NPC: Ah!!! What?!? Who's there?!? My goodness... never sneak up on me like that again, understand? You never know if it isn't one of these ugly little beasts.

Your response: Uh, yes... sorry. Won't happen again.

NPC: Yes yes, it's okay. I'm just a little nervous about the spiders. So, what do you want from me?

Your response: Mr. Jones sent me. I'm supposed to get some mini-buggy-prototype-thingamabob.

NPC: Jones, eh? Well, screw him. He always wants, wants, wants. I asked for a cleansing 6 weeks ago, and he still didn't send it. I live in a frickin' spiders nest. Stupid things are crawling all over the place. And I HATE spiders. But Jones doesn't care. As soon as he wants something from me though, he is fast as hell.

Your response: Will you give me that thing or not?

NPC: No! I've finally had enough. I cannot work under these conditions. Go to Jones, and tell him that he should first send the vermin exterminators. When they are done, he can have the mini-prototype. Not a second earlier.

Your response: And what if I kill those spiders? Will you give it to me then?

NPC: Do you have a vermin exterminators license level 4 or above?

Your response: You need a license for that now? No, I don't think I do.

NPC: Then I'm sorry but I can't let you do that. You might get hurt.

Your response: Hurt? By these little scrabblers? Trust me, I'll wipe all of them out without a problem.

NPC: Well okay... But don't say I didn't warn you. When you wiped out this brood, you will get the mini-prototype for Jones. Get going already! These spiders!!

NPC: Good grief. You know your handywork. I am very satisfied. The biting and pinching will finally stop. These bastards crawl everywhere I tell ya, you wouldn't believe how much such an eight-legged freak can hurt when he crawls up your...

Your response: ...I do not need to hear these things. Will you give me the prototype already?

NPC: These SPIDERS! KILL THEM ALREADY!!!

NPC: Oh yes, of course. Here you go. But be careful. It is an exact micromodel with all functions. You can generate a complete blueprint from it. Do not break it, or the customers might wonder where the steering wheel went... hahaha!

NPC: Hmm? What else do you want? You already have the blueprint! Do not waste my precious time!

NPC: Ah, back again I see. Listen, Would you sell me that chair over there, bychance? I used to have one of these, but unfortunately it broke, when my ex-wife...

Your response: I don't really have time for you right now.

Your response: Come on, Jones. What do I need to do for you now?

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great. I like a straight shooter. I'll get straight to the point then. You will remember the mini-prototype you brought to me. It is time to start the production. Usually I would only give this job to someone, who has been a member of our faction for a long time, but I like you and I trust you.

Your response: Are you really asking me to construct a vehicle now?

Your response: I'm supposed to bring a car up here?!? How am I supposed to do that?

NPC: No, no. You will see. Not a car. I will explain everything to you, when you are back. In the meantime, get going.

NPC: There you are... Do you have what I want?

Your response: If it is this key, then yes!

NPC: Your job isn't finished yet. Come back when you are done!

NPC: Yes, that's what I mean. This is wonderful... You really did pay off. We can now start producing the 4 Wheeler Buggy and you did a really big part in that. Like I promised, you shall not go unrewarded.

Your response: Does that mean you will finally pay me for my work?

NPC: Even better. You can keep the key. The 4 Wheeler is yours!

Your response: WOW!!! Now this is great. But... where is it and how can I drive it?

NPC: It's like this: You can only use vehicles outside the city, otherwise the city would be all clogged up. You will find a big terminal next to most city exits to the wastelands. So called 'Carports'. There you can get your vehicle, if you have the proper key.

Your response: Sounds great. I think I might try that right now.

NPC: You go ahead and do that... But if I may advise you: Do not just train driving, do something for your body, too. You should be ready to defend yourself, when you go out there. The beings that you could meet out there can be bigger and badder than everything you have seen until now.

Your response: I see...

NPC: And if you get raided, it won't help if you're a master of controlling your vehicle, but everyone can take it from you by force. So you should also concentrate on your fighting abilities.

Your response: Thanks. I think I would have done that anyway, though.

NPC: I'm sure of that. Anyway - I'm gonna have to leave now. Other matters require my attention. Maybe we will meet again sometime. Best of luck until then. I'm not needed anymore. Watch yourself.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

NPC: Yes? What is it?

NPC: That depends on who's asking.

Your response: Jones sent me.

NPC: Oh... okay... about the blueprint, right?

Your response: Exactly. Here's the prototype.

NPC: Very good... oh, that's simple. Wait a second... ... ... ... ... ...

Your response: ... ... ... ... ... *pfffff* ... ...

NPC: You don't have it? Come back when you do! My time is precious.

NPC: ... compensate a little... *mumble* ... ... from the other side... ... *grumble* ... ...

Your response: ... ... ... Excuse me! Will this take much longer?

NPC: Ah! No! It's getting done. Here you go, take it. I will handle the disposal of the prototype. And tell your Mr. Jones, that payment better not take as long as it took last time, please.

Your response: Will do. Do you happen to know where the production pipeline is? Jones was a little confused and forgot to tell me.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• You are welcome. You served your faction very well. Now I have other matters to attend, but we will meet sometime later. My advice: train your droning skill but don't forget to spend also some time with your other skills, you should not be fully dependant on your technical friends. There are beings out there that you would never even dream of... Good luck.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

• Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• I have other matters to attend now and leave you to yourself. If you keep training hard, you can get hired by a clan community. They always need good hackers. Good luck in your further way. We will surely meet again.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

• Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: You know where to find me.

NPC: Oh, nice to see you. Got accommodated yet? I have a little something that needs to be done. Are you interested in helping me and your faction out a little?

Your response: I have no time right now.

Your response: Of course.

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Great... This is the deal: We need some data from a database, and a direct access would be too risky. That's why I want you go 'go in' and get that data for me. You need to get the password from... an informed person, though.

Your response: I basically just arrived, I can hardly find my shoes right now. How am I gonna find all this?

Your response: Yes, but how do I find him? I don't know the way...

NPC: Use your Nav-Ray. It should be easy to find the guy with that.

Your response: Okay... and when I have the data, I come back here to you, right?

NPC: Exactly - good luck.

NPC: You're back. Did everything work out?

Your response: Yes, it did. I have your data...

NPC: You did not finish your mission. Come back when everything is done.

NPC: Hmmm... this data is encoded. Another problem that needs solving... First, thanks a lot.

Your response: No problem, glad I could help.

NPC: Good, because I might soon have another job for you. Until then, you should train your Hacking skills so you'll be able to crack even better security systems.

NPC: Who are you? I don't know you.

Your response: Jones sent me for a password.

NPC: Ah, the netrunner, Jones wanted to send to me. You're late...

Your response: Sorry, I was trying to hurry up.

NPC: Hey, it's allright - I just don't have much time because I have other matters to attend. Anyway, the password is 'Silverfuture06# ...good luck.

Your response: Wait! Jones told me you could tell me where the database is.

NPC: D A T A S E R V E R   ´ S I L - P 5´
PASSWORD:

Your response: SILVERFUTURE06

NPC: PASSWORD ACCEPTED

Your response: (Start Download...)

NPC: DOWNLOAD COMPLETE

NPC: ACCESS DENIED

NPC: There you are. As if I called you... great. Do you have the free ressources to help me a little?

Your response: My ressources are limited right now, sorry.

Your response: At your service...

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: It's about the data you downloaded for me. They need to be decoded by our mainframe. Then you need to upload the data onto the account 'Silverdivision' from a different terminal.

Your response: First things first... where do I decode the data and where do I upload it?

Your response: Good, and then?

NPC: That was quick... did you send the data?

Your response: Yes, I did... easy as ever.

NPC: You did not finish your mission. Come back when everything is done.

NPC: Nice to see that you enjoy browsing through the net. But remember that there is a real world out here, where you might not be as strong as you are in there. You should also train some basic combat skills, to be able to defend yourself in the real world. You will never be as strong as a real fighter, but it is important not to ignore your body.

Your response: Thanks for the tip, I will get to training right away.

NPC: Very good. Come back later, I will have more stuff for you to do.

NPC: PLEASE SELECT DESIRED FUNCTIONALITY

Your response: (Decode data)

NPC: PLEASE INSERT DATA FOR DECODING

Your response: (Enter Data)

NPC: DATA DECODING STARTED
PROGRESS: 24 PERCENT

Your response: ... Hmmm ...

NPC: PROGRESS: 62 PERCENT

Your response: ... this is taking forever ...

NPC: PROGRESS: 87 PERCENT

Your response: ... oh man ...

NPC: PROGRESS: 100 PERCENT
DECODING FINISHED

NPC: DECODING NOT ACCESSIBLE. SYSTEM RECALIBRATION IN PROGRESS

NPC: SUPERNODE X363KST02 - 2
PLEASE SELECT DESIRED FUNCTIONALITY

Your response: (Upload data to net account)

NPC: SESSION TERMINATED : DATA NOT ENCODED!

NPC: SUPERNODE X363KST02 - 2
PLEASE ENTER ACCOUNTNAME

Your response: Silverdivision

NPC: SUPERNODE X363KST02 - 2
UPLOAD COMPLETE - SESSION TERMINATED

NPC: SESSION TERMINATED

NPC: Hello... you look like you want to help me out a little again.

Your response: Not at the moment.

Your response: Sure, shoot.

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

Your response: And what is the password?

NPC: The password is 'Quicksilver7' ...keep it well. If it wasn't so important, we could have sent it through the net.

NPC: You look a little beaten... where have you been? What's wrong?

Your response: I was just delivering the password and then I had to off your stupid contact person! That's wrong!

NPC: You didn't finish your mission. Come back when you did.

NPC: What the fried f..! Why?! Have you lost your mind? Our clients will hold me responsible and have my ass!

Your response: Calm down... whoever those clients were - they wanted to screw us over! He was a double agent and worked for the other side. Whoever that other side is...

NPC: Oh shits... and you finished him before he could get his hands on the data? You did a great service to us. If this material in its decoded form had fallen into the wrong hands, many people would have had problems. Really, you helped us a lot.

Your response: I didn't have much of a choice... the man tried to kill me!

NPC: Take this TL90 Hacktool as a token of my appreciation and the appreciation of our faction - it will surely be of as much help to you as you were to our faction. Furthermore, you should keep training your Hacking skill. But as you saw, it is essential to be able to also defend yourself in the real world.

Your response: Thank you...

NPC: I have other matters to attend now and leave you to yourself. If you keep training hard, you can get hired by a clan community. They always need good hackers. Good luck in your further way. We will surely meet again.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

NPC: Ah, the youngblood again... what's up?

Your response: I'm supposed to give you the password for the server with the decoded data.

NPC: Oooohh... yess... of course... gimme, gimme!

Your response: Well... the password is 'Quicksilver7'...

NPC: Hehehehe... thanks, youngblood - nice doggie.

Your response: Uh... yes... you're welcome... Jones told me, you have something for him?

NPC: Oh yes, I almost forgot... I do have something for him. Your body in a bag, you stupid idiot.

Your response: Uh... Excuse me? What...

NPC: Shut it - you played your part nicely and Jones didn't notice a thing. It never even occured to him, that I could be a double agent. Yeah well... he is surely gonna notice when he finds his newest pet chopped up into parts in his mail... Hehehe...

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Mr. Jones

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• I now have other things to do. Other matters require my attention. Keep training and you might be one of the big ones someday. Thank you again in the name of our faction. We will surely meet again.
Oh, and: Visit the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job!

• Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.
Anyway, I highly suggest you to have a look at the Job Center (Plaza Sector 2) for a job.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: You know where to find me.

NPC: Ah, hello! How are you feeling in your new home? I have a small problem at the moment, and I cannot handle it myself right now. Could you help me with it?

Your response: Not right now, sorry.

Your response: Sure, I'll do that.

Your response: I don't need you, Mr. Jones. I can take care of myself! Thanks for your offer!

NPC: As you wish. Come back when you are free. I will wait here for you.

NPC: Here's what it's about: The routes of our... not entirely legal transports have been checked too often lately. That got our attention. But now we heard from an external source, that we have a mole in our middle who has been mouthing off about things he is not even supposed to know.

Your response: And how am I supposed to find him?

Your response: It's a little smelly down at the smugglers...

NPC: You did not finish your mission. Come back when everything is done.

NPC: I'll try and find out the mole's position. Until then, you should train your Tech-Combat skills. It's a rough world out there and nobody is gonna wrap you in silk. Come back later - I will have more stuff for you to do.

NPC: Hey... how's it hangin'?

Your response: Jones sent me... it's about the... mole.

Your response: Sounds like a swell fella. Where do I find him?

NPC: You can find the Smuggler Caver in PEPPER SEC-3!

NPC: Who are you? If you want shit, I'm all out of it and waiting for the next delivery.

NPC: Yes, I know... Shit - sure I know who's behind that.

Your response: Would you be willing to tell me?

NPC: Hehehe... sure!... course... um... you don't have some booze for me, do ya?

Your response: No, I don't, and now please tell me who's the mole or Mr. Jones might be very disappointed.

NPC: Aw crap... why didn't you say that Jones wants to know... hehehe... stupid old f...! I'm gonna send Jones a message over the net with the name. Got a couple of questions about that last payment for him anyway...

Your response: Okay... but don't forget it... I don't want to have to come back.

NPC: Jaja... you me too. Now piss off!

Your response: I will... by the way, anyone ever told you that lighting a fire in a closed environment is a bad idea? - really bad for your health!

NPC: GET YOUR ASS OUT!!!
