NPC: Before you can work for me, you have to work for Pierre (Job Center).

NPC: A new face in town - Welcome!

Your response: Indeed, and looking for a job right now.

Your response: New and busy, will catch up later eventually.

NPC: Bye.

NPC: Sure thing. Are you ready for some action? It could be quite dangerous.

Your response: I can handle everything, trust me.

NPC: Alright than.
Have you heard about the Outposts in the Wastelands?

Your response: A little bit, yes... You want me to destroy one?

NPC: You can't destroy those, trust me.

Your response: *click *

NPC: You can capture an Outpost as a Clan, if you attack the current holder.

Your response: For what reason I should do that?

NPC: By capturing an Outpost you will get honour and glory.
Your clan also gets cash for holding it, plus an extended bonus on your subskill, depending on the Outpost you're holding.

Your response: *click*

NPC: If you're holding a Factory for example your Construction skill is increased. Even if an allied faction is holding it!
But you get the most effective bonus when your clan is holding the Outpost.

Your response: Nice! So I could construct stuff?

NPC: Well, it depends on your skills, but you could possibly perform easy construction jobs, if you're not a constructor, like modding a weapon. But only in the sector of the Outpost of course.

Your response: Cool stuff! Didn't know that!

NPC: That's the reason why I'm telling you this, but let us not waste time, you're looking for a job and I've got one for you.

Your response: Shoot.

NPC: You know what we're planning here on the third floor, right?

Your response: Yeah, purging the world...

NPC: Yes. And now it get's a bit ugly...

Your response: Okay...

NPC: I told you about those Outposts...
Those are all over the Wastelands.
Connected to the GenRep System you know from the inner city.

Your response: *click*

NPC: Once you have activated those, you can use those, when they're not blocked by a hostile faction for example.
Use that system to travel fast from point A to point B.

Your response: *click*

NPC: For your assignment you have to travel far away from Neocron City. Deep into the Wastelands to hunt down some flying Bots.

Your response: Flying Bots?

Your response: I'm listening...

NPC: Those fields are disturbing our communication systems. We need the ability to communicate with our away teams! Eliminate those bastards!

Your response: Sounds hard...

NPC: We're not giving candies here, it's a tough job. Decide yourself whether you're in or not!

Your response: I'm in!

Your response: I think I have to get some more experience for that... Sorry!

NPC: Oh my gosh... You really did it. KUDOS!
Our communication is - finally - restored, many thanks!

Your response: It was not an easy task, but yes...

Your response: I want the rifle, please!

Your response: I want the pistol, please!

Your response: I want the passive PSI module, please!

Your response: I want the aggressive PSI module, please!

NPC: I'm looking for a more experienced runner for this job. Complete Very Easy missions from a Citycom in Viarosso and come back when you reach rank /10.

NPC: You again? Good job last time, but there is nothing you can do for me. Talk to Peps in the Job Center!

NPC: Before you can work for me, you have to work for Jonathan (Job Center).

NPC: WHAT?!

Your response: Calm down... Jonathan told me you might have a job for me.

Your response: Fuck off!

NPC: Tosser!

NPC: Oh, sorry... Jonathan told you I have a job for you? Seems you impressed him! Wait... You're %PLAYER_NAME(), right?

Your response: Yes. Glad to hear my name's getting around. So, you have a job?

NPC: Ya, sure! You ready to get your hands dirty?

Your response: Tell me more!

NPC: We have a problem in our sewers...

Your response: The sewers? Sounds lovely.

NPC: Indeed. A build up of wild plant life in our Plaza Sewers that we need to destroy.

Your response: All of them?

NPC: Step by step, chummer. The sewers aren't exactly the cleanest and wiping out all the plant life would be impossible! The cities waste has mutated them into a dangerous challenge.

Your response: Plants, dangerous? You're kidding, right?

NPC: No! The mutated plants are dangerous enough to destroy but if left alone they can spread their poison into the water and the other creatures down there and the whole city could end up infected or dead!

Your response: Okay. So the job is to go and eliminate those plants?

NPC: Yep. Kill 25 Cankered Plants in any Plaza Sewers!

NPC: You killed them?

Your response: What do you think? I did it!

NPC: Before you open your mouth: kill 25 Cankered Plants!

NPC: Good Job, %PLAYER_NAME()! Talk to Peps (Job Center) if you need another job!

entries.description: Quest-related dialogue from the game files.
entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• The kind that does not go into any file. We are a contract army, recruit. Everything we do is signed, stamped and paid for. Almost everything. There is a woman in Sector 1 who has spent three weeks measuring this Base with her eyes. Shift changes, camera arcs, which door the medics carry the dead out of. Her name is Nadia Roost, and we have to assume that she is selling that intel to whoever buys. Close her account with extreme prejudice.

• In the middle of Sector 1?

• Sector 1 is reporting that a contractor had a heart attack in the strip. Nobody has asked a second question yet. Anything I should know?

• Roost is still drinking and you are still standing here. Sector 1. The bar next to the Gene Replicator. Go.

• It is about an envelope. One that came through your paperwork and ended with a woman dead in Sector 1.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I read your file. Twice. Once for the scores, once for the gaps. And there are a lot of gaps. Most recruits fill those in with lies, but you left them deliberately empty. An unusual choice in your line of work, which piqued my interest. So: do you want work, or do you want a uniform?

Your response: Work. What kind?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: The kind that does not go into any file. We are a contract army, recruit. Everything we do is signed, stamped and paid for. Almost everything. There is a woman in Sector 1 who has spent three weeks measuring this Base with her eyes. Shift changes, camera arcs, which door the medics carry the dead out of. Her name is Nadia Roost, and we have to assume that she is selling that intel to whoever buys. Close her account with extreme prejudice.

Your response: In the middle of Sector 1?

NPC: Where she stands, and I want the people around her still talking about work shifts and the weather afterwards. She drinks in the bar next to the Gene Replicator, same spot every evening. Walk up, do it, keep walking. Do not explain yourself to her. Do not explain yourself to anyone. Go.

NPC: Sector 1 is reporting that a contractor had a heart attack in the strip. Nobody has asked a second question yet. Anything I should know?

Your response: She didn't expect me at all. I found a Merc credit chip on her. If she were selling us out, why would she be paid by a Merc?

NPC: Roost is still drinking and you are still standing here. Sector 1. The bar next to the Gene Replicator. Go.

NPC: A Merc credit chip, you say. Now that is a surprise, and I hate surprises. Normally, recon espionage is a slow Tuesday for us. But spies aren't paid with Merc credit chips. This smells. The thing is: Your contract was passed to me, I did not write it. Somebody is playing a dangerous game, here. Get your breath back. This is not finished.

NPC: This has turned into a real rabbit hole. I have not slept. Are you ready to work?

Your response: I am. Who gave you that contract?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Do not take long. I am no good at waiting.

NPC: That is the question, and unfortunately, it is not one I can ask out loud. Contracts reach me through the HQ gate paperwork: requisitions that are not requisitions. There is a clerk at the Military Entrance called Pell through whom all this paperwork goes, which means he has seen everything worth seeing. He knows whose handwriting was on my envelope.

Your response: Will he talk to me?

NPC: Oh yes. He will talk to anyone who makes silence look expensive. You are not there to hurt him: a frightened clerk invents, a comfortable one remembers. Get to the Military Entrance and bring me a name.

NPC: You have a name for me, or you have an excuse. Which is it?

Your response: A name. Lieutenant Aksel Corso. He passed that contract to you. And Jones? Roost was working for Vashenko, an auditor who checks Corso's work. He was paying her to photograph what leaves the gate at night.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance and he is not going to come to you. Go.

NPC: Corso. So he spotted the snoop shadowing him and felt the heat. And he got rid of the snoop, and laundered it. A green runner, a name in an envelope, no trail, and a recruiter who gave the paperwork the benefit of the doubt. Vashenko hasn't reported for his last three shifts, we were about to mark him AWOL. He probably went into hiding, afraid for his life. Roost was not selling this Base out. She was documenting the man robbing it, and I handed you the knife to kill her. That is a lot to take in. Take an hour. Then come back, and we will go after the right target this time.

NPC: Vashenko is the last name on that list and Corso can feel the gate closing. Are you in?

Your response: I'm in. Where is he?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Be quick. Corso is working to a schedule, and so are we.

NPC: CityMercs HQ, signing off manifests as though today were any other day. I put a word in the wrong ear an hour ago to see what would move, but Corso didn't move. He knows you are coming, though. Good. Let him spend the afternoon watching the door.

Your response: And if he wants to talk?

NPC: Oh, he will want to talk. Men like Corso have talked their way out of everything they have ever done, and he will offer you more than this Base pays in a year. Let him finish the sentence if it amuses you. Then end him.

NPC: Bar is behind me, friend. I am busy.

Your response: My mistake.

NPC: No worries. Long day for everybody.

NPC: If you have a requisition, hand it over, otherwise please move on, I am a very busy-

Your response: It is about an envelope. One that came through your paperwork and ended with a woman dead in Sector 1.

NPC: What? You're talking to the wrong person, then. I move paper, I do not read it.

Your response: Pell. You read all of it. Everyone in this Base knows you read all of it.

NPC: Alright, alright. That envelope came down from the armory office. Lieutenant Corso. He signs the manifests, he signs the corrections to the manifests, and lately he signs a great many corrections. They went unreviewed, since Vashenko went missing.

Your response: What do you mean, Vashenko went missing? Where is he?

NPC: Listen, pal. I just move paper, like I said. Vashenko checks Corso's numbers against what actually goes out the gate. I assume it's him who hired that gal who then ended up face down in that bar. She was probably tracing cargo movements out of this Base for him. Take that to whoever sent you and leave my name out of it.

Your response: Oh no. Jones needs to hear this.

NPC: Jones? Never heard that name. Very uncommon name. Tell her whatever you wish. Go on. I'm busy.

NPC: We never spoke. Move along.

NPC: You are the one Jones sent after the surveyor. I have been expecting a knock since lunch, though I will admit I expected somebody older.

Your response: You put Roost's name in her hand.

NPC: I put a name in an envelope, she passed it along, you pulled the trigger. Three signatures, one dead contractor, and not one of us did the whole thing. That is how this Base operates. Nobody carries all of it.

Your response: That death does not faze you at all, does it?

NPC: Auditors and their spies. Do you know what an audit is, recruit? It is someone deciding that a number matters more than the people the number belongs to. I have moved more hardware out of that armory than you will see in your career, and every crate went to a Merc who was going to die without it because requisitions run nine weeks behind. It doesn't have to be like this. Paperwork shouldn't matter more than people. You're sharp. Come and work for me instead. I will pay you what you are actually worth. And you will never end up in anybody's envelope yourself.

Your response: You do go on, don't you.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I am not going to pretend to be impressed by your temper. Everybody arrives here angry. What I want to know is whether yours does any work, or whether it is just noise you make on the way to being carried out. Interested in finding out in front of me?

Your response: I'm interested. Point me at something.

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Go on, then. Military Storage 6. Ten of whatever is moving down there. It is not much of a fight and that is deliberate: I want to see what you look like when the room is easy, because that is where the bad habits live. Anybody can be impressive when they are frightened.

Your response: Ten. Fine.

NPC: Fine. And come back with your kit intact, because the second half of what I am judging is what condition you are in afterwards. Storage 6. Go.

NPC: Ten, and you walked back up under your own power. How much of your kit did you use?

Your response: Less than half. That was not a fight, it was a chore. Give me a proper challenge next time.

NPC: Storage 6 is still crawling and the easy room is still the easy room. Go.

NPC: Cool down. You didn't enjoy it? Good! Keep not enjoying it. The ones who enjoy the easy room are the ones who go looking for a harder one on their own time and come back on a sled. Rest up. I have a room that will not be a chore.

NPC: Ready for the one that bites back?

Your response: Tell me where.

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. Take two. You will want them later.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3. Stacked hulls, no room to swing properly, and everything in there is bigger and meaner than what you met under the barracks. Eight of them. You will not get to pick your ground and you will not get to back off.

Your response: Eight, in a scrapyard. Understood.

NPC: I do not think you do yet, and that's fine, that is what the afternoon is for. One thing before you go: if it turns badly in there, leave. Walk out, breathe, go back in. Nobody up here is counting minutes. Storage 3. Go.

NPC: Eight, out of the wreck yard. So tell me: Did you have to walk out and go back in?

Your response: Twice. The second time I sat down outside for a while first.

NPC: The wreck yard in Storage 3 has eight of them left with your name on. Go.

NPC: Twice, and you told me about it without being asked twice. Do you know how rare that is in your specialty? I have had recruits bleed out rather than admit they stepped outside for a minute. That is the whole thing I was testing, and you have passed it, and now I am going to spend it on something I have been putting off for some time. Talk to me again soon.

NPC: This last one is not vermin and I am not going to dress it up. In?

Your response: I'm in. What is it?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Take your time on this one. I have taken months.

NPC: Gunnar Holt. Sector 1. He fought for this Base for years, and he came back alive and barely harmed every time. Of course, we could never prove it, or he would have been court-martialed, and we would've executed his ass. But he is a coward who weasels out of his fights. Has to be. And now, people have caught on. He cannot be sent out any more, because no one wants to go with him. He has become sort of a bad luck charm. Last spring, he went MIA, two of my people went in after him, and only one came back. With him, of course.

Your response: So he needs... what? An honorable way out?

NPC: That would be best. He has taken to drinking heavily. I think he thinks his life hasn't worked out, but being a coward, he is too frightened to oof himself. Do not laugh it off. He has asked for this with everything except words. This is a mercy. Sector 1. Go.

NPC: Big guy! Have a drink with me! ...Nah, you're not here to drink, are you? Has the day finally come?

Your response: Jones sent me. Yes, it has.

NPC: ...Say that again.

Your response: Yes. The day has come.

NPC: You have no idea how long I have wanted to hear someone say that. You know what they do instead? They laugh, they buy me a drink, they tell me I am the luckiest guy on this Base, and then they leave and they tell the gate not to put me on a roster. Do you know what that means for a Merc?

Your response: Listen, I will not guess as to what keeps transpiring out there. But you must know that it can't go on like this.

NPC: I do. But be warned. I keep coming out alive. I used to think that was the best thing about me. Now I sit in a corner being the bad luck charm no one wants to be with, while my Base goes out the gate without me. I am a weapon with no handle. Useful to nobody. But a weapon, nonetheless.

Your response: So let's find out if you are invincible, or just a coward.

NPC: Maybe one, maybe the other. Maybe both. Let's do this.

NPC: ...

NPC: Sector 1 says it took a while and that nobody interfered. Did he say anything worth repeating?

Your response: He said he was a weapon with no handle. Then he died. As quickly as I could manage.

NPC: Holt is in his corner in Sector 1, drinking his fill. Cut him off.

NPC: A weapon with no handle. A while ago he was the best forward fighter this Base had, or so we thought. Came back every time. With nobody guiding him, one weak moment turned into a habit. And we did that to him. There was no clean way out of this anymore, I suppose.

Your response: He wanted it finished.

NPC: He wanted what he always ran away from. In the end, he managed not to run, so you gave him a final victory over himself. Do not carry it as a kindness, recruit. Carry it as a bill that came due, and then look very carefully at how it got run up, because you are built exactly the way he was. Do not lie to yourself the way he did.

Your response: What lie?

NPC: That getting afraid for your life is a weakness. Gunnar couldn't reconcile his fear with his sense of pride and duty, and it broke him. Not being afraid is easy: you were born to do that. The thing that keeps you useful for twenty years is being the one who can be scared shitless, stop, get their act together, and come back for somebody. To walk out of a room they could have won, or would have lost, not because of fear, but because it is the right thing to do. Ignoring your fears doesn't make you strong, but neither does giving in to them. There is a sword coming your way, so keep training that Melee Combat and learn where you stop before somebody has to find out for you. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• Nothing, yet. Nobody signs a Merc vehicle out to an unrated driver, and I am not making an exception on your first morning. The motor pool chief is a woman named Mara Ivec. You will find her in Sector 1 with the vehicle dealer. She holds the stamp. Go and be worth it.

• Ask her. She will tell you at length, and most of it will be about people who did not listen. Let her talk. A driver who cannot stand being lectured by a mechanic is a driver who breaks down alone. Sector 1, by the vehicle dealer. Go.

• Ivec is still in Sector 1 and you are still unrated. Nothing moves until that changes. Go.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Your file says you can drive. Everybody's file says that. This Base does not run on rifles, it runs on things arriving, and at the moment things are not arriving. I need somebody who understands logistics. Interested?

Your response: I'm interested. What are you moving?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Nothing, yet. Nobody signs a Merc vehicle out to an unrated driver, and I am not making an exception on your first morning. The motor pool chief is a woman named Mara Ivec. You will find her in Sector 1 with the vehicle dealer. She holds the stamp. Go and be worth it.

Your response: What does it take to get stamped?

NPC: Ask her. She will tell you at length, and most of it will be about people who did not listen. Let her talk. A driver who cannot stand being lectured by a mechanic is a driver who breaks down alone. Sector 1, by the vehicle dealer. Go.

NPC: Ivec put your name on a rating this morning. She does not do that often. What did she make you sit through?

Your response: She went on and on about tire pressure, what else? But there was one sentence that wasn't about tires: she has not released a vehicle out the gate in six days.

NPC: Ivec is still in Sector 1 and you are still unrated. Nothing moves until that changes. Go.

NPC: Six days. I have three requisitions on my desk that have gone quiet in that time and I put it down to the wastes being the wastes. Ivec does not freeze a motor pool because she is in a mood. Somebody made that call above her. Get some rest, recruit. You have a rating now, which means from here on the problems are yours as well as mine.

NPC: Rated and rested. Ready to actually move something?

Your response: Tell me about the freeze.

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. The load is not going anywhere, which is the entire problem.

NPC: There is a pallet in the depot with the evening convoy's name on it, and it has been there long enough that somebody at an outpost is rationing. The freeze is not Ivec's and it is not mine. It is sitting with a clerk near the gate to the HQ at the Military Entrance. He is called Pell, and he is the one who decides which paper is real. No release, no wheels.

Your response: Then I go and get a release.

NPC: You do. Do not lean on him, he is not the enemy and he has been doing this since before either of us. Ask him what he is afraid of, then listen to the answer properly. Military Entrance. Bring me a release and the reason behind it.

NPC: You have a release in your hand and a face on you. Let me have both.

Your response: It's security concerns. The three Quads came back. On the sled, all three, all hit on the same bend. One driver told Pell the raiders were waiting on the minute - because he had been selling them the schedule for safe passage. He was in the second wreck.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance and the pallet is still in the depot. Go and get me that release.

NPC: So he bought his own safe passage and it lasted exactly as long as he was useful. I would like to tell you there is a lesson in that. Probably, there is, somewhere. Nobody has to hunt that traitor down. The road already collected. What is left is a bend that is still perilous, a pallet that has still not moved, and a convoy that still needs a point vehicle. Come back when you are ready to be the one who moves it.

NPC: Last thing, and it is the least glamorous work I will ever give you. In?

Your response: I'm in. What am I driving?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not be long. That pallet has a name on it and the name is getting hungry.

NPC: Nothing, until you go and get it. The one Quad still worth having is broken down, and needs a replacement part. The depot keeps them in Military Storage 3, where the sled drops what it drags in. The part you need has been sitting there six days in the dark, and six days is long enough for the dark to move in around it. The recovery crew took one look and found somewhere else to be.

Your response: So I go and dig the stuff for my own vehicle out.

NPC: You do, and you will do it again, and one day you will do it with something chewing on the axle while you work. Basically, make the junkyard quiet. The bots will then bring the part up, and we will talk about what you have earned.

NPC: Do not lean on that. What do you want?

Your response: Mara Ivec? Mrs. Jones sent me for a rating.

NPC: Ugh, of course she did. Let me guess: you can drive. Everybody can drive. I have buried four people who could drive. Answer me one thing honestly and I will think about the stamp. You are twenty minutes out with a load, temperature climbing, nothing on the scanner. What do you do?

Your response: Stop, before it stops for me.

Your response: Push for the gate. Twenty minutes is nothing.

NPC: Correct, and you said it without thinking about it, which is the part I was actually testing. A vehicle tells you it is dying about ten minutes before it dies. Everybody hears it. Almost nobody stops. You get the stamp.

Your response: That's it? No test drive?

NPC: Wrong. Why did I even bother. You still get the stamp. At least you answered fast. Listen to me: a vehicle tells you it is dying about ten minutes before it dies. Everybody hears it. Almost nobody stops. Push for the gate and you will walk the last twenty minutes carrying whatever you can lift and leaving the rest for the wastes.

Your response: Noted. So I get the stamp?

NPC: Yeah. Not that the stamp buys you much this week. I have not put a vehicle through the gates in six days and it is not my call to make. Take it up with the people who sign paper. Now go on, and stay off the panels.

NPC: Rated and everything. Come back when you have broken something.

NPC: If this is about an outbound release, the answer is the same as it was yesterday and the day before-

Your response: It is. And Mrs. Jones would like to know what you are afraid of.

NPC: Afraid, yeah, that's one word for it. Three Quads out this week. Do you know what came back? The Quads. Do you also know what didn't? Most of the entire rest. That is the part nobody wants to hear. All three came back on the recovery sled, in pieces, hit on the same bend of the same road inside the same hour of the evening. With almost everything else gone.

Your response: The same bend three times isn't just the wastes being the wastes. But what does 'almost' mean, here?

NPC: No, it's not the wastes being the wastes. What did come back was the second driver. Well, most of him. He was still talking when they brought him in. He said they were waiting. Not looking - waiting, on the minute. Because they had the schedule in front of them, as it turned out. He had been trading it to them for a quiet run of his own, and this time they decided to not make good on the deal.

Your response: Where is he now?

NPC: Six feet under. So there is nobody left to arrest, nobody to make an example of, and a bend that is exactly as dangerous as it was before. That is why I froze it. Won't send any more hapless drivers to their deaths.

Your response: Cut me the release, Pell. Somebody has to be the first one back on that road.

NPC: Sure. At least you know what is going on. Maybe that will make a difference. There. Stamped, and on your head. Tell Jones the freeze lifts when a load gets through, and not one second before.

NPC: You have your release. Go and use it.

NPC: Ivec says the yard is quiet and her bots went down without issue for the first time in a week. And?

Your response: And that hopefully means I get my Quad now, even if it needs an axle and about six hours. As long as it runs.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3 is still crawling and the pallet is still in the depot. Make it quiet.

NPC: Oh, it will run. Don't you worry about that. Six days of paper, three wrecks, one dead driver and a frozen gate, and the thing that ends it is a runner with a lamp going down into the dark to clear the area around a vehicle part by hand. Nobody will write that up. 'The pallet went out on the evening convoy and it arrived'. That will be the only sentence in this that anybody at the far end cares about.

Your response: So what about the bend? Did nobody ask about the bend?

NPC: Nobody ever does. That is the job, recruit, and you may as well learn it from me instead of the hard way. The road does not care whose fault it was, the road does not care that a man sold us out, or that he paid for it, or that the bend is still there tomorrow, with bandits behind every rock. The only question anybody asks at the other end is whether the cargo arrived. Everything else is something you carry on your own time.

Your response: So what do I get for arriving?

NPC: What you wanted all along: Wheels of your own. There is a Quad coming to you - the paperwork came through, so this is all legit, which is more than most people can say about their first vehicle. Keep training that Vehicle Use, and do the maintenance yourself: a driver who lets somebody else look under the panel is a driver who finds out about the fault at speed. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

 180      ANSWER("Noted. So I get the stamp?", 54)
 181  
 182  NODE(54)

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• Tam Oduya, Sector 1. He builds and rebuilds every drone that flies out of this Base and he has views about who gets one. I have already had the argument with him on your behalf and I won it, which took most of an afternoon. Go and let him finish the job.

• The part I am not qualified to teach and he is. Sector 1. Listen to him properly, and do not touch anything on his bench.

• Oduya is in Sector 1. Go.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Half the Base thinks your specialty is cowardice with a license. I don't, but I am going to make you prove it twice, because the other half of the Base has to carry you if you're wrong. Interested?

Your response: I'm interested. Prove it how?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Military Storage 6. Long straight bays, clean sightlines, and enough vermin in it that my crews will not go down. Four of them. This is the easy room, recruit, and I want you to notice that while you are in it, because you will not get another one.

Your response: Only four?

NPC: Only four. Before you wonder if that is an insult: It sort of is. But it is not a day's work, it is the number I can afford to watch you be bad at. You have had that thing a fortnight. You will lose it in a doorway, you will fly it into a wall all the time, and you will spend a good while finding out that your drone does not work like your head. Four is enough to learn all of that and cheap enough that nobody pays for it. Find your corner, keep your body somewhere a runner would not think to look, and take four. Storage 6. Go.

NPC: Four, and the crews went down after you. It took you a while, and it was supposed to. Where did you leave your body while you were flying?

Your response: Behind a corner at the entrance, out of the lane, with the door in view.

NPC: Storage 6 is still crawling and it is the easy room. Go.

NPC: With the door in view. Good, that is the answer I wanted and I get it about one time in four. Most of them park themselves somewhere comfortable, with absolutely no backup plan whatsoever. Rest up. Tomorrow I take the sightlines away.

NPC: Ready for the room that does not cooperate?

Your response: Quite a lead-in. Where is it?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Sure. Bad ground stays bad.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3, where the recovery sled drops whatever it drags in off the road. Stacked scrap, no straight lines, no lane longer than a few strides. Very much interested in where you're gonna park yourself in this one. Three of them.

Your response: Fewer even than the storage bay? Come on!

NPC: Fewer, and it will take you longer. That is the entire lesson and you have just said it out loud without noticing. Everything in there is half blind, including you, which is the only advantage you get. I do not care how long it takes. I care that you come out of it with the same number of drones you went in with, and with your own skin unpunctured. Storage 3. Go.

NPC: You did it. So tell me, what did you do differently?

Your response: Moved my body three times. Every time the drone got more than about thirty strides out I lost the room, so I stopped treating my own position as the safe one and started treating it as the slow one.

NPC: The wreck yard in Storage 3 is still full and you are still up here. Go.

NPC: The slow one. Say that to Oduya when you meet him and he will probably shake your hand. No, actually, he won't. That is something he does not do. That is the whole discipline, recruit: the drone is the fast part of you and your body is the slow part, and the slow part is the one that dies. Now, the part you already know: you are still clumsy with the thing. There is no trick to it, it only comes with hours, and nothing else. Come back when you are rested. You have earned some iron of your own.

NPC: Ready to collect something that is actually yours?

Your response: I'm ready. From who?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. He closes the bench when he feels like it.

NPC: Tam Oduya, Sector 1. He builds and rebuilds every drone that flies out of this Base and he has views about who gets one. I have already had the argument with him on your behalf and I won it, which took most of an afternoon. Go and let him finish the job.

Your response: What is left to finish?

NPC: The part I am not qualified to teach and he is. Sector 1. Listen to him properly, and do not touch anything on his bench.

NPC: Do not touch that. Or that. You are the one from the wreck yard. Three, in bad ground, no losses. Slowly, I hear, which is the right way round to be bad at it.

Your response: Mrs. Jones says you have something for me.

NPC: She says a lot of things, and about half of them cost me a week. Before I hand you anything: what killed the last four droners out of this Base? Guess.

Your response: Something shot the drone.

Your response: Something walked up to their body.

NPC: No. Nothing shot the drone in any of the four. A drone is a spare part, you build another one every half hour. Something walked up to their body while they were three rooms away being brave through a camera. Even in the nine seconds in which they died, they never noticed.

Your response: All four the same way?

NPC: All four. Nine seconds each, roughly. Nothing so much as scratched the drones - a drone is a spare part. Something walked up to the meatsack, and that was the end of it.

Your response: I get it. The drone is never the thing at risk.

NPC: Exactly, the drone is never the thing at risk. You are. Every hour you fly, you have to stay in the room with your own body, and the day somebody finds you kneeling behind a crate with your eyes closed is your last. Now. Return to Jones. You will be pleased.

Your response: What about the thing you were supposed to give me?

NPC: ZG 21. I built her myself, she pulls very slightly left and I am not fixing it because it will teach you to compensate. Jones has it. Go and tell Jones I said you can have her, which is not the same as saying I agree with her.

NPC: Slightly left. Compensate. Off you go.

NPC: He wanted you to have it, then. And he told you about the four.

Your response: Nine seconds each. Nothing ever touched the drones - something walked up to the body while they were three rooms away being brave through a camera. That's how he told the story.

NPC: Oduya is in Sector 1. Go.

NPC: Yes, and they were experienced. Every one of them was better at flying than you are today. That is not me being unkind, I'm not aiming to demoralize you. It's me telling you the danger does not scale down as you get good. It scales up, because the better you fly the further out you push and the longer you leave yourself alone.

Your response: Then how do the good ones survive?

NPC: They are boring about it. They pick the corner before the fight, they move when the fight moves, and they come back to their own eyes every so often for no reason at all. That's neither being brave nor clever. Boring, that's what it is. But they do go on. Others don't.

Your response: I can be boring.

NPC: Everybody says that on day one. The drone is the fast part of you and your body is the slow part, and the slow part is the one that dies: put that above your bench and read it every time you launch. Keep training that Remote Control, keep a hand free, and never once let the room you are actually in go quiet on you. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• By looking, properly, at something you would normally walk past. Mara Ivec runs the motor pool out of Sector 1, by the vehicle dealer. Ask her to show you the oldest temporary repair job she knows of in this Base. Do not argue with what she shows you. Just stand there and look at it.

• That is the first half. The second half is what you decide to do about it, and you are not ready for that until you have done the first. Sector 1, by the dealer. Go.

• Ivec is in Sector 1 by the vehicle dealer. She has all day, you don't. Go.

• A run that nobody has been able to find on a schematic since before either of us arrived here. When it let go it took the lights, the fans and the door seals on that level with it. We've been on emergency power in that sector ever since. I want to know what it was actually built out of, and I do not trust a word of the paperwork.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Your file says construction and repair. Good. Half this Base is held together by people who could do neither, and it has been standing for decades regardless. I would like to know whether that impresses you or worries you. Interested in finding out which it ought to be?

Your response: I'm interested. Where do I start?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: By looking, properly, at something you would normally walk past. Mara Ivec runs the motor pool out of Sector 1, by the vehicle dealer. Ask her to show you the oldest temporary repair job she knows of in this Base. Do not argue with what she shows you. Just stand there and look at it.

Your response: Looking at a repair job. That is my whole task?

NPC: That is the first half. The second half is what you decide to do about it, and you are not ready for that until you have done the first. Sector 1, by the dealer. Go.

NPC: So Ivec has shown you the brace, then. What did you see?

Your response: A brace welded out of scrap pipe. Nineteen years old. Somebody wrote TEMPORARY on it in marker, and the marker has faded worse than the weld.

NPC: Ivec is in Sector 1 by the vehicle dealer. She has all day, you don't. Go.

NPC: Nineteen years, and it holds. Reassurance? Hardly. A bodge that holds stops being a bodge and quietly becomes structure, and then people build on top of it without ever knowing what is underneath. This Base is a stack of exactly that. Keep it in your head, because I am about to show you what it looks like when one of them finally lets go.

NPC: A power run under the HQ went dark two nights ago. Ready to go and find out why?

Your response: What went dark, exactly?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Do not be long. Dark rooms fill up.

NPC: A run that nobody has been able to find on a schematic since before either of us arrived here. When it let go it took the lights, the fans and the door seals on that level with it. We've been on emergency power in that sector ever since. I want to know what it was actually built out of, and I do not trust a word of the paperwork.

Your response: Then I go and look at the run itself.

NPC: You do. That run crosses the whole CityMercs HQ, and its junction boxes go with it - squat metal access boxes, set low against the walls, one every fifty strides or so. Open them, and where you find a splice, cut the spliced section out and bring it to me. Four will be enough to make somebody explain themselves. Take a lamp and expect to walk.

NPC: Tell me what I am looking at.

Your response: Splices. Four of them, none of it logged, and the last one was carrying about twice what it was rated for.

NPC: The junction boxes are still shut. They run right across the CityMercs HQ. Go.

NPC: Four splices and no paperwork anywhere. That is not an oversight. Somebody made a decision, and then chose not to write it down, four times, and got away with it four times. I want the name on it. Come back when you are ready to go and take it off them.

NPC: Ready to go and ask somebody an awkward question?

Your response: I'm ready. Who am I asking?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not take long. Awkward questions get less useful the longer they sit.

NPC: The quartermaster's engineer at the CityMercs HQ, Kettel. Every repair certificate on that run carries his mark, including the ones for work that was never done. I have known the man nine years and I would have sworn he was the last honest signature left in the requisition chain.

Your response: And if he isn't?

NPC: Then I will have been wrong about somebody for the second time this month. Go and find out which it is. Do not go in swinging: I want the truth considerably more than I want to be right.

NPC: You're not here for a vehicle by the look of you. What does Jones want this time?

Your response: She wants me to see the oldest temporary repair in this Base.

NPC: Of course she does. Look up, then. That brace, up under the walkway. Scrap pipe, welded by hand, and somebody wrote TEMPORARY on it in marker. That was nineteen years ago. The marker has mostly faded, the weld hasn't.

Your response: Why has nobody replaced it?

NPC: Because it holds. Nobody replaces what holds. And now there is a walkway above it, a cable run through it and about two tons of ducting sitting on top, all put there by people who never once looked underneath. What started as a shoddy repair job has effectively become the building.

Your response: I'm guessing Jones is going to want that word for word?

NPC: Eh, she has heard it before. She sends me one of you every other week or so, and I say the same thing every time. Off you go now.

NPC: Mind the bracket on your way out.

NPC: If this is about the sublevel run, I have filed the report and I stand behind every line of it-

Your response: You certified four splices on that run. None of them logged, and the last one was carrying double its rating.

NPC: Ah. Well, yes. Yes, I did. All four of them.

Your response: So why? Why did you build in substandard parts, not fit for the task?

NPC: Because there are no other parts. There have been no parts for months, now. I can requisition a cable run and be told nine weeks, or I can take the redundancy feed off a bay nobody uses, splice it into the primary, and sign a certificate saying the work was done properly. Only one of those keeps the lights on. Nobody has ever thanked me for it. Nobody has ever asked, either.

Your response: So you spent the redundancy to keep the primary running.

NPC: I spent all of it. Every system on this level has one way of working now where it used to have two, and every certificate says otherwise, and I have not slept properly since spring. Whenever I tried to sound the alarm about this, it got buried. So write it down. Give it to Jones. I would rather be finished than keep carrying this by myself.

Your response: I'll tell her exactly that.

NPC: Thank you. Genuinely. Now go, before I say some of the other things I have been holding in.

NPC: It is out of my hands now. That is the best I have felt in months.

NPC: So you got a full disclosure out of Kettel. Nine years and that man has never filed anything late in his life. What did you say to him?

Your response: Almost nothing. He wanted to be asked. He has been holding this level together on his own and signing his name to the lie that let him do it.

NPC: Kettel is at the CityMercs HQ and the question is not going to ask itself. Go.

NPC: On his own. That is the part I am taking to the Base commander, and I am taking it loudly. One man's failure of character is not the issue here. We're dealing with a broken supply chain that everybody upstairs has quietly agreed not to look at.

Your response: So what happens to Kettel?

NPC: He keeps the job and loses the certificates, and every splice he ever made gets found and redone by people with the parts to do it properly. I will make sure of that.

Your response: And the part I was actually supposed to learn?

NPC: I would've thought that it would be obvious by now. A fix that holds becomes structure, and structure nobody logged becomes a trap for whoever comes after you. So log it. Every time, even when it is scrap pipe and marker pen and you are ashamed of it. Especially then. Anyway, good work. There is a construction tool coming your way and it is a good one, so keep training that Construction and build things the next poor idiot can actually understand. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have a problem and no time to be gentle about it. Three of my people came up out of the storage sublevel this morning bleeding, and the aid post could not treat them, because the aid post has nothing in it. Your file says you can patch a runner up. Right now I need somebody who can find me something to patch them with.

Your response: Tell me where to look.

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: The emergency caches. They are scattered all around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and the corridors around it - the room with the Medicare recreation units and the Paramedic in it. By regulation every one of those caches holds sealed dressings against exactly this. Nobody has opened one in a year.

Your response: How many do you need?

NPC: Six would let the aid post work today. Yeah. Bring me six sealed dressings out of those caches and do not be gentle with the lids. And find the old medic who works out of that medbay while you are there - his name is Ferreira and you will need him tomorrow. CityMercs HQ. Go.

NPC: Very good. The aid post is working and all three of my people are still breathing. Now tell me the part you are chewing on, because you came in here with a face.

Your response: I opened all twelve caches to get six. Half of them were empty, and every one of the empty ones had a restock seal on it dated last month.

NPC: The caches are in and around the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, and I need the contents of six of them. Go.

NPC: Mmh. Sealed last month and empty this month. Somebody signed for stock that never went in, and my people bled on a corridor floor this morning to prove it. That is a thread I'm gonna pull on. But not with you, not yet: you are a medic who has never been taught the one thing that actually keeps casualties alive, and I am not sending you out until you have been. Come back when you are rested. I am sending you to the man who taught me.

NPC: Ready to be taught something by somebody with far more right to teach it than me?

Your response: Ready. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. He is not going anywhere and neither is the lesson.

NPC: Doc Ferreira. You may have already met him. He runs the medbay at the CityMercs HQ, the one you emptied the caches out of this morning. He was a field medic for eighteen years before his knees retired him and he has forgotten more about triage than this Base collectively knows. He will not be kind about it. He has earned that.

Your response: I'll go and get told.

NPC: Yeah. Good. Listen to all of it, even when he repeats himself. Especially then. Same medbay as before. Go.

NPC: Well? What did the old man leave you with?

Your response: The order, and the rest of my answer. Those caches are his to stock. He has been signing for medical stock he never receives - eleven months of it, written off as expended.

NPC: Ferreira is in the medbay at the CityMercs HQ and he is expecting you. Go.

NPC: Expended. That word does a great deal of quiet work around here. Six dressings out of twelve caches, and the reason is sitting in a requisition ledger with somebody's initials on it. Get some rest. Then we are going to go and get to the bottom of this.

NPC: There you are. Ready to go and be very polite to somebody who is about to have a really bad afternoon?

Your response: I'm ready. Who signs the ledger?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. Ledgers get tidied.

NPC: Corporal Vane, Supply Depot, Sector 1. Every one of those write-offs went through his desk. I will say this before you go and I will not say it again afterwards: Vane is not a thief. He is a man who does what the paper in front of him says, and somebody has figured that out about him.

Your response: So I am not there to accuse him.

NPC: You are there to make him look at what he has been signing. That is worse than an accusation and considerably more useful. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go.

NPC: You are the one who emptied every cache in my medbay. Get comfortable. No, I'm not treating you, I'm talking at you, which will be a lot more painful for you. What I'm teaching you is not a technique. Two men down in front of you. One is screaming and one is not saying anything at all. Which one do you go to?

Your response: The one screaming. He is clearly in agony.

Your response: The quiet one.

NPC: You do, don't you? Your feet will take you to the noise. Everybody's do. But he is screaming because he has air in his lungs and blood in his brain to be frightened with: that is a man with time.

Your response: And the quiet one doesn't.

NPC: Exactly. The quiet one has nothing, especially not time, and quiet is not patience, it is a countdown. The whole job is learning to walk past the screaming.

Your response: How do you learn that?

NPC: Badly, and only once. Some day you will walk past somebody begging you for help and go to the man who cannot ask, and you will be right, and it will feel exactly like being a monster. Do it anyway. Now, while you are there: you emptied twelve caches this morning to find six dressings. Do me a favor and look at this.

Your response: What am I looking at?

NPC: My stock book. Eleven months of deliveries I signed for and never saw. Every line closed out as expended before it reached me. I have raised it four times and been thanked four times. If your Mrs. Jones has any teeth left, tell her about it, because I have run out.

Your response: I'll tell her tonight.

NPC: Good. Now get out of my medbay and go and be monstrous at somebody screaming.

NPC: Go on. The quiet one. Every time.

NPC: You are the one Jones sent for dressings. Good luck to you.

Your response: She said there were caches around here.

NPC: There are. Take a look around, you'll spot them easy enough. Nobody has opened one since before I got here.

Your response: So they're all full?

NPC: I didn't say that. I said that nobody has opened them since before I got here. Just walk the whole quarter and open every medical box you find. And do not be disappointed: about half of them have nothing in them at all, and that is a conversation you and I are going to have later.

NPC: What is it? If it is not on a requisition I cannot help you, and if it is on a requisition it is probably nine weeks out.

Your response: It is about medical stock. Eleven months of it, closed out as expended before it ever reached the medics.

NPC: That is- those are all properly signed. I do them myself. Expended is what you write when a consignment is used before it is booked in, it is standard, it happens every-

Your response: Eleven months, Corporal. Every consignment. Read your own ledger back to yourself.

NPC: ...That is not possible. That would be every single one. I would have- I have been signing what came down on the sheet. The sheet comes from the quartermaster's office, it arrives already filled in, I check the totals against the manifest and the totals always match-

Your response: Because whoever fills in the sheet also writes the manifest.

NPC: Yes. Yes, they do. Oh, that is- I have been the signature on this. Not the hand. The signature. Somebody has figured out that I check totals and never check the paper the totals came on, and they have been using me as the honest part of it ever since.

Your response: Then be the honest part properly. Give it to Jones, all eleven months.

NPC: All of it. Every sheet, every manifest, and the names on the covering slips. Tell her I want to be in the room when it is read. I would like to be useful for once. Apparently, I haven't been.

NPC: It is all in her hands now. Go on, I have a lot of reading to do.

NPC: Vane sent me eleven months of paper himself and asked to be in the room when it is read. I have never seen him volunteer for anything. What did you do to him?

Your response: Made him read his own ledger out loud. He was not stealing anything. He was being used because he checks totals and never checks the paper they came on.

NPC: Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1 and that ledger is not going to read itself. Go.

NPC: Yeah. Used. That word does some heavy lifting around here. But anyway, the provosts have the covering slips and the names on them, and the medics get their stock back this week, which is the only part that saves anybody.

Your response: Ferreira raised this four times.

NPC: Four times, and was thanked four times, and nothing moved until somebody who had just carried a bunch of gauze up the stairs said it in front of me. That is not a compliment to you, recruit. It is a fairly ugly thing to know about how this place works, and you should always keep that in mind.

Your response: So what do I take away from all this?

NPC: Two things, and they are the same thing. Go to the quiet one, and read the paper the totals came on. A sealed cache nobody opens is the quiet casualty of a supply chain, and it stayed quiet for a year because everybody trusted a sheet that arrived already filled in. There is a healing module coming your way for the work, so keep training that PSI Use and stay the person who walks past the screaming. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have a month of door logs for the armory level and there is nothing wrong with them. No failed entries. No mistyped codes. Not one drunk corporal leaning on a panel at four in the morning. A month of perfect human beings. Does that sound like this Base to you?

Your response: It sounds like somebody tidied up.

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: That was quick. Good. I cannot take this to anybody upstairs on a feeling, so I want it read properly by somebody who does this for a living. Sector 1, the Supply Depot. Ask for Sable. She used to do rather more interesting work than selling software and she still knows what a scrubbed log looks like from across the room.

Your response: And if she says I'm imagining it?

NPC: Then I am wrong and we both get an early night. That would be a nice change. Sector 1, the Supply Depot. Take the log to her and listen to the whole answer, not just the part you already agree with. Go.

NPC: Well? Am I paranoid or am I right?

Your response: You are right, but not the way you thought. Nothing was deleted. The failures were never written. Somebody is telling the door to open directly instead of authorizing at the panel, so the panel has nothing to fail.

NPC: Sable is somewhere around the Supply Depot in Sector 1 and that log is not getting any younger. Go.

NPC: Never written. That is worse, and it is also a lot harder to do. You do not fake a clean month, recruit, you build a way of walking through a door that no system ever has to think about. Somebody in this Base has forsaken keys altogether. Get some sleep. Tomorrow we go and find the one log they could not reach.

NPC: Ready to go and read something extremely boring very carefully?

Your response: Which log could they not reach?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. Boring things keep.

NPC: The gate. Every door in this Base is a system, and systems can be taught to look the other way. The gate is a man with a clipboard called Pell, and clipboards are stupid in a way that is very hard to corrupt. If somebody is walking through doors unseen by the system, they are still walking past Pell to do it.

Your response: So I put the two lists side by side.

NPC: You do, and you do it with him, because he has been at that gate for years and years, and he remembers faces the way you remember syntax. Military Entrance. Find me the name that is in one list and not the other.

NPC: Give me the name.

Your response: Karn. Nineteen entries at the armory doors this month and not one crossing at the gate. Pell knows the face. She signs in every morning as a contractor with somebody else's chip - a Merc who died in the wastes in spring and was never taken off active.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance with eleven years of clipboards. Go and read them with him.

NPC: A dead man's credentials. We bury people out here, and their chips keep walking around, because deactivation is somebody's third priority on a bad week. She is not breaking our security, recruit. She is using it exactly as designed. That is the part that should keep you awake. Come back when you are ready to finish up.

NPC: Karn signed in this morning and has not signed out. In?

Your response: I'm in. Where is she?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not take long. She does not stay in one place for a whole afternoon.

NPC: Sitting out the afternoon in the Black Ribbon Bar at the CityMercs HQ, because she does not move until the evening shift change and the man on the evening gate does not look up. She is carrying whatever she took off the armory level this month, and that chip. I want both back. Preferably intact.

Your response: And if she will not hand it over?

NPC: Then drop her where she stands, and let the guys from reclamation do their jobs. She is not a soldier, she is a woman who has spent a lot of time being invisible, and invisible people fight badly when somebody finally looks straight at them. CityMercs HQ, the Black Ribbon Bar. Go.

NPC: What do you want? Software is on the rack, licenses are on the board, and no, I do not do custom work any more.

Your response: Mrs. Jones sent me. She wants you to read a door log.

NPC: Of course she did. Give it here. A month of the armory level, and- huh. Well, that is clean.

Your response: Too clean. Somebody scrubbed it.

NPC: No. That is what you are supposed to think, and it is what I thought for a few seconds. A scrub leaves a shape: gaps, reindexed sequence numbers, timestamps that step wrong. This has none of that. The sequence is perfect. These failures were not deleted, they were never generated.

Your response: Then the panel never rejected anybody all month.

NPC: The panel was never asked. Somebody is authorizing upstream of it. Ancient trick, and it needs real access to set up: you bypass the control system altogether and just tell the door to open. So the panel has nothing to fail and nothing to log. To the system, nobody was ever there.

Your response: So how do you catch somebody the system cannot see?

NPC: You stop asking the system. Everything digital in this Base can be told what to remember. Go and find someone who remembers with their brain and writes with a pen. Tell Jones that, and tell her I said she still owes me for the last time she was right.

NPC: Go on. Someone with a pen.

NPC: Whatever it is, it will be in the book. Everything is in the book. That's the only reason anybody talks to me.

Your response: That is exactly why I am here. I need your crossings against a month of armory door entries.

NPC: Now that is a proper question. Get comfortable, this may take a while and I am not letting you touch the book. Read me your names, I will tell you who came through my gate.

Your response: Start with the ones that repeat. Karn. Nineteen entries at the armory doors this month.

NPC: Karn. Karn... no. Not once. Not one crossing in the book all month, and I would remember, because I know her face. Comes in most mornings. Contractor, ducting work, signs the day sheet, very polite. Never once in my crossings book because contractors sign the sheet, not the book.

Your response: Whose chip does she sign with?

NPC: Let's find out - here. Hollis. That is Hollis's number. Hollis has been dead since spring, went out on a wastes patrol and did not come back. Nobody deactivates a dead soldier's chip. It's on a form, and the form is on a desk, and the desk is weeks behind, like everything else in this Base.

Your response: Then Karn has been walking around with the ID of a dead Merc all that time.

NPC: And my book says she was never here at all. Take that to Jones and tell her the book is still right. It is the only thing around here that is.

NPC: Nineteen times. And not one crossing. Go on, tell her.

NPC: Afternoon. Waiting on the shift change like everybody else. You want the bar, it is behind me.

Your response: Hollis died in spring, Karn. You have been walking around the place on his chip, teaching the security systems to look the other way.

NPC: ...Ah. You are the reason the panel logs got pulled. I did wonder who they would send and I will be honest, I expected somebody with more rank and less curiosity.

Your response: Nineteen entries this month. What have you been taking out?

NPC: Nothing they were using. Not defending myself, it's just true. This Base writes off more hardware in a month than most clans own, including mine. None of it is missed, because nobody counts what is already dead on paper. I didn't break anything to do this. I read your paperwork properly, which is more than anyone here has managed in years.

Your response: You're done. Hand over whatever you took this time, and the chip.

NPC: No, I do not think I will. Do you know what happens to a woman who gets caught being invisible? She stops being anything at all.

NPC: ...

NPC: The Black Ribbon is asking why there is a body in their bar and no name in the book to go with it. What about the chip?

Your response: Intact, I checked. She did not think much of our security. She was mostly complimenting our paperwork.

NPC: Karn is in the Black Ribbon Bar at the CityMercs HQ until the shift change, and after that she is gone. Go.

NPC: She was right to. Hollis's chip should have been dead the week Hollis was. Instead it has been walking through our armory for months because deactivation is a low priority for people already overworked. That is what makes me tired.

Your response: So the system was never actually broken.

NPC: Not broken, bypassed in some places, outwitted in others. And that is the whole lesson, so take it properly: a system does not have to be broken to be wrong. It only has to be obeyed by somebody who understood it better than the people who built it. You will spend your career being that person. Try to spend it on our side of the door.

Your response: What happens to the dead chips?

NPC: They get deactivated this week, all of them, because I am about to make that somebody's first priority instead of their third. There is a hacktool coming your way and a piece of software Sable insisted on throwing in, so keep training that Hacking and remember what you learned at a gate with a paper book on it: when everything digital agrees, go and find the thing that writes with a pen. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

Go to Corporal Vane at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Find out what it is that he watches.

• A supply clerk who can tell you the weight of a crate by the sound it makes on the ramp and could not tell you the color of the door it came through. That is the most useful conversation you will have for some time. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go and listen.
