entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Everybody in your line of work who comes to me asks the same question first, which is how to not be seen. But that's the wrong question and it would get you killed soon. Would you like to know the right one?

Your response: Go on. What is the right question?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Who is looking, and at what. Nobody watches everything, recruit. People watch the thing they are responsible for and they are magnificently blind to everything else, and if you know which is which, you can walk through the middle of a room with nobody noticing you. Go to Corporal Vane at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Find out what it is that he watches.

Your response: A supply clerk? Really?

NPC: A supply clerk who can tell you the weight of a crate by the sound it makes on the ramp and could not tell you the color of the door it came through. That is the most useful conversation you will have for some time. Sector 1, Supply Depot. Go and listen.

NPC: What does Corporal Vane watch?

Your response: Numbers. He knows every crate in his depot by weight and count, but he couldn't describe one person who carried one in. He has been robbed twice this year by people he looked directly at.

NPC: Vane is at the Supply Depot in Sector 1. Go and ask him what he actually looks at.

NPC: Twice that he knows of. It's actually been five times, and he still could not pick any of them out of a line. Now do that for every post in this Base: the gate watches faces, the armory watches badges, the medics watch bodies. Learn the shape of what each of them is not looking at, do your best to become that shape, and people will simply look past you. You will just be standing in the part of the room nobody is responsible for.

NPC: Theory is over. Time for practice. Ready for the part where it is dark and something is already in there?

Your response: Ready. Where am I going?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. The dark is patient. That is rather the point of it.

NPC: The wreck yard in Military Storage 3, where the recovery sled drops what it drags in. No clean lines, no lit corridors, nothing that behaves like a room. I want you in and out of there. There are things living in there and they do not care how quiet you are, which is exactly the lesson.

Your response: So this is not a stealth exercise.

NPC: It is the other half of one. Sooner or later something sees you, and everything you know about not being seen becomes worthless in the same second. Put down eight of them and come back out. I want to know what you are like after it goes wrong.

NPC: So you're back, and in one piece I might add. How far did you get before something noticed you?

Your response: About a third. After that it was just work. I stopped trying to be quiet and started trying to be finished.

NPC: You're still here. The wreck yard in Storage 3. Go.

NPC: Good. That is how you do it. Most recruits try to do it another way, where they get all the way through untouched. Those recruits are either lying or extremely lucky, and both of those would eventually run out. Next thing to do will be both halves, all in one afternoon. Come back when you have your wind.

NPC: There is a man in this Base selling the result of what I have been trying to teach you. In?

Your response: I'm in. Who is he?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not be long. He is careful, and careful men get restless.

NPC: Ivo Mattis, CityMercs HQ. He has spent quite some time mapping what every post in this Base fails to look at, and for the last few weeks he has been selling that information to whoever is buying. Not our layout, or our codes, but our blind spots. Somebody walked into the armory level last week on the strength of it.

Your response: Sounds like he is very good at the job you are teaching me.

NPC: He is the best I ever taught. Yes, it was me who taught him. And yes, I am aware of what that makes today. He will know you are there before you are close, so do not waste your afternoon trying to be invisible at a man who knows every trick in the book. Walk up to him. CityMercs HQ. Finish it.

NPC: Depot's closed for intake until further notice. If it's not a requisition, it can wait.

Your response: It's not a requisition. What do you actually watch, Corporal?

NPC: What do I w- the stock. I watch the stock. Weight, count, seal numbers. I can tell you what is in a crate from the noise it makes coming down the ramp and I can tell you if a pallet is two units light from across the bay.

Your response: And the people carrying it?

NPC: What about them? They are hands. I do not- all right, I can see where this is going, and Jones has made this point at me before. No, I could not pick out even one man who has carried a crate through that door this year. Yes, I have been robbed twice, and both times I stood there and watched it happen and gave the provosts nothing worth writing down.

Your response: Because you were looking at the crate.

NPC: Because I was counting the crate. That's my job. Nobody has ever once asked me to look at a face, and if I started, I would miss a short pallet in no time, and somebody in the wastes would run out of ammunition because of it. So no, I do not watch people. I watch numbers, and I'm very good at it.

Your response: That is exactly what she wanted me to hear.

NPC: Then tell her she has made her point and she can stop sending people to make it. Go on, intake is in ten minutes.

NPC: Numbers. Every time. Now let me count.

NPC: You have been in the doorway for about five seconds. Come in properly, she taught you better than that. How do I know that? She taught me as well, and now she has taught you, and here we are.

Your response: You have been selling the Base's blind spots.

NPC: I have been selling a lot of work that nobody here would pay me for. I brought her the first survey right at the beginning. Do you know what it got me? Filed. Filed, and a note about my initiative. Every post in this Base is blind in an almost ridiculous way. I can draw that on a page. In fact, I did. But nobody upstairs wanted that page.

Your response: So you sold it to people who came in through the armory last week.

NPC: What I sold is basically a map. What anybody does with it is not my department. And before you say the word: I did not tell them about Hollis, or the sublevel, or any of the other holes this place opens on its own every other week. I only ever wrote down what was already true.

Your response: Two Mercs died on the armory level standing in a spot you drew a circle around.

NPC: Yes. They did. I know both names. I have known them every day since. They hound me every night. And do you know what I do? I keep selling.

NPC: ...

NPC: It is done, then. Did he talk?

Your response: He said he brought you the first survey right at the beginning and it got filed. He knew the names of the two who died in that robbery, and he kept selling anyway.

NPC: Mattis is at the CityMercs HQ and he does not sit still forever. Go.

NPC: He did bring me that survey. I read it, I agreed with every line, and I passed it up. It came back stamped and went in a drawer. And I let it stay in the drawer because I had eleven other things to do. So he is not lying and I do not get to pretend that he is.

Your response: That is not the same as what he did with it.

NPC: No, it's not, and I do not need comforting, thank you very much. He made the choice. I made the filing. Both of those are real, only one of them is a crime, and I have to live in a Base where the second one happens every week.

Your response: So what am I supposed to do differently?

NPC: Know who is looking and at what: that is the craft, and it is yours now. But when you bring somebody the page and they file it, do not go quiet and do not go and sell it. Come back and put it on the desk again, and keep doing that until somebody finally pays attention or throws you out. There is a stealth tool coming your way, so keep training that Pistol Combat and stay somewhere you can stand being invisible. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: The storage sublevel is crawling and the crews will not go down there. Ten of them, Military Storage 6, whatever is moving. There is no principle in it, no judgment to make, nobody to be right at. Just a dark room, and a job.

Your response: And this tells you what exactly about me?

NPC: Whether you can do the part with no audience. People who want to enforce a standard are usually in love with the part where everybody is looking. I have been at the burials of a few of those. Storage 6. Go.

NPC: The bay is quiet, and you did not come back up here to tell me how it was going. Noted. Now relax, because the next one is the reason I sent for you at all.

Your response: Go on.

NPC: Storage 6 is still crawling. There is no audience down there and the work is still the work. Go.

NPC: Article Nine of the Merc contract. A man who abandons wounded under his command forfeits everything, including the presumption that anybody will come for him. It is the oldest line we have and it is the only one this Base has never argued about. I have a signed accusation under it on my desk. Come back when you are ready, and we will talk about what that costs.

NPC: Are you ready?

Your response: Tell me about the accusation.

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. Take two.

NPC: Sergeant Dain Vos. Wastes patrol, three weeks ago, contact at the ridge. Two of his people went down alive. He stripped their ammunition and their medkits and he walked, and he has been drinking in Sector 1 ever since, telling anybody who asks that they were already gone. Yeah, they were not. One of them lasted six hours.

Your response: Who signed the accusation?

NPC: A quartermaster's man who was on the ridge with them. It is witnessed, it is filed, and the provosts have already found the ammunition in Vos's locker with two other people's marks on it. Article Nine does not go to a court, recruit. It goes to whoever the Base sends. Today that is you. Sector 1, the bar next to the Gene Replicator. He will know why you are there.

NPC: It's done. Did he give you anything before the end?

Your response: He did not argue about the ridge. He wanted to know who signed the paper, and said that if it was who he thought, I should look at that man's crate manifests for spring.

NPC: Vos is in the bar next to the Gene Replicator in Sector 1 and Article Nine does not expire. Go.

NPC: ...Come again? Because I have just pulled those manifests, and there are four months of them signed by our witness, and every one has a hole in it about the size of what a man could carry out of an armory. Vos was guilty. But he knew about those holes. He is still guilty. And the mouth that told us so was buying itself an afternoon where nobody was looking. NPC: Well? Have you decided how you feel?

Your response: I did the right thing for a reason that was somebody else's. That is not the same as being used, but it is close enough to anger me.

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Take it. I have been sitting with the same question since last night.

NPC: Close enough is right. Here is what I want done with it, and it is not another execution. Chaplain Reyn took that accusation and passed it to me. He vouched for the witness personally. He has known the man for years, and he did not test one word of it, because he did not think he had to.

Your response: You want me to put that to a chaplain.

NPC: I want you to make him look at it, because he is the man this Base takes its conscience from and he handed me a true thing from a rotten mouth without checking which was which. Sector 1. He is expecting somebody. He is not expecting it to be the one who carried out the sentence.

NPC: I know why you're here. You have the walk. Three weeks I have been in this bar every day, waiting for somebody with that walk.

Your response: The ridge. Two of your people were alive when you left them.

NPC: ...Yes. They were. I'm not gonna even try to tell you that they weren't. You have the report and I've had weeks to get tired of lying about it to myself and everyone else. Kell lasted six hours. I have thought about that every night since.

Your response: Then you know how this ends.

NPC: ...

Your response: You vouched for the witness. Personally.

NPC: I did. Years and years I have known that man. He came to me on the ridge night with his hands shaking and I did not test a single word, because a man does not shake like that over a lie. That is what I told myself and it is what I told her.

If I will pass an untested accusation when it happens to be true, then I will pass one when it is not. The article will do exactly what it did this week, and a man will die correctly for the wrong reason. The code is not what protects us. Testing it is.

Your response: Then say that to the provosts, not to me.

NPC: I am saying it to them at first watch, with my name on it and all the facts, so nobody has to dig for them. Go and tell her. And- thank you for coming yourself. It would have been easier from anybody else, and I do not wish this to be easy.

NPC: First watch. My name at the top. Go on.

NPC: Reyn has put his name on an appointment in front of the provosts. How did he take it?

Your response: Badly, and then properly. He said the code is not what protects us. Testing it is.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

• Chaplain Reyn. Sector 1. He has buried more Mercs than you have met and he has never once told any of them that it was all for some greater good or something. So go and ask him what this Base actually believes in. Do not argue with the answer, even though you might want to.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. You have come to a mercenary base to talk to people about their souls. That is either very brave, or a filing error. I will assume brave. Before I let you say one word to my runners, you are going to sit with the man who already has that job. Interested?

Your response: Oh yes. Who is he?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Chaplain Reyn. Sector 1. He has buried more Mercs than you have met and he has never once told any of them that it was all for some greater good or something. So go and ask him what this Base actually believes in. Do not argue with the answer, even though you might want to.

Your response: Why would I want to?

NPC: Because it is not what they taught you it should be. Because you will think that this cannot possibly be it. And because you are young enough to think that is a problem. Sector 1. Sit down and listen to the whole thing. Go.

NPC: What does this Base believe in?

Your response: Each other, and nothing above that. He said faith out here is not what a runner thinks on a good day, it is who they will go back into a burning room for.

NPC: Reyn is in Sector 1 and he has all the time in the world. That is rather his condition. Go.

NPC: Oh yes. Hold on to that, because a man at my gate is currently offering my runners something much better than that, and eleven of them have taken him up on it. Get some rest. Then we are going to talk about him.

NPC: Ready to hear about the competition?

Your response: Who is at the gate?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. He preaches every evening, so we know exactly where he will be.

NPC: He calls himself Brother Ossian. For weeks, every evening, he has been telling tired runners at the Military Entrance that the wastes are cleaner than the City and that there is a place out past the ridge where nobody is anybody's contract. Unfortunately, he is a good speaker. He is a very good speaker.

Your response: And eleven went with him. Where are they?

NPC: That's the thing. Nine are dead. Two came back and will not say what happened to the others, which tells me most of it. There is no shangrila past the ridge, recruit. There is a man who needs an audience, and a wasteland that eats whoever he sends into it. He preaches at the gate tonight. Stop him.

NPC: So tell me just one thing. Did he believe any of it?

Your response: All of it. That was the worst part. He was not selling anything, he genuinely thought the nine had made it, because he never once walked out there himself.

NPC: Ossian preaches at the Military Entrance every evening. Go.

NPC: I can't say that I'm surprised. They usually do, but it never makes the dead any less dead. But here's the kicker, the part nobody warned me about the first time I did this: his congregation is still standing at that gate. Thirty-odd runners who were promised something, and tonight there is nobody there to say something to them. A silence like that gets filled, recruit. Always. Come back when you are ready.

NPC: About thirty runners are looking forward to some sermon tonight. Ready?

Your response: What do you mean? What am I supposed to say to them?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long, lest we just have to deal with the next wannabe messiah.

NPC: No. No no, calm down. Not even I would expect that of you right now. That is why you are going back to Reyn instead of to the soapbox. He knows how to deal with this situation. He will know the words.

Your response: Didn't he just lose them, when they turned to that Ossian fellow?

NPC: I didn't say that he wouldn't learn something tonight as well. Sector 1. Go and ask him what he wishes he had said instead of what he did say.

NPC: Ah. Get comfortable. Jones only sends people to me for one of two reasons, and you do not look bereaved.

Your response: She wants me to ask you what this Base actually believes in.

NPC: Yeah, that's the other one. Everybody expects a long answer and it is a short one. Each other. That's it. That is the whole creed of the City Mercs, and I have yet to find the bottom of it.

Your response: But that's not faith. That's just a working relationship.

NPC: I could imagine that this answer is not to your liking. Let me tell you what I have learned burying people out here: faith is not what a runner thinks about on a good day. It is who they will go back into a burning room for when there is no possible profit in it. I have watched men who couldn't even name a scripture or an ethical code, but who would go back into that burning room three times for their comrades. I have also buried a man who could recite the whole liturgy and left two people on a ridge.

Your response: So what is there for me to do here?

NPC: You disappoint me. Faith gives you wings, no matter if your faith is with some deity, or just with one another. These people do the most extraordinary things for each other, and nobody ever tells them so. They go out into the wastes believing they are only worth their contract rate. You do not need to bring them any enlightenment. You need to be able to sustain their trust in one another.

Your response: Jones said I would want to argue with all this.

NPC: And you did. You complained that this would not be faith. You heard me, but you haven't understood what I'm telling you, yet. You will, in about a year. Go on. And when she gets to the part about the gate - and she will - come back to me before you do anything clever.

NPC: We have each other. That is all of it. Go on.

NPC: Come closer, friend, you are just in time. I was telling good people about a place past the ridge where nobody is anybody's contract and nothing is owed.

Your response: Just in time, eh? You can say that again. Nine of the eleven you sent out there are dead.

NPC: Dead? No no! They arrived, that is the whole- the two who came back were not ready, that is all, the wastes test whether you are ready and some people are not, but the nine, the nine got through-

Your response: How do you know? Have you ever walked out there yourself?

NPC: I do not need to walk it. I have seen it. I have seen it every night for months, and it is more real to me than this Base. And if you had seen it you would not be standing there with that face on you.

Your response: You have sent nine people to die on a thing you have never once gone to look at yourself.

NPC: ...You are trying to make me small. Everyone tries to make me small. They stood there, and listened, and they were happy for the first time in years. And you want to take that away from me, and instead give them- what? A contract? A rate? You disgust me!

NPC: ...

NPC: I heard about Ossian before you got here. And thirty of them still standing there this evening with nothing to look at. You came back before you did anything clever. Good.

Your response: You have stood in front of those stares before.

NPC: And I failed every single time. The first time, I climbed straight up, and I told them the man had been a liar and they were fools for listening: I was right on both counts, and I lost every one of them. The rest was just variations on a theme. Being right at people who have just been made stupid is the fastest way to make them somebody else's.

Your response: So what will you say?

NPC: Me? Nothing. If that is the question you carried all the way here, it is the wrong one. Ossian gave them a mythical paradise some days past the ridge. You do not beat that with a reminder to trust one another. You beat it by pointing at something in this Base that is much more real than some imaginary paradise that might or might not be there. And then you get out of the way.

Your response: Point at what, then?

NPC: Do you remember what I told you the first time you came to me? Men who couldn't even name a scripture, going back into a burning room three times for their comrades. I was not being poetic. I was referring to Kettel, the man I saw perform that feat of will in Bay Nine.

Your response: Kettel? The quartermaster's engineer, down in HQ?

NPC: The very same. And in all that time not one person on this Base has asked him about it. Not one, myself included, and I have thought about it most weeks. You will be the first. Go and ask him. Then ask him to stand in front of those people tonight, and to tell them what happened, in his own flat unbearable way. Let thirty runners work out for themselves if some mythical shangrila is worth giving up their mates.

Your response: And if he says no?

NPC: Oh, he will say no. He said no to the citation, he said no to the transfer, and he will say no to you. Do not argue him out of it. He is not refusing because he is modest, but because he thinks this doesn't count. Find out why he thinks that, and then tell him the truth about it. That is the entire job.

Your response: Why would he think it does not count?

NPC: Because of who he brought out on the third trip. Ask him. That's not my story. Go on.

NPC: Ask him yourself about Bay Nine.

NPC: If this is about those spillages again, I have filed the report and I am not filing another one.

Your response: It is not. Reyn sent me. I want to ask you about Bay Nine.

NPC: ...No. No, you do not. That case is closed, and I have no use for it open. Whatever Jones is running, run it somewhere else.

Your response: Nobody has asked you. I checked. I am asking.

NPC: Because there is nothing to ask. The feed went up, the bay filled with smoke, I went in. That is not a story, that is a Tuesday with a worse outcome. People do it every week out here and nobody puts anybody on a plinth for it.

Your response: You went in three times.

NPC: Yes. Because I got it wrong twice. I came out with Ravi, and then I came out with that Odell boy, and then I stood in this corridor doing the math like an idiot and worked out that I had left Sarnow, and by then it had been four minutes, and I went back anyway.

Your response: And?

NPC: And I brought him out. And he died on the floor eleven minutes later with me pumping his chest. So you can see why I do not tell it. It is not a story about a man who saved somebody. It is a story about a man who was too slow twice and then carried a body up a stairwell so it would not be by itself.

Your response: You are wrong about which part matters.

Your response: You saved two men. That counts whether you like it or not.

NPC: Go on, then. Which part does matter?

Your response: Sarnow was not by himself. You knew he was probably already gone, the math told you to stay out. And yet, you went in for a man who could not pay you and could not thank you. That is the only thing anybody on this Base actually believes in. You have spent quite some time now filing it as just a... a failed repair.

NPC: There it is. Everybody arrives there eventually and it is always in that tone, the one that has already decided what I am permitted to think about my own night. Two men. I can count. I was there for the counting.

Your response: That was the wrong thing to say. Let me try again.

NPC: Heh. Sure. Try. I have got until the shift change.

Your response: You are wrong about which part matters.

NPC: ...

Your response: And now, thirty runners are waiting for the next sermon, because that liar, Ossian, told them there's an easy way out. That may even be the truth, but they were told by the wrong man. I would rather they got the proper truth, from you.

NPC: Eff that. I'm not a speaker. I am not a well-spoken man.

Your response: Good. Ossian said everything well. Just tell them about the four minutes.

NPC: ...Right. I will stand next to Reyn, I will talk about the four minutes, and nothing else. And if anybody claps, I'm leaving. And- listen. All that time, and you are the first one who asked. I want you to know that I appreciate it.

NPC: The four minutes. Nothing else.

NPC: Reyn tells me that an engineer who has not volunteered for anything in two years will be his speaker tonight. What did you say to him?

Your response: Nothing he didn't already know. I told him the four minutes counted, and I asked. Reyn says nobody had ever asked him.

NPC: Reyn gave you a name and the name is upstairs in the CityMercs HQ. Go and ask him. Asking is the whole of it.

NPC: Reyn is in Sector 1. Go and ask him.

NPC: You asked. That's all you had to do, and it is going to fix more than any sermon would have. Do you understand what you avoided?

Your response: Reyn told me to point at something more real, and then just get out of the way.

NPC: Then he has told you the whole job, and I don't have to pretend I am adding anything. I will say only this: I have had four preachers at this Base recently, and the three who left all left the same way. They started saying the true thing, it went well, and then they started enjoying standing on the soapbox much more than speaking the truth.

Your response: How do I know if that happens to me?

NPC: You will not, which is why you keep Reyn at the back of the room and Kettel at the front of it. When somebody hands you silence, do not fill it with yourself. Find the person in that room who has already answered it with their life, and make them heard. There are two PSI modules coming your way for this, so keep training that PSI Use, and keep somebody around who is allowed to call you an idiot. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. There is a woman in Sector 1 with a theory about why the vermin in this Base have got worse this year, and no data, because that would require her to be in two places at once: Collecting some of the data, and processing another part of it. You have her training and, according to your file, patience and an eye for detail. Interested?

• She will tell you herself. At length, if you let her. What I want from you first is the boring half. She has sample traps set all through the Supply Depot in Sector 1, the shop level downstairs, and nobody has emptied them in months. Bring me six... umm... specimina from the different traps, and pay attention while you do it: size, condition, whether the things in them have been feeding on each other. She needs samples, and she needs somebody who can describe what they saw without decorating it.

• It is, and you should say so to her face when you get there, because it is the first sensible thing anybody has said about this. The Supply Depot, Sector 1. Go and get me six specimina and an honest description.

• The Supply Depot in Sector 1, six traps, and eyes open. Go.

• Doctor Elin Varga, Sector 1. She was doing serious work in the City before she came out here and she has spent six months being told that the sublevel is somebody else's department. Take her the specimens and your description, in that order, and let her do the talking.

• Then we have a problem under this Base with a cause, which is better than a problem with a rumor. Sector 1. Go.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. There is a woman in Sector 1 with a theory about why the vermin in this Base have got worse this year, and no data, because that would require her to be in two places at once: Collecting some of the data, and processing another part of it. You have her training and, according to your file, patience and an eye for detail. Interested?

Your response: Very. What theory is she trying to prove?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: She will tell you herself. At length, if you let her. What I want from you first is the boring half. She has sample traps set all through the Supply Depot in Sector 1, the shop level downstairs, and nobody has emptied them in months. Bring me six... umm... specimina from the different traps, and pay attention while you do it: size, condition, whether the things in them have been feeding on each other. She needs samples, and she needs somebody who can describe what they saw without decorating it.

Your response: Six traps. That's a rather small sample size, isn't it?

NPC: It is, and you should say so to her face when you get there, because it is the first sensible thing anybody has said about this. The Supply Depot, Sector 1. Go and get me six specimina and an honest description.

NPC: So. Six traps emptied. What did you actually see in them?

Your response: They are bigger than the records say and they are not fighting each other over food, which means there is more of it than there should be. Something is feeding them.

NPC: The Supply Depot in Sector 1, six traps, and eyes open. Go.

NPC: Yeah. That is very close to what Varga has been saying for quite some time now, and I want you to be careful about how pleased that makes you. You will take it to her, next. And when she tells you her theory - and she will, before you have even come to a standstill - remember that you went looking for results she already fully expected.

NPC: So. Ready to go and make a certain person's entire year?

Your response: I guess so. Where do I find her?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. She has waited so long, she can wait another few minutes.

NPC: Doctor Elin Varga, Sector 1. She was doing serious work in the City before she came out here and she has spent six months being told that the sublevel is somebody else's department. Take her the specimens and your description, in that order, and let her do the talking.

Your response: And if she is right?

NPC: Then we have a problem under this Base with a cause, which is better than a problem with a rumor. Sector 1. Go.

NPC: Well? Was she right?

Your response: Her theory fits every one of the six. Then she took it apart in front of me and said one sector is not a result, it is an anecdote with six legs or something.

NPC: Varga is in Sector 1 and she has waited six months. Go.

NPC: An anecdote with six legs? Right. I like her more every time somebody quotes her at me. That is *so* her: Months of being ignored and the moment somebody hands her the answer she wanted, she is the one who refuses to take it. That is what science is all about, recruit, and most people never manage it once. She will want a second set. Come back when you are ready to go and elate or disappoint her.

NPC: Ready for the second set?

Your response: Ready. Where are they?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. The first sector is already changing while we discuss it.

NPC: The Black Ribbon Bar, far side of the CityMercs HQ. Different ground, different air, different water table, and crucially, not the sector her theory was built on. She talked the Base Commander into letting her set a second line in among the tables, and by now the regulars drink around them. Five will do. Same eyes, same honesty.

Your response: And if the second set says the opposite?

NPC: Then she was wrong for months in public, and she will be the first person to say so. The important part is that this Base will finally know what is actually happening under it. Not a bad afternoon's work. CityMercs HQ, far side, the Black Ribbon Bar. Go.

NPC: Whatever it is, I am in the middle of- are those from my traps? Those are from my traps! Put them down. Gently! Gently.

Your response: Six of them, out of the Sector 1 line. Mrs. Jones sent me.

NPC: Ugh, for so long I have been asking somebody to collect those samples for me. Every time I was told that vermin are - let me quote - shit, that the aforementioned shit happens, and that it wouldn't be science. Right. Talk to me. Not what you concluded, what you saw.

Your response: They are oversized against the records, and they were not competing over food.

NPC: Not competing? Not competing. That's it, that's exactly it! There is a nutrient load coming into that sector from somewhere and it has been coming in long enough to change the size distribution. Water table, most likely. A cracked waste run feeding it from underneath, and it fits every observation I have made since spring...

Your response: So you were right. What's the matter?

NPC: ...No. No, stop. Listen to what I just said. I had that answer in my head for months, and the first data anybody brings me fits it perfectly. This shouldn't make you feel reaffirmed, it should frighten you. One sector is not a result. It is an anecdote about the behavior of six-legged things, collected by somebody who was told what I was hoping for before they went out there.

Your response: But you didn't tell me. Jones didn't either.

NPC: Then you are a better lab assistant than I could have hoped for, and still, it is not enough. Get me a second set, from a different site with a different water table. If it agrees, I will write it up and put my name on it. Yours too, even, under acknowledgements. If it doesn't, I have been wrong loudly since spring and I will say that just as loudly. Because that is how science is supposed to work. Go on.

NPC: A second site. Different level. Go.

NPC: So. Five from the second set. Did they agree with her?

Your response: Sadly, not at all. Same overgrowth, no water anywhere near it, and the things in them had been competing over food. Whatever is happening, it is not that cracked waste run.

NPC: The second set of traps, the Black Ribbon Bar on the far side of the CityMercs HQ. Five. Same eyes. Go.

NPC: You wanna know the funny part? Varga already expected your results. She all but withdrew her paper before dinner. And she has already sent me a new list of sectors she wants sampled, and an apology addressed to the facilities officer she has been rude to for months, which I am told is unprecedented.

Your response: So that's it? She was just... wrong?

NPC: This is the whole lesson right there, recruit. Science is what you can prove. Forming a theory is not what matters. You need to be able to prove it right... or wrong, for that matter. As long as you can provide definitive proof, being wrong is just as valuable as being right. Now go and count the people in this Base who would have quietly not mentioned the second set. Most of them outrank her.

Your response: So the lesson isn't about the sublevel at all.

NPC: It never was. Anybody can collect the sample that agrees with them, and out here most people stop there and get promoted for it. Go and get the second set. Every time, especially when the first one made you happy: that is the whole of it, and it is the only thing that separates a scientist from somebody with a strong opinion. There is a research tool coming your way, and Varga insisted on sending that ridiculous toy thing as well. Said that it would amuse you. Keep training that Research. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. Everybody assumes your trade is about getting things past people. Yeah, it is not. It is about being the one person in a very long chain that nobody in the chain has a reason to cheat. I have a woman in Sector 1 who never understood that. Interested in her job?

Your response: I'm interested, alright, but what do you mean? What happened to her?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Nothing happened to her, yet. Livia Tam has moved goods for this Base for years and years, and has shorted every single crate by a little. Two units here, a case there, never enough that any one buyer would burn a working route over it. Yeah. But last month the outpost run came up short of ammunition during a contact.

Your response: So nobody caught her in years?

NPC: That is beside the point. Everybody caught her. And everybody decided it was cheaper than finding somebody new, which is exactly what she was counting on. That arithmetic ended when two of my people had to break contact and walk. So she messed up, and now she is paying the price. She is in Sector 1 and she thinks this is another conversation about percentages. Settle it.

NPC: It is done. Did she understand why, at the end?

Your response: No. She kept explaining the percentages. Right up to the last she thought the numbers were what mattered.

NPC: Livia Tam is in Sector 1, and she is not expecting anything. Go.

NPC: The numbers never matter. She was cheaper than replacing her for years and then, in one afternoon, she was not, and she never once saw the line move because she was looking at her margin instead of at the people either side of her. Rest. And then, I will show you the part of this job that actually makes you money.

NPC: Ready to learn how goods really leave this Base?

Your response: I am. So who do I talk to?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: Take it. Nothing crosses that gate before evening anyway.

NPC: A clerk called Pell at the Military Entrance, who is the guy who decides what leaves this Base. I'm not talking about smuggling. He is the guy who decides. Every crate that goes out either has paper or has a reason, and he is the man who knows which is which. Go and cozy up to him.

Your response: And he will just show me the books, will he?

NPC: He will show you. Because I asked him to, and because he is tired. Do not try to be clever at him, and do not offer him anything. Military Entrance.

NPC: What did the man at the gate teach you?

Your response: That the paperwork is not the system at all, he is. Crates went out with nothing on them but his say-so, and every one of them was going somewhere it needed to be.

NPC: Pell is at the Military Entrance and the evening shift is the one worth watching. Go.

NPC: Yep. Years of it, and not one crate that went anywhere it should not have. That is what your trade actually is, recruit: a reputation so solid that nobody bothers checking your crate in the first place. Livia Tam spent four years turning that into two units a run. Come back when you are rested. There is a route to open.

NPC: Ready to earn your first honest crate?

Your response: I'm ready. Where is it going?

Your response: Give me a moment.

NPC: Do not be long. The outpost run has already waited a week on Livia Tam's arithmetic.

NPC: Out to the outposts, through the wreck yard in Military Storage 3, because the surface road is watched and the yard connects to the lower service run. It is the route Pell has been holding open for years and at the moment nothing can use it, because the yard is crawling.

Your response: So the job is not moving the crate.

NPC: The job is never moving the crate. The job is that the route works, and everybody in the chain knows it will work next week, too. So whatever crawls there, eight of them, Storage 3, and then the run goes out. Go.

NPC: If Jones has sent you about the outpost run, the answer is the same as it was: the manifest is the manifest and shrinkage is shrinkage.

Your response: She did, but not about that. You pinched those last few rounds that would've saved lives.

NPC: Oh yeah. And who tells you that these few rounds would've made a difference, eh? You can look it up, there was never a run with above-average losses, and I defy you to find a mover anywhere between here and the City who does better than-

Your response: You have shorted every crate for years, Livia.

NPC: And every crate arrived. Every. Single. One. In years I have never lost a load, never missed a window, never once been late, and the whole Base has been perfectly happy with the arrangement because the arrangement worked. Nobody complains about a little spillage.

Your response: Actually, they stopped being happy last month. You just didn't notice.

NPC: No, wait. Look at the numbers. Look at the actual numbers, they are right here-

NPC: ...

NPC: She said you were coming. Stand there, do not touch the book, and pick up whatever I tell you to.

Your response: She said you decide what leaves or enters this Base.

NPC: The paperwork decides what leaves this Base. I decide what the paperwork means, which is a different job. See that crate? Full manifest, three signatures, going nowhere. And that one, no paper at all, goes out at seven.

Your response: Why that way round?

NPC: Because the first one is signed by a man who signed four things last spring that got people killed, and the second is medical stock for an outpost that has been out for nine days and whose requisition is somewhere in a pile in the HQ. One of them is legal. The other one is right. For years, I have been picking the second one and writing the reason in the margin.

Your response: Nobody has ever pulled you up on it?

NPC: Every year somebody new arrives who wants to. Then they read the margins. Everything I have ever waved through went where it needed to be and I can show you the line for all of it, which is the only reason I am still here and not in a cell. I know why you're here - that is what your trade is. It's not about any gap. Your margin note needs to stand up years later.

Your response: And if I ever want a crate through that will not stand up?

NPC: Then you will find I am extremely stupid that evening and cannot read my own handwriting. Now let me handle that crate, it goes out at seven. Tell Jones you were useful.

NPC: Seven o'clock. It goes out on time or it doesn't go out at all.

NPC: The run went out on time. Full count. What did the yard cost you?

Your response: Some nerves and most of my ammunition. The route is open and it will still be open next week.

NPC: The wreck yard in Storage 3 is still crawling, and the run is still sitting at the gate. Go.

NPC: It's been quite a while since a full count went off this Base. Not because of raiders or because of the wastes. Too many people decided a percent was invisible, and too many agreed with them.

Your response: And now everyone in the chain knows the route works.

NPC: Correct, and that is worth more than every crate you will ever move. You can't have a route nobody trusts. Pell has spent years being boringly, tediously reliable and it has made him the most powerful clerk in the wastes, and he could not tell you one clever thing he has ever done.

Your response: So where does the money come from?

NPC: From being the one nobody checks. That is the whole trade: be so consistently worth trusting that your crate goes through, while everybody else's is being opened. And you never ever spend that trust on something trivial. There is a barter CPU coming your way, so keep training that Barter and remember that the number is never what matters. And do yourself a favor: the mission terminals here at the Base always need the wastes thinned out. Steady work keeps a runner sharp. Dismissed. Welcome to the Mercs.

NPC: Sure about that? I do not make the offer twice.

Your response: I'm sure.

Your response: Actually, no. I'll hear you out.

NPC: Think carefully. Walk away now and that frequency goes cold for good.

Your response: I have thought about it. Goodbye.

Your response: On reflection, I'll stay.

NPC: Your call. The Mercs know where to find talent when it grows up. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's floor space. The Base mission terminals will keep you busy - steady work keeps a runner sharp. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, recruit. You made rank without me. Go find a war worth your time. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You are not the kind of specialist I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Ah, there you are. Allow me to introduce myself: Jones, at your service. Well, not really. I have read your file. Not just the marksmanship scores, the other columns too. Most recruits here are muscle. I think you might be something more useful. Interested in finding out?

Your response: I'm interested. What did you have in mind?

Your response: Not right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested. Leave me be.

NPC: The offer stands. Find me before you outrank it: I do not recruit past level /25.

NPC: Simple problem first. I like to watch how people work before I trust them with the complicated kind. Storage went hot when the maintenance units turned on us, and with the housekeeping iron offline, the whole bay has filled up. Rogue bots, and every crawling thing that slipped in behind them. It's a mess. Get into Military Storage 6 and clear it out. Ten of them, I do not much care what: bots, bugs, whatever is moving. Just make the bay quiet again.

Your response: Malfunctioning bots. Anything else I should know?

NPC: Good. Your Nav-Ray will point you to the Storage entrance from anywhere in the Base. Follow it in, clear the bay, then report back to me. Move.

NPC: Back in one piece, and the bay is quieter. Tell me one thing: the bots in there, how did they fight?

Your response: Not like malfunctions. Even with all that vermin around them, they moved in a pattern. Coordinated. Like something was giving the orders.

NPC: The bay is still crawling. Finish the job, then report back to me.

NPC: Coordinated, eh? That is what I was afraid of. Housekeeping bots do not coordinate, and they do not move like that on their own. Somebody reached into their heads. Keep working that Heavy Combat of yours while I pull a service record. You handled yourself well, but well is not good enough out here.

NPC: Ready for the part they do not teach in basic?

Your response: What did the record say?

Your response: Give me a minute.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: The last tech to service those bots signed off a diagnostic patch across the whole fleet. Six hours before they turned. His name is Corporal Vane, and he works out of the Supply Depot. Go have a word with him. Quietly.

Your response: And if he does not want to talk?

NPC: You are not there to shoot him. You are there to make him nervous enough to tell the truth. There is a difference, and you had better learn it. You will find Vane at the Supply Depot.

NPC: You look like you came back with something. Talk.

Your response: Vane was bought. A patch that reads as certified, paid in cash by a man with real Sergeant's clearance. Rurik Kessler. Vane says that this guy's been selling more than bots: gate rotations, patrol gaps... and he thinks Kessler already knows we are onto him.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Vane yet. He is at the Supply Depot. Go.

NPC: Kessler. Decorated, and lately the subject of a file I kept telling myself was nothing. Late to muster. Requisitions that did not reconcile. We had our suspicions. Selling the Base's arteries to the scrap-runners is another level entirely. I should've followed my gut. That is on me, but it will not stay that way. Keep that Heavy Combat sharp: the next part is not a conversation.

NPC: This one is not a training exercise, and I won't pretend otherwise. You in?

Your response: I'm in. Where is Kessler?

Your response: Give me a moment to gear up.

NPC: Do not take too long. Men like Kessler get nervous, and nervous men run.

NPC: Yeah. They never do. You closed a leak today that I did not even realize was open. Questioned a suspect, followed the thread, put the right man in the ground. That is not jarhead work, recruit. That is the other kind.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You again? Good job last time, but there is nothing you can do for me. You should talk to Tasha.

NPC: You better talk to Lorcan first.

NPC: Don't blow up my vehicle!

Your response: Okay.. damn idiot..

Your response: You really called Ezra Reid? Not related to Jeremy Clarkson?

NPC: Weak Bastard...

NPC: You keep walking...

NPC: Idiot..

NPC: Really? C'mon!

NPC: What the...?

NPC: Really..?

Your response: Okay.. Never mind. What are you doing here?

NPC: I flew over that hill too fast and got stuck between these trees. Damn thing won't budge.

Your response: Maybe the both of us can get it free?

NPC: Nah. The controls are shot anyway. Just waiting for it to recall.

Your response: Recall?

NPC: Yeah, recall. Don't own a ride? Remember this, then.

Your response: *click*

NPC: If you lose a vehicle somewhere in the wastelands or it gets stuck, it will eventually recall to the vehicle depot. 
 It can take some time, though.

Your response: So, why are you waiting here by it if it would automatically recall anyway?

NPC: To make sure no jackasses blows it up.

Your response: Oh, weak.

NPC: Yeah, but you don't have to worry about that, if you drive carefully. And always remember to DISMISS your vehicle when you park at a depot.

Your response: Right

NPC: Actually, you can do something for me. I'm almost out of ammo, and I'm a recycler. I use shit I find from animals to replicate more ammo and some other stuff.

Your response: Sounds great!

NPC: Yeah, and now I need some shit, but I can't leave this place - Have to wait for the recall, you know? If you could find me two Entrails, it'd help a lot.

Your response: Entrails?

NPC: Yeah well, we're in a wasteland. I'd guess that there isn't an Archer & Wessons on the other side of that cliff.

Your response: *click*

NPC: The recycler can break down crap from animals and rematerialize it into something useful, like ammo or medkits.
Remember this: The Techlevel of the item you want to clone is the required Skill-level!

Your response: Sounds very useful and cheap!

NPC: Very! Come back if you have the stuff. Remember: I need two Entrails.

Your response: On my way!

NPC: I really need that stuff..

NPC: You got it?

Your response: Sure!

NPC: Actually, you don't have enough. Find at least two Entrails. Try scorpions and crabs. Easy kills and easy loot!

NPC: Perfect stuff! Here, I recycled you some First Aid Kits out of the leftover materials.

Your response: Very nice, thank you!

NPC: You're welcome. Could you do me a favour too?

Your response: Yeah sure, what is it?

NPC: When I crashed into the tree I was on the way to help out an old friend.
Her name is Tasha!
I flew in from the north, and she baled out just before I crashed here.
Could you please lend her a hand?

Your response: Of course I can. Tasha is her name, right?  Thanks again for the Medkits and take care!

NPC: Yes, Tasha! Thank you too and have a nice, productive, day!

entries.conversation:
NPC: You again? Good job last time, but I think you already know how constructing and researching works.

NPC: Hi Runner. I think you should try to find Tasha and lend her a hand.

NPC: Hi Runner. I think you should try to find Ezra Reid and talk to him.

NPC: Hi Runner. I think you should try to find Lorcan and talk to him.

NPC: Hey there!

Your response: Hi, What are you doing here?

NPC: Me? Does that mean you do not know who I am? Seriously?

Your response: Err... to be honest... no. I don't think I've ever heard your name before.

NPC: *Sigh* My name is Geordi, owner of Star Enterprises, and I'm one of the most ingenious scientists in the world.

Your response: Yeah of course. The most ingenious scientist in the world lives and works in a place like this, far away from...everything?

NPC: You don't believe me? YOU DON'T BELIEVE ME??? I'll show you what real scientist can do. You better run and hide!

Your response: Calm down please! I'm sorry. Of course I believe you!

NPC: Ok, that's better. Why didn't you say that in the first place? Well, never mind, let me show you what scientists can do in the world of Neocron.

Your response: Err.. now I wanna hide...

NPC: No no no, you're safe. I'm going to show you how you can make really good items like weapons or armour.

Your response: Oh okay. That sounds interesting.

NPC: First you need to know - items such as weapons and armour which are purchased from a shop are of poor quality.
 In order to get an item of better quality you'll have to construct it. This of course means that constructed items are a lot better than the ones from the shops.

Your response: continue

NPC: Constructed weapons of 'better', 'perfect' or even 'artifact' quality deal way more damage, have increased range, better frequency - that's lower time between shots, and handling - they are easier to aim. They also have the chance of having slots - which can be equipped with modifiers, like scopes, laser-pointers or ammunition converters.

Your response: Oh wow. I could really do with one of those!

NPC: Alright, let's see what we can do for you. In order to build items of higher quality you need to improve your 'Construction' skill which is an 'INTELLIGENCE skill. The higher your skill the better the quality of the item.

Your response: Ouch, I don't think my Construction skill is high enough to build anything at all.

NPC: Don't worry my friend. I'll do the constructing and you will deliver all the required materials. Ready?

Your response: Yes of course!

NPC: Before we can build an item, we'll need a sample of it. By researching this sample, you get a blueprint of the item. The blueprint lists all the materials you need for the Construction process.

Your response: Oh dear! I'm afraid my research skills are worse than my Construction skill.

NPC: That doesn't matter. That's why I'm known as one of the most ingenious scientists in the world! Since 'Construction' and 'Research' are both 'INTELLIGENCE' skills it's not very wise to invest skill points to both subskills. You'll either have to find a Researcher and construct the item yourself or vice versa.

Your response: But YOU can do both?

NPC: Of course I can! I'm one of ...

Your response: ... the most ingenious scientists in the world. Yeah, I know!

NPC: Exactly! Before we can start, you'll have to choose which kind of weapon you would like me to construct. Choose wisely because you'll have to use this weapon out there in the wastelands!

Your response: I'm so excited!

Your response: I'm sorry, but I don't think I already know what kind of weapon I need.

NPC: Choose your weapon!

Your response: A rifle, please

Your response: A pistol, please

Your response: A cannon 'heavy combat', please

Your response: A drone, please

Your response: A PSI module, please

Your response: A melee weapon, please

NPC: Ok, no problem. Come back to me later.

NPC: Alright, a rifle. Let's see if we can make you a Mendicant Rifle. First of all we need a sample of the rifle so that I can research it.

Your response: Well, yeah that sounds cool but I don't have one.

NPC: That doesn't matter. I've seen a group of Nomad Traders a few steps from here to the south east. I'm pretty sure that one of them sells some shabby weapons.

Your response: So you want me to buy a Mendicant Rife from them and bring it to you?

NPC: Indeed. You are smarter than you look!

NPC: Excellent. Good job.

Your response: I spent so many credits and what did I get? A shabby rifle...

NPC: Head south east to find the trader camp and buy a Mendicant Rifle.

NPC: I need all the parts listed on the blueprint!

NPC: I need all the parts listed on the blueprint!

NPC: You again? Good job last time, but I don't need more dru.... errr Solantium now. If you are looking for a job and more information talk to Ezra Reid!

NPC: WHO ARE YOU? GET OUT!!!

Your response: Whoa, relax! I was just looking around. I just woke up in MC5. Do you live here?

Your response: Okay.. Damn Idiot..

NPC: Weak Bastard...

NPC: They won't stop, will they? They said... they'll destroy my home.
I'll kill them. I'll... Did you know they got in your skull... They put a machine... inside your brain!!

Your response: Look, I'm really sorry to have bothered you. I'll be going

NPC: No no no. I'm sorry. Can you help me? I'm terribly sick. I need chems.

Your response: Chems?

NPC: Chemicals! Grey tubes. I need them... to make medicine. Do you have any? I just need three of them!

Your response: Are you a... a doctor?

NPC: Please get them for me. Get me three Solantium. I'll reward you.

Your response: I'll see what I can find. Any hint where I can find Solantium?

NPC: There are blue chemical boxes in the area where you can find Solantium!
I really need those chems, hurry up!

NPC: You got the chemicals?

Your response: So, these are for... medicine, you said?

NPC: It's you! Let's see the chemicals... No no no no. You don't have enough. Get me at least three Solantium.

NPC: Almost complete... I'll stop them... Everything will be better, you have my word... Thank you!

Your response: What are you talking about?

NPC: The chip in our head!  Our memories, my family... I'm going to kill them.

Your response: I'm sorry dude, but I really don't know what you are trying to tell me.

NPC: The three guys up there on the small hill can tell you more about what's going on here, but I recommend you talk to the guy over there who just crashed his glider into the tree.

Your response: Crashed a glider into a tree? Alright dude, what's his name?

NPC: His name is Ezra Reid and he's an old friend of mine... I think...

NPC: You again? Good job last time, but there is nothing you can do for me. You should talk to Geordi next.

NPC: I don't think my friend Ezra sent you. Talk to him first!

NPC: SNAKES EVERYWHERE! AAAHHHHHHHH

Your response: Calm down! What's your problem?

Your response: Lunatic..

NPC: Pff..

NPC: My problem? Are you serious? There are thousands of them. Snakes everywhere!

Your response: Kill em'?

NPC: I can't!

Your response: You can't? Why not? Are you paralysed?

NPC: No.. 
 I'm a passive PSI Monk.

Your response: What?

NPC: I can cast PSI modules on other people to boost their skills or resistance to damage. I can shield and heal them. 
 And when somebody dies, I can revive him.

Your response: Sounds amazing! So you're a healer?

NPC: Yes, I am. And because of that, I can't kill the snakes. Maybe you can help me?

Your response: Why not.. Sounds you're a good person. Maybe I need your help in the future..  What exactly do you want me to do?

NPC: Just kill these bastards in the 'Strange Cave' or in the area around me, they really scare the shit out of me!

Your response: No problem at all, sweetheart!

NPC: Kill 5 Small Rattlesnakes, then I'm safe - hopefully!

NPC: You killed them?

Your response: Sure.. That was easy!

NPC: Are Rattlesnakes too strong for you?

NPC: You are my hero! THANK YOU VERY MUCH!

Your response: You're welcome, Honey.

NPC: Let me give you some advice: On your way to me you must have noticed a shack that looks like an improvised weapon- and amour store. It's not!
The guys who run the 'shop' are here to help out people who were able to resist the brainwashing process. People like you!

Your response: Brainwashing? People like ME?

NPC: Yeah, people like you! I have no idea how they do it, but sometimes the system fails and people withstand the process. This happened to you.
The regime already put a chip in your head but it looks like you have not lost all your memories.

Your response: What the hell are you talking about? THEY saved me!

NPC: Yeah, people like you! I have no idea how they do it, but sometimes the system fails and people withstand the process. This happened to you.
The regime already put a chip in your head but it looks like you have not lost all your memories.

Your response: My memories? Are you saying they tried to reprogram my brain?

NPC: Indeed. And the people in the shack are here to help you. They let the regime think that they are running a store but they'll teach you all the stuff that got deleted from your brain during the brainwash.

Your response: But my brain... it feels ok... I don't think I ...

NPC: Trust me. You really need help. Go and find Geordi!

Your response: Alright, Geordi in the shack that looks like a weapon-store. Got it.

NPC: Take care!

NPC: I see. They did their job well. This facility is called -Area MC5-. If I told you this place were a brainwashing facility created by Reeza, you wouldn't believe me anyway.

Your response: Damn right, liar! I should report you to my friends in there!

NPC: Nevermind. Thanks for your help! Bye!
