entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Now, what am I supposed to make of you? The City would have us believe that killers do it for a fee. I am looking for people who do it for a cause. So I wonder: Which are you?

Your response: I joined the cause, not the mercs, didn't I?

Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: I don't. Please go away.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: That says much less than you think it does. But no matter. We're gonna find out together, anyway. And step one is to see how you work where nobody is watching: In a dark cave. Canyon Cave 2, to be exact. Put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. It's the honest test of a killer.

Your response: Killing vermin in a cave tests my skills as a killer? What do you expect to gain by watching me do that?

NPC: I didn't say anything about your skills. And neither will I be watching you do it. What I will be watching, though, is your attitude about it, and how you behave once you're back. So get going. Canyon Cave 2, eight creepy crawlies.

NPC: So, tell me, honestly: Were you bothered at all by killing those beasts?

Your response: Why would I be bothered by exterminating some pests?

NPC: Do you honestly want me to report that you came back before the task was finished? Get going!

NPC: This is the correct attitude towards a cave full of pests. And it would be the entirely wrong attitude about a person. The difference between those two will determine how good you are at your job. The City will send its goons to kill anyone without ever thinking twice about it. As soon as we do the same, we become just like them. Get back to me soon.

NPC: Last time, I asked you to exterminate a cave full of pests. Wanna learn how the movement picks its targets?

Your response: I'm especially interested in who does the picking.

Your response: Yes, but... hang on.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: There's a regular in our bar. Wren Halasz is the name, drinks in there pretty much every evening, talks a lot and listens a lot. Knows all the regulars on a first name basis, and also knows which ones of them have quietly made their peace with the City. Something the movement calls various things, from collaboration to treason. Not a definition anyone in that bar got to vote on.

Your response: What exactly do you mean? Do the drinkers in there know they are being sorted?

NPC: Of course they don't, that's the whole point. Neither does Halasz, for that matter, and we'd like you to keep it that way. Just buy a round, and listen to what is being said.

NPC: Which name did she land on?

Your response: Tomas Bierko. Really nice guy, apparently. Never complains, gets on well with everybody.

NPC: Wren Halasz in our bar. Don't make me ask again.

NPC: Bierko. Yeah, I know him. He moves goods here from the City, and does well doing it. His smuggling means that the people he feeds would rather keep him. Getting rid of him would cost us dearly. But leaving him be would incur an even greater cost, an ideological one. And that is a price we can't afford. His fate is decided. Get back to me, and you're gonna seal it.

NPC: I'm not gonna beat around the bush, not gonna soften it for you. This is not a cave full of vermin, but a person, in a room full of people who like him. Are you up to the task?

Your response: If that is what it takes.

Your response: I'll need to think about that, if I'm honest.

NPC: That's a good sign. I won't accept such a task being done half-heartedly. You need to believe.

NPC: Bierko is sitting in the same bar Wren Halasz sits in. Do it right there, do not take him to some back alley. The movement does not hide what it decides.

Your response: Wren specifically asked me not to do it in front of her. What should I expect to happen after... the deed?

NPC: What do you think is gonna happen? They're gonna hate you for it, for a while. Especially Wren. But they're gonna turn back to their drinks. That is the cost you will have to pay for your conviction. No sense in me sugar-coating it.

NPC: Yes? I am trying to enjoy my beer, thank you very much. But I assume you want something from me.

Your response: Not really. Jones told me that you could use a friendly ear. Let me buy you a drink.

NPC: Jones? Oh, alright, I like her, so I'll like you, especially if you're buyin'. Let me tell you about this bar, and the people walking in and especially out of here. Those who walk out, who still believe in anything, and those- well, those who don't.

Your response: You can tell the difference, simply by watching how they walk out of here?

NPC: If they can still walk, that is. There are those that never complain, and always have something to sell, you know, under the table. Take Tomas, for example. Tomas Bierko. He's quite decent to people, never complains about anything. I'll be damned if he actually believes anything. Those who believe are the ones with loud opinions or spectacular breakdowns. He'd never show either.

Your response: Let's be honest, here. You do realize what just happened, don't you? Why I am here, and what is gonna happen now?

NPC: Please. I am not dense. Of course I know. Doesn't mean that I want to know, or that I am proud of it. Just... don't do it right in front of me, okay?

NPC: (Wren makes a very conscious effort not to notice you again.)

NPC: Ah, a new face! Welcome, friend!

Your response: You betrayed the movement, Tomas. And I am here to put an end to that.

NPC: I see. You want to know what I think? What I did means that people around here stay fed who would otherwise go hungry. Yes, I'm being paid by the City, and I use this money to help the people around here. So tell me: Who exactly have I betrayed?

Your response: I have no answer for you. All I can tell you is that your fate has been decided.

NPC: Right. At least you're being honest about it. Can you say the same about the people who sent you?

NPC: ...

NPC: The deed is done. You were asking me, now I am asking you: How did the room react?

Your response: Initially, they were curious. Then they got the hint, and started looking away. Wren was trying very hard to leave her own body.

NPC: Don't pretend it is done. It isn't, so get a move on.

NPC: Doesn't feel glamorous, does it? It's not supposed to, and I'm not going to congratulate you for it. This is the part the City never has to live with. We do - and that's what makes this movement stronger than them, not weaker.

Your response: I just executed the guy who helped a lot of our families survive. Are we truly better off, now?

NPC: Yes. We are. I can say that without any doubt in my heart, and still, I can be honest about the cost that this will entail. These kinds of decisions are supposed to be hard. Your beliefs are what help guide you through them. The movement will prevail, but only if it doesn't cozy up to the fascist oppressors it seeks to overthrow.

Your response: I guess I can live with that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a rifle your way. You've earned it. Keep your Rifle Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The movement is short on people, and has plenty of jobs open for more brawn than brains. The good news is: that means you'll be quite welcome here. The bad news is that, unless I am underestimating you, you won't last long. I want you to prove me wrong. Will you?

Your response: We're gonna have to see, won't we?

Your response: I will, if you just gimme a minute.

Your response: Piss off, won't you.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Then first, you need to prove me right, on the brawn at least. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down twelve of whatever is down there. No, you do not get to prove your brains as well on this one.

Your response: Suits me fine, actually.

NPC: Good. And don't you worry: You, I will pay properly for this.

NPC: And here's your payment. Was this kind of work agreeable to you?

Your response: Uh-huh.

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still a-crawlin'. Don't make me punch your lights out. And don't say 'Oh yeah, I'd like to see you try.'

NPC: That was exactly the type of grunt I was hoping to hear. It is also what I had feared. But no matter. Come back to me, once you have restocked and re-whatever'd it is you do.

NPC: You enjoyed your last job, even though it was me sending you into a shithole. Ready for a bigger hole, and bigger shit?

Your response: Uh... how much bigger?

Your response: I will be, just gimme a moment.

NPC: Oh sure, take a moment. Take two.

NPC: You'll see for yourself. It's Canyon Cave 3 this time, and you need to exterminate twelve of them again. Harder ground, bigger critters. Oh, and once again. Good news: I have organized some backup for you. You know, PPUs, equipment, the works. Bad news: It was all reassigned, to something the movement values more than your life, apparently.

Your response: FML. Does it pay well, at least?

NPC: No.

Oh, you're still here. Let me elaborate: No, with more o's. This will pay less than the last one did, and I'll once again be blunt: The movement won't pay more, because the movement doesn't have to pay more, and that is because you will go in regardless. They know that, I know that, you know that.

NPC: Here you go, your payment.

Your response: You weren't kidding, were you. That's all?

NPC: Nice try. Back to Canyon Cave 3 it is.

NPC: Yes it is, and that's the honest version of what the movement is doing with us. Most people in my position would have beaten around the bush, or hidden it in the paperwork. I'm not gonna pretend otherwise. You do not do this, our cause, for the glamour or the money. There is somebody you need to meet. Get back to me.

NPC: Good news is: It's not a cave this time. Will you take it?

Your response: So what's the bad news?

Your response: Gimme a minute.

NPC: No problem.

NPC: The bad news? Oh, that. Well, the bad news is that you get to off your predecessor. That's the brawn. And you know what that tells you about you being on that job. That's the brains. His name is Dragan Volk - years in the Canyon. Same as you, he has worked out what he was for. It has not stopped him, and now he is a danger to the people around him. Question is, will it stop you?

Your response: But why are you sending me after him? Why not somebody else?

NPC: I had hoped you'd understand that by now. But no matter. You're the reason he is finished. Sending anybody else would be an insult.

NPC: Runner. I know exactly why you are here. And I thank you for this honor.

Your response: So. How long did you have this job before me?

NPC: So many years. I was the one who was sent first through so many doors. Every time, they relied on me to... geez, listen to me, going on about this as if it were some great deed.

Your response: So why did you never stop?

NPC: Listen to me very closely: Being the first through that door was the only thing that ever made me feel worth a damn. I didn't have anything else going for me, but this was the thing they always admired me for.

Your response: And now I'm supposed to be the one always charging first.

NPC: Yes. That is how replaceable I am. And how replaceable you're gonna be one day as well.

NPC: ...

NPC: You seem somber. That tells me you did it.

Your response: He told me how replaceable he is. And now, I am just as replaceable.

NPC: You still need to take care of Volk.

NPC: ...Yes. And I'm not gonna pretend otherwise. I do hope you understand why I sent you, and not some other upstart, though.

Your response: In a couple of years, you're gonna do the same to me, won't you?

NPC: Me? Probably not. One of my successors? Absolutely. You see, I am just as replaceable as you are. The movement will use whatever and whoever it is given, for as long as it benefits the movement. That applies both to you and to me. The only thing I can offer is that I won't sugar-coat it. I'll be honest about it. Dead honest. And that is more than the City can say about the people it uses.

Your response: So I guess there is nothing for me but to accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a sword your way. You've earned it. Keep your Melee Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. So they tell me you can drive. I hope you realize what that means. The Canyon has no rail and no subway, and our internal logistics is done by hand. So everything the movement has was transported here on chains or wheels, which makes a driver like you one of our supply lines.

Your response: Well, I have seen those vehicles parked outside. They looked rather wrecked for the most important supply line of the Canyon.

Your response: Yes. Give me a moment, though.

Your response: I'm not interested. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Yes. Now why is that? Why does the movement drive decrepit wrecks, when clearly, it could afford better? I will send you to Ilka Radu. Go on and ask that question. You will get the real answer, and I'd much rather have you get it straight from a dealer than from me.

Your response: I'm honestly supposed to walk over to the dealers, only to ask a question that you already know the answer to?

NPC: I hope I am not inconveniencing you. Seriously though. From me, it would only sound like a slogan. From Radu, it will sound like a plain and simple truth. Go.

NPC: Good, you're back. So what did Radu say?

Your response: That a wreck can be abandoned without so much as a second thought, and without anyone being ruined. A good vehicle can't.

NPC: I know that you haven't spoken to Radu yet.

NPC: That makes perfect sense, doesn't it? In addition, what Radu left out, because it is none of her business, is this: The movement plans around losing vehicles. Because it has never once been able to plan around keeping them.

NPC: The work never ends. So it's work, this time. Not a lesson.

Your response: Oh yeah? What happened?

Your response: Sure, just gimme a moment.

NPC: Those crates are not going anywhere. I'll be here.

NPC: A freight load is lying scattered across the Canyon and needs picking up. It is what it is, a plain and simple recovery.

Your response: A recovery from what? Whose load was it?

NPC: I'm not gonna beat around the bush: The freight belonged to a City haulage contractor, who now lies dead on the road. Some of our comrades took it, but then got into a fight over the spoils. The movement decided to take it, because the alternative is the Canyon going short on supplies. Yes, that means that you get to play the vulture, picking at the bones. I'm not asking you to feel good about that.

NPC: There's all the crates. Good job. Did you find the manifest as well?

Your response: I did. And I read it. There were many more crates. And that haulage contractor did not just supply the City, but also several wasteland refugee camps.

NPC: The crates are still spread across the Facility. Go and get them!

NPC: Reading the manifest was the right instinct. Any driver worth their salt should, or I'd worry. I will find out about those additional crates. And as for the haulage contractor, let me be blunt: This is what an insurrection eats. Pretending otherwise is how movements like ours start lying to themselves.

NPC: So. There is a good part of the haul which didn't make it to the Canyon. Are you ready to go get it?

Your response: So all those crates are still lying out there in the wastes? Are we sure they're not gone by now?

Your response: I will, but I need a moment first.

NPC: Don't be long. The movement needs those goods, they have already been promised to people who are counting on them.

NPC: Oh, they are, because I sent a recovery crew for them. Unfortunately, when they reached the Canyon, they got too close to Canyon Cave 1, and were attacked by the things in there. Now they refuse to go in there and get the crates back. I shouldn't be angry at them, fighting is not their job. But I have nobody else to send. Except you.

Your response: So what happens if those crates don't come out of there, and need to be declared lost?

NPC: Then our whole promise falls apart. The movement's whole claim is that we can live out here without the City. If we cannot make good on that promise, then it was just a speech. The movement will not fall apart without those crates. But a piece of it will crumble. Too many pieces, and the entire thing falls. So let's not let it come to that. Clear out Canyon Cave 1, and the recovery crew can do the rest.

NPC: Yes? You don't look like the sort of person who could afford anything I have on sale here...

Your response: Jones sent me. Wanted me to ask you why all the vehicles out here seem to be such wrecks.

NPC: Hahaha. Oh emm gee, how clueless. You must be completely new. Do you know how much a new vehicle costs? Do you know how much a run is worth? Do you know how often neither comes back?

Your response: Yes, well, better vehicles would increase the chances of coming back, wouldn't they?

NPC: Marginally, perhaps. Not worth the additional cost, though. It's not like the movement can insure its vehicles, can it? If it is lost, or breaks down and cannot be repaired, the vehicle is gone, and whatever it was worth zeroes. So we only drive what we can afford to abandon at a moment's notice, without running into fiscal trouble due to mounting costs. And I sell these- 'wrecks', as you call them, to anyone who wants one. You probably still can't afford one, but nobody has ever complained about my prices. At least not to my face.

Your response: So you sell to anyone, even those people the movement dislikes?

NPC: Yup. And let me tell you: I don't lose any sleep over it. The road doesn't care what anyone believes. Neither do I.

NPC: If you're not gonna buy anything, move on.

NPC: The cave has gone quiet. The recovery crew went in behind you, and the crates have been recovered. Give it to me straight: How bad was it?

Your response: Not too bad, actually. I hope it was worth it.

NPC: Canyon Cave 1 is still full, and the recovery crew is still waiting on you to do your job.

NPC: 17 of our families have food on their table this week. Five of our vehicles could get a long-overdue servicing. Our water reclamation system had one of its parts replaced, one that would surely have broken within the next five weeks. So yes, it was worth it.

Your response: What about the family of that contractor, or the wasteland refugees? Are they eating, this week?

NPC: No. They aren't. And I am quite aware of that. But if the price of continuing our movement out here is a little lost sleep over a nagging conscience, then so be it. It at least tells us that we are still human.

Your response: I guess I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Quad Key your way. You've earned it. Keep your Vehicle Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Listen. The movement is short on people and long on ways to die. So people like you, who fight the good fight from behind a wall, are quite popular among our recruiters, and very much not so among the soldiers. But the work never ends, and I am offering. Are you interested?

Your response: Sure I am. What's the job?

Your response: Let me get back to you.

Your response: No. Honestly, no, not at all. Please go away.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Then go into Canyon Cave 1, and kill four of its creepy-crawly denizens. Don't give me that look. Four.

Your response: Are you serious? Four? That's barely worth the walk over there...

NPC: Let me be perfectly clear. Four is what I can afford to watch a greenhorn like you be bad at. You're gonna bump your drone into walls, you're gonna get disoriented, you're gonna lose your drone. That's all part of the learning process, and better it happens now, on my budget, than on a run that actually matters. So get going, and stop complaining.

NPC: So? Still flying the same drone, or is there a little pile of scrap in that cave that wasn't there before?

Your response: Four are dead, that's what matters, isn't it?

NPC: I did say four, in Canyon Cave 1, didn't I?

NPC: Very good. Four done is still done. I've seen people insist on 10, and run out of drones before they could complete their task. Coming back with something small is always better than coming back with nothing at all. Remember that, and get back to me.

NPC: When we met, I told you that your profession is very unpopular among our soldiers. You didn't react to that. Before we get any further, I think you should know why that is.

Your response: Okay, I'll bite. What is it?

Your response: One moment please.

NPC: Sure. The reason isn't going anywhere.

NPC: I'm not gonna tell you. But the drone dealer here in the Canyon will. Goes by the name of Teo Lanz. That's right, he makes a living selling drones to people like you, while thinking that the movement should use neither them nor you.

Your response: How does a dealer argue against their own stock? I'm no expert in economics, but that sounds like bad business.

NPC: It is, and no mistake about it. Lanz is honest, to the point of being bad at his business. You may not like what he has to say. But you should hear it, anyway.

NPC: You talked to Lanz. Now explain his point to me, calmly and rationally.

Your response: He is in two minds. He believes that a revolution that won't risk bodies has already decided it is going to lose. But he doesn't want to lose the people, either.

NPC: You still need to talk to Lanz. You'll find him here in the Canyon.

NPC: I'll be honest: This kind of claptrap really gets me. The movement can't afford to be romantic about itself! The City can replace everyone it loses, the Canyon can't. We can't borrow the luxury of being willing to spend bodies from an enemy that has ten times as many of them. It's that simple. Digest that, then get back to me.

NPC: As I said, the work never ends, and I have a job for you that proves my point. I assume you are willing.

Your response: I am. What's up?

Your response: Give me a minute, and I'll get back to you.

NPC: Sure. Nobody else is gonna do it in the meantime. That's sort of the whole point.

NPC: What's 'up' is that two scouts went into Canyon Cave 3 and did not come out. These Gnawers in there are what did them in. I want you to make an example of them, and I don't want to risk anyone's life while doing it. Two was already a number we shouldn't have spent. No more. So take your drone, and kill Gnawers in that cave. Three of them. One more of them than they killed of us.

Your response: Why not simply send a squad and exterminate them all?

NPC: Have you been listening? I already sent two, and I have nothing to show for it except two bodies. I'm not gonna make it three, just because one squaddie isn't paying attention. My budget of lives to waste is thoroughly tapped out. Which is why I am risking your drones, not a squad, and not you. That's the kind of arithmetic that people like Lanz refuse to do.

NPC: Welcome. I sell these drones here. Do you want to buy one? Why would you do that?

Your response: Jones sent me. Wants me to hear your objection to my profession.

NPC: My objection? Yeah, I'll give you my objection. We're fighting the good fight against the fascist oppressors in the City. How does it make us look, if we won't stand up for our cause in person? Awesome rebels we are, sending these automatons against theirs. This is not how you get people to believe our cause is just!

Your response: So in your opinion, it's only a proper rebellion if we all die instead?

NPC: ...Look, I- No, of course I don't want us to die. Duh. But- it didn't use to be like this. Used to be that when we went out, we went out ourselves. Stood up for what we believe in.

Your response: So if you abhor drones so much, why do you sell them?

NPC: Because they work, simple as that. I know that my attitude isn't exactly consistent there. I don't wanna lose the people. I just- I just wish it were different. But it isn't. So that's that.

NPC: I have nothing else to say to you.

NPC: You're back, all in one piece, and the three Gnawers are dead. Tell me you didn't take unnecessary risks.

Your response: I barely set foot into the cave. My drones did the rest.

NPC: Those three Gnawers in Canyon Cave 3 won't kill themselves.

NPC: Two people, dead. That is the subtotal of doing it how Lanz thinks we should do it. I think I'm gonna tell him just that.

Your response: So Lanz is just plain wrong, then?

NPC: Wrong doesn't quite hit the mark. Deluded, more like. His idea of our movement has principles the real deal simply can't afford. Not to say that his version is unattractive, not even to me. But I'd much rather win this fight than slowly get wiped out because we couldn't let go of some old-fashioned honor-of-the-battlefield principles.

Your response: He makes you angry because you're afraid he might be right, aren't you?

NPC: I'm not afraid. Anyway, I'm gonna send a drone prototype your way. You've earned it. Keep your Remote Control skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

 138              SAY("You still need to talk to Lanz. You'll find him here in the Canyon.")
 139              SETNEXTDIALOGSTATE(30)
 140              ENDDIALOG()

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Your classical engineer training has probably always held all of your work to the highest standards. Well, let me disabuse you of that notion right away. There are no standards out here. If it works, it is good enough. Doesn't matter a bugger to anyone if it still works in 50 years, when it took you six weeks to finish it, while something that lasts a month could have been a five minute job. What does that sound like to you? Like freedom, or like a problem?

Your response: Like interesting new work conditions, but I have always been good at thinking on my feet. What's the assignment?

Your response: Hold that thought, I'll be right back.

Your response: Words cannot describe how uninterested I am. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: First assignment is to take stock. Having to think on your feet is one thing, not knowing what to work with is another. So go through the scrap across the Canyon, and find us six couplings that are actually still working properly.

Your response: You don't need an engineer for scavenging. What gives?

NPC: Oh, come on. The interesting bit is the telling if a coupling is fused or still working. Find someone to carry them for you, if that is beneath you. Now get out there, and get me those couplings.

NPC: You got the couplings. So give me an estimate: How much of that scrap out there is still in working condition?

Your response: Honestly? Not much.

NPC: Still waiting on those couplings.

NPC: Yeah, that's hardly surprising. Most structures the Canyon relies on are in pretty bad condition, and unfortunately, even most of our own people don't realize that. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So, these couplings. Do you want to know what they are holding together?

Your response: I'm almost afraid to ask...

Your response: Yes, but hang on. I still need a moment.

NPC: Sure. I'll be here.

NPC: Rightly so. Go to Ondrej Vask at the supply depot. The entire Canyon's water supply depends on one machine that came out of a City plant decades ago, and there's nobody left alive who fully understands it. Vask is the guy who comes closest to that.

Your response: That can't be right. Why did nobody write it all down, back then?

NPC: Let me put it this way: The movement's founding claim is that people can live free out here. Writing down how many parts of our machines come from the City, and only the City... well, it could be seen as a written confession that this claim is less than true. Still. Get as much information out of Vask as you can.

NPC: So what did Vask admit to?

Your response: The anti-radiation regulator is failing, probably only has weeks still in it. And no amount of wishful thinking from him is gonna fix that.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Vask yet.

NPC: Once again, I suspected as much. That's the most fragile part of the entire machinery, and it already didn't look that good anymore last year. So far, I have raised this through the discreet channels inside the movement that are available to me, but to no avail. We may need to evaluate alternative arrangements. Give me a moment to make a few calls, then get back to me again.

NPC: Alright. I have found a way to procure the required item. It will allow us to keep operating. And as long as neither you nor I blab about it, our ideology stays intact. Can I rely upon your discretion?

Your response: I'm not going to like this, am I? Just tell me where.

Your response: Can I... think about this for a minute?

NPC: Alright, but make your mind up. The machine is not waiting for anybody's conscience.

NPC: No one official will approve any requisitioning, because doing so would be admitting failure. That's how they think. But I have been made to understand that if I were to somehow magically come up with that part, nobody would ask any uncomfortable questions. There is a smuggler in the Canyon - goes by the name of Ilka Radu. She has confirmed that she could procure such a part for us. From the City, I'd imagine. And at a Smuggler's price.

Your response: So we're doing now exactly what the movement condemns? And you're keeping clean by sending me?

NPC: Absolutely. Make no mistake about it. You and me, we are gonna be the ones that will make the idea of the Canyon live on, and nobody will thank us for it. Nobody will even want to know. The Canyon's independence is bought from the very system it hates much more often than it would care to admit. Now, go to Radu and get that part. Take a shower after, if you must, with the water you ensured that we're gonna keep having.

NPC: Yeah, what do you want? The water plant is working fine, thank you very much!

Your response: Calm down, I'm not here to file anything. Jones sent me.

NPC: Alright then. You want some straight shootin', then? Keeping this machine alive, by now, has become more of a ritual than actual repair work. We go through motions handed down through the years, without any idea why we do what we do, imitating what we observed from people long dead by now.

Your response: More straight shootin', please. In your honest opinion, what's the first part that's likely to fail soon?

NPC: It's the anti-radiation regulator. I've been nursing it for months, now. I've also tried to put my ear to the ground, but there is no replacement to be taken from anywhere in the wastes. Only the City has these parts, and I don't have to explain to you why that is not an option for us.

Your response: So why haven't you raised this topic higher up?

NPC: You mean an escalation? An escalation would become an admission, an admission that the Canyon cannot sustain itself. I won't have that. No, I'll manage to keep the old part working. Somehow.

NPC: Leave me be, I have stuff to attend to that I barely understand myself.

NPC: Radu's the name, and... oh. You're the one Jones sent, hmm? Not so conceited about pure ideology now, is she? Heh heh heh.

Your response: Less gloating, more anti-radiation regulator giving, please.

NPC: Oh, I don't mean to be cruel about all this. It's just refreshing not to have people look down their noses at me for a change. In your own story, you're probably the hero who does what needs to be done, aren't you? Well, without me and what I do, there's no heroism to be had. So where does that leave me?

Your response: You do it for the money. And I bet you exploit our vulnerability in these matters regularly.

NPC: You know what? This part is dirt cheap in the City. But Jones is gonna wire me 5,000 NC for it. And like all the others from the Command Center, she won't thank me, yet she knows my name. They all do. Ask yourself how that could be.

Your response: I'd rather not. I'll have that regulator now, thank you.

NPC: Here you go. Just think: Which one of us is actually keeping the Canyon alive?

NPC: You're still here. Back to acting all better-than-thou?

NPC: You got the part, while I got Radu's hefty bill. Did she say anything worth repeating?

Your response: She asked me to think about which one of us is actually keeping the Canyon alive.

NPC: We still need that regulator from Radu.

NPC: Here's what's gonna happen. The movement will fix the water plant, tell nobody where that part came from, and go on making pretty little speeches about self-sufficiency. Our burden of knowledge is having peeked behind the curtain, and knowing that these speeches are really just that.

Your response: And that doesn't bother you at all?

NPC: It does, and having vultures like Radu gloat about it does not make it more agreeable. I do believe in the idea of the Canyon, however. And that is worth a few sleepless nights.

Your response: I guess I can live with that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Construction Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Construction skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. You are trained in treating casualties. Most of the people in need of treating around here aren't casualties at all. Interested in finding out what I mean by that?

Your response: That probably sounded better in your head. But I'll take it.

Your response: In a minute.

Your response: Ugh. No. Not at all. Please leave. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: First things first: Some medical supplies came off a supply drom that panicked in a narrow passage on the lower level of the Canyon. The crates burst, and scattered their contents all over that passage. Get me six of the dressing packs that were inside, before people start quietly pocketing them.

Your response: Come on. You don't need a medic for this kind of work.

NPC: Yes I do. A medic is the only one who will bother checking which packs are still sterile, instead of just counting them up, and proudly presenting me with a bunch of unusable trash. So get down there, and get me those packs.

NPC: You got them. So how much of the stuff lying about was still usable?

Your response: Well, most of the usable stuff has been pocketed by now. The stuff that was strewn across the floor clearly already had been gone through a couple of times.

NPC: I still need those packs. Get them, before they're gone.

NPC: That's the entire Canyon's medical supply situation right there: Nothing arrives reliably, and everything that does arrive gets rationed by whoever is standing closest. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So. I already told you that most people treated around here aren't casualties at all. Do you want to know what they get treated for, or what they don't get treated for, and then die of?

Your response: I do.

Your response: Yes, but hang on. Not ready yet.

NPC: I'll be here.

NPC: Then head over to Doc Sarn in the Barracks, in HQ. He has been treating people in the Canyon longer than the movement has held it. The answer will become clear.

Your response: So what am I supposed to expect, down there?

NPC: That it is actually not the fighting that accounts for most deaths around here. Well, at least not directly. But you don't need to hear second-hand information from me. Go directly to the source, Doc Sarn.

NPC: So. Doc Sarn's patients. Anything about them that you'd notice?

Your response: He's mostly treating people suffering from cave injuries, heatstroke or untreated old injuries, barely any recent combat casualties. And about half of the people he's treating aren't even from our movement at all.

NPC: You need to speak to Doc Sarn in the Barracks.

NPC: I know. And I have been getting asked from above about this more and more, recently. Take a breather, then get back to me. Unfortunately, the position of the movement on matters like these is quite clear.

NPC: I have spent some time trying to come up with ways of dressing this up like a lesson. But it's not. So I'm gonna stop pretending that it is. This is an order, plain and simple. You're going to deliver it and Doc Sarn is going to obey it. And that's that.

Your response: I'm not going to like this, am I. What is it?

Your response: Uh, I'm gonna need a moment.

NPC: Take that moment. I'd much rather have you do this reluctantly than cheerfully.

NPC: It's precisely what you already guessed. Doc Sarn is to stop treating people aligned with the City. Our medical supplies are finite, and the movement will not spend them on people who would hand the Canyon back to the City tomorrow.

Your response: This goes against everything I stand for. I can't imagine you agree with that order.

NPC: The point of an order is that it comes from people you don't get to overrule. I don't get to overrule them, and you don't get to overrule me. And Sarn doesn't get to overrule you. That he gets that order from a fellow medic is the modicum of comfort I can offer him.

NPC: No grave external injuries. Take a seat, I'll be right with you. Actually, you don't look injured at all. Why are you taking up space here?

Your response: Jones sent me. I'm a medic as well, although not nearly as experienced as you are.

NPC: Oh, you are of the trade as well? I could use the extra hands, sure. You see, there are so many people to treat here, cave wounds, heat, and above all injuries that were survivable a year ago and were never treated back then.

Your response: You know, I cannot help but notice that a lot of those people you treat around here do not seem to be of our movement at all...

NPC: Oh, less than half, make no mistake about it. Everyone within a day's walk comes here if they get injured, simply because there is nowhere else. And me, well, I have never asked anyone what they believe in before I treat them. And neither should you.

Your response: I didn't even know the guards at the gate would let people in, just like that. Does nobody object to what you're doing?

NPC: They have started to, recently. The more people come here, the bigger the problem some people seem to have with it. But I'm not in the habit of turning people away, so anyone who has a problem with that can just come up to me and say it to my face. That's all I have to say about it.

NPC: I must get back to my patients.

NPC: No. Don't say it. Don't say anything. You're forbidding me from treating people not of the Canyon, aren't you.

Your response: You are hereby ordered to stop treating people aligned with the City. Our supplies are finite, and we cannot spend them on people who might come back in the next attack wave against us.

NPC: I bet you rehearsed that line in your head over and over again on your way here. Unfortunately for you, I've been expecting this to happen for some time, and I've had time to prepare myself, too. So let me ask you one simple question of procedure: How exactly am I supposed to make out a patient's politics with blood gushing from their open wounds and them screaming and crying for their mothers?

Your response: I... have no procedure to offer you about that.

NPC: Figures. They never even thought this through, did they? Headful of ideology, and no practical considerations ever spent. But if they want ideology, here's one for them: As soon as we start doing triage by loyalty rather than by severity of injury, this becomes just another installation of the same system the City is running, and the movement will have lost the only thing it can honestly claim to be better at.

Your response: I don't know what to say to you. What do you expect me to report back, now?

NPC: You want something to report back? Here goes, and do take note, so you get the wording exactly right: Fuck the lot of you. There you go, report that. I will not have someone bleeding out under my care because some people deem them not ideologically pure enough. I'm not scared of you, I'm not scared of that bitch Jones, and I'm certainly not scared of the chief ideologists who think they actually run this place. ...Actually, I'm gonna take that 'bitch' back. I know Jones, and honestly, I don't think she really wants me to obey that order.

NPC: You don't want me to obey that order either. That's plain as day. So I'll be going back to work now, if you don't mind.

NPC: So. How'd it go? Did he tell you where you can shove that order?

Your response: He asked me to relay his reply word for word, and it was: 'Fuck the lot of you.'

NPC: You still need to deliver that order. It's not gonna get easier by procrastinating.

NPC: I expected no less. ...Sorry. You probably expected me to know what to do now. The truth is: I don't.

Your response: He raised the good point of how to find out the politics of someone with blood gushing out of them, and them crying for their mommies. Maybe that helps?

NPC: It may. I will do the only thing I can do, which is the same thing you did: I will report that refusal upward, along with that very valid question. No editing, no mincing words. They can have that problem sit on their plate and stare at their faces. I have spent years justifying everything the movement asks. But this is one I just can't. And I will not insult a medic by trying to.

Your response: Does that change anything for you? Or me?

NPC: No. I still believe in the movement. People fail, the idea doesn't. If the idea collapses on one doctor refusing an order to stop treating people, it won't survive the City's onslaught, either. I'm gonna send a Healing Module your way. You've earned it. Keep your Passive Psi Use skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Now, good news first: This place is virtually impossible to hack. The bad news: That's because there is almost no technical infrastructure that could be hacked. Which limits your options somewhat. But the movement wants you anyway. Know why that is?

Your response: This does not start promising. But I'm interested.

Your response: Let me get back to you on that.

Your response: No I don't, nor have I the slightest interest in finding out. Now leave my apartment, please.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Then head over to our Intelligence Center. Talk to Adela Prosk, and learn how City data actually reaches the Canyon, because it is not over any wire. Or WiFi, for that matter.

Your response: So all the data arrives physically?

NPC: I can neither confirm nor deny that. Just talk to Prosk. It will change your perception of what your skill is for out here. The Intelligence Center can be found inside HQ. There's a hatch.

NPC: You're back. So what did Prosk show you?

Your response: Loads of physical media, a story about couriers, and the fact that the movement's real output appears to be respun City propaganda rather than intelligence.

NPC: You need to speak to Prosk in the Intelligence Center before we can continue.

NPC: You got that exactly right. And here is the political point: The movement does not steal City data to know things, it steals City data so that people in the City have to know things they have arranged their lives around not knowing. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So, I have a job for you. It may or may not be a little more up your street. What do you say?

Your response: I'm gonna say: I'm in.

Your response: I'm gonna say: Hang on a moment.

NPC: I'll be here. Don't know if the job will still be, though.

NPC: So, one of those couriers who was supposed to carry loads of data into our Intelligence Center? Yeah, he arrived running for his life, dropping half of his haul all over the place. He was running because City agents were waiting on his route. Recover these data cubes from all around the Canyon, five at least.

Your response: Hold up, this doesn't exactly sound like a chance encounter.

NPC: We're thinking the same thought, then. Maybe the data on those cubes will tell us. I do have a suspicion, though. But I won't say it out loud before we've had a look at that data.

NPC: I assume you had a look at that data by now. I'd ask you to get out of my sight if you hadn't.

Your response: All the files on those cubes had very recent access timestamps. That data was read, even before I did.

NPC: You still need to retrieve those cubes.

NPC: So this data was read, possibly even manipulated, before it even reached us, and the City knew the route of our courier. Quite obviously, despite our precautions, data is leaving the Canyon after all. Something out here is connected. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: I have good news and bad. The good news is that this time, the job IS a hack. Are you in?

Your response: Yes I am. I assume that the bad news is what it is that you need hacked?

Your response: You asked for a moment, now I still need one.

NPC: Hurry up, then. That open connection needs to close as soon as possible.

NPC: Not exactly, but the bad news is that we have confirmed that there is an open connection leading here, into the Canyon. We've traced the signal, and it is leading right into the Canyon Facility, but we couldn't pinpoint its exact location. So you're gonna have to look for it, I guess. Some terminal, data interface, something that looks out of place. And it is definitely in the Canyon itself, not in some cave or building. Find it, break its encryption, and get its log files.

Your response: How could such a line be open without anyone in the Canyon knowing about it?

NPC: It couldn't. Or at least, that's what I suspect. But we won't know for sure until you get us these logs. So hurry up and get them!

NPC: Just put the latest discs over there, would y- what? A hacker? What are you doing here?

Your response: Jones sent me. Asked me to learn how data actually gets here.

NPC: Ah, I see. Well, it's simple, really. Nothing arrives here over any network. If it did, anything coming in would be accompanied by ten times as much data going out. So all the data arrives in someone's coat. That's 'coat' if we are lucky. The Canyon's entire intelligence capacity is people willing to walk the distance, and smuggle data out the old-fashioned way.

Your response: And what does the movement do with that data?

NPC: We publish it, mostly. It's the City's own propaganda, spun against itself, aimed at City workers who may not yet be fully indoctrinated.

Your response: Does that even work at all?

NPC: I'll be honest: Most of our numbers are guesstimates, and even those are low. But actually, that's not our concern around here. What we do is make sure that what gets published and what is being stolen remains the same - if that makes any sense at all to you.

NPC: Back to stacks of data discs to go through.

NPC: Did you find it? What do the logs say?

Your response: I could only read the header info. The log itself is heavily encrypted. I think the line had already existed before the movement set up shop in this Canyon. Forgotten infrastructure.

NPC: Get me those log files! The connection leads somewhere inside the Canyon Facility!

NPC: Yes. That would be a classic attack vector: Nobody is aware that the old infrastructure even still exists, so it is not actively monitored and not secured. But it works, and the attacker exploits it.

Your response: You got that right. I can't even count how many systems I entered myself using similar techniques. Old, unmonitored parts of a system are the easiest to compromise.

NPC: This is exactly why we make do without any connection to the outside. Not by choice, but by sheer necessity. This line was found by an outside attacker - in this case, City agents - and has been exploited against us for who knows how long. So keep this as a warning example: Don't open a connection to the outside from here. Not even for five minutes.

Your response: Bit difficult to work under these conditions, but I guess I'll manage.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Hacking Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Hacking skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Every recruit that specializes in the field of infiltration we've ever gotten thought that 'getting in' is the difficult part of the job. It isn't. Let me tell you: We have never once lost anybody on the way in. Where we lose them comes after. Are you willing to learn?

Your response: I am, but I find it hard to believe that you never lost anyone on the way in.

Your response: Yes, but I'll need a moment, first.

Your response: This is a joke, right? If you've never lost anyone on the way in, you're aiming at the wrong targets. I can't learn anything from you. I'm out.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: So I may have exaggerated slightly for emphasis. That's not important. I'm gonna send you to Marek Toth in the Barracks. He's been running people into the City for years. And whatever comes back, he's the one who has to deal with that, as well.

Your response: What do you mean, 'whatever comes back'?

NPC: Oh, you will find out, believe you me. Talk to Toth. What he will tell you will be the most honest answer to that question possible, since he's the one who has to look at them.

NPC: You look thoughtful. What did Toth tell you?

Your response: Funny thing is, getting people out never even came up. Not once. His problem is the opposite: the longer they stay in the City, the less they're themselves. They stop complaining and start building a life there. We're losing them, basically.

NPC: You haven't spoken to Toth yet. He's in the Barracks.

NPC: That's the problem right there. The City is comfortable. Rebelling against it from some stony Canyon... isn't. And that's fine, while you haven't actually experienced the comfort. But once you do, the politics slowly start ebbing away. That's the one weapon the enemy has, to which the movement has no counter. We'll get back to that.

NPC: You're back, good. This time, there is a practical problem I'm gonna task you with resolving, instead of a lecture about the problems with infiltration we currently have.

Your response: Sounds good. What is it?

Your response: In a moment.

NPC: Makes no difference, I guess. The problem doesn't resolve itself.

NPC: Here's the thing: When we actually do exfiltrate people from the City, we can't lead them through the Canyon entrance. Virtually all of the City's eyes are pointed at that gate. So we lead them through Canyon Cave 3. Only problem: That cave is very popular among the wildlife, and it's time to decimate it again. Kill eight of whatever has moved into there, so that our exfiltration route is usable again.

Your response: That sounds pressing. How many people are currently depending on that route being open?

NPC: Relax. So far, it's only five people waiting, and they haven't waited long, yet. But let's not let that number get bigger, and that waiting time longer, shall we?

NPC: Good work. The route is open again. In fact, one of the people who needed it has used it already.

Your response: That's good to hear. Who was it that used the route?

NPC: The route through Canyon Cave 3 is still not clear.

NPC: Yeah. About him. His name is Cass Roeder, has been inside the City for years. His debrief was flawless, he said all the right things. Given what you heard from Toth, that's precisely what should worry us. Get your breath back, then talk to me again.

NPC: So. This one will be ugly, I won't pretend otherwise. I also won't pretend that the evidence is conclusive, or that we can be absolutely certain. But we have to do it anyway. In, or out. Tell me.

Your response: In.

Your response: Can I... get some time to think about this?

NPC: Oh yes, absolutely. Think about it properly, since I am asking you to act on a judgment rather than a proof.

NPC: Then let me lay it out for you plainly: Roeder was not turned, was not paid, and he has betrayed nothing. His 'crime' is liking it in there. And he has started describing the City life in a way that is starting to spread through the Canyon.

Your response: Well, that's hardly treason, is it?

NPC: It is not. If it were, I would not have to ask you to deal with him, but put him in front of a tribunal. We have to consider the ongoing survival of our movement, though. And an honest man describing a comfortable life with the enemy will empty the Canyon faster than any City operation ever could. So go deal with a threat to our continued existence.

NPC: That's close enough. What makes you come here? Are you reporting for infiltration duty?

Your response: No, at least not yet, I guess. Jones sent me.

NPC: I see. So she wants me to explain what we do around here. We put our people into the City is what it is. We create the best covers for them we can afford, hope that they last slightly longer than the previous guy did, and lament how little support we can give them.

Your response: I had come to believe that some of them do come back?

NPC: Oh, they do. The coming back is not the issue. Well, sometimes we just lose contact. Most people come back, no problem. But, you see, they're never quite the same when they do. They're getting a taste of the 'sweet life' that the City uses to pacify its populace. And let me tell you: That siren song is strong. So the failures aren't the ones who get caught. The ones who settle in are the problem. You can never tell if what they have is a good cover, or... well, a life.

Your response: So how can you tell the difference?

NPC: That's the problem right there. I can't. There are just the ones I worry about, and they are the ones that do not in fact complain. I mean, have you ever met anyone who has nothing to complain about? ...I think I've said all I can, really. Probably more than I should have.

NPC: I have nothing more to say to you. At least for now.

NPC: My friend! Great to meet another infiltrator, I'm really pleased! Wanna go for a couple of cold ones, and exchange war stories from behind enemy lines?

Your response: Sure, but first, tell me: What is it really like, over there in the City?

NPC: Oh, let me tell you, if they send you there, that's gonna be the best assignment of your life. The food, the quiet... no one I met over there is any kind of monster, they're actually really nice people!

Your response: So why did you come back at all, and not stay with your new friends?

NPC: I got the communication to report back, so I did, but then I'm gonna head back- Wait just a minute! I see now where this conversation is going. Let's get this over with, then.

NPC: ...

NPC: I can see by the look on your face that the deed is done. What did he say, in the end?

Your response: He talked about the food and the quiet, said that nobody he met in the City was a monster, and that if I were ever sent there, it would be the best assignment I'd ever be on.

NPC: Roeder is still in the Facility, still talking too much.

NPC: That's exactly what we feared. So at least we weren't wrong in our suspicions. So it had to be done. Doesn't mean we have to like it.

Your response: Do you think he was right, though? About the City, and the life there?

NPC: He probably was. But that is beside the point. A golden cage is still a cage. The people in the City are leading comfy lives, but they are not free. And we intend to free them. That is the good fight we are fighting.

Your response: Yeah, I guess I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Stealth Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Pistol Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Look, I'll be blunt. The Canyon distrusts Monks. That can't possibly be a surprise to you, given the history between our movement and the tyranny of the Monks. So you're gonna have to earn our trust by being useful. Until then, best I can do is give you the benefit of the doubt. Will you take that chance?

Your response: I intend to prove myself, ten times over.

Your response: I will. You're gonna have to give me a moment, though.

Your response: I'm going to prove myself, alright. But not to you. Please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Then let's start with something straightforward. Go to Canyon Cave 2, and put down eight of whatever crawls around in there. If you cannot fight, you are just a liability, another mouth to feed. So let's see how you handle that.

Your response: Is that really all there is to it?

NPC: For now? Yes. After that? Well, let's see. The job I actually want you for isn't one I'm gonna describe to someone I haven't watched work.

NPC: That was a satisfactory performance. So aren't you going to ask me what I have been assessing you for?

Your response: *sigh* What have you been assessing me for?

NPC: Canyon Cave 2 is still crawling. Prove yourself to me.

NPC: Let me explain part of the problem: We have no courts. No judges. No prisons. At most, we can convene a tribunal, for the very few cases where one can actually do any good around here. What we do have, though, is people trained to ask questions, and people trained to give believable answers. More details when you get back to me.

NPC: Right. So, there is an accusation on my desk. I need you to look into the case.

Your response: Who is it that is being accused here? And of what?

Your response: I will, just give me five minutes.

NPC: Yeah. Accusations don't go stale, they keep. Surprisingly well.

NPC: To learn that, I'm going to send you straight to the source: Reva Sikora is the person who made the accusation. And I want to be perfectly clear, here: I want the accuser assessed as much as their accusation.

Your response: Understood. But what is the charge?

NPC: The charge is nothing of the usual sort, like theft or treason. It is that Emilia Bracha has quietly stopped believing. That's all. But perhaps you should let Sikora put it in her own words.

NPC: So you talked to Sikora. What's your read on her?

Your response: Hard to tell how much of her accusation is true, but she clearly has something to gain by making it.

NPC: You still need to hear Sikora out first.

NPC: Most accusers have their own reasons. That much is not surprising. But, and this may be uncomfortable to you: That the accusation is made in self-interest does not make it false. So take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So. The next part is what you might call 'the job itself'. Nobody else in the Canyon wants it, and you're uniquely qualified to deal with it. So what do you say? Will you take it?

Your response: What does taking the job mean, exactly?

Your response: Let me prepare for this, first.

NPC: You need to be sure about what you're doing, because I'm giving you all the leeway. I will not review the outcome. It's all up to you.

NPC: You are to question Bracha yourself, and then act on what you conclude. There will be no tribunal, and no appeal afterwards. There will be a judge, a jury, and an executioner. And it will all be you.

Your response: So what if I conclude that she is innocent?

NPC: Then nothing happens, and Sikora will be furious. It will be up to you. It may not be what the movement expects. But don't let that make you waver.

NPC: Emilia Bracha has stopped believing in the cause of the Canyon! Why won't somebody do something about her spreading falsehoods?! The movement cannot afford to suffer the likes of her!

Your response: Alright, I'm listening. What did she actually do?

NPC: She did what? What she did? Well, nothing! It's what she has been saying, and who she has been saying it to!

Your response: So explain to me where the crime is.

NPC: Why won't anybody take this seriously?! Belief is the only thing that holds this movement together! Someone quietly dissolving it is doing more damage to us than even the worst of City agents ever could!

Your response: What's your game? What do you get out of this accusation, personally?

NPC: What do you mean? Why would you ask a thing like that?! I don't have to stand here and take this abuse! Maybe your own beliefs are wearing thin too, huh? How about that!

NPC: I have nothing further to say to the likes of you!

NPC: I can guess why you're here. I have been expecting this. At least ask me properly.

Your response: Emilia Bracha, do you still believe in the movement?

NPC: I do not. I think the movement is misguided, and that it is trying to save people from something they do not wish to be saved from. My husband was an infiltrator. When he came back here from his assignments, he described the fulfilled, content lives the people in the City live. And the movement couldn't have that, so he was killed. And I will never forgive them for it.

Your response: So this is what you have been telling people around here?

NPC: I have. I'd much rather be honest with people than keep them in for a cause that has lost all its credibility to me. So what is it you're going to do about it?

Your response: I was prepared to give you what I was given recently: The benefit of the doubt. But I see that you are beyond salvation.

NPC: Salvation? There is no salvation! And when you realize that, in maybe a year, remember me!

NPC: ...

NPC: So what did Bracha say? Did you ask her properly?

Your response: Her husband turned, when he infiltrated the City. And when he was brought to justice for it, she lost her conviction.

NPC: You still need to deliver the verdict on Bracha.

NPC: You still need to question Bracha.

NPC: That is a serious reason, not to be dismissed easily. The siren song of the City is strong. And that's precisely why the movement wanted a Monk like you to deal with this situation. You'd be willing to listen to the reason, first.

Your response: I was prepared to give her what you gave me: The benefit of the doubt. But she didn't deserve it. Even though the accusation seemed so flimsy.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.
