• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me state the problem plainly: We are not fighting the City for territory or resources, we are fighting over people. And while we live in this Canyon, the people in the City have jobs and are mostly fine. So do you think we can argue someone out of being comfortable?

Your response: Intriguing. Do go on.

Your response: I may need to get back to you on that.

Your response: This is so far beneath me, honestly, it is insulting. Please leave my apartment. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: First, I'm going to send you to Halina Brecht in the Barracks. She is the one responsible for the recruitment of our movement. You should ask her what it is that she promises those willing to listen.

Your response: Are her promises truthful, or does she peddle falsehoods?

NPC: Talk to her. She will answer your question better than I ever could. Pay close attention to what she says, but even closer to the parts she doesn't mention. Go.

NPC: So what did you learn? Is her speech truthful, or a lie? Is it good, or bad? Is it successful, or failing?

Your response: Her rhetoric is flawless, and she manages not to say one falsehood. But her success rate leaves something to be desired. About three quarters of the recruits are back in the City within half a year.

NPC: You have not spoken to Brecht yet. She is in the Barracks.

NPC: That is a big number, make no mistake about it. But you assume that the best speech in the world would achieve a success rate of ten out of ten. My experience says that it doesn't. But you'll draw your own conclusions, anyway. Which is good. Get back to me in a bit.

NPC: So. Your next job will be unpleasant and administrative. But I need a preacher to do it, not a clerk. Will you do it?

Your response: For certain, but you have failed to tell me what it is, yet.

Your response: I will not falter. But you will need to give me a moment.

NPC: Sure. This matter has waited that long, it can wait a bit longer.

NPC: There are some lockers in HQ. We have no organized system here, people just set up their locker somewhere safe, put their stuff in it, then padlock it. Some of our dead sisters and brothers still have their locker up in HQ. They need to be cleared. Clear at least five of them, then bring me their contents, all the personal effects they left in there.

Your response: First you make me learn about Canyon propaganda, then you make me do a clerk's job. What am I supposed to make of this?

NPC: Nothing, yet. But a clerk would just bring five boxes with stuff in them, and a preacher will bring back five names with stories behind them. And that will be the only material you're ever going to work with. So go to HQ, and clear those lockers out.

NPC: Did you read the names on the labels? Have you read the stories behind the personal effects?

Your response: I did. And when I did, I noticed a name I glimpsed earlier, but it was listed as active. Might be a relative, perhaps. The name was 'Ruz'.

NPC: You still need to clear those lockers.

NPC: That would be Peter Ruz who's dead, and Stefan Ruz, who's still alive. That makes sense, and I think Stefan already knows. He's been going on about how our cause isn't worth it. And people are listening. So you may already guess what I expect next from you. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: The last job is a conversation. Plain and simple, and yet it will be the hardest thing I could ask of you. Are you ready?

Your response: I assume I am going to talk Stefan into not abandoning the movement.

Your response: Not yet.

NPC: Take your time, get ready, and then talk to me again.

NPC: That's exactly right. You are going to take his brother's effects to him personally, and you are going to make him believe all the more in the movement, not less.

Your response: So I am supposed to take his grief, twist it, and then turn him around, all the way.

NPC: Absolutely. And I won't pretend that it is anything other than that, I am fully aware what I am asking of you. The City buries its dead quietly and hopes their family stays quiet, too. The movement will call out its losses, by name. It will weep, it will mourn. And it will be stronger for it.

NPC: Welcome, my friend, to the Canyon! You will quickly understand what our movement is all about, and equally quick in joining up, once you... wait a minute, that's not why you're here, are you?

Your response: Jones sent me. I mean to hear what you tell those people who come to our gates.

NPC: This is what I tell them: You're here because deep down, you know the promises of the City to be false. It took your life, then rented it back to you, a bed, a wage and a number. And then it taught you to say 'thank you' for it, instead of wondering what happens when you ask the wrong question. Here, in the Canyon, nobody counts you, and nobody decides for you where to stand when the shooting starts. The City has a place for you: replaceable, fed, forgotten. We offer you a purpose, and people who will know your name!

Your response: Great rhetoric. So how much of all that survives the first month, here?

NPC: What do you think? What people who arrive here experience day to day, even when their heads are filled with ideas to the brim, is bad pay, worse food, and things crawling out of the caves to terrorize them at night. More than three quarters of our recruits disappear here and magically reappear in the City within half a year, telling tall tales of being abducted.

Your response: That's not a great success quota for your speech then, is it.

NPC: I'm not lying about what life in the Canyon is like. All I'm making is a claim about what we're all here for. In my personal opinion, that's the more important argument, and I absolutely stand by it, one hundred percent.

NPC: That's really all I have to say about it.

NPC: ...so why do we keep fighting a fight that we cannot possibly win? It is this simple truth... hang on. What are you carrying there? Oh no. Oh no. Please, don't show me. If this is what I think it is, I don't want to know.

Your response: Son, these are the earthly effects of your brother. May he rest in peace.

NPC: This... this is his picture of us two, on a drom hunt as little kids. And this... oh no, I cannot... Oh geez...

Your response: Your brother, Peter Ruz, fought the good fight, and he died a hero to our people. We will mourn his death together.

NPC: Thanks... Honestly, thank you. He was such a good person, always believed in the good cause. What am I supposed to do without my brother? He always knew what to do.

Your response: He always believed in the cause of our movement. And where he dropped the torch, you're going to pick it up, and carry it further, further than it's ever been. To honor his memory.

NPC: Yes. Yes, I will. And I have been telling people that our fight is pointless. Oh no, what have I done? Guys! Come back! I've made a terrible mistake! Our cause is just! Please, listen to me! We need to...

NPC: Please! I need to undo some of the damage I did!

NPC: Ruz took the personal effects of his brother, I assume. So how did it go down?

Your response: He remembered how his brother always believed in the good cause. And that made him see the error of his ways.

NPC: You still need to carry the personal effects of Peter Ruz to his brother.

NPC: That one concession is worth more than a hall full of people cheering. I hope you realize what a great service you have done to us. This is how the movement is held together.

Your response: Your turn to answer truthfully: Do you feel anything at all about how this was actually accomplished?

NPC: I do, absolutely. There is a whole rainbow of emotions going through me right now. And unless you can say the same about yourself, you're of no use to me.

Your response: I can.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send two modules your way, an aggressive and a passive one. I assume you understand the symbolism. You've earned them. Keep your Psi skills well trained, you're gonna need them. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Let me be perfectly clear. Nobody around here funds 'interesting research', and the only science happening around here is done by people with no equipment, and on problems the City has no reason to care about. And this is the point where you either lose all interest, or where your interest is actually piqued.

Your response: Piqued, definitely.

Your response: Give me a moment to consider.

Your response: Oh, I believe there is interesting research here, you're just not offering it. So please go.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Then let's begin with some fact finding. Go see Doc Sarn in the Barracks. Find out what the people in this Canyon actually present with. I don't want to just trust my impression of it.

Your response: What you're expecting might be important, though.

NPC: I'm not going to tell a researcher what to expect. That's how you get the answer you wanted, not necessarily the right one. Let's see what answer you come up with on your own, and then we can compare notes.

NPC: So you talked to Sarn. What did he observe?

Your response: There seems to be a cluster of infectious diseases going on based on where people live, or spend the night, rather than on what they do.

NPC: You still need to talk to Doc Sarn in the Barracks.

NPC: And the pattern that follows where people live and not what they do points at either parasites, or something everybody is drinking. I had hoped for someone qualified to say that out loud. Thank you. Give me some minutes to do some communications, then get back to me.

NPC: If we want to turn this problem into something that's certain not to be waved away, we need some field work done.

Your response: Alright, what do you need?

Your response: Hang on a moment.

NPC: If I am right, the water is not going to get better while we think about it.

NPC: What I need is eight samples from the water sampling points set across every level of the Facility. Not just one level, or our case goes straight out the window and will be dismissed. We need to be able to compare sites.

Your response: What do you mean? Who will be doing the dismissing?

NPC: That is a very good question. But before you've gotten the results, better not to burden you with the politics behind it all. So get going.

NPC: You've succeeded. What do the samples say?

Your response: I wanted to draw up a chart on where the water seems to be most contaminated. But as it turns out, there is just one source. Look.

NPC: Do take a look at those sampling points, now.

NPC: I know that site. There's a fuel and chemical dump there. Has been there since before the Canyon was properly settled, really. That's not- Hmmm. Get back to me on that one.

NPC: These results need to go up. I'd take it myself, but I'd say it's probably better if it is brought up by the person who took the samples. Will you do that?

Your response: And why would that be better?

Your response: Give us a moment, please.

NPC: Don't sit on it too long. Sitting on findings is how they turn into somebody else's decision.

NPC: What you will report is a legitimate finding. Anything I report immediately becomes part of the politics. This needs to be addressed. So go to the Intelligence Center in HQ, and talk to Commissar Ledek in there.

Your response: What should I expect Ledek to do?

NPC: I honestly do not know. My advice is to give him those numbers straight, and not to negotiate on them. They are facts, and should be treated as such.

NPC: Pull a number and take a seat, I'll be with you shortly.

Your response: I'm not here about that. I want to know what people around here are presenting with.

NPC: Do you? That's unusual. Nobody asks, normally. But anyway, I treat mostly wounds from battle with the City or from cave critters, and more and more infectious diseases.

Your response: Those infectious diseases are what interests me, does the infection pattern follow any particular group?

NPC: Not so much by social group or faction. It's more along regional lines. Basically, it's where people sleep. Some parts of the Canyon seem to lead to more infections. Cause unknown.

Your response: That sounds bad. Why have you never reported this?

NPC: What makes you think I haven't? In fact, I did! Twice! And nothing came of it. They said they'd look into this, and that was that. You asking is actually the first sign I ever saw that somebody seems to be looking into this.

NPC: I must get back to my patients. Too many sick, too little time worrying about why they're getting sick.

NPC: Welcome to the Intelligence Center, comrade. What can I do for you? I hear that you have made a certain discovery. Am I correct in believing that you are here to report your findings?

Your response: Yes, you are. The old fuel and chemical dump seems to have corroded its way into the local water pipes, and the people living in that part of the Canyon are getting sick from it.

NPC: Let me see those findings of yours - yes, that is unequivocal, isn't it. Those numbers make for grim, but clear reading, and your analysis is flawless.

Your response: So what's going to happen to my findings now?

NPC: What do you mean? Your findings are not in question here. The science does not lie. There is however a political dimension that I cannot afford to ignore. Our whole movement is based on the claim that we can live freely out here. Any story that casts doubt on our self-reliance immediately makes our numbers of new recruits drop, and the City has eyes and ears everywhere. A proper reaction to these findings would be an immediate quarantine of the area, and that is something we cannot do.

Your response: But you can't ignore my findings either! If people get sick around here, that won't exactly be a recruitment slogan either, will it?

NPC: No, it won't. Make no mistake: I was not prepared to sweep this under the rug. But our reaction will not be as expeditious as it would be without this political dimension. We will clean that area of the Canyon up, fix the pipes, the whole works. But slowly, quietly. That will mean that until the work is finished, more people will get sick. That is unfortunate, but sadly, cannot be helped. You are to be commended for a great service to the Canyon, however. Please do accept my sincere thanks. The Canyon is glad to have bright minds like yours among its ranks.

NPC: Do not let me keep you.

NPC: Your face tells me that Ledek reacted exactly the way I had feared.

Your response: He says quickly cleaning it up would lead to bad PR, so they're gonna do it, but slowly and quietly.

NPC: You still need to deliver your findings. Ledek is in the Intelligence Center, in HQ.

NPC: I won't defend his decision. I have watched the movement do this before. It seemed quite wrong then, and it seems quite wrong now. I have no other words for that.

Your response: Are you going to fight this?

NPC: The best I can do is make sure that those numbers do not get lost. In fact, now that you have raised them, I will raise them again, and again, regularly. That's not the same as fighting, I have to admit. I hope you can find solace in the fact that your findings are true, they're yours, and no one can take that away from you.

Your response: I'm a scientist. What am I supposed to do with that?

NPC: Your job. Keep taking samples, keep the record honest - and sometimes, just outlast the people who would rather not know. I'm gonna send a Research Tool your way. You've earned it. Keep your Research skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. Your trade is considered a crime in the City. Around here, it is considered 'the economy'. A person who gets you what you need can go far around here. Can you?

Your response: Given time, yes. Didn't have much time to organize a distribution network, though.

Your response: If you'll give me a moment first, sure.

Your response: Not for you. I'll do quite fine on my own. Please leave.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: For your first task, you won't need one. We're starting off with a simple pickup: We have dead drops, spread across the Canyon. Clear five of them out and bring me their contents. And don't ask what's in them.

Your response: So what's in them?

NPC: Very funny. I will not tell you. And you will not risk a peek, either. I will not accept opened merchandise. Get used to that. Out here, the person carrying the stuff often doesn't know what it is that they're carrying. So get going.

NPC: So. Did you peek?

Your response: I didn't need to. By the weight, and the way they felt, I'm pretty sure I already know what's inside. And that makes me wonder who actually agreed my price.

NPC: You still need to clear out those five drops.

NPC: I did, and you're in no position to negotiate. Not if you want to work for us, anyway. You're right, though. The much more interesting question is who sets the price on the far end. Take five, then get back to me, and you're gonna find out that that person is not in the Command Center.

NPC: You're back. So, do you want to meet the person who actually decides how much the Canyon can afford?

Your response: Sure. Who is that?

Your response: Could you give us a moment, please?

NPC: Oh, sure. She will still be setting the prices tomorrow.

NPC: Bara Tesar is the name. You will find her by the wasteland traders. Tesar knows the price of everything that crosses into this Canyon. And who fixes each price.

Your response: That seems like a weird arrangement. Why does the movement put up with that?

NPC: We put up with it, because the alternative is nothing arriving at all. But I will let Tesar explain the mathematics behind all that.

NPC: Yeah. I can see it in your face that you have now understood the barrel she has us over.

Your response: She said that there's the guy in the City, guy who cleans the route, guy who runs the route and her. Each taking their cut, their hazard pay and a monopoly margin.

NPC: You still need to talk to Tesar.

NPC: Honestly, this makes me so mad that it is difficult for me to keep my composure. We threw off a government, only to let one person with a monopoly on the only route become another quasi-government, with all taxes and no representation. Because I sure as hell did not vote for this woman.

Your response: The only feasible route, that is.

NPC: What do you mean? Did she say that? If there is another route, we must use it. And if it is unfeasible, we need to make it feasible. Let me make a few calls, then get back to me.

NPC: There *is* a second route in. And no matter what Tesar says, it is feasible. It just collapsed and had some critters move into the remains. I had someone clear out the debris, and someone else move stuff from a passing trader into there. Now I need you to prove that this new route will work end to end. You in?

Your response: Absolutely. I'd love to wipe that smirk off Tesar's face.

Your response: Hang on, let me get my stuff.

NPC: Hurry up. Those caches will not sit there indefinitely. And my patience with the current arrangement is stretched to the limit as well.

NPC: The end of the route goes through Canyon Cave 1. Carry three consignments out of there from the caches, and we can finally undercut this choking monopoly.

Your response: What will happen to the people whose prices we break?

NPC: They lose parts of their margins, not their lives. This is no time to be hesitant. Go into that cave and get the goods!

NPC: What have we here? A fellow trader. And one who knows how to get things, but doesn't know how the prices around here work yet, I'd wager.

Your response: Yes, about that. How *do* the prices work here, actually?

NPC: You know what a new, pristine water purifier costs in the City? Around 30 K. You know what that thing costs here? About 100 K. And make no mistake: I know how indecent that gap is. But everyone along the line gets their cut, their hazard pay, and so on.

Your response: Who does, besides you?

NPC: The people I made the arrangement with. The operator within the City, the guy who keeps my route free, and the guy who runs the route. Plus: There's no alternative. So everyone takes a monopoly markup. Yes, myself included. Nobody is arguing about those margins.

Your response: Has anyone tried?

NPC: Oh yes. But sooner or later, they stopped. Because mine is the only way in. Well, the only feasible one, that is.

NPC: I have said all I'm gonna say to you.

NPC: It worked. You got the consignments out of there. How did the route hold up?

Your response: The beasts in there are a bit of a nuisance, but nothing that can't be handled.

NPC: Canyon Cave 1. Go!

NPC: Then the old monopoly has just crumbled. Prices are gonna drop hard for a lot of stuff that is normally difficult to come by out here.

Your response: Are they, though? Or are you planning to be the new monopoly, and I do the runs for you?

NPC: No. I made sure that will never happen. I already told several people about the new route. Now I will just confirm that it is fully open. This will not be a secret, but common knowledge. We won't get held over a barrel again. It's great when people like you can get you what you need. But if they run a monopoly on half the Canyon's needs, we cannot accept that.

Your response: Fair enough, I guess.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send an Experimental Barter CPU your way. You've earned it. Keep your Bartering skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: You are past the point where I can teach you anything, comrade. You earned your spurs without me. Go keep our cause alive. Shall I clear out of your quarters?

Your response: Yes. Thanks anyway, Jones.

NPC: You don't have the skills I am looking for. No offense.

NPC: Let's get one thing out of the way, first: 'Jones' isn't my real name. And don't tell me yours, or I'd have to kill us both. And believe me: I can. People around here like to call themselves soldiers, but they're volunteers who showed up when they liked, and they can leave whenever they like. So self-references aside, this is no army. Can you work under these conditions?

Your response: Yes, ma'am.

Your response: I can, I just need a moment.

Your response: May I invite you to leave my barrack room. Now.

NPC: Offer remains open, the work never ends. Find me before you outrank it, though: I don't recruit past level /25.

NPC: Then the first thing I will send you out to deal with is Canyon Cave 1. Clear out ten of whatever critters have moved in there. And in case you're wondering: Yes, this is a test, not a crisis intervention.

Your response: So what is it that I am being tested for?

NPC: I am testing whether you finish a tedious job that nobody makes you finish. That is the only kind of discipline I have access to. So get going, clear out ten of them from Canyon Cave 1, and then come back. Or, you know, don't come back.

NPC: You killed the full ten, didn't you? Had it ever occurred to you to stop at six, and just claim it was ten? I wouldn't have had any way to check.

Your response: That would have been dishonest.

NPC: Canyon Cave 1 is not cleared out yet, and yet here you are.

NPC: That's all we rely upon out here. In the City, you can bet that somebody would have checked, honesty be damned. That is the trade the movement made out here, and it costs us more than people think. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: Ah, there you are. I'd like you to spend some time with the person who trains the Canyon's fighters.

Your response: That makes sense.

Your response: I will, but I need a moment, first.

NPC: Sure. Vada is not going anywhere.

NPC: Then go and meet Ilinca Vada here in the Canyon. Be sure to ask her what she is actually allowed to make anybody do around here.

Your response: Given what I've heard so far, I assume she is allowed very little?

NPC: Close to nothing, more like, and yet, Vada gets results anyway. So that is definitely a trick worth learning.

NPC: Have you learned what Vada does instead of giving orders?

Your response: She makes people take pride in what they do, and they don't want to fail. Slower than an order, and more personal, but effective.

NPC: You still need to speak with Vada.

NPC: Exactly right. A City sergeant can produce obedience in a week, and yet a frightened City soldier may still desert. Vada needs months, but after that, our soldiers fight to the death without fear. Take five, then get back to me.

NPC: So remember what you learned from Vada? Good, because this is a bit of an embarrassment: we haven't had a failure like this in months. Unfortunately, as you discovered, I am not able to deal with this - how shall I put it? - the easy way. At least not right away. I'm gonna ask you to deal with it.

Your response: What's the matter?

Your response: In a minute, hang on.

NPC: We're in a bit of a hurry here, so hurry, too. Please.

NPC: One of our guards, Niko Prey, has left his guard post. Simply walked off, and it is one that matters. Now he hangs out in the bar and is getting drunk instead. In an army, this would be a simple case for disciplinary action. Here, it is not.

Your response: Disciplinary action? Leaving your post on duty is desertion, the guy should be shot!

NPC: Probably, yes. But - and I'm not gonna give you any twaddle about motivation, there - shooting him would prove the City's account of what the Twilight Guardian is. I'm not going to hand them that PR victory over one man's failure of character. I hate it myself, but I'm going to ask you to go to him, and talk him into going back on duty.

NPC: Come here, join the training. We're right in the middle, but you'll catch on quickly enough.

Your response: Jones sent me. She wants me to ask you what you can actually order anyone to do.

NPC: Ha! Order? That's a good one. Everyone here is a volunteer, and can walk out of my session and out of the Canyon at any time. I won't rely on orders, I can't and I don't need to.

Your response: Then how do you get anything done?

NPC: Oh, quite simple. I make people want to be the person who didn't leave. I make them take pride in what they do, and not want to endure the shame of having failed. There is no other way.

Your response: And what do you do if it fails?

NPC: Then I lose the person I have worked with, try to learn what I could have done differently and better, and then I move on to the next. And for them, there is no punishment detail, no stockade. That is how our movement operates, and it does well like that.

NPC: I need to get on with the training.

NPC: Yeah? Yeah! I'm not at my post, and I'm drinkin'. In fact, I'm drunk. What'chu gonna do about it, huh? Nothing. So shove off!

Your response: Soldier, why are you not at your post?

NPC: Why would I? What difference does it make? They sent my buddy, Rex, to guard some broken down City transport until our reclamation teams could get the goods. Yeah, when they got there, the goods were gone, and Rex was perforated like a sieve. They sent one man. Of course he wasn't going to survive that!

Your response: That does seem like really bad judgment, I'll give you that.

NPC: You don't understand, you- wait, what? You're agreeing with me? Well, agreeing won't change anything. If this is how they waste the people on guard duty around here, what's the point? Huh? What's the point?

Your response: It's not about duty. You never guard a thing, or a post. You guard for your fellow people, so that they can get the goods, so that they are not shot and killed by surprise. You always guard with your life. Some posts are just more dangerous than others. But no guarding is wasted. Rex was defending all of us. We should be thankful and honor his memory.

NPC: Jones sent you, didn't she. Well, you can tell her that she sent no idiot. Finishing my drink now. And then you can report that I am back on guard. The fresh air will sober me right up.

NPC: I am on my way back out there, now.

NPC: Niko Prey is back at his post, albeit swaying slightly. What did you say to him?

Your response: I reminded him that he stands guard for his fellow people. His grievance was legitimate, though. Sending one person out to guard a downed transport is a waste of a good life. And in this case, it was his personal friend.

NPC: Niko Prey is still in the bar instead of at his post.

NPC: That's what happened? I agree that this was a gross oversight. I will look into that matter, you have my word.

Your response: Would you really have had him shot, if I hadn't convinced him?

NPC: I want to, and I make no bones about it. Every single time something like this happens, I do. I haven't yet, though. And so far, it has never become necessary. Let's just hope it stays that way. I don't want the movement to turn into the very thing it fights, but that restraint comes with a price tag of uncovered posts, and there is only so much we can afford.

Your response: I guess I can accept that.

NPC: Good. I'm gonna send a Flamer your way. You've earned it. Keep your Heavy Combat skill well trained, you're gonna need it. Pay those terminals a visit, the Canyon has lots of missions on offer. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Are you quite sure? If I am gone, I am gone for good.

Your response: Yes, I am sure. Bye, already.

Your response: Uh, come to think of it, can we take this from the top?

NPC: Last chance. No changing your mind afterwards.

Your response: Geez. Are you going, or should I?

Your response: You know what? I just did.

NPC: Alright then. Remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

NPC: Fair enough. I will not waste a veteran's bunk space. The mission terminals will keep you busy - remember that the work never ends. Watch yourself out there.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Ah, runner.  Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Although Tech Haven is a dedicated technocracy, we do keep a small contingent of specialists who are able to take... practical measures to ensure Tech Haven's safety.

Your response: I'm not exactly what you'd call 'muscle'.

NPC: No. However, we have an opening for an agent with the skills to neutralise threats covertly. Looking at your profile, I believe you may be what I'm looking for.

Your response: You're talking about a Hit-Man?

NPC: No - that implies a lack of finesse. We're looking for professional - someone who can eliminate calmly and efficiently, and then disappear...

Your response: Alright - I'm interested.

NPC: Good. Firstly, I want to run you through a quick combat test. We've established drones at the Drone Racetrack for you to fight. Take down 5 of them and report back to me.

NPC: Excellent. I was concerned that your time in stasis may have interfered with your weapon skills. It appears that is not the case.

Your response: That's good to know, what next?

NPC: Go and finish off the drones, and then we'll talk.

NPC: I think it's time we give you something a little more realistic and see how you do. Talk to me again, once you're ready.

NPC: Am I right to assume you wish to continue with your mission?

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Ah Runner, welcome to Tech Haven. I've been reading your notes, and it appears that you are quite handy in a fight. I have something for you, if you're interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Good. Now, you've been in MC5 for some time, and I want to make sure none of your motor-functions are impaired. We've set up some training bots at the Drone Racetrack - go and kill 5 of them.

Your response: Are you sure I shouldn't start on sewer rats or something?

NPC: Very funny. Get going.

NPC: Welcome back runner. That was better than a sewer, wasn't it?

Your response: Marginally. What's next?

NPC: Go and finish off the drones, and then we'll talk!

NPC: Well, that weapon you're using isn't really up to the job. Let's sort you out with something a little better. Speak with me again, when you're ready.

NPC: Right - I've had word that the geek... erm... Scientists have come up with some kind of new polymer.

Your response: Okay...

NPC: It's extremely light, but very strong.

Head to Tech Haven Sec-3's Retail Area and speak with Jared Hanson. Retrieve some of the polymer for me - I have an idea.

NPC: Yes, can I help you?

Your response: Jones sent me, about the polymer you're working on.

NPC: Ah yes, it's quite remarkable. We've taken a standard ultradence polycarbide, and increased its tensile strength by...

Your response: Uh huh. Look, I don't really care. I'm just here for the polymer, pal.

NPC: Oh. Oh no, that's not really possible, you see this...

Your response: Again - not interested. Hand it over.

NPC: *Hanson looks down at your fists and turns white*
I... I c-could c-call Security...

Your response: And I could beat you to death with your own shoes. Polymer! Now!

NPC: Oh. G-good point, w-well made! Here, take it.

NPC: You got what you came for - head back to your apartment and leave me alone!

NPC: Ah you're back.

Your response: Yes, and I have the polymer!

NPC: Go and speak with Jared and check on production, %PLAYER_NAME().

NPC: So, I've had a report coming in about 'a shaved Gorilla', putting the frighteners on lab staff. You wouldn't know anything about this, would you?

Your response: Nope. Nothing.

NPC: You need to get the polymer from Hanson.

NPC: Thought not. Well done at any rate. I have one more task for you - speak with me when you're ready.

NPC: Right - the final step. We have the polymer - now to put it to good use.
I've forwarded some plans to a contact of mine, Cory Weyland. He's going to turn this stuff into a decent blade for you.

Your response: Sounds good, where do I take this stuff?

NPC: Head back to the Drone Racetrack and speak with Cory Weyland.

NPC: Ah, Jones told me to expect you. Let me take a look at that stuff... Yes... fantastic. This will make a fine blade. Let me load it into the constructor.

Your response: Wait - you don't make them with a forge and a hammer?

NPC: Jones said you were bring me a new type of Polymer. Return with it and we'll begin.

NPC: Two things: One - It's plastic. Two - does this look like the 19th Century?

Your response: Fair...

NPC: Won't take me long... There, finished. Take it back to Jones, make sure it matches her plans.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Ah you're back.

Your response: Indeed!

NPC: Go and speak with Weyland.

NPC: Let me have a look at the sword.

Your response: Here it is.

NPC: Don't come back until you have the sword from Weyland.

NPC: Excellent. You could shave with this. Weyland has done a fantastic job with this sword. Well, I said you needed a better tool for your job - here, take the sword.

Your response: Seriously? This is fantastic!

NPC: Well, giving you this sword benefits Tech Haven as a whole. Make good use of it, %PLAYER_NAME()!

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Ah, runner. I am Mrs. Jones. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm led to believe that you have a particular set of skills. Skills I would like to make use of.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Glad to hear it. As you're likely aware, Tech Haven is situated quite comfortably
in a mountain range, half way between the Dome of York and Neocron City.

Your response: Uh huh.

NPC: Although this affords us security and a necessary amount of solitude, it also raises logistical issues.

Your response: Yeah, I bet. Go on.

NPC: We rely on drivers to transport both supplies and personnel safely across the toxic wastes. This is where you come in.
We're working on a new all-terrain vehicle, which should make transport equipment and personnel more efficient, and we'd like you to test it.

Your response: Amazing - how do I start?

NPC: I'm a big believer in drivers understanding their vehicles. With that in mind, you're going to assist in the building of the prototype, and the construction of the vehicle. So first, head over to Sean Burton at the ASG in sector F07. He's in the process of breaking down a number of vehicles, and has some parts you will require.

NPC: Oh, for pity's sake! Not more garbage. Put it over there with the rest.

Your response: Actually, I'm making a collection, not a delivery. Jones said you have some parts for an ATV?

NPC: Thank goodness. I kept getting brought trash - I've got a pile of it bigger than me... well, you know - it's pretty big. Anyway. Yes, here are the components you'll need.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: There you are! How are you?

Your response: That wasn't an easy task, but I walked over to Sean Burton and carried those parts back like a true champion.

NPC: You got nothing for me...?

NPC: You need to go and speak with Sean Burton. Come back when you have.

NPC: Very funny. Now give me a moment to double-check these. Speak with me again when you're ready to proceed.

NPC: Okay - time to fit those parts. Head out and speak with Dana Ord, she will guide you. Don't let her age fool you - she might be a youngster, but she's one hell of a mechanic. It's like machines speak to her.

Your response: Hey, as long as she can do the job, I'm happy

NPC: That's the spirit. She's waiting for you at the 'Hacker's Delight' bar at the Drone Racetrack.

NPC: Hiya, I'm Dana. I heard you have parts for George.

Your response: George?

NPC: Oh... sorry - that's what I called the quad. Ahem. Anyway, pass them here and I'll get them fitted.

Your response: Make sure you don't hurt George.

NPC: There we go - and he ticks over as well! Shiny!

Your response: Wow, that was impressively fast!

NPC: Aww thanks! Okay, now we know that this little guy runs, take the production datacube back to Jones. She knows what to do.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Did you enjoy meeting Dana?

Your response: Oh yeah... she's something else.

NPC: Don't keep Dana waiting, or she'll deconstruct the air vents again...

NPC: Isn't she just. She can strip an engine faster than I can tie my shoes. Hand me the production datacube.

Your response: Here you go!

NPC: I need the datacube!

NPC: Great. Now, all we need to do is get the schematics off for production. Let's talk again when you have time to do that.

NPC: Alright - final part. I've sent the schematics through to Jase Cubbon in Tech Haven Sec-1 - he usually hangs around near the Gravity Lifts. Go and check on the production of these things.

NPC: What do you want?

Your response: Jones sent me about plans - she said we're ready for a test run.

NPC: Oh did she now? Well, that's just great. I'm up to my eyeballs here and she sends you sauntering in and... Fine. Fine. Let's see what she sent me... Hmm, actually, this isn't a bad design. I see what they've done here... clever.

Your response: It sounds like we're good to go then, right?

NPC: Sure. Actually, it looks like my assistance already started the run, and one's ready - take it to Jones.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: Ah you're back. I hope Cubbon didn't give you any trouble.

Your response: Nothing I couldn't handle - but he did give me this.

NPC: Go and speak with Jase and check on production, %PLAYER_NAME().

NPC: Ah, fantastic. This will allow you to retrieve one of the test quads from an ASG station.
I'll tell you what, you keep hold of that - as payment for your help.

Your response: Hey thanks, I'll try not to break it.

NPC: I thought Cubbon gave you something?

NPC: Actually, it wouldn't be a bad thing if you did break it. We'd learn from the experience and make improvements. Anyway, I have things to tend to. Take care, %PLAYER_NAME().

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• Hello Runner, I am Mrs. Jones. I represent the Administration of Tech Haven, and I have use of an individual with your professional interests. Are you interested?

• No doubt you are already aware - Tech Haven is mostly a self-sufficient sanctuary for the scientific minds of the Fallen Angels. However, there are certain materials and supplies which cannot be produced here. For these items, we rely on trade caravans from the waste lands. Recently, one such caravan came under attack - its occupants mostly wiped out.

• Of that, I am not currently sure. The bodies have been recovered, and are being investigated by Doctor Tyrell outside of Tech Haven in E07 - she will be near the ramp. If you speak with her, she should be able to shed more details on the situation.

• There are security measures at the entrance to Tech Haven, turrets, put in place to prevent intrusion. I have had a report that they have come online just now and killed someone attempting to enter the facility. Call this intuition, but it seems strange that this has occurred so soon after the attack on the traders. Go to Tech Haven Sec-1 - near the bottom of the Gravity Lifts and see what you can find.

• (After searching the body, you find a canister and a technical diagram of Tech Haven's ventilation systems. It seems that the plan was to use the contents of the canister attack the inhabitants of Tech Haven. However, there are no signs as to whom the individual is working for. This should be reported to Jones at once.)

• The administration has given me this to pass to you - as a token of their appreciation. Keep up the good work - Tech Haven can use someone with your potential.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Hello Runner, I am Mrs. Jones. I represent the Administration of Tech Haven, and I have use of an individual with your professional interests. Are you interested?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now.  Another time?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: No doubt you are already aware - Tech Haven is mostly a self-sufficient sanctuary for the scientific minds of the Fallen Angels. However, there are certain materials and supplies which cannot be produced here. For these items, we rely on trade caravans from the waste lands. Recently, one such caravan came under attack - its occupants mostly wiped out.

Your response: What attacked them?

NPC: Of that, I am not currently sure. The bodies have been recovered, and are being investigated by Doctor Tyrell outside of Tech Haven in E07 - she will be near the ramp. If you speak with her, she should be able to shed more details on the situation.

NPC: Ah, you must be the Runner that Jones sent - she just contacted me to say that you were coming. I see you are a Monk... you are too late to save these people.

Your response: Jones mentioned that you might have some information on the cause of death?

NPC: Quite so. We have completed the autopsy. There are significant wounds on each body - they had all been shot. But that's not all: Each of them was found to have chemical burns to their lungs. We believe that, and not the gunshots, was the cause of death. However, we would need a fresher sample to determine the nature of the chemicals used.

Your response: But why would you bother wasting ammunition by shooting a dead body? It makes no sense.

NPC: I'd wager that they were attempting to cover up the true nature of the attack - the gunshots would be sufficient to fool a casual observer. Please, take my findings back to Jones. She will decide what to do next.

NPC: Please return to Mrs. Jones at your apartment to report these findings.

NPC: Ah Runner - what did you discover?

Your response: Dr. Tyrell advised that the caravan appears to have been attacked with a type of chemical agent, and that the bodies were shot afterwards as a coverup.

NPC: You need to speak with Dr. Tyrell regarding the autopsy report!

NPC: And the type of chemical are we talking about?

Your response: Unknown - she said we'd require a fresh sample to determine that.

NPC: I see. This is peculiar. I will see if I can find any more information for myself. I will be in touch soon.

NPC: Ah, perfect timing, I have another task for you. Are you interested?

Your response: Not right now, I will be back though.

Your response: Of course - what do you need?

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me.

NPC: There are security measures at the entrance to Tech Haven, turrets, put in place to prevent intrusion. I have had a report that they have come online just now and killed someone attempting to enter the facility. Call this intuition, but it seems strange that this has occurred so soon after the attack on the traders. Go to Tech Haven Sec-1 - near the bottom of the Gravity Lifts and see what you can find.

NPC: (After searching the body, you find a canister and a technical diagram of Tech Haven's ventilation systems. It seems that the plan was to use the contents of the canister attack the inhabitants of Tech Haven. However, there are no signs as to whom the individual is working for. This should be reported to Jones at once.)

NPC: (You can't find any more information here.)

NPC: You're back. What did you find?

Your response: A corpse, a canister, and a diagram of our ventilation systems. Here, take a look.

NPC: Come back to me with whatever you find.

NPC: You should know what to do!

NPC: What?! This is an outrage! I need to contact the Administration with these findings, and ensure that that appropriate measures are taken. Please, take this reward, and speak with me shortly. You have done a very good job today.

NPC: Your assistance has been invaluable to us so far. Are you ready for one last task?

Your response: Of course, how can I help?

Your response: I have other things to do. I will be back though.

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me.

NPC: I need you to take the canister straight to Dr. Carylon Thoran at the Fallen Angels Tech Core's Medical Room. She is ready to analyse the contents, so that we know what we're dealing with.

NPC: Ah, greetings Runner. Jones told me all about it. Give me the canister, and we'll see what we're working with...

Your response: Yeah, sure!

NPC: Now, let me just feed a sample into the analyser...

Your response: So how long is this gonna take?

NPC: I need the canister if you want me to continue.

NPC: Oh, this will likely take a few hours. Please return to Mrs. Jones and let her know that I will contact her once I know the nature of the contents - and I have a suitable plan for neutralising their usage.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting...

NPC: Runner, your assistance has been invaluable. Soon, Dr. Thoran will have a counter-measure in place against any more attempted attacks.

Your response: That's good to know!

NPC: Take the canister to Dr. Thoran at the Fallen Angels HQ's Medical Room.

NPC: The administration has given me this to pass to you - as a token of their appreciation. Keep up the good work - Tech Haven can use someone with your potential.

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Ah Runner, welcome to Tech Haven. It says here that you have network security experience. I have use of your skills, if you're interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: Good to hear it. As you probably already know, Tech Haven has one of the most sophisticated networks in the world - and has access to both Neocron and the Dome of York's networks.

Your response: If I understand it correctly, Tech Haven is a hub, and also keeps a lot of the uplinks in the wastelands going.

NPC: Something like that. I'm not a tech-specialist. However, as you can appreciate, being at the top also paints a large target on our backs. So we have to routinely monitor network security.

Your response: Let me guess, that's where I come in right?

NPC: Exactly. Head to the Small Database Link terminal in Tech Haven Sec-2 - you'll find it near the tools and parts traders. Access the ALPHA TERMINAL inside there, and run this program. Come back when it's done.

NPC: (The scanner whirls away for a few moments, and then identifies that a number of ports have been opened recently. Checking the logs, it appears that they were all done by the same person. It feels unusual. This should be reported to Jones.)

NPC: E R R O R  4 0 1  - - -  A B O R T  - - -  N O   I N P U T   F O U N D

NPC: Welcome back runner. I trust everything is in order?

Your response: Actually, I've spotted something which I think you should take a look at.

NPC: Go and complete the security scan, and we will talk.

NPC: Hmm. This is very peculiar. All of these ports correspond with some very sensitive material. It looks like these changes might have been internal as well.

Your response: You mean someone in Tech Haven did this? Do you have any idea who?

NPC: Not yet. Give me a moment to think, and we will discuss this further!

NPC: It's my understanding that we have a secondary system which logs all access to our networks. It uses a form of internal authentication to prevent external changes.

Your response: I'm assuming that this system has some form of logging procedure. So, we can find out who made the changes?

NPC: That's the plan. The secondary system isn't something we publicise, so there's a very good chance our friend wasn't aware their actions were recorded. Head back to the same Hacknet Terminal in Sector 2 and access BETA TERMINAL within!

NPC: (It appears that the system has indeed taken a full log of the security breach. Jones would be interested in seeing this.)

NPC: Connection terminated!

***Access Denied!***


***Authorisation required from Agent Jones to access***

NPC: You're back, and with the security logs. Let me see.

Your response: Here they are.

NPC: Come back with the security logs.

NPC: Oh my. Not good. Did you read these?

Your response: Yes, I did. All the ports were opened by one employee - Harrington, G.

NPC: Agreed. I will begin a search for Mr. Harrington. Speak with me in a moment, and we can proceed.

NPC: Alright, I've located Harrington. He's in Energy Core 1. The entrance to that is located within Tech Haven Sec-1 - I want you to question him.

Your response: Why not just send security?

NPC: I don't want to scare him off. See what you can learn, then return to me.

NPC: Yes? Can I help you?

Your response: George Harrington, I have a couple of questions for you.

NPC: I'm sorry, I really don't have time to chat right now.

Your response: I recommend that you make time, this is about a security breach in Tech Haven's network.

NPC: W-what? No. I d-don't know anything about that.

Your response: I pulled logs from another system which recorded your access credentials, and the changes that were made.

NPC: Oh... No. That wasn't me. S-someone must have used my password!

Your response: Then why are you sweating so much? Listen, answer my questions, or I'll call security. Co-operate and I'll see what can be done for you!

NPC: No, please. Don't. Okay, look. I admit that I opened the ports. I needed the money, and I thought I could sell some research projects or something.

Your response: You were trying to sell out the whole of Tech Haven for a few credits? That's pretty low.

NPC: You don't understand. I owe money to the kinds of people you don't want to owe anything to. This was my last chance to get clean, now I have nothing.

Your response: Okay. Look, the only thing I can suggest is we take you in - place you in custody, so they cannot get to you.

NPC: And let Tech Haven security have their way with me instead? No way.

Your response: What's it gonna be, then?

NPC: I'm a dead man now - but I can still go on my own terms! (Before you have time to react, Harrington pulls out a pistol, places it in his mouth and pulls the trigger. You should let Jones know about this.)

NPC: Did you deal with Harrington?

Your response: Yeah - he iced himself.

NPC: Don't come back until you've spoken with Harrington.

NPC: What? He's dead? Did you have a chance to speak with him?

Your response: Briefly, before he ate his own pistol. He said he was working alone - selling data to cover some debts.

NPC: Selfish idiot. He risked lives over something so trivial?

Your response: He did. What happens now?

NPC: I'll set a team plugging any remaining security holes. I'm going to go and check Harrington's apartment and make sure he was working alone. Here, take this - I think we might speak again in the future.

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

entries.details:
CONTACT
Not identified in the client NPC definitions.

CONDITIONS FOUND
• Checks base rank: at most 25; outcome depends on the dialogue branch.

POSSIBLE LOCATION CLUES IN DIALOGUE
• Ah, runner. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I have a task that I need assistance with, if you are interested.

• First: Although Tech Haven is a dedicated technocracy, I do want to assure you that you are welcome here.

• We have an agreement of sorts with settlers in the area. We trade equipment made here for supplies they bring in from the outside world. However, we have reason to believe they are attempting to spread an alien influence within Tech Haven.

• It appears that the leader of the wastelanders is about to enter a meeting to negotiate further trade with Tech Haven. I want you to question him first, then return to me. You should find him near the Fallen Angels Tech Core entrace, in Tech Haven Sec-2.

• Go and speak with the Wasteland Lt. outside of the Fallen Angels Tech Core, in Tech Haven Sec-2.

• Yes, mutants... a reconnaissance crew picked up a mutant camp in the hills outside of Tech Haven - they're using Tech Haven equipment.

This script can include several missions and alternative outcomes. Read the dialogue for context; items listed may apply only to particular choices.
entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Ah, runner. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I have a task that I need assistance with, if you are interested.

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: First: Although Tech Haven is a dedicated technocracy, I do want to assure you that you are welcome here.

Your response: Reassuring - I thought you'd look down on a PSI Monk.

NPC: We are reasonable and logical - we learned difficult lessons from your predecessors, but we do not hold those experiences against you personally.

Your response: Fine - what about this task you mentioned?

NPC: We have an agreement of sorts with settlers in the area. We trade equipment made here for supplies they bring in from the outside world. However, we have reason to believe they are attempting to spread an alien influence within Tech Haven.

Your response: What sort of influence are you referring to?

NPC: We're unsure at the moment. They have been limiting key resources - releasing them only when we agree to supply weapons - something which they have not previously requested.

Your response: Protecting yourself in the wastes isn't suspicious.

NPC: No, but the frequency and volume is. We need to ensure that they are not distributing them to Neocron - or to any other unsavoury party

Your response: Okay, and where do you recommend I start looking?

NPC: Go ahead and speak with Declan Swan inside the Fallen Angels Tech Core. He's their primary handler and might be able to give you some insight on where to begin looking.

NPC: Yes? How can I help? Keep it brief.

Your response: Jones sent me about the unusual demands being made by local traders.

NPC: Ah yes... that. They've begun to request weapons, ammunition, clothing, and other supplies. All in much larger volumes than a settlement of their size could require.

Your response: Do you have any idea why that is?

NPC: I only asked once, and their response was quite disagreeable. I understand that they are expecting an influx of new occupants in the near future.

Your response: I wonder where they might be coming from. There are only so many folks in the wastes.

NPC: Honestly, I couldn't say. We've left them encamped outside the city as a precaution, but I understand one of their lieutenants is currently outside the Command Centre, waiting for a meeting.

Your response: Thanks for the info, Declan.

NPC: You should head back to Jones and let her know about this...

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Welcome back - did Declan give you anything useful?

Your response: Not really. He thinks that the traders are preparing for a sudden settlement expansion.

NPC: Come back once you've spoken with Declan.

NPC: Peculiar. I'm not aware of any groups in the area which would be large enough to require this amount of equipment. What else did he say?

Your response: One of their leaders is currently in front of the Fallen Angels Tech Core, waiting for a meeting.

NPC: Ah yes, I seem to remember hearing about that. Let me check on the reason for the meeting - speak to me again in a moment.

NPC: Am I right to assume you wish to continue with your mission?

Your response: Let's do this!

Your response: I've got other things to do. Speak soon?

NPC: It appears that the leader of the wastelanders is about to enter a meeting to negotiate further trade with Tech Haven. I want you to question him first, then return to me. You should find him near the Fallen Angels Tech Core entrace, in Tech Haven Sec-2.

NPC: Very well, I shall wait here for you.

NPC: Make it quick, I'm heading in there soon.

Your response: I'd like to know why you're suddenly ramping up your equipment requests.

NPC: Yeah, and what's it to you?

Your response: I'm the one asking the questions here. There aren't enough people in the wastes to warrant that much stuff.

NPC: Sure, there's not enough humans, but settlements do grow, you know!

Your response: Wait. What do you mean by that? You said not enough humans...

NPC: No, I said enough people - you're mishearing things!

Your response: And now you're sweating. Just what are you up to out there?

NPC: You're deluded pal, I never said...

Your response: Drop the act. Tell me what you're up to, or I'll have you placed in custody and find out.

NPC: Oh, well now. That's going to be difficult - IF YOU'RE DEAD!

NPC: ...

NPC: There was talk of a commotion outside the Fallen Angels Tech Core - was that you?

Your response: Yes, I met with the wastelander - he's not supplying the equipment to people... but to something else entirely!

NPC: Go and speak with the Wasteland Lt. outside of the Fallen Angels Tech Core, in Tech Haven Sec-2.

NPC: Yes, mutants... a reconnaissance crew picked up a mutant camp in the hills outside of Tech Haven - they're using Tech Haven equipment.

Your response: Wow... pretty stupid to bring them along, huh?

NPC: That's what happens when you let people raise children in an irradiated wasteland... but that's beside the point. We need to deal with them. Speak with me when you're ready.

NPC: Are you ready to hit those mutants?

Your response: Sure, might as well finish this.

Your response: I'll come back to you

NPC: Very well, I shall wait here for you

NPC: Okay, then head out of Tech Haven Sec-3 into F_07, down the ramp and head straight. Once you have killed 5 Mutant Scouts, come back to report to me.

NPC: I take it you got them all?

Your response: I sure did!

NPC: Wipe out the mutants and come back here.

NPC: Good. That's at least one potential danger removed.

Your response: What about the other mutants that have already been armed?

NPC: Experience tells us that they'll mainly stay in the hills. Perhaps this time, we need to pay them a visit. Before I go - take this as a reward for your assistance.

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

entries.conversation:
NPC: Sorry, but you are definitely over-qualified for this job. Do you want me to leave?

Your response: Yes, please!

NPC: Sorry, but I am not available for you.

NPC: Ah, runner. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I'm looking for someone to assist me in an urgent matter, are you interested?

Your response: I'm interested, how can I help?

Your response: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Another time?

Your response: I'm not interested in your tasks - please leave.

NPC: Very well, I will remain here for a while. (Return before level /25 to resume.)

NPC: I'm glad to hear this. We've had word that a member of Tech Haven's research team, Jason Wang, has been kidnapped.

Your response: Really? What were the demands?

NPC: Mainly, the blueprints his team was working upon. Secondly, a sum of credits in the form of precious metals.

Your response: What do you need me to do?

NPC: We're happy to release the credits, but not the blueprints. We're hoping the metals might buy some time for us to consider our next step.

Your response: Okay - tell me where I need to go.

NPC: Take this package and give it to Susan Yang who should be waiting near the stairway to the Fallen Angels Tech Core - the kidnappers requested that she handle the drop. Don't get any funny ideas about keeping the contents - we've placed tracking nanites on them.

NPC: Do you have the package from Jones?

Your response: Yes, it's right here.

NPC: I'm waiting for a courier from Jones!

NPC: Thank you for this. Return to Jones - she might have further instructions for you.

NPC: Mrs. Jones is waiting!

NPC: Excellent. Susan is going to act as an intermediary - she'll pass the package onto the kidnappers.

Your response: Why did they ask for her specifically?

NPC: Go and take the package to Susan Yang.

NPC: She's his wife - perhaps the figured she was less likely to try and trick them - since her husband's life is on the line. Speak with me in a moment, I'm starting up the tracking software.

NPC: Am I right to assume you wish to continue with your mission?

Your response: Let's do this!

Your response: I'll come back to you

NPC: Very well, you know where to find me

NPC: The tracking beacon seems to have stopped.

Your response: Want me to go and check it out?

NPC: Well... you look like you can take care of yourself, so that might not be a bad idea. The signal has stopped inside Energy Core 2. Head down and scout it out - but stay out of trouble.

NPC: (It looks like the body has been here for a few days. It appears he's been shot in the face making identification difficult, but the name tag on his chest says 'Yang, J'. The package is beside the body - opened, but the contents are still there. You should return to Jones.)

NPC: (You can't find anything else here.)

NPC: Well, did you find our man?

Your response: I can't be 100 percent, but I'm pretty sure I found his body in the Energy Core. Looked like he'd been dead for a couple of days.

NPC: You got nothing for me...?

NPC: Go and check out The Energy Core and come back to me.

NPC: Hmm - this isn't right. If his body has been there for days, then that's before his wife reported the kidnapping. This doesn't sit right at all.

Your response: They also left behind the metals. They opened the package, but then abandoned it. What do we do now?

NPC: I've just received some cleaned up security footage from the Scientists' apartment prior to the kidnapping. Speak with me in a moment, and we'll see what it tells us.

NPC: Are you ready for your last task?

Your response: Sure, might as well finish this.

Your response: I'll come back to you.

NPC: Very well, I shall wait here for you.

NPC: We've analyzed the footage. It begins several days before the kidnapping was reported and shows Jason and Susan Wang leaving together.

Your response: Go on.

NPC: Following them on the camera, we could see Susan leads Jason to the Energy Core. She sends him in first, before drawing a pistol and following him.

Your response: Holy shit! She was in on it?!

NPC: So it would appear. I need you to go and apprehend Susan Yang. I think we need to take her into custody and question her thoroughly.

NPC: Oh, hello, I wasn't expecting to see you again.

Your response: I need you to come with me and answer some questions about your husband's murder.

NPC: Murder? What do you mean? Why do you need to speak with me?

Your response: We have footage of you leading Jason into the Energy Core with a pistol. I found a body down there - I'm assuming it's his.

NPC: (Susan is silent for a few seconds, then sighs and looks at the ground.)
I had to do it. I had to get away from him.

Your response: What do you mean?

NPC: Jason was a horrible man. He mistreated me - badly. I was going to leave him.

Your response: So why the 'kidnapping' - why the request for the blueprints?

NPC: Honestly, I thought his research might be worth something - I was going to use it to buy my way into Neocron. The other stuff was just a diversion to keep everyone busy.

Your response: I think I understand. You have my sympathy, if this is true, but I still need to take you in.

NPC: I don't regret it... killing him, I mean. But I'm sorry for this...

NPC: ...

NPC: Did you take Susan Yang into custody?

Your response: No, she's dead.

NPC: Come back once you have spoken with Susan Yang, %PLAYER_NAME().

NPC: Unfortunate, what happened?

Your response: She admitted that the kidnapping was a cover-up. She wanted to take the blueprints and sell them to the City, in order to make a new life for herself. When I told her I still need to take her in, she drew a gun at me.

NPC: Self-defense, then. I'll feed this back to management. Speaking of - they have authorised me to present you with a gift for your services.

Your response: What is it?

NPC: I have two PSI modules, and you can choose which one you would like - offensive or defensive.

Your response: I'll take the offensive module please

Your response: I'll take the defensive module please

NPC: Are you sure you would like the offensive PSI module?

Your response: Yes, please.

Your response: Let me choose again, please!

NPC: Okay, here you are then! Thank you for your service. I imagine we may meet again in the future.

NPC: Are you sure you would like the defensive PSI module?

Your response: Yes, please.

Your response: Let me choose again

NPC: Here you are then! Thank you for your service. I imagine we may meet again in the future.

NPC: Are you sure about that?

Your response: Yes, I am!

Your response: Actually, no. I'll give it a try.

NPC: Think about it. I will not come back if you decide not to use my services.

Your response: I did think about it. Now please leave me alone.

Your response: Uh, ahm, oh well, I think I just reconsidered.

NPC: Okay, as you wish. I will go. Take care of yourself.

• Ah, runner. Welcome to Tech Haven - your new home. I hear you're interested in using Drones. We've set up a tutorial for you if you'd like to take part?
